- Root: ذ-خ-ر (dh-kh-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Storing, treasuring, laying up as a reserve for future need.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological context, a deed stored with Allah as an enduring reward (ajr) for the Hereafter.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of hoarding wealth; here metaphorical (majāz) for the spiritual merit reserved by divine acceptance.
- Root: و-ز-ر (w-z-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Burden, heavy load; also refuge (from wazara, to shelter).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Sin as a weight upon the soul; the supplication seeks its removal (waḍʿ) by divine pardon.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal physical burden; metaphorical for moral culpability.
- Root: ج-ب-ر (j-b-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To set a bone, mend, restore; to compensate.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Divine restoration of the servant’s deficiencies—physical, spiritual, or worldly.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal mending; here figurative for Allah’s repairing the worshipper’s state.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — The phrase «كما تقبلتها من داود» functions as a tasbīb (causal annex) linking the supplication to prophetic precedent, requiring the verb’s object to be understood as the prostration itself (al-sajdah), not merely the duʿāʾ.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that when one prostrates for the recitation (of the Qurʾān), it is recommended (mustaḥabb) to say in that prostration what we have mentioned regarding the prostration of the prayer.

And it is recommended to say along with it: 153 — «Allāhumma-jʿalhā lī ʿindaka dhukhran, wa-aʿẓim lī bihā ajran, wa-ḍaʿ ʿannī bihā wizran, wa-taqabbalhā minnī kamā taqabbal tahā min Dāwūda ʿalayhi al-salām» (O Allah, make it for me a treasure with You, and magnify for me thereby a reward, and remove from me thereby a burden, and accept it from me as You accepted it from David, peace be upon him).

And it is also recommended to say: «Subḥāna rabbinā in kāna waʿdu rabbinā la-mafʿūlā» (Glory be to our Lord—indeed, the promise of our Lord is ever fulfilled). Al-Shāfiʿī explicitly stated this latter (supplication).

154 — We have related in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd, al-Tirmidhī, and al-Nasāʾī, on the authority of ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to say in the prostration of the Qurʾān: «Sajada wajhī li-lladhī khalaqahu, wa-shaqqa samʿahu wa-baṣarahu bi-ḥawlihi wa-quwwatihi» (My face has prostrated to the One who created it, and who opened its hearing and sight by His might and His power). Al-Tirmidhī said: A sound ḥadīth. Al-Ḥākim added: «Fa-tabāraka Allāhu aḥsanu al-khāliqīn» (So blessed is Allah, the best of creators). He said: This addition is sound according to the condition of the Two Ṣaḥīḥs.

As for his saying: «Allāhumma-jʿalhā lī dhukhran...» etc., al-Tirmidhī related it as raised (marfūʿ) from the narration of Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, with a good (ḥasan) chain. And al-Ḥākim said: A sound ḥadīth.

(Chapter on what is said upon raising the head from prostration and during the sitting between the two prostrations)

The Sunnah is to pronounce the takbīr from the moment one begins to raise (the head), extending the takbīr until one is settled in a sitting position. We have already presented the explanation of the number of takbīrs, the disagreement concerning their extension, and the extension that invalidates them. When one finishes the takbīr and is settled sitting, the Sunnah is to supplicate with what we have related in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd, al-Tirmidhī, al-Nasāʾī, al-Bayhaqī, and others, on the authority of Ḥudhayfah, may Allah be pleased with him, in his previously mentioned ḥadīth concerning the Prophet’s prayer, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, at night—his lengthy standing with (Sūrat al-Baqarah), (al-Nisāʾ), and (Āl ʿImrān), his bowing similar to his standing, and his prostration similar to that. He said:

155 — He used to say between the two prostrations: «Rabbi-ghfir lī, Rabbi-ghfir lī» (My Lord, forgive me; my Lord, forgive me), and he sat for a duration equal to his prostration.

156 — And by what we have related in the Sunan of al-Bayhaqī, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās, in the ḥadīth of his overnight stay at the house of his maternal aunt Maymūnah, may Allah be pleased with her, and the Prophet’s prayer, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, at night—he mentioned it, saying: When he raised his head from the prostration, he said: «Rabbi-ghfir lī wa-rḥamnī wa-jburnī wa-rfaʿnī wa-rzuqnī wa-hdinī» (My Lord, forgive me, have mercy on me, mend me, raise me, provide for me, and guide me).

Section: When one prostrates the second prostration, he says in it the same as what we mentioned for the first. When he raises his head from it, he raises with a takbīr, and sits for the sitting of rest (jalsat al-istirāḥah)—a brief sitting such that his movement settles with a clear stillness. Then he rises to the second rakʿah, extending the takbīr with which he raised from prostration until he stands upright, the extension being after the lām of «Allāh». This is the most correct of the positions (awjaḥ al-wujūh) of our companions. They also hold a position that he raises without a takbīr, sits for the rest, and when he rises, he says the takbīr. And a third position: he raises from prostration with a takbīr, then when he sits, he cuts off the takbīr, then rises without a takbīr.

There is no disagreement that he does not utter two takbīrs in this place. Our companions only said the first position is most correct so that no part of the prayer is devoid of remembrance (dhikr).

157 — Know that the sitting of rest is an established, sound Sunnah in the Ṣaḥīḥ of al-Bukhārī and others, from the actual practice of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Our school holds it recommended (istiḥbāb) due to these sound ḥadīths. It is recommended after the second prostration of every rakʿah from which one rises, and it is not recommended in the prostration of recitation during the prayer. And Allah knows best.

(Chapter on the remembrances of the second rakʿah)

Know that the remembrances we mentioned for the first rakʿah are all performed in the second, just as we detailed for the first—regarding supererogatory (nafl) aspects and other mentioned branches—except in certain matters.

First: The first rakʿah contains the takbīrat al-iḥrām, which is a pillar (rukn); the second is not so, for one does not say the takbīr at its beginning—rather, the takbīr before it is for rising from prostration, and it is a Sunnah.

Second: The opening supplication (duʿāʾ al-istiftāḥ) is not prescribed in the second, unlike the first.

Third: We have stated that one seeks refuge (taʿawwudh) in the first without disagreement; in the second there is disagreement. The most correct view is that he seeks refuge.

Fourth: The chosen view is that the recitation in the second is less than the first, and therein lies the disagreement we have already presented. And Allah knows best.

(Chapter on the Qunūt in the Dawn Prayer)

Know that the qunūt in the dawn prayer (ṣalāt al-ṣubḥ) is a Sunnah.

158 — Due to the sound ḥadīth therein, on the authority of Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, never ceased performing the qunūt in the dawn prayer until he departed this world. Al-Ḥākim Abū ʿAbd Allāh related it in his book al-Arbaʿīn, and he said: A sound ḥadīth.

Know that the qunūt is legislated in our school for the dawn prayer, and it is an emphasized Sunnah (sunnah muʾakkadah). If one abandons it, his prayer is not invalidated, but he performs the prostration of forgetfulness (sujūd al-sahw)—whether he abandons it deliberately or forgetfully.

As for the other prayers among the five, is the qunūt performed therein? There are three positions of al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah have mercy on him. The most correct and well-known of them: if a calamity (nāzilah) befalls the Muslims, they perform the qunūt in all the prayers during that time; otherwise, no.

The second: they perform it absolutely.

The third: they do not perform it absolutely. And Allah knows best.

It is recommended in our school to perform the qunūt in the latter half of Ramaḍān, in the last rakʿah of the witr prayer. We also hold a position to perform it throughout all of Ramaḍān, and a third position: throughout the entire year—which is the school of Abū Ḥanīfah. The well-known view of our school is the first. And Allah knows best.

chapters.title_en: Section 25 — On the Qunūt in the Morning Prayer (Ṣalāt al-Ṣubḥ)
chapters.arabic_text:
# فصل:
# اعلم أن محل القنوت عندنا في الصبح بعد الرفع من الركوع في الركعة

الثانية.
# وقال مالك رحمه الله: يقنت قبل الركوع.
# قال أصحابنا: فلو قنت شافعي قبل الركوع لم يحسب له على الأصح، ولنا  وجه

أن يحسب، وعلى الأصح، يعيده بعد الركوع ويسجد للسهو، وقيل: لا يسجد.
# وأما لفظه، فالاختيار أن يقول فيه: 

| 159 - 
# ما روينا في الحديث الصحيح في سنن أبي داود، والترمذي، والنسائي، وابن

ماجه، والبيهقي، وغيرها، بالإسناد الصحيح عن الحسن بن علي رضي الله عنهما

قال: علمني رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كلمات أقولهن في الوتر: " اللهم

اهدني فيمن هديت، وعافني
# فيمن عافيت، وتولني فيمن توليت، وبارك لي فيما أعطيت، وقني شر ما قضيت،

فإنك تقضي ولا يقضى عليك، وإنه لا يذل من واليت، تباركت ربنا وتعاليت ".
# قال الترمذي: هذا حديث حسن، قال: ولا نعرف عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

في القنوت شيئا أحسن من هذا.
# وفي رواية ذكرها البيهقي: أن محمد بن الحنفية (1) ، وهو ابن علي بن أبي

طالب رضي الله عنه قال: إن هذا الدعاء [هو الدعاء] الذي كان أبي يدعو به في

صلاة الفجر في قنوته (2) .

| 160 - 
# ويستحب أن يقول عقيب هذا الدعاء: " اللهم صل على محمد، وعلى آل محمد وسلم

"، فقد جاء في رواية النسائي في هذا الحديث بإسناد حسن (3) : " وصلى الله

على النبي ".

| 161 - 
# قال أصحابنا: وإن قنت بما جاء عن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه كان حسنا،

وهو أنه قنت في الصبح بعد الركوع فقال: " اللهم إنا نستعينك ونستغفرك ولا

نكفرك، ونؤمن بك ونخلع من يفجرك، اللهم إياك نعبد، ولك نصلي ونسجد، وإليك

نسعى ونحفد، نرجو رحمتك ونخشى عذابك، إن عذابك الجد بالكفار ملحق.
# اللهم عذب الكفرة الذين يصدون عن سبيلك، ويكذبون رسلك، ويقاتلون أولياءك.
# اللهم اغفر للمؤمنين والمؤمنات والمسلمين والمسلمات، وأصلح ذات بينهم،

وألف بين قلوبهم، واجعل في قلوبهم الإيمان والحكمة، وثبتهم على ملة رسولك

صلى الله عليه وسلم، وأوزعهم أن يوفوا بعهدك الذي عاهدتهم عليه، وانصرهم

على عدوك وعدوهم إله الحق واجعلنا منهم ". 
# واعلم أن المنقول عن عمر رضي الله عنه " عذب كفرة أهل الكتاب "، لأن

قتالهم ذلك الزمان كان مع كفرة أهل الكتاب، وأما اليوم، فالاختيار أن يقول:

" عذب  الكفرة " فإنه أعم.
# وقوله: نخلع: أي نترك، وقوله: يفجر أي: يلحد في صفاتك، وقوله نحفد بكسر

الفاء، أي: نسارع، وقوله: الجد بكسر الجيم: أي الحق، وقوله: ملحق بكسر

الحاء على المشهور، ويقال بفتحها، ذكره ابن قتيبة وغيره وقوله: ذات بينهم،

أي: أمورهم ومواصلاتهم، وقوله: والحكمة، هي: كل ما منع من القبيح، وقوله:

وأوزعهم: أي ألهمهم، وقوله: واجعلنا منهم، أي: ممن هذه صفته.
# قال أصحابنا: يستحب الجمع بين قنوت عمر ي ضي الله عنه وما سبق، فإن جمع

بينهما، فالأصح تأخير قنوت عمر، وإن اقتصر فليقتصر على الأول، وإنما يستحب

الجمع بينهما إذا كان منفردا أو إمام محصورين يرضون بالتطويل.
# واعلم أن القنوت لا يتعين فيه دعاء على المذهب المختار، فأي دعاء دعا به

حصل القنوت ولو قنت بآية، أو آيات من القرآن العزيز وهي مشتملة على الدعاء

حصل القنوت، ولكن الأفضل ما جاءت به السنة.
# وقد ذهب جماعة من أصحابنا إلى أنه يتعين ولا يجزئ غيره.
# واعلم أنه يستحب إذا كان المصلي إماما أن يقول: " اللهم اهدنا " بلفظ

الجمع، وكذلك الباقي، ولو قال " اهدني " حصل القنوت وكان مكروها، لأنه يكره

للإمام تخصيص نفسه بالدعاء.

| 162 - 
# وروينا في سنن أبي داود، والترمذي، عن ثوبان رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول

الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " لا يؤم عبد قوما فيخص نفسه بدعوة دونهم، فإن

فعل فقد خانهم " قال الترمذي: حديث حسن.
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق-ن-ت (q-n-t)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of devout obedience, standing in supplication, and humility before God; in prayer, it denotes a specific posture of supplication.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Theological nuance — qunūt is an act of servitude (ʿubūdiyyah) combining prayer (duʿāʾ), submission (khushūʿ), and persistence (dawām) in invoking God.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — standing in obedience; metaphorical (majāz) — the specific liturgical supplication recited in a prescribed posture.
- Root: ر-ف-ع (r-f-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To raise, elevate; in prayer, the act of rising from bowing (rukuʿ).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Elevation as a physical marker of transition between liturgical states.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — bodily raising; metaphorical — spiritual elevation toward the Divine.
- Root: س-ج-د (s-j-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Prostration; the act of placing the forehead on the ground in worship.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The ultimate physical expression of servitude and annihilation of ego before God.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — physical prostration; metaphorical — humility of the heart.
- Root: س-ه-و (s-h-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Forgetfulness, inadvertence; in prayer, a lapse requiring compensatory prostration.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Human fallibility in worship; the legal remedy (sajdat al-sahw) restores liturgical perfection.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — mental absence; metaphorical — ritual imperfection needing expiation.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — The text employs conditional clauses (e.g., "if he does X, then Y") and exceptions ("on the soundest opinion") requiring precise parsing of protasis and apodosis to preserve legal nuance.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that the place of the qunūt in our school (al-Shāfiʿī) in the morning prayer is after the raising from the bowing (rukuʿ) in the second unit (rakʿah).

Mālik — may God have mercy on him — said: He performs the qunūt before the bowing.

Our companions (aṣḥābunā) said: If a Shāfiʿī performs the qunūt before the bowing, it is not counted for him on the soundest opinion (al-aṣaḥḥ); and we have a face (wajh) that it is counted. On the soundest opinion, he repeats it after the bowing and prostrates for forgetfulness (sajdat al-sahw). And it was said: He does not prostrate.

As for its wording, the choice (al-ikhtiyār) is that he says therein:

[159] — What we have related in the authentic hadith in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd, al-Tirmidhī, al-Nasāʾī, Ibn Mājah, al-Bayhaqī, and others, with an authentic chain (isnād) on the authority of al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī — may God be pleased with them both — who said: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and grant him peace — taught me words to say in the witr prayer: «اللهم اهدني فيمن هديت، وعافني فيمن عافيت، وتولني فيمن توليت، وبارك لي فيما أعطيت، وقني شر ما قضيت، فإنك تقضي ولا يقضى عليك، وإنه لا يذل من واليت، تباركت ربنا وتعاليت» (O God, guide me among those whom You have guided, and grant me well-being among those whom You have granted well-being, and take me into Your charge among those whom You have taken into Your charge, and bless me in what You have given, and protect me from the evil of what You have decreed — for You decree and none decrees over You, and he whom You take as friend is not humiliated. Blessed are You, our Lord, and exalted).

Al-Tirmidhī said: This is a good (ḥasan) hadith. He said: We do not know of anything from the Prophet — may God bless him and grant him peace — concerning the qunūt more excellent than this.

In a narration mentioned by al-Bayhaqī: That Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥanafiyyah — and he is the son of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib — may God be pleased with him — said: This supplication is the supplication that my father used to make in the morning prayer in his qunūt.

[160] — It is recommended (yustaḥabb) that he say after this supplication: "O God, send blessings upon Muḥammad and upon the family of Muḥammad, and grant them peace." For it has come in a narration of al-Nasāʾī in this hadith with a good chain: "And may God send blessings upon the Prophet."

[161] — Our companions said: If he performs the qunūt with what has come from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb — may God be pleased with him — it is excellent. And it is that he performed the qunūt in the morning prayer after the bowing and said: "O God, we seek Your aid and seek Your forgiveness and do not disbelieve in You, and we believe in You and we repudiate (nakhlaʿu) whoever disobeys You (yafjuruk). O God, You alone we worship, and to You we pray and prostrate, and to You we hasten and strive (naḥfid). We hope for Your mercy and fear Your punishment — indeed, Your severe punishment (al-jadd) is surely to be inflicted upon the disbelievers (mulḥaq). O God, punish the disbelievers who turn away from Your path, deny Your messengers, and fight Your allies. O God, forgive the believing men and believing women, and the Muslim men and Muslim women, and set right their affairs (dhāt baynihim), and unite their hearts, and place in their hearts faith and wisdom (al-ḥikmah), and establish them upon the creed of Your Messenger — may God bless him and grant him peace — and inspire them (awziʿhum) to fulfill Your covenant which You have made with them, and grant them victory over Your enemy and their enemy, O God of Truth, and make us among them."

Know that what is transmitted from ʿUmar — may God be pleased with him — is "punish the disbelievers of the People of the Book," because their fighting at that time was against the disbelievers of the People of the Book. As for today, the choice is that he say: "punish the disbelievers" — for it is more general.

His saying "nakhlaʿu" (we repudiate) means: we abandon. His saying "yafjur" (disobeys) means: he deviates (yalḥad) regarding Your attributes. His saying "naḥfid" — with a kasrah on the fāʾ — means: we hasten. His saying "al-jadd" — with a kasrah on the jīm — means: the truth (al-ḥaqq). His saying "mulḥaq" — with a kasrah on the ḥāʾ on the well-known (mashhūr) pronunciation, and it is said with a fatḥah — was mentioned by Ibn Qutaybah and others. His saying "dhāt baynihim" (their affairs) means: their matters and their mutual connections. His saying "al-ḥikmah" (wisdom) is: everything that prevents from the reprehensible. His saying "awziʿhum" (inspire them) means: instill in them (alhimhum). His saying "make us among them" means: among those who possess this description.

Our companions said: It is recommended to combine between the qunūt of ʿUmar — may God be pleased with him — and what preceded. If he combines between them, the soundest opinion is to delay the qunūt of ʿUmar. If he limits himself, let him limit himself to the first. And combining between them is only recommended when he is praying alone or as an imam for a limited congregation (maḥṣūrīn) who are content with prolongation.

Know that the qunūt is not restricted to a specific supplication on the chosen school (al-madhhab al-mukhtār). Whatever supplication he makes, the qunūt is fulfilled — even if he performs the qunūt with a verse, or verses, of the Mighty Qurʾān that contain supplication, the qunūt is fulfilled. But the most virtuous is what has come in the Sunnah.

A group of our companions have held that it is restricted and that nothing else suffices.

Know that it is recommended, when the worshipper is an imam, that he say: "O God, guide us" (allahumma ihdinā) in the plural form, and likewise the rest. If he says "guide me" (ihdinī), the qunūt is fulfilled but it is disliked (makrūh), because it is disliked for the imam to single himself out with the supplication.

[162] — We have related in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd and al-Tirmidhī, on the authority of Thawbān — may God be pleased with him — who said: The Messenger of God — may God bless him and grant him peace — said: «لا يؤم عبد قوما فيخص نفسه بدعوة دونهم، فإن فعل فقد خانهم» (No servant leads a people in prayer and singles himself out with a supplication to the exclusion of them; for if he does so, he has betrayed them). Al-Tirmidhī said: A good (ḥasan) hadith.

# فصل:
# اختلف أصحابنا في رفع اليدين في دعاء القنوت ومسح الوجه بهما على ثلاثة

أوجه.
# أصحها: أنه يستحب رفعهما، ولا يمسح الوجه.
# والثاني: يرفع ويمسحه.
# والثالث: لا يرفع ولا يسمح.
# واتفقوا على أنه لا يمسح غير الوجه من الصدر ونحوه، بل قالوا: ذلك مكروه.
# وأما الجهر بالقنوت والإسرار به، فقال أصحابنا: إن كان المصلي منفردا أسر

به، وإن كان إماما جهر على المذهب الصحيح المختار الذي ذهب إليه الأكثرون

والثاني: أنه يسر كسائر الدعوات في الصلاة، وأما المأموم، فإن لم يجهر

الإمام قنت سرا كسائر
# 
# الدعوات، فإنه يوافق فيها الإمام  سرا.
# وإن جهر الإمام بالقنوت، فإن كان المأموم يسمعه أمن على دعائه، وشاركه في

الثناء في آخره، وإن كان لا يسمعه، قنت سرا، وقيل: يؤمن، وقيل له أن يشاركه

مع سماعه، والمختار الأول.
# وأما غير الصبح إذا قنت فيها حيث يقول به، فإن كانت جهرية وهي المغرب

والعشاء، فهي كالصبح على ما تقدم، وإن كانت ظهرا أو عصرا، فقيل: يسر فيها

بالقنوت، وقيل: إنها كالصبح.

| 163 - 
# والحديث الصحيح في قنوت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على الذين قتلوا

القراء ببئر معونة يقتضي ظاهره الجهر بالقنوت في جميع الصلوات، ففي صحيح

البخاري في باب تفسير قول الله تعالى: (ليس لك من الأمر شئ) عن أبي هريرة

رضي الله عنه، أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم جهر بالقنوت في قنوت النازلة.

| (باب التشهد في الصلاة)
# اعلم أن الصلاة إن كانت ركعتين فحسب، كالصبح والنوافل، فليس فيها إلا

تشهد واحد، وإن كانت ثلاث ركعات أو أربعا، ففيها تشهدان: أول، وثان.
# ويتصور في حق المسبوق ثلاثة تشهدات، ويتصور في حقه في صلاة المغرب أربعة

تشهدات، مثل أن يدرك الإمام بعد الركوع في الثانية، فيتابعه في التشهد

الأول والثاني، ولم يحصل له من
# الصلاة إلا ركعة، فإذا سلم الإمام قام المسبوق ليأتي بالركعتين الباقيتين

عليه، فيصلي ركعة، ويتشهد عقبها لأنها ثانيته، ثم يصلي الثالثة ويتشهد

عقيبها.
# أما إذا صلى نافلة فنوى أكثر من أربع ركعات ولو نوى مائة ركعة، فالاختيار

أن يقتصر فيها على تشهدين، فيصلي ما نواه إلا ركعتين ويتشهد، ثم يأتي

بالركعتين، ويتشهد التشهد الثاني ويسلم.
# قال بعض من أصحابنا: لا يجوز أن يزيد على تشهدين، ولا يجوز أن يكون بين

التشهد الأول والثاني أكثر من ركعتين، ويجوز أن يكون بينهما ركعة واحدة،

فإن زاد على تشهدين، أو كان بينهما أكثر من ركعتين، بطلت صلاته.
# وقال آخرون: يجوز أن يتشهد في كل ركعة، والأصح جوازه في كل ركعتين، لا في

كل ركعة، والله أعلم.
# واعلم أن التشهد الأخير واجب عند الشافعي وأحمد  وأكثر العلماء، وسنة عند

أبي حنيفة ومالك.
# وأما التشهد الأول فسنة عند الشافعي ومالك وأبي حنيفة والأكثرين، وواجب

عند أحمد، فلو تركه عند الشافعي صحت صلاته، ولكن يسجد للسهو سواء تركه عمدا

أو سهوا، والله أعلم.
#
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ر-ف-ع (rafʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Lifting, elevating physically; raising a thing from its place.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In ritual acts, rafʿ al-yadayn signifies an outward gesture of humble petition (ḍarāʿah) toward the Divine.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in physical lifting; metaphorical (majāz) when denoting exaltation of rank — here literal.
- Root: م-س-ح (masḥ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Passing the hand over a surface; wiping.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In worship, masḥ al-wajh after supplication is a symbolic seeking of blessing (barakah) from the invoked Name.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal action; debated whether it carries ritual legitimacy or is a mere customary gesture.
- Root: ج-ه-ر (jahr)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Audibility, openness, as opposed to concealment.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Jahr in prayer relates to the legal distinction between silent (sirr) and audible recitation, tied to the nature of the prayer (jaharī vs. sirrī).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal in acoustic terms; legally technical in fiqh discourse.
- Root: ت-ش-ه-د (tashahhud)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Bearing witness; uttering the testimony of faith.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In prayer, the tashahhud is the verbal confession of divine unity and prophethood, a pillar of communicative worship.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal as a speech act; legally denotes the specific formula recited in the sitting posture.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Disjunctive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-taqsīm) — The text employs "إن كان... وإن كان..." to enumerate legal scenarios, requiring precise parsing of protasis and apodosis to preserve the juristic distinctions.
chapters.translation:
I say — Know that our companions (the Shāfiʿī jurists) differed concerning the raising of the hands in the qunūt supplication and the wiping of the face with them, holding three positions.

The soundest of them: that it is recommended (mustaḥabb) to raise them, and not to wipe the face.
The second: that one raises them and wipes the face.
The third: that one neither raises them nor wipes.

They unanimously agreed that one does not wipe anything other than the face, such as the chest and the like; rather, they said: that is disliked (makrūh).

As for audibility (al-jahr) in the qunūt and silence (al-isrār) therein, our companions said: if the worshipper is praying alone, he recites it silently; and if he is an imam, he recites it audibly — this is the sound and chosen position (al-madhhab al-ṣaḥīḥ al-mukhtār) adopted by the majority. The second position: that he recites it silently like the rest of the supplications within the prayer.

As for the one praying behind an imam (al-maʾmūm): if the imam does not recite audibly, he performs the qunūt silently like the rest of the supplications, for he follows the imam therein silently. And if the imam recites the qunūt audibly, then if the follower hears him, he says "āmīn" to his supplication and joins him in the praise (al-thanāʾ) at its end. And if he does not hear him, he performs the qunūt silently; and it was said: he says "āmīn"; and it was said: he may join him even upon hearing — but the chosen position is the first.

As for prayers other than the dawn prayer (al-ṣubḥ), when one performs the qunūt therein — in the position that holds it — then if it is an audible prayer (jaharīyah), namely the sunset (al-maghrib) and the night (al-ʿishāʾ), it is like the dawn prayer according to what has preceded. And if it is a noon (al-ẓuhr) or afternoon (al-ʿaṣr) prayer, then it was said: one recites the qunūt silently therein; and it was said: it is like the dawn prayer.

| 163 —

The authentic hadith concerning the qunūt of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) against those who killed the reciters (al-qurrāʾ) at the well of Maʿūnah — its apparent meaning (ẓāhiruhu) necessitates audibility of the qunūt in all prayers. For in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, in the chapter on the explanation of the saying of Allah the Exalted: {«لَيْسَ لَكَ مِنَ الْأَمْرِ شَيْءٌ»} ("You have no part in the matter"), on the authority of Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) recited the qunūt audibly in the qunūt of calamity (qunūt al-nāzilah).

| Chapter on the Tashahhud in Prayer |

Know that if the prayer consists of two rakʿahs only, such as the dawn prayer and the supererogatory prayers (al-nawāfil), then there is in it only a single tashahhud. And if it consists of three or four rakʿahs, then there are two tashahhuds in it: the first and the second.

It is conceivable, in the case of one who is preceded (al-masbūq), that there be three tashahhuds; and it is conceivable in his case, in the sunset prayer, that there be four tashahhuds — such as when he catches the imam after the bowing (al-rukūʿ) in the second rakʿah, then follows him in the first and second tashahhud, while he has not completed from the prayer except one rakʿah. So when the imam gives the salutation, the preceded one stands to complete the two remaining rakʿahs incumbent upon him: he prays one rakʿah and performs the tashahhud after it, because it is his second; then he prays the third and performs the tashahhud after it.

As for when one prays a supererogatory prayer and intends more than four rakʿahs — even if he intends one hundred rakʿahs — the preferred choice (al-ikhtiyār) is that he restrict himself therein to two tashahhuds: he prays what he intended except two rakʿahs, then performs the tashahhud, then comes with the two rakʿahs, performs the second tashahhud, and gives the salutation.

Some of our companions said: it is not permissible to exceed two tashahhuds, and it is not permissible that there be between the first and second tashahhud more than two rakʿahs; and it is permissible that there be between them a single rakʿah. For if one exceeds two tashahhuds, or there is between them more than two rakʿahs, his prayer is invalidated.

Others said: it is permissible to perform the tashahhud in every rakʿah. And the soundest position (al-aṣaḥḥ) is the permissibility of it in every two rakʿahs, not in every rakʿah. And Allah knows best.

Know that the final tashahhud is obligatory (wājib) according to al-Shāfiʿī, Aḥmad, and the majority of scholars; and it is a sunnah according to Abū Ḥanīfah and Mālik. As for the first tashahhud, it is a sunnah according to al-Shāfiʿī, Mālik, Abū Ḥanīfah, and the majority; and it is obligatory according to Aḥmad. Thus, if one omits it according to al-Shāfiʿī, his prayer is valid, but he performs the prostration of forgetfulness (sujūd al-sahw) — whether he omitted it deliberately or forgetfully. And Allah knows best.

# فصل:
# وأما لفظ التشهد، فثبت فيه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ثلاث تشهدات (1)

.

| 164 - 
# أحدها: رواية ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

" التحيات لله، والصلوات والطيبات، السلام عليك أيها النبي ورحمة الله

وبركاته، السلام علينا وعلى عباد چلله الصالحين، أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله،

وأشهد أن محمدا عبده ورسوله، رواه البخاري ومسلم في " صحيحيهما ".
# الثاني: رواية ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

" التحيات المباركات، الصلوات الطيبات لله، السلام عليك أيها النبي ورحمة

الله وبركاته، السلام علينا وعلى عباد الله الصالحين، أشهد أن لا إله إلا

الله، وأن محمدا رسول الله "، رواه مسلم في " صحيحه ".
# الثالث: رواية أبي موسى الأشعري رضي الله عنه، عن رسول الله صلى الله

عليه وسلم: " التحيات الطيبات الصلوات لله، السلام عليك أيها النبي ورحمة

الله وبركاته، السلام علينا وعلى عباد الله الصالحين، أشهد أن لا إله إلا

الله وأن محمدا عبده ورسوله "، رواه مسلم في " صحيحه ".

| 165 - 
# وروينا في سنن البيهقي بإسناد جيد (2) عن القاسم قال: علمتني عائشة رضي

الله عنها قالت: هذا تشهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " التحيات لله

والصلوات والطيبات، السلام عليك أيها النبي ورحمة الله وبركاته، السلام

علينا وعلى عباد الله الصالحين، أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله، وأشهد أن محمدا

عبده ورسوله "، وفي هذا فائدة حسنة، وهي أن تشهده صلى الله عليه وسلم بلفظ

تشهدنا.

| 166 - 
# وروينا في موطأ مالك، وسنن البيهقي، وغيرهما بالأسانيد الصحيحة، عن عبد

الرحمن بن عمر القاري - وهو بتشديد الياء - أنه سمع عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله

عنه 
# وهو على المنبر وهو يعلم الناس التشهد يقول: قولوا: " التحيات لله،

الزاكيات لله، الطيبات الصلوات لله، السلام عليك  أيها النبي ورحمة الله

وبركاته، السلام علينا وعلى عباد الله الصالحين، أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله

وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن محمدا عبده ورسوله ".

| 167 - 
# وروينا في الموطأ، وسنن البيهقي، وغيرهما أيضا بإسناد صحيح، عن عائشة رضي

الله عنها أنها كانت تقول إذا تشهدت: " التحيات الطيبات الصلوات الزاكيات

لله، أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وأن محمدا عبده ورسوله، السلام عليك أيها

النبي ورحمة الله وبركاته، السلام علينا وعلى عباد الله الصالحين ".
# وفي رواية عنها في هذه الكتب: " التحيات الصلوات الطيبات الزاكيات لله،

أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأن محمدا عبده ورسوله، السلام

عليك أيها النبي ورحمة الله وبركاته، السلام علينا وعلى عباد الله الصالحين

".

| 168 - 
# وروينا في الموطأ، وسنن البيهقي أيضا بالإسناد الصحيح، عن مالك، عن نافع،

عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما، أنه كان يتشهد فيقول: " بسم الله، التحيات لله،

الصلوات لله، الزاكيات لله، السلام على النبي ورحمة الله وبركاته، السلام

علينا وعلى عباد الله الصالحين، شهدت أن لا إله إلا الله، شهدت أن محمدا

رسول الله " والله أعلم.
# فهذه أنواع من التشهد.
# قال البيهقي: والثابت عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ثلاثة أحاديث (2)

: حديث ابن مسعود، وابن عباس، وأبي موسى، هذا كلام البيهقي.
# وقال غيره: الثلاثة صحيحة (3) وأصحها حديث ابن مسعود (4) .
# واعلم أنه يجوز التشهد بأي تشهد شاء من هذه المذكورات، هكذا نص عليه

إمامنا الشافعي (5) وغيره من العلماء رضي الله عنهم.
# وأفضلها عند الشافعي: حديث ابن عباس 
# للزيادة التي فيه من لفظ المباركات.
# قال الشافعي وغيره من العلماء رحمهم الله: ولكون الأمر فيها على السعة

والتخيير اختلفت ألفاظ الرواة، والله أعلم.

# فصل] :
# الاختيار أن يأتي بتشهد من الثلاثة، الأول بكماله، فلو حذف بعضه فهل

يجزيه؟ فيه تفصيل.
# فاعلم أن لفظ المباركات، والصلوات، والطيبات والزاكيات، سنة ليس بشرط في

التشهد، فلو حذفها كلها واقتصر على قوله: التحيات لله السلام عليك أيها

النبي ... إلى آخره، أجزأه.
# وهذا لا خلاف فيه  عندنا.
# وأما في الألفاظ من قوله: السلام عليك أيها النبي ... إلى آخره، فواجب لا

يجوز حذف شئ منه إلا لفظ " ورحمة الله وبركاته "، ففيهما ثلاثة أوجه

لأصحابنا، أصحها: لا يجوز حذف واحدة منهما، وهذا هو الذي يقتضيه الدليل

لاتفاق الأحاديث عليهما.
# والثاني: يجوز حذفهما.
# والثالث يجوز حذف " وبركاته " (1) دون " رحمة الله ".
# وقال أبو العباس بن سريج من أصحابنا: يجوز أن يقتصر على قوله: التحيات

لله، سلام عليك أيها النبي، سلام على عباد الله الصالحين، أشهد أن لا إله

إلا الله وأن محمدا رسول الله.
# وأما لفظ السلام، فأكثر الروايات، السلام عليك أيها النبي، وكذا " السلام

علينا " بالألف واللام فيهما.
# وفي بعض الروايات: " سلام " بحذفهما فيهما.
# قال بعض أصحابنا: كلاهما جائز، ولكن الأفضل: " السلام " بالألف واللام

لكونه الأكثر، ولما فيه من الزيادة والاحتياط.

| 169 - 
# أما التسمية قبل التحيات، فقد روينا حديثا مرفوعا في " سنن النسائي "

والبيهقي وغيرهما بإثباتها، وتقدم إثباتها في تشهد ابن عمر، لكن قال

البخاري والنسائي
# وغيرهما من أئمة الحديث: إن زيادة التسمية غير صحيحة عن رسول الله صلى

الله عليه وسلم، فلهذا قال جمهور أصحابنا: لا تستحب التسمية، وقال بعض

أصحابنا: تستحب، والمختار أنه لا يأتي بها، لأن جمهور الصحابة الذين رووا

التشهد لم يرووها.

- Root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To bear witness, to testify; presence and attestation.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The act of declaring faith with certainty, affirming the Oneness of Allah and the prophethood of Muhammad.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in legal context; metaphorical (majāz) when used for the ritual utterance itself.
- Root: ح-ي-ي (ḥ-y-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Life, greetings, salutations; derived from the root of "living" — implying enduring homage.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the tashahhud, "al-taḥiyyāt" denotes all forms of sovereignty and homage due exclusively to Allah.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for greetings; here transferred to divine worship (majāz mursal).
- Root: ط-ي-ب (ṭ-y-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Goodness, purity, pleasantness; opposite of khabīth (evil/foul).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): "Al-ṭayyibāt" refers to pure words and righteous deeds offered to Allah.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for wholesome things; metaphorical for prayers and virtuous acts.
- Root: ز-ك-و (z-k-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Growth, purification, increase in blessing.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): "Al-zākiyāt" — acts that purify the soul and are accepted by Allah.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for growth; metaphorical for spiritual purity in supplication.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — The sequence "al-ṣalawāt wa-al-ṭayyibāt" functions as coordinated appositives, each independently qualifying the preceding noun, requiring precise parsing to avoid redundancy.
chapters.translation:
**Section 27**

**Chapter: On the Wording of the Tashahhud**

Know that regarding the wording of the tashahhud, three authentic versions are established from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him).

**164.** The first is the narration of Ibn Masʿūd (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him): «Al-taḥiyyātu lillāhi, wa-al-ṣalawātu wa-al-ṭayyibāt, al-salāmu ʿalayka ayyuhā al-nabiyyu wa-raḥmatu Allāhi wa-barakātuh, al-salāmu ʿalaynā wa-ʿalā ʿibādi Allāhi al-ṣāliḥīn, ashhadu an lā ilāha illā Allāh, wa-ashhadu anna Muḥammadan ʿabduhu wa-rasūluh» — "All greetings, prayers, and pure words are for Allah. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon us and upon Allah's righteous servants. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger." This was narrated by al-Bukhārī and Muslim in their Ṣaḥīḥ collections.

The second is the narration of Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both), from the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him): «Al-taḥiyyātu al-mubārakāt, al-ṣalawātu al-ṭayyibāt lillāh, al-salāmu ʿalayka ayyuhā al-nabiyyu wa-raḥmatu Allāhi wa-barakātuh, al-salāmu ʿalaynā wa-ʿalā ʿibādi Allāhi al-ṣāliḥīn, ashhadu an lā ilāha illā Allāh, wa-anna Muḥammadan rasūlu Allāh» — "All blessed greetings, prayers, and pure words are for Allah. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon us and upon Allah's righteous servants. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." This was narrated by Muslim in his Ṣaḥīḥ.

The third is the narration of Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him): «Al-taḥiyyātu al-ṭayyibātu al-ṣalawātu lillāh, al-salāmu ʿalayka ayyuhā al-nabiyyu wa-raḥmatu Allāhi wa-barakātuh, al-salāmu ʿalaynā wa-ʿalā ʿibādi Allāhi al-ṣāliḥīn, ashhadu an lā ilāha illā Allāh wa-anna Muḥammadan ʿabduhu wa-rasūluh» — "All greetings, pure words, and prayers are for Allah. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon us and upon Allah's righteous servants. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger." This was narrated by Muslim in his Ṣaḥīḥ.

**165.** We have also narrated in the Sunan of al-Bayhaqī with a good chain (isnād jayyid), from al-Qāsim, who said: ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) taught me, saying: "This is the tashahhud of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him): «Al-taḥiyyātu lillāhi wa-al-ṣalawātu wa-al-ṭayyibāt, al-salāmu ʿalayka ayyuhā al-nabiyyu wa-raḥmatu Allāhi wa-barakātuh, al-salāmu ʿalaynā wa-ʿalā ʿibādi Allāhi al-ṣāliḥīn, ashhadu an lā ilāha illā Allāh, wa-ashhadu anna Muḥammadan ʿabduhu wa-rasūluh»." In this there is a valuable benefit: namely, that his tashahhud (peace and blessings be upon him) was with the very wording of our tashahhud.

**166.** We have also narrated in the Muwaṭṭaʾ of Mālik, the Sunan of al-Bayhaqī, and others, with authentic chains, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿUmar al-Qārī — with the shaddah on the yāʾ — that he heard ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb (may Allah be pleased with him), while he was on the pulpit teaching the people the tashahhud, saying: "Say: «Al-taḥiyyātu lillāh, al-zākiyātu lillāh, al-ṭayyibātu al-ṣalawātu lillāh, al-salāmu ʿalayka ayyuhā al-nabiyyu wa-raḥmatu Allāhi wa-barakātuh, al-salāmu ʿalaynā wa-ʿalā ʿibādi Allāhi al-ṣāliḥīn, ashhadu an lā ilāha illā Allāh waḥdahu lā sharīka lah, wa-ashhadu anna Muḥammadan ʿabduhu wa-rasūluh»" — "All greetings are for Allah, all pure offerings are for Allah, all good words and prayers are for Allah. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon us and upon Allah's righteous servants. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger."

**167.** We have also narrated in the Muwaṭṭaʾ, the Sunan of al-Bayhaqī, and others, with an authentic chain, from ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her), that she used to say when she performed the tashahhud: «Al-taḥiyyātu al-ṭayyibātu al-ṣalawātu al-zākiyātu lillāh, ashhadu an lā ilāha illā Allāh wa-anna Muḥammadan ʿabduhu wa-rasūluh, al-salāmu ʿalayka ayyuhā al-nabiyyu wa-raḥmatu Allāhi wa-barakātuh, al-salāmu ʿalaynā wa-ʿalā ʿibādi Allāhi al-ṣāliḥīn» — "All greetings, pure words, prayers, and purified offerings are for Allah. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon us and upon Allah's righteous servants."

In another narration from her in these books: «Al-taḥiyyātu al-ṣalawātu al-ṭayyibātu al-zākiyātu lillāh, ashhadu an lā ilāha illā Allāh waḥdahu lā sharīka lah, wa-anna Muḥammadan ʿabduhu wa-rasūluh, al-salāmu ʿalayka ayyuhā al-nabiyyu wa-raḥmatu Allāhi wa-barakātuh, al-salāmu ʿalaynā wa-ʿalā ʿibādi Allāhi al-ṣāliḥīn» — "All greetings, prayers, pure words, and purified offerings are for Allah. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon us and upon Allah's righteous servants."

**168.** We have also narrated in the Muwaṭṭaʾ and the Sunan of al-Bayhaqī, with an authentic chain, from Mālik, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both), that he used to perform the tashahhud saying: «Bismillāh, al-taḥiyyātu lillāh, al-ṣalawātu lillāh, al-zākiyātu lillāh, al-salāmu ʿalā al-nabiyyi wa-raḥmatu Allāhi wa-barakātuh, al-salāmu ʿalaynā wa-ʿalā ʿibādi Allāhi al-ṣāliḥīn, shahidtu an lā ilāha illā Allāh, shahidtu anna Muḥammadan rasūlu Allāh» — "In the name of Allah. All greetings are for Allah, all prayers are for Allah, all purified offerings are for Allah. Peace be upon the Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon us and upon Allah's righteous servants. I have borne witness that there is no god but Allah, and I have borne witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." And Allah knows best.

These, then, are the various forms of the tashahhud.

Al-Bayhaqī said: "What is firmly established from the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) are three hadiths: the hadith of Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿAbbās, and Abū Mūsā." This is the statement of al-Bayhaqī.

Others said: "All three are authentic (ṣaḥīḥ), and the most authentic of them is the hadith of Ibn Masʿūd."

Know that it is permissible to perform the tashahhud with any of these mentioned versions one wishes. This is precisely what our Imām al-Shāfiʿī (may Allah be pleased with him) and other scholars explicitly stated.

According to al-Shāfiʿī, the most virtuous is the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbās, due to the additional wording of "al-mubārakāt" (the blessed) contained therein.

Al-Shāfiʿī and other scholars (may Allah have mercy on them) said: "Because the matter is one of latitude and choice, the wordings of the narrators differed." And Allah knows best.

**Chapter: On the Optimal and Obligatory Elements of the Tashahhud**

The preferred practice is to recite one of the three tashahhuds in its complete form. If one omits part of it, does it suffice? There is a detailed ruling.

Know that the words "al-mubārakāt," "al-ṣalawāt," "al-ṭayyibāt," and "al-zākiyāt" are Sunnah (recommended), not conditions (sharṭ) in the tashahhud. If one omits all of them and restricts oneself to saying: "Al-taḥiyyātu lillāh, al-salāmu ʿalayka ayyuhā al-nabiyyu..." to the end, it suffices. There is no disagreement on this among our school.

As for the words from "al-salāmu ʿalayka ayyuhā al-nabiyyu..." to the end, they are obligatory (wājib); it is not permissible to omit anything from them, except the phrase "wa-raḥmatu Allāhi wa-barakātuh" (and the mercy of Allah and His blessings). Regarding these two phrases, there are three opinions (wujūh) among our companions. The most correct (aṣaḥḥ) is that it is not permissible to omit either of them — and this is what the evidence necessitates, given the consensus of the hadiths upon both. The second opinion: it is permissible to omit both. The third: it is permissible to omit "wa-barakātuh" (and His blessings) but not "raḥmatu Allāh" (the mercy of Allah).

Abū al-ʿAbbās ibn Surayj, one of our companions, said: "It is permissible to restrict oneself to saying: 'Al-taḥiyyātu lillāh, salāmun ʿalayka ayyuhā al-nabiyyu, salāmun ʿalā ʿibādi Allāhi al-ṣāliḥīn, ashhadu an lā ilāha illā Allāh wa-anna Muḥammadan rasūlu Allāh.'"

As for the word "al-salām" (peace), the majority of narrations have "al-salāmu ʿalayka ayyuhā al-nabiyyu" and likewise "al-salāmu ʿalaynā" with the definite article (alif and lām) in both. In some narrations, it appears as "salāmun" without the definite article in both instances. Some of our companions said: "Both are permissible, but the preferred is 'al-salām' with the definite article, because it is more frequent, and because it contains an increase and greater caution."

**169.** As for the basmalah (saying "Bismillāh") before the greetings, we have narrated a marfūʿ hadith in the Sunan of al-Nasāʾī, al-Bayhaqī, and others affirming it, and its affirmation has already been mentioned in the tashahhud of Ibn ʿUmar. However, al-Bukhārī, al-Nasāʾī, and other leading hadith scholars said: "The addition of the basmalah is not authentic (ṣaḥīḥ) from the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him)." For this reason, the majority of our companions said: "The basmalah is not recommended (lā yustaḥabb)." Some of our companions said: "It is recommended." The chosen position (al-mukhtār) is that one should not recite it, because the majority of the Companions who narrated the tashahhud did not include it.

chapters.title_en: Section 28 — On the Tashahhud, Salāh upon the Prophet ﷺ, and Supplication After the Final Tashahhud
chapters.arabic_text:
# فصل] :
# اعلم أن الترتيب في التشهد مستحب ليس بواجب، فلو قدم بعضه على بعض جاز

على المذهب الصحيح المختار الذي قاله الجمهور، ونص عليه الشافعي رحمه الله

في " الأم ".
# وقيل: لا يجوز كألفاظ الفاتحة، ويدل للجواز تقديم " السلام " على لفظ

الشهادة في بعض الروايات، وتأخيره في بعضها كما قدمناه.
# وأما الفاتحة، فألفاظها وترتيبها معجز، فلا يجوز تغييره، ولا يجوز التشهد

بالعجمية لمن قدر على العربية، ومن لم يقدر، يتشهد بلسانه ويتعلم كما ذكرنا

في تكبيرة الإحرام.

# فصل] :
# السنة في التشهد الإسرار لإجماع المسلمين على ذلك، ويدل عليه من الحديث:

| 170 - 
# ما رويناه في سنن أبي داود والترمذي والبيهقي عن عبد الله بن مسعود رضي

الله تعالى عنه قال: " من السنة أن يخفي التشهد  ".
# قال الترمذي: حديث حسن.
# وقال الحاكم: صحيح.
# وإذا قال الصحابي: من السنة كذا (4) كان بمعنى قوله: قال رسول الله صلى

الله عليه وسلم، هذا هو المذهب الصحيح المختار الذي عليه جمهور العلماء من

الفقهاء والمحدثين، وأصحاب الأصول والمتكلمين رحمهم الله، فلو جهر به كره،

ولم تبطل صلاته، ولا يسجد للسهو.

| (باب الصلاة على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بعد التشهد)
# اعلم أن الصلاة على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم واجبة عند الشافعي رحمه

الله بعد التشهد الأخير، فلو تركها لم تصح صلاته، ولا تجب الصلاة على آل

النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فيه على المذهب
# الصحيح المشهور، لكن تستحب.
# وقال بعض أصحابنا: تجب.
# والأفضل أن يقول:

| 171 - 
# " اللهم صل على محمد عبدك ورسولك النبي الأمي، وعلى آل محمد وأزواجه

وذريته، كما صليت على إبراهيم وعلى آل إبراهيم وبارك على محمد النبي الأمي،

وعلى آل محمد وأزواجه وذريته، كما باركت على إبراهيم، وعلى آل إبراهيم في

العالمين إنك حميد مجيد ". 
# وروينا هذه الكيفية في صحيح البخاري ومسلم، عن كعب بن عجرة، عن رسول الله

صلى الله عليه وسلم ألا بعضها (1) ، فهو صحيح من رواية غير كعب، وسيأتي

تفصيله في كتاب الصلاة على محمد صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم إن شاء الله

تعالى، والله أعلم.
# والواجب منه: اللهم صل على النبي، وإن شاء قال: صلى الله على محمد، وإن

شاء قال: صلى الله على رسوله، أو صلى الله على النبي.
# ولنا وجه أنه لا يجوز إلا قوله: اللهم صل على محمد.
# ولنا وجه أنه يجوز أن يقول: وصلى الله على أحمد.
# ووجه أنه يقول: صلى الله عليه، والله أعلم.
# وأما التشهد الأول، فلا تجب فيه الصلاة على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بلا

خلاف، وهل تستحب؟ فيه قولان: أصحهما: تستحب، ولا تستحب الصلاة على الآل على

الصحيح، وقيل: تستحب، ولا يستحب الدعاء في التشهد الأول عندنا، بل قال

أصحابنا: يكره لأنه مبني على التخفيف، بخلاف التشهد الأخير، والله أعلم.

| (باب الدعاء بعد  التشهد الأخير) 
# اعلم أن الدعاء بعد التشهد الأخير مشروع بلا خلاف.

| 172 - 
# روينا في " صحيحي البخاري ومسلم " عن عبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنه
# " أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم علمهم التشهد ثم قال في آخر: " ثم يتخير

[بعد] من الدعاء " وفي رواية البخاري: " [ثم ليتخير من الدعاء] أعجبه إليه

فيدعو ".
# وفي روايات لمسلم: " ثم ليتخير من المسألة ما شاء ".
# واعلم أن هذا الدعاء مستحب ليس بواجب، ويستحب تطويله، إلا أن يكون إماما،

وله أن يدعو بما شاء من أمور الآخرة والدنيا، وله أن يدعو بالدعوات

المأثورة، وله أن يدعو بدعوات يخترعها، والمأثورة أفضل.
# ثم المأثورة منها ما ورد في هذا الموطن، ومنها ما ورد في غيره، وأفضلها

هنا ما ورد هنا.

| 173 - 
# وثبت في هذا الموضع أدعية كثيرة، منها ما رويناه في " صحيحي البخاري

ومسلم " عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

" إذا فرغ أحدكم من 
# التشهد الأخير فليتعوذ بالله من أربع: من عذاب جهنم، ومن عذاب القبر، ومن

فتنة المحيا والممات، ومن شر المسيح الدجال ".

| 174 - 
# وروينا في " صحيحي البخاري ومسلم " عن عائشة رضي الله عنها، أن النبي صلى

الله عليه وسلم كان يدعو في الصلاة: " اللهم إني أعوذ بك من عذاب القبر،

وأعوذ بك من فتنة المسيح الدجال، وأعوذ بك من فتنة المحيا والممات، اللهم

إني أعوذ بك من المأثم والمغرم ".

| 175 - 
# وروينا في " صحيح مسلم " عن علي رضي الله عنه قال: كان رسول الله صلى

الله عليه وسلم إذا قام إلى الصلاة يكون من آخر ما يقول بين التشهد

والتسليم: " اللهم اغفر لي ما قدمت وما أخرت، وما أسررت وما أعلنت، وما

أسرفت، وما أنت أعلم به مني، أنت المقدم وأنت المؤخر، لا إله إلا أنت ".

| 176 - 
# وروينا في " صحيحي البخاري ومسلم "، عن عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص،
# عن أبي بكر الصديق رضي الله عنهم: أنه قال لرسول الله صلى الله عليه

وسلم: علمني دعاء أدعو به  في صلاتي، قال: " قل: اللهم إني ظلمت نفسي ظلما

كثيرا، ولا يغفر الذنوب إلا أنت، فاغفر لي مغفرة من عندك، وارحمني إنك أنت

الغفور الرحيم " هكذا ضبطناه: " ظلما كثيرا " بالثاء المثلثة في معظم

الروايات، وفي بعض روايات مسلم: " كبيرا " بالباء الموحدة (2) ، وكلاهما

حسن، فينبغي أن يجمع بينهما فيقال: " ظلما كثيرا كبيرا ".
# وقد احتج البخاري في " صحيحه "، والبيهقي، وغيرهما من الأئمة بهذا الحديث

على الدعاء في آخر الصلاة، وهو استدلال صحيح، فإن قوله: في صلاتي، يعم

جميعها، ومن مظان الدعاء في الصلاة هذا الموطن.

| 177 - 
# وروينا بإسناد صحيح في سنن أبي داود، عن أبي صالح ذكوان، عن بعض أصحاب
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ر-ت-ب (r-t-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Arrangement, order, sequence; establishing a fixed succession of parts.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In ritual acts, tartīb denotes the prescribed sequential order of integral components (arkān), distinct from mere preference.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is physical ordering; here it is a juristic (sharʿī) application, not metaphorical.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — The phrase "law qaddama" (if one advances) sets a hypothetical condition whose answer (jāza) is permissibility, indicating legal flexibility.
chapters.translation:
**Section**: Know that the sequential order in the tashahhud is recommended (mustaḥabb), not obligatory. Thus, if one advances some parts over others, it is permissible — according to the sound and chosen school (al-madhhab al-ṣaḥīḥ al-mukhtār) which the majority (al-jumhūr) held, and which al-Shāfiʿī — may Allah have mercy on him — explicitly stated in *al-Umm*.

It was also said: It is not permissible, like the words of the Fātiḥah. Evidence for permissibility is the advancement of the *salām* over the wording of the testimony (al-shahādah) in some narrations, and its delay in others, as we have previously mentioned.

As for the Fātiḥah, its words and their order are miraculous (muʿjiz), so it is not permissible to alter them. Nor is it permissible to recite the tashahhud in a non-Arabic tongue for one who is capable of Arabic. As for one who is not capable, he recites the tashahhud in his own language and learns it, as we mentioned regarding the opening takbīr (takbīrat al-iḥrām).

**Section**: The Sunnah in the tashahhud is to recite it quietly (al-isrār), due to the consensus of the Muslims upon that. Evidence for it from the ḥadīth is what we narrated in the *Sunan* of Abū Dāwūd, al-Tirmidhī, and al-Bayhaqī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd — may Allah Most High be pleased with him — who said: "It is from the Sunnah to conceal the tashahhud." Al-Tirmidhī said: A good (ḥasan) ḥadīth. Al-Ḥākim said: Authentic (ṣaḥīḥ).

When a Companion says "It is from the Sunnah such-and-such," it carries the meaning of his saying: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said such-and-such." This is the sound and chosen school upon which the majority of scholars — jurists, ḥadīth specialists, scholars of uṣūl, and theologians (mutakallimūn) — may Allah have mercy on them, agree. If one recites it aloud, it is disliked (makrūh), but his prayer is not invalidated, nor does he perform the prostration of forgetfulness (sujūd al-sahw).

**(Chapter on the Salāh upon the Prophet ﷺ after the Tashahhud)**

Know that the salāh upon the Prophet ﷺ is obligatory (wājib) according to al-Shāfiʿī — may Allah have mercy on him — after the final tashahhud. If one omits it, his prayer is not valid. It is not obligatory to send salāh upon the family (āl) of the Prophet ﷺ therein, according to the sound and well-known school, but it is recommended (mustaḥabb). Some of our companions said: It is obligatory.

The most virtuous is to say:

| 171 |
"O Allah, send Your blessings upon Muḥammad, Your servant and Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, and upon the family of Muḥammad, his wives, and his descendants, as You sent blessings upon Ibrāhīm and upon the family of Ibrāhīm. And bless Muḥammad, the unlettered Prophet, and the family of Muḥammad, his wives, and his descendants, as You blessed Ibrāhīm and the family of Ibrāhīm in the worlds. Indeed, You are Praiseworthy, Glorious."

We narrated this manner in *Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* and *Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*, from Kaʿb ibn ʿUjrah, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ — except that part of it is authentic from a narration other than Kaʿb's. Its detailed exposition will come in the Book of the Salāh upon Muḥammad ﷺ, Allah willing. And Allah knows best.

The obligatory portion of it is: "O Allah, send blessings upon the Prophet" (Allāhumma ṣalli ʿalā al-nabī). If he wishes, he may say: "May Allah send blessings upon Muḥammad" (ṣallā Allāhu ʿalā Muḥammad), or "May Allah send blessings upon His Messenger" (ṣallā Allāhu ʿalā rasūlihī), or "May Allah send blessings upon the Prophet" (ṣallā Allāhu ʿalā al-nabī).

We hold one position (wajh) that it is not permissible except to say: "O Allah, send blessings upon Muḥammad." Another position holds that it is permissible to say: "And may Allah send blessings upon Aḥmad." Another position holds that one may say: "May Allah send blessings upon him" (ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi). And Allah knows best.

As for the first tashahhud, the salāh upon the Prophet ﷺ is not obligatory therein, without disagreement. Is it recommended? There are two opinions; the more correct of them is that it is recommended. It is not recommended to send salāh upon the family (āl), according to the sound opinion. It was also said: It is recommended. Supplication (duʿā) in the first tashahhud is not recommended in our school; rather, our companions said: It is disliked (makrūh), because it is founded upon brevity (al-takhfīf), unlike the final tashahhud. And Allah knows best.

**(Chapter on Supplication After the Final Tashahhud)**

Know that supplication after the final tashahhud is legislated (mashrūʿ), without disagreement.

| 172 |
We narrated in *Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* and *Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd — may Allah be pleased with him — that the Prophet ﷺ taught them the tashahhud, then said at its end: "Then let him choose [afterwards] from the supplication." In al-Bukhārī's narration: "Then let him choose from the supplication what is most pleasing to him, and let him supplicate." In some narrations of Muslim: "Then let him choose from the request (al-masʾalah) whatever he wishes."

Know that this supplication is recommended, not obligatory. It is recommended to lengthen it, unless one is an imām (leading the prayer). He may supplicate with whatever he wishes of the matters of the Hereafter and this world. He may supplicate with the transmitted supplications (al-daʿawāt al-maʾthūrah), and he may supplicate with supplications he devises himself. The transmitted ones are more virtuous. Among the transmitted ones, some are reported specifically for this station (mawṭin), and some are reported for other stations. The most virtuous here is what was reported specifically for this station.

| 173 |
Many supplications are established for this station. Among them is what we narrated in *Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* and *Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*, from Abū Hurayrah — may Allah be pleased with him — who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When one of you finishes the final tashahhud, let him seek refuge with Allah from four things: from the punishment of Hellfire, from the punishment of the grave, from the trial of life and death (fitnat al-maḥyā wa al-mamāt), and from the evil of the False Messiah (al-Masīḥ al-Dajjāl)."

| 174 |
We narrated in *Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* and *Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*, from ʿĀʾishah — may Allah be pleased with her — that the Prophet ﷺ used to supplicate in the prayer: "O Allah, I seek refuge with You from the punishment of the grave, and I seek refuge with You from the trial of the False Messiah, and I seek refuge with You from the trial of life and death. O Allah, I seek refuge with You from sin and debt (al-maʾtham wa al-maghram)."

| 175 |
We narrated in *Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*, from ʿAlī — may Allah be pleased with him — who said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood for prayer, among the last things he would say between the tashahhud and the taslīm was: "O Allah, forgive me what I have done before and what I have delayed, what I have concealed and what I have declared, and what I have exceeded in, and what You know better than I. You are the Advancer (al-Muqaddim) and You are the Delayer (al-Muʾakhkhir). There is no god but You."

| 176 |
We narrated in *Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī* and *Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, from Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq — may Allah be pleased with them all — that he said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: Teach me a supplication with which I may supplicate in my prayer. He said: "Say: O Allah, I have wronged my soul with great wrongdoing (ẓulman kathīran), and none forgives sins but You. So forgive me with a forgiveness from You, and have mercy upon me. Indeed, You are the Forgiving, the Merciful."

Thus we have recorded it: "great wrongdoing" (ẓulman kathīran) with the dotted thāʾ (thāʾ muthallathah) in most narrations. In some narrations of Muslim: "great" (kabīran) with the single-dotted bāʾ. Both are good, so one should combine them and say: "great, immense wrongdoing" (ẓulman kathīran kabīran).

Al-Bukhārī in his *Ṣaḥīḥ*, al-Bayhaqī, and other imāms have used this ḥadīth as evidence for supplication at the end of the prayer. This is a sound inference, for his saying "in my prayer" encompasses all of it, and among the places where supplication is sought in the prayer is this very station.

| 177 |
We narrated with an authentic chain (isnād ṣaḥīḥ) in the *Sunan* of Abū Dāwūd, from Abū Ṣāliḥ Dhakwān, from some of the Companions...

chapters.title_en: Section 29 — On Remembrances After Prayer, the Salutations of Dissolution, and Related Matters
chapters.arabic_text:
النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لرجل: " كيف

تقول في الصلاة؟ " قال: أتشهد 
# وأقول: اللهم إني أسألك الجنة، وأعوذ بك من النار، أما إني لا أحسن

دندنتك ولا دندنة معاذ، فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: " حولها ندندن ".
# الدندنة: كلام لا يفهم معناه، ومعنى: " حولها ندندن " أي: حول الجنة

والنار، أو حول مسألتهما، إحداهما سؤال طلب، والثانية سؤال استعاذة، والله

أعلم.
# ومما يستحب الدعاء به في كل موطن: اللهم إني أسألك العفو والعافية، اللهم

إني أسألك الهدى والتقى والعفاف والغنى، والله أعلم.

| (باب السلام للتحلل من الصلاة)
# اعلم أن السلام للتحلل من الصلاة ركن من أركان وفرض من فروضها لا تصح إلا

به، هذا مذهب الشافعي، ومالك، وأحمد، وجماهير السلف والخلف، والأحاديث

الصحيحة المشهورة مصرحة بذلك.

| 178 - 
# واعلم أن الأكمل في السلام أن يقول عن يمينه: " السلام عليكم ورحمة الله

" وعن يساره: " السلام عليكم ورحمة الله " ولا يستحب أن يقول معه - أن مع

السلام عن التحلل من الصلاة - وبركاته، لأنه خلاف المشهور عن رسوله الله

صلى الله عليه وسلم، وإن كان قد جاء في رواية لأبي داود، وقد قال به جماعة

من أصحابنا منهم إمام الحرمين، وزاهر السرخسي، والروياني في " الجلية "

ولكنه شاذ، والمشهور ما قدمناه (1) .
# قال السيوطي في " تحفة الأبرار بنكت الأذكار ": قال الحافظ ابن  حجر: قد

وردت عدة طرق ثبت فها " وبركاته " بخلاف ما يوهمه كلام الشيخ - يعني النووي

- أنها رواية فردة، قال الأذرعي في " المتوسط ": المختار استحبابها في

التسليمتين، فقد فال في " شرح المهذب ": إن حديث أبي داود إسناد صحيح ثبت

ذلك أيضا من حديث ابن مسعود، رواه ابن ماجه في سننه، وابن حبان في صحيحه،

قال: والعجب من الشيخ - يعني النووي - مع شدة ورع عه كيف يصوب تركه، مع

ثبوت السنة، وحكمة بصحة إسناد الحديث الأول، وزيادة الثقة مقبولة عند

الفقهاء، وقد استحسنها أيضا الدارمي، في " الاستذكار " وغره من المقدمين من

أصحابنا، ويؤيده إثباتها في التشهد وفاقا ... إلخ.
# وسواء كان المصلي إماما أو مأموما أو منفردا في جماعة، قليلة أو كثيرة في

فريضة أو نافلة، ففي كل ذلك يسلم تسليمتين كما ذكرنا، ويلتفت بهما إلى

الجانبين، 
# والواجب تسليمة واحدة، وأما الثانية، فسنة لو تركها لم يضره، ثم الواجب

من لفظ
# السلام أن يقول: السلام عليكم، ولو قال: سلام عليكم، لم يجزئه على الأصح:

ولو قال: عليكم السلام، أجزأه على الأصح، فلو قال: السلام عليك، أو سلامي

عليك، أو سلام عليكم، أو سلام الله عليكم، أو سلام عليكم بغير تنوين، أو

قال: السلام عليهم، لم يجزئه شئ من هذا بلا خلاف، وتبطل صلاته إن قاله

عامدا عالما في كل ذلك، إلا في قوله: السلام عليهم، فإنه لا تبطل صلاته به

لأنه دعاء (1) ، وإن كان ساهيا لم تبطل، ولا يحصل التحلل من الصلاة بل

يحتاج إلى استئناف سلام صحيح، ولو اقتصر الإمام على تسليمة واحدة، أتى

المأموم بالتسليمتين.
# قال القاضي أبو الطيب الطبري من أصحابنا وغيره: إذا سلم الإمام فالمأموم

بالخيار، إن شاء سلم في الحال، وإن شاء استدام الجلوس للدعاء وأطال ما شاء،

والله أعلم.

| (باب ما يقوله الرجل إذا كلمه إنسان وهو في الصلاة)

| 179 - 
# روينا في " صحيحي البخاري ومسلم " عن سهل بن سعد الساعدي رضي الله عنه أن

رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " من نابه شئ في صلاته، فليقل:  سبحان

الله ".
# وفي رواية في الصحيح: " إذا نابكم أمر فليسبح الرجال، ولتصفق النساء ".
# وفي رواية: " التسبيح للرجال والتصفيق للنساء ".

| (باب الأذكار بعد الصلاة)
# أجمع العلماء على استحباب الذكر بعد الصلاة، وجاءت فيه أحاديث كثيرة

صحيحة في أنواع منه متعددة، فنذكر طرفا من أهمها.

| 180 - 
# روينا في كتاب الترمذي، عن أبي أمامة رضي الله عنه قال: قيل لرسول الله

صلى الله عليه وسلم: أي الدعاء أسمع؟ قال: " جوف الليل الآخر، ودبر الصلوات

المكتوبات ".
# قال الترمذي: حديث حسن.

| 181 - 
# وروينا في " صحيحي البخاري ومسلم " عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال:
# " كنت أعرف انقضاء صلاة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بالتكبير ".
# وفي رواية مسلم: " كنا " وفي رواية في " صحيحيهما ".

| 182 - 
# عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: " أن رفع الصوت بالذكر حين ينصرف

# الناس من المكتوبة كان على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم (1) "، وقال

ابن عباس: " كنت أعلم إذا انصرفوا بذلك إذا سمعته ".

| 183 - 
# وروينا في " صحيح مسلم "، عن ثوبان رضي الله عنه قال: كان رسول الله صلى

الله عليه وسلم إذا انصرف من صلاته استغفر ثلاثا وقال: " اللهم أنت السلام

ومنك السلام، تباركت يا ذا الجلال والإكرام ".
# قيل للأوزاعي (2) وهو أحد رواة الحديث: كيف الاستغفار؟ قال: تقول: استغفر

الله، أستغفر الله.

| 184 - 
# وروينا في " صحيحي البخاري ومسلم " عن المغيرة بن شعبة رضي الله عنه، أن

رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا فرغ من الصلاة وسلم قال: " لا إله

إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، له الملك وله الحمد وهو على كل شئ قدير، اللهم

لا مانع لما أعطيت، ولا معطي لما منعت، ولا ينفع ذا الجد منك الجد ".

| 185 - 
# وروينا في " صحيح مسلم " عن عبد الله بن الزبير رضي الله عنهما، أنه كان

يقول دبر كل صلاة حين يسلم: " لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، له الملك

وله الحمد وهو على كل شئ قدير، لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله، لا إله إلا الله

ولا  نعبد إلا إياه له النعمة وله الفضل، وله الثناء الحسن، لا إله إلا الله
chapters.anchors:
- Root: د-ن-د-ن (dan-dana)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Repetitive, indistinct humming or murmuring; speech whose articulation is blurred and meaning concealed.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Denotes utterance devoid of intelligible content — a verbal husk without semantic kernel.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for inarticulate sound; here metaphorical for the Prophet's concise, all-encompassing supplications which the companion deemed beyond his own rhetorical grasp.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Circumstantial Accusative (al-ḥāl) — "ḥawlahā nudandinu" (around it we hum) employs an adverbial accusative governing the verb, indicating the object of circling intent.
chapters.translation:
The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said — and he said to a man: "How do you say [your supplication] in prayer?" He replied: "I recite the tashahhud, and I say: O God, I ask You for Paradise, and I seek refuge in You from the Fire. But verily, I do not excel at your humming, nor at the humming of Muʿādh." The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Around it we hum."

The "humming" (dandana) is speech whose meaning is not understood. The meaning of "around it we hum" is: around Paradise and the Fire, or around the asking of them both — one being a request of seeking, and the second a request of seeking refuge. And God knows best.

Among the supplications recommended to be uttered in every station: "O God, I ask You for pardon and well-being. O God, I ask You for guidance, piety, chastity, and sufficiency." And God knows best.

| (Chapter on the Salutation for the Dissolution of Prayer)

Know that the salutation (salām) for the dissolution of prayer is a pillar (rukn) of its pillars and an obligation (farḍ) of its obligations — prayer is not valid without it. This is the school of al-Shāfiʿī, Mālik, Aḥmad, and the majority of the early and later scholars, and the authentic, well-known hadiths explicitly state this.

| 178 —

Know that the most complete form of the salutation is that one says to his right: "Peace be upon you and the mercy of God" and to his left: "Peace be upon you and the mercy of God." It is not recommended to add — along with the salutation of dissolution from prayer — "and His blessings" (wa-barakātuh), because this contradicts the well-known practice transmitted from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, even though it has come in a narration of Abū Dāwūd, and a group of our companions have adopted it, among them Imām al-Ḥaramayn, Zāhir al-Sarakhsī, and al-Rūyānī in "al-Jaliyyah." However, it is anomalous (shādhdh), and the well-known [practice] is what we have presented.

Al-Suyūṭī said in "Tuḥfat al-Abrār bi-Nukat al-Adhkār": Al-Ḥāfiẓ Ibn Ḥajar said: Several chains have been transmitted in which "and His blessings" is established, contrary to what the Sheikh's — meaning al-Nawawī's — words suggest, that it is a solitary narration. Al-Adhruʿī said in "al-Muṭawwasit": The chosen position is its recommendation in both salutations. For he said in "Sharḥ al-Muhadhdhab": The hadith of Abū Dāwūd has a sound chain, and this is also established from the hadith of Ibn Masʿūd, narrated by Ibn Mājah in his Sunan and Ibn Ḥibbān in his Ṣaḥīḥ. He said: It is astonishing of the Sheikh — meaning al-Nawawī — given the intensity of his scrupulousness, how he deems its omission correct, despite the establishment of the Sunnah, and his ruling on the soundness of the chain of the first hadith; and the addition of a trustworthy narrator is accepted by the jurists. Al-Dārimī also deemed it good in "al-Istidhkār," as did others among the leading early scholars of our companions. And it is supported by its inclusion in the tashahhud by consensus... etc.

Whether the prayer is an imam, a follower, or one praying alone — in a congregation, small or large, in an obligatory or supererogatory prayer — in all of this one gives two salutations as we have mentioned, turning with them to both sides.

The obligatory [minimum] is a single salutation. As for the second, it is a Sunnah — if one abandons it, no harm befalls him. Then, the obligatory [part] of the wording of the salutation is that one says: "Peace be upon you" (al-salāmu ʿalaykum). If he says: "Peace upon you" (salāmun ʿalaykum), it does not suffice him according to the soundest opinion. If he says: "Upon you be peace" (ʿalaykum al-salām), it suffices him according to the soundest opinion. But if he says: "Peace be upon you" (singular), or "My peace upon you," or "Peace upon you" (without the definite article), or "The peace of God upon you," or "Peace upon you" (without tanwīn), or says: "Peace be upon them" — none of this suffices him without disagreement, and his prayer is invalidated if he says it deliberately and knowingly in all of these cases, except in his saying "Peace be upon them," for his prayer is not invalidated by it, because it is a supplication. And if he was forgetful, it is not invalidated, but the dissolution of prayer is not achieved; rather, he needs to recommence a valid salutation. And if the imam limits himself to a single salutation, the follower performs two salutations.

Al-Qāḍī Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Ṭabarī, among our companions, and others said: When the imam gives the salutation, the follower has the choice: if he wishes, he gives the salutation immediately, and if he wishes, he prolongs his sitting for supplication and lengthens it as he pleases. And God knows best.

| (Chapter on What a Man Says When Someone Speaks to Him During Prayer)

| 179 —

We have narrated in the two Ṣaḥīḥs of al-Bukhārī and Muslim, from Sahl ibn Saʿd al-Sāʿidī, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Whoever is alerted to something during his prayer, let him say: Glory be to God (subḥān Allāh)."

And in another narration in the Ṣaḥīḥ: "If something befalls you, let the men glorify [God] and let the women clap."

And in another narration: "Glorification is for men and clapping is for women."

| (Chapter on Remembrances After Prayer)

The scholars are unanimous on the recommendation of remembrance (dhikr) after prayer, and numerous authentic hadiths have come regarding its various types. We shall mention a portion of the most important of them.

| 180 —

We have narrated in the book of al-Tirmidhī, from Abū Umāmah, may God be pleased with him, who said: It was said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Which supplication is most heard? He said: "The depths of the latter part of the night, and the conclusions of the prescribed prayers."

Al-Tirmidhī said: A good (ḥasan) hadith.

| 181 —

And we have narrated in the two Ṣaḥīḥs of al-Bukhārī and Muslim, from Ibn ʿAbbās, may God be pleased with them both, who said: "I used to know the conclusion of the prayer of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, by the takbīr."

And in a narration of Muslim: "We used to." And in another narration in their two Ṣaḥīḥs.

| 182 —

From Ibn ʿAbbās, may God be pleased with them both: "That raising the voice in remembrance when the people departed from the prescribed prayer was [the practice] during the era of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace." And Ibn ʿAbbās said: "I used to know when they departed by that — when I heard it."

| 183 —

And we have narrated in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, from Thawbān, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he departed from his prayer, would seek forgiveness three times and say: "O God, You are Peace, and from You is peace. Blessed are You, O Possessor of Majesty and Honor."

It was said to al-Awzāʿī — and he is one of the narrators of the hadith: How is the seeking of forgiveness? He said: You say: I seek the forgiveness of God, I seek the forgiveness of God.

| 184 —

And we have narrated in the two Ṣaḥīḥs of al-Bukhārī and Muslim, from al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he finished his prayer and gave the salutation, would say: "There is no god but God alone, with no partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He is over all things capable. O God, there is no preventer of what You have given, nor giver of what You have withheld, and the wealth of the wealthy avails nothing against You."

| 185 —

And we have narrated in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr, may God be pleased with them both, that he used to say at the conclusion of every prayer, when he gave the salutation: "There is no god but God alone, with no partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He is over all things capable. There is no might and no power except with God. There is no god but God, and we worship none but Him. His is the grace and His is the bounty, and His is the beautiful praise. There is no god but God..."

chapters.title_en: Section 30 — Remembrances Following the Prescribed Prayers (Adhkār Dubur al-Ṣalāh)
chapters.arabic_text:
مخلصين له الدين ولو كره الكافرون ".
# قال ابن الزبير: وكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يهلل بهن دبر كل

صلاة.

| 186 - 
# وروينا في " صحيحي البخاري ومسلم " عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه، أن فقراء

المهاجرين أتوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم.
# فقالوا: ذهب أهل الدثور بالدرجات العلى والنعيم المقيم، يصلون كما نصلي،

ويصومون كما نصوم، ولهم فضل من أموال يحجون بها 
# ويعتمرون ويجاهدون ويتصدقون، فقال: " ألا أعلمكم شيئا تدركون به من سبقكم

وتسبقون به من بعدكم، ولا يكون أحد أفضل منكم إلا من صنع مثل ما صنعتم؟

قالوا: بلى يارسول الله قال: تسبحون وتحمدون وتكبرون خلف كل صلاة ثلاثا

وثلاثين ".
# قال أبو صالح الراوي عن أبي هريرة: لما سئل عن كيفية ذكره؟ يقول: سبحان

الله، والحمد لله، والله أكبر، حتى يكون منهن كلهن ثلاث وثلاثون.
# الدثور: جمع دثر بفتح الدال وإسكان الثاء المثلثة: وهو المال الكثير.

| 187 - 
# وروينا في " صحيح مسلم "، عن كعب بن عجرة رضي الله عنه، عن رسول الله صلى

الله عليه وسلم قال: " معقبات لا يخيب قائلهن أو فاعلهن دبر كل صلاة

مكتوبة، ثلاثا وثلاثين تسبيحة، وثلاثا وثلاثين تحميدة، وأربعا وثلاثين

تكبيرة ".

| 188 - 
# وروينا في " صحيح مسلم " عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه، عن رسول الله صلى

الله عليه وسلم
# قال: " من سبح الله في دبر كل صلاة ثلاثا وثلاثين، وحمد الله ثلاثا

وثلاثين، وكبر الله ثلاثا وثلاثين، وقال تمام المائة: لا إله إلا الله وحده

لا شريك له، له الملك وله الحمد وهو على كل شئ قدير، غفرت خطاياه وإن كانت

مثل زبد البحر ".

| 189 - 
# وروينا في " صحيح البخاري " في أوائل " كتاب الجهاد " عن سعد بن أبي وقاص

رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يتعوذ دبر الصلاة بهؤلاء

الكلمات: " اللهم إني أعوذ بك من الجبن، وأعوذ بك أن أرد إلى أرذل العمر،

وأعوذ بك من  فتنة الدنيا وأعوذ بك من عذاب القبر ".

| 190 - 
# وروينا في " سنن أبي داود والترمذي والنسائي " عن عبد الله بن عمرو رضي

الله عنهما، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " خصلتان أو خلتان (1) لا

يحافظ عليهما عبد مسلم إلا دخل الجنة، هما يسير، ومن يعمل بهما قليل، يسبح

الله تعالى دبر كل صلاة عشرا ويحمد عشرا، ويكبر عشرا، فذلك خمسون ومائة

باللسان، وألف وخمسمائة في الميزان، ويكبر أربعا وثلاثين إذا أخذ مضجعة،

ويحمد ثلاثا وثلاثين، ويسبح ثلاثا وثلاثين فذلك مائة باللسان، وألف

بالميزان، قال: فلقد رأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يعقدها بيده،

قالوا: يارسول الله كيف هما يسير، ومن يعمل بهما قليل؟ قال: يأتي أحدكم -

يعني الشيطان - في منامه، فينومه قبل أن يقوله، ويأتيه في صلاته، فيذكره

حاجة قبل أن 
# يقولها "، إسناده صحيح، إلا أن فيه عطاء بن السائب، وفيه اختلاف بسبب

اختلاطه (1) .
# وقد أشار أيوب السختياني إلى صحة حديثه هذا (2) .

| 191 - 
# وروينا في سنن أبي داود، والترمذي، والنسائي وغيرهم عن عقبة بن عامر رضي

الله عنه، قال: " أمرني رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن أقرأ بالمعوذتين

دبر كل صلاة ".
# وفي رواية أبي داود: " بالمعوذات "، فينبغي أن يقرأ: " قل هو الله أحد،

وقل أعوذ برب الفلق، وقل أعوذ برب الناس ".

| 192 - 
# وروينا بإسناد صحيح في سنن أبي داود، والنسائي، عن معاذ رضي الله عنه، أن

رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أخذ بيده وقال: " يا معاذ والله إني لأحبك "

ثم قال: " أوصيك يا معاذ لا تدعن في دبر كل صلاة تقول: اللهم أعني على ذكرك

وشكرك وحسن عبادتك ".

| 193 - 
# وروينا في كتاب ابن السني، عن أنس رضي الله عنه، قال: كان رسول الله صلى

الله عليه وسلم إذا قضى صلاته مسح جبهته بيده اليمنى، ثم قال: " أشهد أن لا

إله إلا الله الرحمن الرحيم، اللهم أذهب عني الهم والحزن " (3) .

| 194 - 
# وروينا فيه عن أبي أمامة رضي الله عنه قال: ما دنوت من رسول الله صلى

الله عليه  وسلم في دبر مكتوبة ولا تطوع إلا سمعته يقول: " اللهم اغفر لي

ذنوبي وخطاياي كلها، اللهم انعشني واجبرني، واهدني لصالح الأعمال والأخلاق،

إنه لا يهدي لصالحها ولا يصرف سيئها إلا أنت ".

| 195 - 
# وروينا فيه عن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه، أن النبي صلى الله عليه

وسلم كان إذا فرغ من صلاته، لا أدري قبل أن يسلم أو بعد أن يسلم يقول: "

سبحان ربك رب العزة عما يصفون، وسلام على المرسلين، والحمد لله رب العالمين

" (4) .

| 196 - 
# وروينا فيه عن أنس رضي الله عنه، قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول

إذا انصرف من الصلاة: " اللهم اجعل خير عمري آخره، وخير عملي خواتمه، واجعل

خير أيامي يوم ألقاك " (1) .

| 197 - 
# وروينا فيه عن أبي بكرة رضي الله عنه، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

كان يقول في دبر الصلاة: " اللهم إني أعوذ بك من الكفر والفقر وعذاب القبر

" (2) .

| 198 - 
# وروينا فيه بإسناد ضعيف، عن فضالة بن عبيد الله قال: قال رسول الله صلى

الله عليه وسلم: " إذا صلى أحدكم فليبدأ بتحميد الله تعالى والثناء عليه،

ثم يصلي على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، ثم يدعو بما شاء " (3) .

| (باب الحث على ذكر الله تعالى بعد صلاة الصبح)
# اعلم أن أشرف أوقات الذكر في النهار، الذكر بعد صلاة الصبح.

| 199 - 
# روينا عن أنس رضي الله عنه في كتاب الترمذي وغيره، قال: قال رسول الله

صلى الله عليه وسلم: " من صلى الفجر في جماعة ثم قعد يذكر الله تعالى حتى

تطلع الشمس ثم صلى ركعتين كانت كأجر حجة وعمرة تامة تامة تامة " قال

الترمذي: حديث حسن.
chapters.anchors:
- Root: خ-ل-ص (kh-l-ṣ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Purity, clarity, and freedom from admixture; the essence of a thing extracted from its dross.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Sincere devotion (ikhlāṣ) — purifying one's act exclusively for the Divine, devoid of ostentation (riyāʾ) or hidden association (shirk khafī).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is physical purity; here it is metaphorical (majāz) for the heart's unalloyed orientation toward God alone.
- Root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Utterance, remembrance, and the presence of something in the mind; also the tongue's articulation of divine praise.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The highest form is remembrance of the heart (dhikr al-qalb) accompanied by the tongue, which elevates the servant to proximity with the Divine.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal is verbal mention; rhetorically extended to encompass all acts of worship performed in devotion.
- Root: ع-ق-ب (ʿ-q-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The heel or the end of a thing; that which follows in succession.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The "after" (dubur) of prayer — the temporal and spiritual sequel where the servant seals the act of worship with remembrance.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal is spatial posteriority; here it is temporal succession (majāz) marking the completion of the ritual.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of ʿAṭf (Coordination) — The conjunction "wa" (و) in sequences like "tusabbiḥūna wa taḥmadūna wa tukabbirūna" coordinates coordinate clauses, each retaining its independent verbal force, without ellipsis of the subject.
chapters.translation:
I say: The Prophet, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, said: "Making the religion sincerely His, even though the disbelievers detest it." {مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ وَلَوْ كَرِهَ الْكَافِرُونَ}

Ibn al-Zubayr said: The Messenger of God, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, used to utter these words of tahlīl (declaration of God's oneness) after every prayer.

| 186 —
We have related in the two Ṣaḥīḥs of al-Bukhārī and Muslim, on the authority of Abū Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, that the poor among the Emigrants (fuqarāʾ al-muhājirīn) came to the Messenger of God, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, and said: "The wealthy possessors of abundance (ahl al-duthūr) have gone off with the highest degrees and the everlasting bliss. They pray as we pray, and they fast as we fast, and they have surplus wealth by which they perform the pilgrimage (ḥajj), the lesser pilgrimage (ʿumrah), strive in the path of God (jihād), and give charity (ṣadaqah)."
