He said: "Shall I not teach you something by which you will overtake those who preceded you, and by which you will surpass those who come after you, and none will be better than you except one who does the like of what you do?" They said: "Yes, O Messenger of God." He said: "You glorify (tusabbiḥūn), praise (taḥmadūn), and magnify (tukabbirūn) after every prayer thirty-three times."

Abū Ṣāliḥ, the narrator from Abū Hurayrah, said: When he was asked about the manner of his remembrance, he would say: "Glory be to God (subḥān Allāh), praise be to God (al-ḥamdu lillāh), and God is Greater (Allāhu akbar)" — until all of them together came to thirty-three.

Al-duthūr (الدثور) is the plural of duthr (دثر), with the fatḥah on the dāl and the sukūn on the thāʾ (the dotted thāʾ): it means abundant wealth.

| 187 —
We have related in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, on the authority of Kaʿb ibn ʿUjrah, may God be pleased with him, from the Messenger of God, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, who said: "There are words that follow (muʿaqqibāt) — the one who utters them, or does them, will not be disappointed — after every prescribed prayer: thirty-three glorifications (tasbīḥah), thirty-three praises (taḥmīdah), and thirty-four magnifications (takbīrah)."

| 188 —
We have related in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, on the authority of Abū Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, from the Messenger of God, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, who said: "Whoever glorifies God after every prayer thirty-three times, and praises God thirty-three times, and magnifies God thirty-three times, and completes the hundred by saying: 'There is no god but God alone, with no partner; His is the dominion, and His is the praise, and He is powerful over all things' {لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ} — his sins are forgiven, even if they were like the foam of the sea."

| 189 —
We have related in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, at the beginning of the "Book of Jihād," on the authority of Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, used to seek refuge after the prayer with these words: "O God, I seek refuge in You from cowardice (jubn), and I seek refuge in You from being returned to the most decrepit age (ardhal al-ʿumur), and I seek refuge in You from the trial of this world (fitnat al-dunyā), and I seek refuge in You from the punishment of the grave (ʿadhāb al-qabr)."

| 190 —
We have related in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd, al-Tirmidhī, and al-Nasāʾī, on the authority of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, may God be pleased with them both, from the Prophet, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, who said: "Two traits — or two qualities — no Muslim servant preserves them except that he enters Paradise. They are easy, yet few are those who act upon them: he glorifies God after every prayer ten times, praises ten times, and magnifies ten times — that is one hundred and fifty on the tongue, and one thousand five hundred on the scale. And he magnifies thirty-four times when he takes to his bed, praises thirty-three times, and glorifies thirty-three times — that is one hundred on the tongue, and one thousand on the scale." He said: "I indeed saw the Messenger of God, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, counting them with his hand." They said: "O Messenger of God, how are they easy, yet few act upon them?" He said: "Satan — meaning the devil — comes to one of you in his sleep, and makes him sleep before he utters them, and comes to him in his prayer, and reminds him of a need before he says them." Its chain of transmission is sound (ṣaḥīḥ), except that it contains ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, and there is disagreement concerning him due to his confusion (ikhtilāṭ) in later life. Ayyūb al-Sakhtiyānī, however, indicated the soundness of this particular ḥadīth of his.

| 191 —
We have related in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd, al-Tirmidhī, al-Nasāʾī, and others, on the authority of ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir, may God be pleased with him, who said: "The Messenger of God, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, commanded me to recite the two chapters of refuge (al-muʿawwidhatayn) after every prayer." In the narration of Abū Dāwūd: "the chapters of refuge (al-muʿawwidhāt)." Thus one should recite: "Say: He is God, One" {قُلْ هُوَ اللهُ أَحَدٌ}, and "Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the Dawn" {قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ الْفَلَقِ}, and "Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of Mankind" {قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ النَّاسِ}.

| 192 —
We have related with a sound chain of transmission (isnād ṣaḥīḥ) in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd and al-Nasāʾī, on the authority of Muʿādh, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, took his hand and said: "O Muʿādh, by God, I truly love you." Then he said: "I counsel you, O Muʿādh: do not abandon after every prayer saying: 'O God, help me to remember You, thank You, and worship You well' {اللَّهُمَّ أَعِنِّي عَلَى ذِكْرِكَ وَشُكْرِكَ وَحُسْنِ عِبَادَتِكَ}."

| 193 —
We have related in the book of Ibn al-Sunnī, on the authority of Anas, may God be pleased with him, who said: When the Messenger of God, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, finished his prayer, he would wipe his forehead with his right hand, then say: "I bear witness that there is no god but God, the Most Merciful, the Compassionate. O God, remove from me anxiety and sorrow" {أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللهُ الرَّحْمَنُ الرَّحِيمُ، اللَّهُمَّ أَذْهِبْ عَنِّي الْهَمَّ وَالْحَزَنَ}.

| 194 —
We have related therein, on the authority of Abū Umāmah, may God be pleased with him, who said: I never approached the Messenger of God, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, after a prescribed prayer or a supererogatory one, except that I heard him say: "O God, forgive me my sins and all my transgressions. O God, revive me, mend me, and guide me to righteous deeds and noble character. Indeed, none guides to their righteousness, and none turns away their evil, except You" {اللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لِي ذُنُوبِي وَخَطَايَايَ كُلَّهَا، اللَّهُمَّ انْعَشْنِي وَاجْبُرْنِي، وَاهْدِنِي لِصَالِحِ الْأَعْمَالِ وَالْأَخْلَاقِ، إِنَّهُ لَا يَهْدِي لِصَالِحِهَا وَلَا يَصْرِفُ سَيِّئَهَا إِلَّا أَنْتَ}.

| 195 —
We have related therein, on the authority of Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, when he finished his prayer — I do not know whether before the salutation or after it — would say: "Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of Might, above what they describe, and peace upon the messengers, and praise be to God, Lord of the worlds" {سُبْحَانَ رَبِّكَ رَبِّ الْعِزَّةِ عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ، وَسَلَامٌ عَلَى الْمُرْسَلِينَ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ}.

| 196 —
We have related therein, on the authority of Anas, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, would say when he departed from the prayer: "O God, make the best of my life its end, and the best of my deeds their conclusions, and make the best of my days the day I meet You" {اللَّهُمَّ اجْعَلْ خَيْرَ عُمُرِي آخِرَهُ، وَخَيْرَ عَمَلِي خَوَاتِمَهُ، وَاجْعَلْ خَيْرَ أَيَّامِي يَوْمَ أَلْقَاكَ}.

| 197 —
We have related therein, on the authority of Abū Bakrah, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, would say after the prayer: "O God, I seek refuge in You from disbelief (kufr), poverty (faqr), and the punishment of the grave" {اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْكُفْرِ وَالْفَقْرِ وَعَذَابِ الْقَبْرِ}.

| 198 —
We have related therein with a weak chain of transmission (isnād ḍaʿīf), on the authority of Fuḍālah ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, who said: The Messenger of God, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, said: "When one of you prays, let him begin with praising God, the Exalted, and extolling Him, then send blessings upon the Prophet, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, then supplicate for whatever he wishes."

| (Chapter on Encouragement to Remember God, the Exalted, After the Morning Prayer)
Know that the most noble time for remembrance in the day is the remembrance after the morning prayer (ṣalāt al-ṣubḥ).

| 199 —
We have related on the authority of Anas, may God be pleased with him, in the book of al-Tirmidhī and others, who said: The Messenger of God, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, said: "Whoever prays the dawn prayer in congregation, then sits remembering God, the Exalted, until the sun rises, then prays two units (rakʿatayn), it will be for him like the reward of a complete, complete, complete pilgrimage (ḥajj) and lesser pilgrimage (ʿumrah)." Al-Tirmidhī said: This is a good (ḥasan) ḥadīth.

chapters.title_en: Section 31 — Remembrances After the Dawn Prayer, and the Morning and Evening Remembrances
chapters.arabic_text:
| 200 - 
# وروينا في كتاب الترمذي وغيره، عن أبي ذر رضي الله عنه، أن رسول الله صلى

الله عليه وسلم قال: " من قال في دبر صلاة الصبح وهو ثان رجليه قبل أن

يتكلم: لا إله 
# إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، له الملك وله الحمد يحيي ويميت وهو على كل شئ

قدير عشر مرات كتب له عشر حسنات،  ومحي عنه عشر سيئات، ورفع له عشر درجات،

وكان يومه ذلك في حرز من كل مكروه وحرس من الشيطان ولم ينبغ لذنب أن يدركه

في ذلك اليوم إلا الشرك بالله تعالى " قال الترمذي: هذا حديث حسن، وفي بعض

النسخ: صحيح (1) .

| 201 - 
# وروينا في " سنن أبي داود " عن مسلم بن الحارث (2) التميمي الصحابي رضي

الله عنه، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه أسر إليه فقال: " إذا

انصرفت من صلاة المغرب فقل: اللهم أجرني من النار سبع مرات، فإنك إذا قلت

ذلك ثم مت من ليلتك كتب لك جوار منها، وإذا صليت الصبح فقل كذلك، فإنك إن

مت من يومك كتب لك جوار منها " (3) .

| 202 - 
# وروينا في مسند الإمام أحمد، وسنن ابن ماجه، وكتاب ابن السني، عن أم سلمة

رضي الله عنها قالت: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا صلى الصبح قال:

" اللهم إني أسألك علما نافعا، وعملا متقبلا، ورزقا طيبا " (4) .

| 203 - 
# وروينا فيه (5) عن صهيب (6) رضي الله عنه، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه

وسلم كان يحرك شفتيه بعد صلاة الفجر بشئ، فقلت: يا رسول الله! ما هذا الذي

تقول؟ قال: " اللهم بك أحاول، وبك أصاول، وبك أقاتل " (7) والأحاديث بمعنى

ما ذكرته كثيرة، وسيأتي في الباب الآتي من بيان الأذكار التي تقال في أول

النهار ما تقر به العيون إن شاء الله تعالى.

| 204 - 
# وروينا عن أبي محمد البغوي في " شرح السنة " قال: قال علقمة بن قيس:

بلغنا أن الأرض تعج إلى الله تعالى من نومة العالم بعد صلاة الصبح (1) ،

والله أعلم.

| (باب ما يقال عند الصباح وعند المساء)
# اعلم أن هذا الباب واسع جدا، ليس في الكتاب باب أوسع منه، وأنا أذكر إن

شاء
# الله تعالى فيه جملا من مختصراته، فمن وفق للعمل بكلها فهي نعمة وفضل من

الله تعالى عليه وطوبى له، ومن عجز عن جميعها فليقتصر من مختصراتها على ما

شاء ولو كان ذكرا واحدا.
# والأصل في هذا الباب من القرآن العزيز قول الله  سبحانه وتعالى: (وسبح

بحمد ربك قبل طلوع الشمس وقبل غروبها) [طه: 13] وقال تعالى: (وسبح بحمد ربك

بالعشي والإبكار) [غافر: 55] وقال تعالى: (واذكر ربك في نفسك تضرعا وخيفة

ودون الجهر من القول بالغدو والآصال) [النساء: 148] قال أهل اللغة: الآصال

جمع أصيل: وهو ما بين العصر والمغرب.
# وقال تعالى: (ولا تطرد الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي يريدون وجهه)

[الأنعام: 52] قال أهل اللغة: العشي: ما بين زوال الشمس وغروبها.
# وقال تعالى: (في بيوت أذن الله أن ترفع ويذكر فيها اسمه، يسبح له فيها

بالغدو والآصال رجال لا تلهيهم تجارة ولا بيع عن ذكر الله ... ) الآية

[النور: 36] .
# وقال تعالى: (إنا سخرنا الجبال معه يسبحن بالعشي والإشراق) [ص: 18] .

| 205 - 
# وروينا في " صحيح البخاري " عن شداد بن أوس رضي الله عنه، عن النبي صلى

الله عليه وسلم قال: " سيد الاستغفار: اللهم أنت ربي لا إله إلا أنت،

خلقتني وأنا عبدك وأنا على عهدك ووعدك ما استطعت، أعوذ بك من شر ما صنعت،

أبوء لك بنعمتك علي، وأبوء بذنبي فاغفر لي فإنه لا يغفر الذنوب إلا أنت،

إذا قال ذلك حين يمسي فمات من ليلته دخل الجنة، أو كان من أهل الجنة، وإذا

قال ذلك حين يصبح فمات من يومه ... مثله " معنى أبوء: أقر وأعترف.

| 206 - 
# وروينا في " صحيح مسلم " عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه، قال: قال رسول الله

صلى الله عليه وسلم: " من قال حين يصبح وحين يمسي: سبحان الله وبحمده.
# مائة مرة لم يأت أحد يوم القيامة بأفضل مما جاء به إلا أحد قال مثل ما

قال أو زاد عليه ". 
# وفي رواية أبي داود: " سبحان الله العظيم وبحمده ".

| 207 - 
# وروينا في سنن أبي داود والترمذي، والنسائي وغيرهما بالأسانيد الصحيحة،

عن عبد الله بن خبيب - بضم الخاء المعجمة - رضي الله عنه، قال: " خرجنا في

ليلة مطره وظلمة شديدة نطلب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ليصلي لنا، فأدركناه

فقال: قل، فلم أقل شيئا، ثم قال: قل، فلم أقل شيئا، ثم قال: قل، فقلت:

يارسول الله ما  أقول؟ قال: قل هو الله أحد والمعوذتين حين تمسي وحين تصبح

ثلاث مرات تكفيك من كل شئ " قال الترمذي: حديث حسن صحيح.

| 208 - 
# وروينا في سنن أبي داود، والترمذي، وابن ماجه وغيرها بالأسانيد الصحيحة،

عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه كان يقول إذا

أصبح: " اللهم بك أصبحنا وبك أمسينا، وبك نحيا، وبك نموت، وإليك النشور "

وإذا أمسى قال: " اللهم بك أمسينا، وبك نحيا، وبك نموت وإليك النشور " قال

الترمذي: حديث حسن.

| 209 - 
# وروينا في " صحيح مسلم " عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه، أن النبي صلى الله

عليه وسلم كان إذا كان في سفر وأسحر يقول: " سمع سامع بحمد الله وحسن بلائه

علينا، ربنا صاحبنا (1) ، وأفضل علينا، عائذا (2) بالله من النار ".
# قال القاضي عياض وصاحب " المطالع " وغيرهما: سمع بفتح الميم المشددة،

ومعناه: بلغ سامع قولي هذا لغيره، تنبيها على الذكر في السحر والدعاء في

ذلك الوقت، وضبطه الخطابي وغيره، سمع: بكسر الميم المخففة، قال الإمام أبو

سليمان الخطابي: سمع سامع، معناه: شهد شاهد.
# وحقيقته: ليسمع السامع وليشهد الشاهد حمدنا لله تعالى على نعمته وحسن

بلائه.

| 210 - 
# وروينا في " صحيح مسلم " عن عبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال: كان
chapters.anchors:
- Root: د-ب-ر (d-b-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The rear, the end, the concluding portion of a thing; "dubr al-ṣalāh" denotes the closing segment of the prayer.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The temporal terminus of an act of worship, carrying the nuance of completion and sealing.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical rear; metaphorical (majāz) for the concluding time of an act.
- Sībawayh Rule: Ḥāl Clause (الْحَال) — The phrase "wa-huwa thānin rijlayhi" (while folding his legs) is a circumstantial accusative clause describing the posture during the utterance.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that the remembrances to be said after the dawn prayer are numerous and well-established. We have related in the Book of al-Tirmidhī and others, on the authority of Abū Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "Whoever says, after the dawn prayer, while folding his legs, before speaking: {«Lā ilāha illā Allāh waḥdahu lā sharīka lah, lahu al-mulku wa lahu al-ḥamdu yuḥyī wa yumītu wa huwa ʿalā kulli shayʾin qadīr»} — 'There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner; His is the sovereignty and His is the praise; He gives life and causes death, and He is over all things competent' — ten times, there will be written for him ten good deeds, and erased from him ten misdeeds, and raised for him ten degrees. And that day of his will be in a fortress against every disliked thing, and a guard against the devil; and no sin will befit to overtake him on that day except associating partners with Allah, the Exalted." Al-Tirmidhī said: This is a good (ḥasan) ḥadīth, and in some copies: sound (ṣaḥīḥ).

We have related in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd, on the authority of Muslim ibn al-Ḥārith al-Tamīmī, the Companion, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that he confided to him secretly, saying: "When you depart from the sunset prayer (al-maghrib), say: 'O Allah, protect me from the Fire' — seven times. For if you say that, then die that night, protection from it will be written for you. And when you pray the dawn prayer, say likewise; for if you die that day of yours, protection from it will be written for you."

We have related in the Musnad of Imām Aḥmad, the Sunan of Ibn Mājah, and the Book of Ibn al-Sunnī, on the authority of Umm Salamah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when he prayed the dawn prayer, would say: "O Allah, I ask You for beneficial knowledge, accepted deed, and wholesome provision."

We have related therein, on the authority of Ṣuhayb, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to move his lips after the dawn prayer with something. I said: O Messenger of Allah! What is this that you say? He said: "O Allah, with You I strive, with You I assault, and with You I fight." The ḥadīths bearing the meaning of what I have mentioned are numerous, and there will come in the following chapter an exposition of the remembrances said at the beginning of the day that will delight the eyes, if Allah the Exalted wills.

We have related from Abū Muḥammad al-Baghawī in his "Sharḥ al-Sunnah," who said: ʿAlqamah ibn Qays said: It has reached us that the earth groans to Allah the Exalted from the sleep of the scholar after the dawn prayer. And Allah knows best.

(Chapter on What is Said at Morning and at Evening)

Know that this chapter is exceedingly vast; there is no chapter in this book broader than it. I shall mention, if Allah the Exalted wills, therein a selection of its abridgments. Whoever is granted success to act upon all of them — that is a grace and bounty from Allah the Exalted upon him, and blessed is he. And whoever is incapable of all of them, let him confine himself to whichever of its abridgments he wishes, even if it be a single remembrance.

The foundation of this chapter from the Mighty Qurʾān is the saying of Allah, Glorified and Exalted: {«Wa sabbiḥ bi-ḥamdi rabbika qabla ṭulūʿi al-shamsi wa qabla ghurūbihā»} — "And glorify the praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting" [Ṭā Hā: 130]. And He, Exalted, said: {«Wa sabbiḥ bi-ḥamdi rabbika bil-ʿashiyyi wal-ibkār»} — "And glorify the praise of your Lord in the evening and in the morning" [Ghāfir: 55]. And He, Exalted, said: {«Wa-dhkur rabbaka fī nafsika taḍarruʿan wa khīfatan wa dūna al-jahri min al-qawli bil-ghuduwwi wal-āṣāl»} — "And remember your Lord within yourself, in supplication and fear, and without loudness of speech, in the mornings and the evenings" [al-Aʿrāf: 205]. The people of language said: al-āṣāl is the plural of aṣīl, which is the time between the afternoon (al-ʿaṣr) and sunset (al-maghrib).

And He, Exalted, said: {«Wa lā taṭrudi alladhīna yadʿūna rabbahum bil-ghadāti wal-ʿashiyyi yurīdūna wajhah»} — "And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening, desiring His Face" [al-Anʿām: 52]. The people of language said: al-ʿashiyy is what is between the sun's decline (zawāl) and its setting.

And He, Exalted, said: {«Fī buyūtin adhina Allāhu an turfaʿa wa yudhkara fīhā ismuh, yusabbiḥu lahu fīhā bil-ghuduwwi wal-āṣāl, rijālun lā tulhīhim tijāratun wa lā bayʿun ʿan dhikrillāh»} — "In houses which Allah has permitted to be raised and in which His name is remembered; therein He is glorified in the mornings and the evenings, by men whom neither commerce nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah" — the verse [al-Nūr: 36].

And He, Exalted, said: {«Innā sakhkharnā al-jibāla maʿahu yusabbiḥna bil-ʿashiyyi wal-ishrāq»} — "Indeed, We subjected the mountains with him, glorifying in the evening and at sunrise" [Ṣād: 18].

We have related in the Ṣaḥīḥ of al-Bukhārī, on the authority of Shaddād ibn Aws, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said: "The master of seeking forgiveness (sayyid al-istighfār) is: {«Allāhumma anta rabbī lā ilāha illā ant, khalaqtanī wa anā ʿabduka wa anā ʿalā ʿahdika wa waʿdika mā staṭaʿt, aʿūdhu bika min sharri mā ṣanaʿt, abūʾu laka biniʿmatika ʿalayya, wa abūʾu bidhanbī fa-ghfir lī fa-innahu lā yaghfiru al-dhunūba illā ant»} — 'O Allah, You are my Lord; there is no god but You. You created me, and I am Your servant, and I am upon Your covenant and Your promise as much as I am able. I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done. I acknowledge to You Your favor upon me, and I acknowledge my sin; so forgive me, for none forgives sins except You.' If he says it when he reaches the evening and dies that night, he enters Paradise — or he is among the people of Paradise. And if he says it when he reaches the morning and dies that day... likewise." The meaning of abūʾu is: I affirm and confess.

We have related in the Ṣaḥīḥ of Muslim, on the authority of Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "Whoever says, when he reaches the morning and when he reaches the evening: {«Subḥāna Allāhi wa bi-ḥamdih»} — 'Glory be to Allah and with His praise' — one hundred times, no one will come on the Day of Resurrection with anything better than what he has brought, except one who said the like of what he said or increased upon it." And in the narration of Abū Dāwūd: {«Subḥāna Allāhi al-ʿAẓīmi wa bi-ḥamdih»} — 'Glory be to Allah the Magnificent and with His praise.'

We have related in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd, al-Tirmidhī, al-Nasāʾī, and others, with sound chains of transmission, on the authority of ʿAbdullāh ibn Khubayb — with the ḍammah on the unpointed khāʾ — may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "We went out on a rainy night of intense darkness, seeking the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, to pray for us. We caught up with him, and he said: 'Say.' I said nothing. Then he said: 'Say.' I said nothing. Then he said: 'Say.' I said: O Messenger of Allah, what shall I say? He said: 'Say: {«Qul huwa Allāhu aḥad»} and the two refuge-seeking sūrahs (al-Muʿawwidhatān) when you reach the evening and when you reach the morning, three times; they will suffice you against everything.'" Al-Tirmidhī said: A good and sound (ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ) ḥadīth.

We have related in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd, al-Tirmidhī, Ibn Mājah, and others, with sound chains, on the authority of Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that he would say when he reached the morning: {«Allāhumma bika aṣbaḥnā wa bika amsaynā, wa bika naḥyā, wa bika namūtu, wa ilayka al-nushūr»} — 'O Allah, by You we reach the morning, and by You we reach the evening; by You we live, and by You we die, and to You is the resurrection.' And when he reached the evening, he would say: {«Allāhumma bika amsaynā, wa bika naḥyā, wa bika namūtu, wa ilayka al-nushūr»} — 'O Allah, by You we reach the evening, and by You we live, and by You we die, and to You is the resurrection.' Al-Tirmidhī said: A good (ḥasan) ḥadīth.

We have related in the Ṣaḥīḥ of Muslim, on the authority of Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when he was on a journey and reached the time of dawn (saḥar), would say: {«Samiʿa sāmiʿun bi-ḥamdi Allāhi wa ḥusni balāʾihi ʿalaynā, rabbanā ṣāḥibnā, wa afḍil ʿalaynā, ʿāʾidhan billāhi min al-nār»} — 'A hearer has heard our praise of Allah and His good trial upon us. Our Lord, accompany us, and favor us, seeking refuge with Allah from the Fire.' Al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, the author of al-Maṭāliʿ, and others said: samiʿa — with the fatḥah on the mīm, which is shaddah'd — and its meaning is: may a hearer convey this saying of mine to others, as an alert to remembrance at the time of dawn (saḥar) and supplication at that time. Al-Khaṭṭābī and others vocalized it: samiʿa — with the kasrah on the mīm, unshaddah'd. The Imām Abū Sulaymān al-Khaṭṭābī said: samiʿa sāmiʿun — its meaning is: may a witness bear witness. And its literal reality is: let the hearer hear, and let the witness witness, our praise of Allah the Exalted for His favor and His good trial.

We have related in the Ṣaḥīḥ of Muslim, on the authority of ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to say in the evening: {«Amsaynā wa amsa al-mulku lillāh, wal-ḥamdu lillāh, lā ilāha illā Allāh waḥdahu lā sharīka lah»} — 'We have reached the evening, and the sovereignty has reached the evening belonging to Allah; and praise belongs to Allah; there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner.' — and he would say likewise in the morning: {«Aṣbaḥnā wa aṣbaḥa al-mulku lillāh»} — 'We have reached the morning, and the sovereignty has reached the morning belonging to Allah.'

chapters.title_en: Section 32 — Evening and Morning Remembrances (Adhkār al-Masāʾ wa al-Ṣabāḥ)
chapters.arabic_text:
النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أمسى قال: " أمسينا وأمسى الملك لله، والحمد

لله، لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له " قال الراوي: أراه قال فيهن: " له

الملك وله الحمد وهو على كل شئ قدير، رب أسألك خير ما في هذه الليلة وخير

ما بعدها وأعوذ بك من شر ما في هذه
# الليلة وشر ما بعدها، رب أعوذ بك من الكسل وسوء الكبر، أعوذ بك من عذاب

في النار وعذاب في القبر، وإذا أصبح قال ذلك أيضا: أصبحنا وأصبح الملك لله

... ".

| 211 - 
# وروينا في " صحيح مسلم " عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: جاء رجل إلى

النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: يا رسول الله ما لقيت من عقرب لدغتني

البارحة؟ قال: " أما  لو قلت حين أمسيت: أعوذ بكلمات الله التامات من شر ما

خلق لم تضرك ".

# ذكره مسلم متصلا بحديث لخولة بنت حكيم رضي الله عنها وهكذا (1) .
# ورويناه في كتاب ابن السني، وقال فيه: " أعوذ بكلمات الله التامات من شر

ما خلق ثلاثا لم يضره شئ " (2) .

| 212 - 
# وروينا بالإسناد الصحيح في سنن أبي داود، والترمذي عن أبي هريرة رضي الله

عنه أن أبا بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه قال: يارسول الله مرني بكلمات أقولهن

إذا أصبحت وإذا أمسيت، قال: " قل: اللهم فاطر السموات والأرض، عالم الغيب

والشهادة رب كل شئ ومليكه، أشهد أن لا إله إلا أنت، أعوذ بك من شر نفسي وشر

الشيطان وشركه، قال: قلها إذا أصبحت وإذا أمسيت وإذا أخذت مضجعك " قال

الترمذي: حديث حسن صحيح.
# وروينا نحوه في " سنن أبي داود " من رواية أبي مالك الأشعري رضي الله عنه

أنهم قالوا: يارسول الله علمنا كلمة نقولها إذا أصبحنا وإذا أمسينا

واضطجعنا، فذكره، وزاد فيه بعد قوله: " وشركه "، وأن نقترف سوءا على أنفسنا

أو نجره إلى مسلم ".
# قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " وشركه "، روي على وجهين: أظهرهما وأشهرهما:

بكسر الشين مع إسكان الراء من الإشراك: أي: ما يدعو إليه ويوسوس به من

الإشراك بالله تعالى.
# والثاني: شركه بفتح الشين والراء: أي: حبائله ومصايده، واحدها: شركة بفتح
# الشين والراء، وآخره هاء.

| 213 - 
# وروينا في " سنن أبي داود " و " الترمذي " عن عثمان بن عفان رضي الله عنه

قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " ما من عبد يقول في صباح كل يوم

ومساء كل ليلة: بسم الله الذي لا يضر مع اسمه شئ في الأرض ولا في السماء

وهو السميع العليم، ثلاث مرات لم يضره شئ " قال الترمذي: هذا حديث حسن

صحيح، هذا لفظ الترمذي.
# وفي رواية أبي داود: " لم تصبه فجأة بلاء ".

| 214 - 
# وروينا في كتاب الترمذي، عن ثوبان رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى

الله عليه وسلم: " من قال حين يمسي: رضيت بالله ربا، وبالإسلام دينا،

وبمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم نبيا، كان حقا على الله تعالى أن يرضيه ".
# في إسناده سعيد بن المرزبان أبو سعد البقال بالباء، الكوفي مولى حذيفة بن

اليمان، وهو ضعيف باتفاق الحفاظ (1) ، وقد قال الترمذي: هذا حديث حسن صحيح

غريب من هذا الوجه، فلعله صح عنده من طريق آخر.
# وقد رواه أبو داود والنسائي بأسانيد جيدة عن رجل خدم النبي صلى الله عليه

وسلم عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بلفظه، فثبت أصل الحديث، ولله الحمد (2)

.
# وقد رواه الحافظ أبو عبد الله في " المستدرك على الصحيحين "، وقال: حديث

صحيح الإسناد.
# ووقع في رواية أبي داود وغيره: " وبمحمد رسولا ".
# وفي رواية الترمذي: " نبيا "، فيستحب أن يجمع الإسان بينهما فيقول " نبيا

ورسولا " ولو اقتصر على أحدهما كان عاملا بالحديث.

| 215 - 
# وروينا في " سنن أبي داود " بإسناد جيد لم يضعفه (3) عن أنس رضي الله
# عنه: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " من قال حين يصبح أو يمسي:

اللهم إني أصبحت أشهدك وأشهد حملة عرشك وملائكتك وجميع خلقك أنك أنت الله

الذي لا إله إلا أنت، وأن محمدا عبدك ورسولك، أعتق الله ربعه من النار، فمن

قالها مرتين أعتق الله نصفه من النار، ومن قالها ثلاثا أعتق الله ثلاثة

أرباعه، فإن قالها أربعا أعتقه الله تعالى من النار ".

| 216 - 
# وروينا في " سنن أبي داود " بإسناد جيد لم يضعفه، عن عبد الله بن غنام

بالغين المعجمة والنون المشددة، البياضي الصحابي رضي الله عنه، أن رسول

الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم قال: " من قال حين يصبح: اللهم ما أصبح بي من

نعمة فمنك وحدك لا شريك لك، لك الحمد ولك الشكر، فقد أدى شكر يومه ; ومن

قال مثل ذلك حين يمسي فقد أدى شكر ليلته " (4) .

| 217 - 
# وروينا بالأسانيد الصحيحة في سنن أبي داود، والنسائي، وابن ماجه، عن

# ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما (1) قال: " لم يكن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يدع

هؤلاء الدعوات حين يمسي وحين يصبح: " اللهم إني أسألك العافية في الدنيا

والآخرة،  اللهم إني أسألك العفو والعافية في ديني ودنياي وأهلي ومالي،

اللهم استر عوراتي وآمن روعاتي، اللهم احفظني من بين يدي ومن خلفي، وعن

يميني، وعن شمالي، ومن فوقي، وأعوذ بعظمتك أن أغتال من تحتي " (2) قال وكيع

(3) : يعني الخسف.
# قال الحاكم أبو عبد الله: هذا حديث صحيح الإسناد (4) .

| 218 - 
# وروينا في سنن أبي داود، والنسائي، وغيرهما بالإسناد الصحيح (5) عن علي

رضي الله عنه، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه كان يقول عند مضجعه: "

اللهم إني أعوذ بوجهك الكريم وبكلماتك التامة من شر ما أنت آخذ بناصيته،

اللهم أنت تكشف المغرم والمأثم، اللهم لا يهزم جندك ولا يخلف وعدك، ولا

ينفع ذا الجد منك الجد، سبحانك وبحمدك ".

| 219 - 
# وروينا في سنن أبي داود، وابن ماجه، بأسانيد (6) جيدة عن أبي عياش -
chapters.anchors:
- Root: أ-م-س (ʾ-m-s)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The entering of evening; the time from sunset to nightfall; "to reach the evening" (amsā) denotes the arrival at a state or time.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, amsā marks the temporal boundary of human agency within God's sovereign dominion (mulk), emphasizing that all states—morning and evening—are contingent upon divine decree.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for the actual time of evening; metaphorical (majāz) when applied to the soul's state, i.e., "we have entered the evening" as a confession of dependence.
- Root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Possession, dominion, sovereignty; the root conveys absolute ownership and authority over a thing.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Kalām, al-mulk (dominion) is exclusively God's, distinguishing His necessary ownership from contingent, borrowed human possession (milk).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for God's absolute kingship; metaphorical for any creaturely "possession," which is merely a trust (ʿāriyah).
- Root: ع-و-ذ (ʿ-w-dh)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To seek refuge, protection, or shelter; to cling to a protector against harm.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The act of istiʿādhah (seeking refuge) is a theological acknowledgment that only God can repel evil, whether spiritual (shayṭān) or physical (calamity).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical shelter; metaphorical for the soul's recourse to divine protection from unseen harms.
- Root: ك-م-ل (k-m-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Completeness, perfection, totality; a thing that lacks no part or attribute.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): "The perfect words of God" (kalimāt Allāh al-tāmmāt) refer to His attributes and decrees that are complete in power and wisdom, leaving no gap for harm.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the totality of God's speech; metaphorical for His comprehensive protection that covers all creation.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — In phrases like "Rabbi kulli shayʾin wa malīkuhu" (Lord of everything and its Sovereign), the second noun (malīk) is in apposition to the first (rabb), reinforcing the attribute without a new syntactic break, as governed by the genitive construct (iḍāfah).
chapters.translation:
I say — may Allah grant us success:

We have narrated in the authentic collections, from the report of ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), when he reached the evening, would say: "We have reached the evening, and the dominion belongs to Allah, and praise belongs to Allah; there is no deity except Allah alone, with no partner to Him." The narrator said: I think he said among these words: "To Him belongs the dominion, and to Him belongs praise, and He is over all things omnipotent. My Lord, I ask You for the good of this night and the good of what comes after it, and I seek refuge in You from the evil of this night and the evil of what comes after it. My Lord, I seek refuge in You from laziness and the evil of senility. I seek refuge in You from punishment in the Fire and punishment in the grave." And when he reached the morning, he would say likewise: "We have reached the morning, and the dominion belongs to Allah..." (narrated by Muslim).

| 211 —
And we have narrated in "Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim," from Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: A man came to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) and said: O Messenger of Allah, what do you say of the scorpion that stung me last night? He said: "Had you said, when you reached the evening: 'I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He has created,' it would not have harmed you." Muslim mentioned it connected to the ḥadīth of Khawlah bint Ḥakīm (may Allah be pleased with her), and likewise (1). We also narrated it in the book of Ibn al-Sunnī, and in it he said: "I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He has created" three times, and nothing would harm him (2).

| 212 —
And we have narrated with the authentic chain in the "Sunan" of Abū Dāwūd and al-Tirmidhī, from Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), that Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq (may Allah be pleased with him) said: O Messenger of Allah, command me with words that I may say when I reach the morning and when I reach the evening. He said: "Say: 'O Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, Lord of everything and its Sovereign, I bear witness that there is no deity except You. I seek refuge in You from the evil of my soul and the evil of the devil and his shirk (association).'" He said: "Say it when you reach the morning, when you reach the evening, and when you take your resting place." Al-Tirmidhī said: A ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ ḥadīth. We also narrated its like in the "Sunan" of Abū Dāwūd, from the narration of Abū Mālik al-Ashʿarī (may Allah be pleased with him), that they said: O Messenger of Allah, teach us words we may say when we reach the morning, when we reach the evening, and when we lie down. He mentioned it, and added after his saying "and his shirk": "and that we should not commit an evil against ourselves or drag it to a Muslim."

His saying (peace and blessings be upon him): "and his shirk" (wa shirkihi) has been narrated in two ways. The more apparent and more famous of them: with a kasrah on the shīn and a sukūn on the rāʾ, from al-ishrāk (association), meaning: what he calls to and whispers of association with Allah the Exalted. The second: shirkuhu, with a fatḥah on the shīn and the rāʾ, meaning: his snares and traps; its singular is shirkah, with a fatḥah on the shīn and the rāʾ, and its final letter is a tāʾ marbūṭah.

| 213 —
And we have narrated in the "Sunan" of Abū Dāwūd and al-Tirmidhī, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "There is no servant who says, in the morning of every day and the evening of every night: 'In the name of Allah, with whose name nothing in the earth or in the heaven can cause harm, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing,' three times, but nothing will harm him." Al-Tirmidhī said: This is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ ḥadīth. This is the wording of al-Tirmidhī. In the narration of Abū Dāwūd: "No sudden affliction will strike him."

| 214 —
And we have narrated in the book of al-Tirmidhī, from Thawbān (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever says, when he reaches the evening: 'I am pleased with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion, and with Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him) as Prophet,' it is incumbent upon Allah the Exalted to please him." In its chain is Saʿīd ibn al-Marzubān, Abū Saʿd al-Baqqāl, with a bāʾ, the Kūfan, the freed slave of Ḥudhayfah ibn al-Yamān, and he is weak by the consensus of the ḥuffāẓ (1). Al-Tirmidhī has said: This is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ gharīb ḥadīth from this path; perhaps it was authentic to him from another route. Abū Dāwūd and al-Nasāʾī have narrated it with good chains, from a man who served the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), with its wording, so the foundation of the ḥadīth is established, and to Allah belongs praise (2). Al-Ḥāfiẓ Abū ʿAbdullāh has narrated it in "al-Mustadrak ʿalā al-Ṣaḥīḥayn" and said: A ḥadīth with an authentic chain. In the narration of Abū Dāwūd and others, it occurs: "and with Muḥammad as Messenger" (rasūlan). In the narration of al-Tirmidhī: "as Prophet" (nabiyyan). Thus it is recommended that one combine both and say: "as Prophet and Messenger"; and if one limits himself to either, he has acted upon the ḥadīth.

| 215 —
And we have narrated in the "Sunan" of Abū Dāwūd, with a good chain that he did not weaken (3), from Anas (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever says, when he reaches the morning or the evening: 'O Allah, I have reached the morning, calling You to witness, and calling the bearers of Your Throne, Your angels, and all Your creation to witness, that You are Allah, there is no deity except You, and that Muḥammad is Your servant and Your Messenger,' Allah frees a quarter of him from the Fire. Whoever says it twice, Allah frees half of him from the Fire. Whoever says it three times, Allah frees three-quarters of him. And if he says it four times, Allah the Exalted frees him entirely from the Fire."

| 216 —
And we have narrated in the "Sunan" of Abū Dāwūd, with a good chain that he did not weaken, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Ghannām — with the dotted ghayn and the shaddah on the nūn — al-Bayāḍī, the Companion (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him and his family) said: "Whoever says, when he reaches the morning: 'O Allah, whatever blessing has come to me this morning, it is from You alone, with no partner to You; to You belongs praise, and to You belongs gratitude,' he has rendered the thanks of his day. And whoever says the like of that when he reaches the evening, he has rendered the thanks of his night" (4).

| 217 —
And we have narrated with the authentic chains in the "Sunan" of Abū Dāwūd, al-Nasāʾī, and Ibn Mājah, from Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both) (1), who said: "The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) would not abandon these supplications when he reached the evening and when he reached the morning: 'O Allah, I ask You for well-being in this world and the Hereafter. O Allah, I ask You for pardon and well-being in my religion, my worldly affairs, my family, and my wealth. O Allah, veil my private parts and calm my fears. O Allah, protect me from before me and from behind me, from my right and from my left, and from above me, and I seek refuge in Your might from being treacherously attacked from beneath me'" (2). Wakīʿ (3) said: Meaning, the swallowing of the earth (khasf). Al-Ḥākim Abū ʿAbdullāh said: This is a ḥadīth with an authentic chain (4).

| 218 —
And we have narrated in the "Sunan" of Abū Dāwūd, al-Nasāʾī, and others, with the authentic chain (5), from ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him), that he would say at his resting place: "O Allah, I seek refuge in Your noble Face and in Your perfect words from the evil of what You take by its forelock. O Allah, You remove debt and sin. O Allah, Your host is not defeated, Your promise is not broken, and the wealth of the wealthy avails nothing against You. Glory be to You, and with Your praise."

| 219 —
And we have narrated in the "Sunan" of Abū Dāwūd and Ibn Mājah, with good chains (6), from Abū ʿAyyāsh —

chapters.title_en: Section 33 — Morning and Evening Remembrances (Adhkār al-Ṣabāḥ wa al-Masāʾ)
chapters.arabic_text:
بالشين المعجمة - رضي الله عنه، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " من

قال إذا أصبح: لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، له الملك وله الحمد وهو

على كل شئ قدير، كان له عدل رقبة من ولد إسماعيل صلى الله عليه وسلم، وكتب

له عشر حسنات، وحط عنه عشر سيئات، ورفع له عشر درجات، وكان في حرز من

الشيطان حتى يمسي، وإن قالها إذا أمسى كان له مثل ذلك حتى يصبح " (7) .

| 220 - 
# وروينا في " سنن أبي داود " بإسناد لم يضعفه (1) عن أبي مالك الأشعري رضي

الله عنه: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " إذا أصبح أحدكم فليقل:

أصبحنا وأصبح الملك لله رب العالمين، اللهم أسألك خير هذا اليوم فتحه ونصره

ونوره وبركته وهداه، وأعوذ بك من شر ما فيه وشر ما بعده، ثم إذا أمسى فليقل

مثل ذلك ".

| 221 - 
# وروينا في " سنن أبي داود " عن عبد الرحمن بن أبي بكرة، أنه قال لأبيه:

يا أبت إني أسمعك تدعو كل غداة: اللهم عافني في بدني، اللهم عافني في سمعي،

اللهم عافني في بصري، اللهم إني أعوذ بك من الكفر والفقر، اللهم إني أعوذ

بك من عذاب  القبر، لا إله إلا أنت، تعيدها حين تصبح ثلاثا، وثلاثا حين

تمسي، فقال: إني سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يدعو بهن، فأنا أحب أن

أستن بسنته (2) .

| 222 - 
# وروينا في " سنن أبي داود " عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما عن رسول الله صلى

الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: " من قال حين يصبح (فسبحان الله حين تمسون وحين

تصبحون وله الحمد في السموات والأرض وعشيا وحين تظهرون.
# يخرج الحي من الميت ويخرج الميت من الحي ويحيي الأرض بعد موتها وكذلك

تخرجون) [الروم: 17، 18] أدرك ما فاته في يومه ذلك، ومن قالهن حين يمسي

أدرك ما فاته في ليلته " لم يضعفه أبو داود، وقد ضعفه البخاري في " تاريخه

الكبير " وفي كتابه " كتاب الضعفاء " (3) .

| 223 - 
# وروينا في " سنن أبي داود " عن بعض بنات النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم رضي

عنهن أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يعلمها فيقول: " قولي حين تصبحين:

سبحان الله وبحمده، لا قوة إلا بالله، ما شاء الله كان، وما لم يشأ لم يكن،

أعلم أن الله على كل شئ قدير، وأن الله قد أحاط بكل شئ علما، فإنه من قالهن

حين يصبح حفظ حتى يمسي ومن قالهن حين يمسي حفظ حتى يصبح ".

| 224 - 
# وروينا في سنن أبي داود، عن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه، قال: دخل رسول

الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ذات يوم المسجد، فإذا هو برجل من الأنصار يقال له:

أبو أمامة، فقال " يا أبا أمامة! ما لي أراك جالسا في المسجد في غير وقت

صلاة؟ " قال: هموم لزمتني وديون يا رسول الله، قال: " أفلا أعلمك كلاما إذا

قلته أذهب الله همك وقضى عنك دينك " قلت: بلى يا رسول الله، قال: " قل إذا

أصبحت وإذا أمسيت: اللهم إني أعوذ بك من الهم والحزن وأعوذ بك من العجز

والكسل، وأعوذ بك من الجبن والبخل، وأعوذ بك من غلبة الدين وقهر الرجال ".
# قال: ففعلت ذلك، فأذهب الله تعالى همي وغمي وقضى عني ديني (1) .

| 225 - 
# وروينا في كتاب  ابن السني بإسناد صحيح، عن عبد الله بن أبزى رضي الله عنه

قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أصبح قال: " أصبحنا على فطرة

الإسلام، وكلمة الإخلاص، ودين نبيا محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، وملة إبراهيم

صلى الله عليه وسلم حنيفا مسلما وما أنا من المشركين ".
# قلت كذا وقع في كتابه: " ودين نبينا محمد " وهو غير ممتنع، ولعله صلى

الله عليه وسلم قال ذلك جهرا ليسمعه غيره فيتعلمه، والله أعلم.

| 226 - 
# وروينا في كتاب ابن السني، عن عبد الله بن أبي أوفى رضي الله عنهما، قال:

كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أصبح قال: " أصبحنا وأصبح الملك لله

عز وجل، والحمد لله، والكبرياء والعظمة لله، والخلق والأمر والليل والنهار

وما سكن فيهما لله تعالى، اللهم اجعل أول هذا النهار صلاحا، وأوسطه نجاحا،

وآخره فلاحا، يا أرحم
# الراحمين " (2) .

| 227 - 
# وروينا في كتابي الترمذي وابن السني بإسناد فيه ضعف، عن معقل بن يسار رضي

الله عنه، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " من قال حين يصبح ثلاث مرات:

أعوذ بالله السميع العليم من الشيطان الرجيم، وقرأ ثلاث آيات من سورة

الحشر، وكل الله تعالى به سبعين 
# ألف ملك يصلون عليه حتى يمسي، وإن مات في ذلك اليوم مات شهيدا، ومن قالها

حين يمسي كان بتلك المنزلة " (1) .

| 228 - 
# وروينا في كتاب ابن السني، عن محمد بن إبراهيم، عن أبيه رضي الله عنه

قال: وجهنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في سرية، فأمرنا أن نقرأ إذا

أمسينا وأصبحنا: (أفحسبتم أنما خلقناكم عبثا) [المؤمنون: 115] فقرأنا،

فغنمنا وسلمنا.

| 229 - 
# وروينا فيه (2) عن أنس رضي الله عنه، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

كان يدعو بهذه الدعوة إذا أصبح وإذا أمسى: " اللهم إني أسألك من فجأة

الخير، وأعوذ بك من فجأة الشر " (3) .

| 230 - 
# وروينا فيه عن أنس رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

لفاطمة رضي الله عنها: " ما يمنعك أن تسمعي ما أوصيك به؟ تقولين  إذا أصبحت

وإذا أمسيت: يا حي يا قيوم بك أستغيث فأصلح لي شأني كله ولا تكلني إلى نفسي

طرفة عين " (4) .

| 231 - 
# وروينا فيه بإسناد ضعيف، عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما، أن رجلا شكا إلى

رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه تصيبه الآفات، فقال له رسول الله صلى

الله عليه وسلم: " قل إذا أصبحت: بسم الله
# على نفسي وأهلي ومالي، فإنه لا يذهب لك شئ "، فقالهن الرجل فذهبت عنه

الآفات.

| 232 - 
# وروينا في سنن ابن ماجه، وكتاب ابن السني، عن أم سلمة رضي الله عنها، أن
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ح-ر-ز (ḥ-r-z)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A fortified enclosure; protection through encircling defense.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Divine safeguarding (ʿiṣmah) as an act of Allah's preservation of the believer.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — physical refuge; metaphorical (majāz) — spiritual immunity from demonic insinuation.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ) — The protasis (jawāʾ al-sharṭ) with "man" governs the apodosis, indicating a causal nexus between utterance and divine reward.
chapters.translation:
I say: With the letter "shīn" (muʿjamah) — may Allah be pleased with him — that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "Whoever says upon rising in the morning: 'There is no deity but Allah alone, with no partner; His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He is over all things competent' — there will be for him the equivalent of freeing a slave from the descendants of Ismāʿīl, peace be upon him; and ten good deeds will be written for him, and ten misdeeds will be erased from him, and he will be raised ten degrees; and he will be in a fortress of protection from Satan until evening. And if he says it upon entering the evening, he will have the like of that until morning."

| 220 —
And we have related in the "Sunan of Abū Dāwūd" with an isnād that he did not weaken, from Abū Mālik al-Ashʿarī, may Allah be pleased with him: that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "When one of you rises in the morning, let him say: 'We have risen, and the dominion belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds. O Allah, I ask You for the good of this day — its opening, its victory, its light, its blessing, and its guidance — and I seek refuge in You from the evil within it and the evil after it.' Then, when he enters the evening, let him say the like of that."

| 221 —
And we have related in the "Sunan of Abū Dāwūd" from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakrah, that he said to his father: "O my father, I hear you supplicating every morning: 'O Allah, grant me well-being in my body; O Allah, grant me well-being in my hearing; O Allah, grant me well-being in my sight; O Allah, I seek refuge in You from disbelief and poverty; O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the punishment of the grave; there is no deity but You' — you repeat it three times upon rising and three times upon entering the evening." He said: "Indeed, I heard the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, supplicating with these words, and I love to follow his Sunnah."

| 222 —
And we have related in the "Sunan of Abū Dāwūd" from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that he said: "Whoever says upon rising in the morning: {«So glorify Allah when you enter the evening and when you rise in the morning; and to Him is all praise in the heavens and the earth, and in the evening and when you are at noon. He brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living, and He revives the earth after its death; and thus shall you be brought forth»} [al-Rūm 30:17-18] — he will attain what he missed of that day. And whoever says them upon entering the evening will attain what he missed of that night." Abū Dāwūd did not weaken it, though al-Bukhārī did weaken it in his "al-Tārīkh al-Kabīr" and in his book "al-Ḍuʿafāʾ."

| 223 —
And we have related in the "Sunan of Abū Dāwūd" from one of the daughters of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, may Allah be pleased with them, that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to teach her, saying: "Say upon rising in the morning: 'Glory be to Allah and with His praise; there is no power except through Allah; whatever Allah wills comes to be, and whatever He does not will does not come to be. I know that Allah is over all things competent, and that Allah has encompassed all things in knowledge.' For whoever says them upon rising will be protected until evening, and whoever says them upon entering the evening will be protected until morning."

| 224 —
And we have related in the "Sunan of Abū Dāwūd" from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, entered the mosque one day, and there was a man from the Anṣār called Abū Umāmah. He said: "O Abū Umāmah! Why do I see you sitting in the mosque at a time other than prayer?" He replied: "Anxieties have clung to me and debts, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Shall I not teach you words which, if you say them, Allah will remove your anxiety and settle your debt?" I said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Say upon rising in the morning and upon entering the evening: 'O Allah, I seek refuge in You from anxiety and grief; and I seek refuge in You from incapacity and laziness; and I seek refuge in You from cowardice and miserliness; and I seek refuge in You from the overwhelming of debt and the domination of men.'" He said: So I did that, and Allah, the Exalted, removed my anxiety and grief and settled my debt.

| 225 —
And we have related in the book of Ibn al-Sunnī with a sound (ṣaḥīḥ) isnād, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Abzā, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, upon rising in the morning, used to say: "We have risen upon the fiṭrah of Islam, and the word of sincere devotion (ikhlāṣ), and the religion of our Prophet Muḥammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and the creed (millah) of Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him, as a ḥanīf and a Muslim, and I am not of the polytheists."

I say: Thus it occurred in his book: "and the religion of our Prophet Muḥammad" — and this is not impermissible. Perhaps he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said it aloud so that others might hear it and learn it. And Allah knows best.

| 226 —
And we have related in the book of Ibn al-Sunnī, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Awfā, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, upon rising in the morning, used to say: "We have risen, and the dominion belongs to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; and praise belongs to Allah; and grandeur and majesty belong to Allah; and creation, command, night, day, and all that dwells within them belong to Allah, the Exalted. O Allah, make the beginning of this day righteousness, its middle success, and its end prosperity, O Most Merciful of the merciful."

| 227 —
And we have related in the two books of al-Tirmidhī and Ibn al-Sunnī with an isnād containing weakness, from Maʿqil ibn Yasār, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said: "Whoever says upon rising in the morning three times: 'I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan,' and recites three verses from Sūrat al-Ḥashr, Allah, the Exalted, will entrust to him seventy thousand angels who send blessings upon him until evening; and if he dies that day, he dies as a martyr. And whoever says them upon entering the evening will be in that same station."

| 228 —
And we have related in the book of Ibn al-Sunnī, from Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, dispatched us on a military expedition (sariyyah), and commanded us to recite upon entering the evening and rising in the morning: {«Did you then think that We created you in vain?»} [al-Muʾminūn 23:115]. So we recited it, and we gained spoils and returned safely.

| 229 —
And we have related therein, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to supplicate with this supplication upon rising in the morning and upon entering the evening: "O Allah, I ask You for the suddenness of good, and I seek refuge in You from the suddenness of evil."

| 230 —
And we have related therein, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to Fāṭimah, may Allah be pleased with her: "What prevents you from hearing what I advise you? Say upon rising in the morning and upon entering the evening: 'O Living, O Self-Subsisting, by You I seek aid; so set right for me all my affairs, and do not entrust me to myself for the blink of an eye.'"

| 231 —
And we have related therein with a weak isnād, from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, that a man complained to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that afflictions kept befalling him. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to him: "Say upon rising in the morning: 'In the name of Allah, upon my soul, my family, and my wealth' — for nothing of yours will be lost." So the man said them, and the afflictions departed from him.

| 232 —
And we have related in the "Sunan of Ibn Mājah" and the book of Ibn al-Sunnī, from Umm Salamah, may Allah be pleased with her, that...

chapters.title_en: Section 34 — Morning and Evening Remembrances (Adhkār al-Ṣabāḥ wa al-Masāʾ)
chapters.arabic_text:
رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا أصبح قال: " اللهم إني أسألك علما

نافعا، ورزقا طيبا، وعملا متقبلا " (5) .

| 233 - 
# وروينا في كتاب ابن السني، عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما، قال: قال رسول

الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " من قال إذا أصبح: اللهم إني أصبحت منك في نعمة

وعافية وستر، فأتم نعمتك علي وعافيتك وسترك في الدنيا والآخرة ثلاث مرات

إذا أصبح وإذا أمسى، كان حقا على الله تعالى أن يتم عليه ".

| 234 - 
# وروينا في كتابي الترمذي وابن السني، عن الزبير بن العوام رضي الله عنه،

عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " ما من صباح يصبح العباد إلا مناد

ينادي: سبحان الملك القدوس " وفي رواية ابن السني: " إلا صرخ صارخ: أيها

الخلائق سبحوا الملك القدوس " (1) .

| 235 - 
# وروينا في كتاب ابن السني، عن بريدة رضي الله عنه، قال: قال رسول الله

صلى الله عليه وسلم: " من قال إذا أصبح وإذا أمسى: ربي الله، توكلت على

الله لا إله إلا هو عليه توكلت وهو رب العرش العظيم، لا إله إلا الله العلي

العظيم، ما شاء الله كان، وما لم يشأ لم يكن، أعلم أن الله على كل شئ قدير،

وأن الله قد أحاط بكل شئ علما، ثم
# مات دخل الجنة ".

| 236 - 
# وروينا في كتاب ابن السني، عن أنس رضي الله عنه، أن رسول الله صلى الله

عليه وسلم قال: " أيعجز أحدكم أن  يكون كأبي ضمضم؟ قالوا: ومن أبو ضمضم يا

رسول الله؟ قال: " كان إذا أصبح قال: اللهم إني قد وهبت نفسي وعرضي لك، فلا

يشتم من شتمه ولا يظلم من ظلمه، ولا يضرب من ضربه ".

| 237 - 
# وروينا فيه عن أبي الدرداء رضي الله عنه، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

قال: " من قال في كل يوم حين يصبح وحين يمسي: حسبي الله، لا إله إلا هو،

عليه توكلت وهو رب العرش العظيم سبع مرات، كفاه الله تعالى ما أهمه من أمر

الدنيا والآخرة " (2) .

| 238 - 
# وروينا في كتابي الترمذي وابن السني بإسناد ضعيف، عن أبي هريرة رضي الله

عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " من قرأ (حم المؤمن) إلى:

(إليه المصير) وآية الكرسي حين يصبح حفظ بهما حتى يمسي، ومن قرأهما حين

يمسي حفظ بهما حتى يصبح " (3) .
# فهذه جملة من الأحاديث التي قصدنا ذكرها، وفيها كفاية لمن وفقه الله

تعالى، نسأل الله العظيم التوفيق للعمل بها وسائر وجوه الخير.

| 239 - 
# وروينا في كتاب ابن السني، عن طلق بن حبيب قال: جاء رجل إلى أبي الدرداء

فقال: يا أبا الدرداء قد احترق بيتك، فقال: ما احترق، لم يكن الله عز وجل

# ليفعل ذلك بكلمات سمعتهن من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، من قالها أول

نهاره لم تصبه مصيبة حتى يمسي، ومن قالها آخر النهار لم تصبه مصيبة حتى

يصبح: " اللهم أنت ربي لا إله إلا أنت عليك توكلت وأنت رب العرش العظيم، ما

شاء الله كان، وما لم يشأ لم يكن، لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله العلي العظيم،

أعلم أن الله على كل شئ قدير، وأن الله قد أحاط بكل شئ علما، اللهم إني

أعوذ بك من شر نفسي، ومن شر كل دابة أنت آخذ بناصيتها، إن ربي على صراط

مستقيم ".
# ورواه من طريق آخر، عن رجل من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، لم يقل:

عن أبي الدرداء، وفيه: أنه تكرر مجئ الرجل إليه يقول: أدرك دارك  فقد

احترقت، وهو يقول: ما احترقت لأني سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "

من قال حين يصبح هذه الكلمات، لم يصبه في نفسه ولا أهله ولا ماله شئ يكرهه

"، وقد قلتها اليوم، ثم قال: انهضوا بنا، فقام وقاموا معه، فانتهوا إلى

داره وقد احترق ما حولها ولم يصبها شئ ".

| (باب ما يقال في صبيحة الجمعة)
# اعلم أن كل ما يقال في غير يوم الجمعة يقال فيه، ويزداد استحباب كثرة

الذكر فيه على غيره، ويزاد كثرة الصلاة على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم.

| 240 - 
# وروينا في كتاب ابن السني، عن أنس رضي الله عنه، عن النبي صلى الله عليه

وسلم قال: " من قال صبيحة يوم الجمعة قبل صلاة الغداة: أستغفر الله الذي لا

إله إلا هو الحي القيوم وأتوب إليه ثلاث مرات غفر الله ذنوبه ولو كانت مثل

زبد البحر " (1) .
# ويستحب الإكثار من الدعاء في جميع يوم الجمعة من طلوع الفجر إلى غروب

الشمس رجاء مصادفة ساعة الإجابة، فقد اختلف فيها على أقوال كثيرة، فقيل: هي

بعد طلوع الفجر وقبل طلوع الشمس، وقيل: بعد طلوع الشمس وقيل: بعد الزوال،

وقيل: بعد العصر، وقيل غير ذلك.
# والصحيح بل الصواب الذي لا يجوز غيره: ما ثبت في " صحيح مسلم "، عن أبي

موسى الأشعري، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، أنها ما بين جلوس الإمام

على المنبر إلى أن يسلم من الصلاة (2) .

| (باب ما يقول إذا طلعت الشمس)

| 241 - 
# روينا في كتاب ابن السني بإسناد ضعيف، عن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه،

قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا طلعت الشمس قال: " الحمد لله

الذي جللنا اليوم عافيته، وجاء بالشمس من مطلعها، اللهم أصبحت أشهد لك بما

شهدت به لنفسك، وشهدت به ملائكتك وحملة عرشك وجميع خلقك إنك أنت الله لا

إله إلا أنت القائم بالقسط، لا إله إلا أنت العزيز الحكيم، اكتب شهادتي بعد

شهادة ملائكتك وأولي العلم، اللهم أنت السلام ومنك السلام وإليك السلام،

أسألك يا  ذا الجلال والإكرام أن تستجيب لنا دعوتنا، وأن تعطينا رغبتنا، وأن

تغنينا عمن أغنيته عنا من خلقك، اللهم أصلح لي ديني الذي هو عصمة أمري،

وأصلح لي دنياي التيي فيها معيشتي، وأصلح لي آخرتي التي إليها منقلبي ".

| 242 - 
# وروينا فيه عن عبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنه موقوفا عليه أنه جعل من

يرقب له طلوع الشمس، فلما أخبره بطلوعها قال: الحمد لله الذي وهب لنا هذا
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Perception, cognition, and the faculty of knowing; knowledge as an attribute of the knower.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): ʿIlm as the apprehension of a thing as it truly is; in the divine context, absolute and encompassing knowledge (iḥāṭah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — knowledge as a real attribute; metaphorical (majāz) — "knowledge" as a means to action.
- Root: و-ك-ل (w-k-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To entrust, delegate, or rely upon; tawakkul as the act of committing one's affairs to another.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Tawakkul — the heart's reliance upon Allah alone as the sufficient Guardian (wakīl), combining trust with action.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — delegation of authority; metaphorical — the soul's repose in Allah's decree.
- Root: ح-ف-ظ (ḥ-f-ẓ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To guard, preserve, protect, and keep safe from harm.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ḥifẓ — divine preservation of the believer from calamities, and the human act of memorizing and safeguarding sacred words.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — physical protection; metaphorical — spiritual preservation through recited formulas.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — The protasis (sharṭ) introduced by "man" (whoever) is answered by a jumla (clause) that may be nominal or verbal, with the apodosis (jawāb) often carrying the semantic weight of a promise or threat, as in "man qāla... kāna ḥaqqan ʿalā Allāh" (whoever says... it is incumbent upon Allah).
chapters.translation:
I say — may Allah grant us success:

We have transmitted in the Book of Ibn al-Sunnī, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "Whoever says upon rising in the morning: 'O Allah, I have risen from You in blessing, well-being, and covering (of faults), so complete upon me Your blessing, Your well-being, and Your covering in this world and the Hereafter' — three times when he rises in the morning and three times when he enters the evening — it is incumbent upon Allah, the Exalted, to complete it upon him."

We have transmitted in the two books of al-Tirmidhī and Ibn al-Sunnī, on the authority of al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said: "There is no morning that the servants rise to, except that a caller calls out: 'Glory be to the King, the Most Holy (subḥāna al-Malik al-Quddūs).'" And in the narration of Ibn al-Sunnī: "Except that a crier cries out: 'O creatures, glorify the King, the Most Holy.'"

We have transmitted in the Book of Ibn al-Sunnī, on the authority of Buraydah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "Whoever says upon rising in the morning and upon entering the evening: 'My Lord is Allah, I have placed my trust in Allah (tawakkaltu ʿalā Allāh), there is no god but He, upon Him I rely, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne. There is no god but Allah, the Most High, the Magnificent. Whatever Allah wills comes to be, and whatever He does not will does not come to be. I know that Allah is over all things Omnipotent, and that Allah has encompassed all things in knowledge' — then dies, he enters Paradise."

We have transmitted in the Book of Ibn al-Sunnī, on the authority of Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "Is any one of you unable to be like Abū Ḍamḍam?" They said: "And who is Abū Ḍamḍam, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "When he rose in the morning, he would say: 'O Allah, I have bestowed my self and my honor to You, so let no one revile the one who reviles him, nor oppress the one who oppresses him, nor strike the one who strikes him.'"

We have transmitted therein, on the authority of Abū al-Dardāʾ, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said: "Whoever says every day, when he rises in the morning and when he enters the evening: 'Allah is sufficient for me (ḥasbī Allāh), there is no god but He, upon Him I rely, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne' — seven times — Allah, the Exalted, suffices him for whatever concerns him of the affairs of this world and the Hereafter."

We have transmitted in the two books of al-Tirmidhī and Ibn al-Sunnī, with a weak chain of transmission (isnād ḍaʿīf), on the authority of Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "Whoever recites {«Ḥā Mīm»} (Sūrat al-Muʾmin) up to {«and to Him is the final return»} (ilayhi al-maṣīr), and the Verse of the Throne (Āyat al-Kursī) upon rising in the morning, he is guarded by them until the evening; and whoever recites them upon entering the evening, he is guarded by them until the morning."

These, then, are a selection of the hadiths which we intended to mention, and in them is sufficiency for whomever Allah, the Exalted, has granted success. We ask Allah, the Magnificent, for success in acting upon them and in all other paths of goodness.

We have transmitted in the Book of Ibn al-Sunnī, on the authority of Ṭalq ibn Ḥabīb, who said: A man came to Abū al-Dardāʾ and said: "O Abū al-Dardāʾ, your house has burned down." He said: "It has not burned — Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, would not do that, because of words I heard from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Whoever says them at the beginning of his day, no calamity befalls him until the evening; and whoever says them at the end of the day, no calamity befalls him until the morning: 'O Allah, You are my Lord, there is no god but You, upon You I rely, and You are the Lord of the Mighty Throne. Whatever Allah wills comes to be, and whatever He does not will does not come to be. There is no might and no power except through Allah, the Most High, the Magnificent. I know that Allah is over all things Omnipotent, and that Allah has encompassed all things in knowledge. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the evil of my own soul, and from the evil of every creature You seize by its forelock. Indeed, my Lord is upon a straight path.'"

And it was transmitted by another route, from a man among the Companions of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, without mentioning Abū al-Dardāʾ, and in it: that the man repeatedly came to him saying: "Reach your house, for it has burned," and he would say: "It has not burned, because I heard the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say: 'Whoever says these words upon rising in the morning, nothing he dislikes befalls him in his self, his family, or his wealth.' And I have said them today." Then he said: "Rise with us." So he rose, and they rose with him, and they reached his house — and what was around it had burned, but nothing of it had been touched.

(Chapter on What Is Said on the Morning of Friday)

Know that everything said on other days is said on it, and the recommendation of abundant remembrance (dhikr) is increased on it over other days, and abundant prayer upon the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is increased.

We have transmitted in the Book of Ibn al-Sunnī, on the authority of Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said: "Whoever says on the morning of Friday, before the dawn prayer: 'I seek forgiveness from Allah, there is no god but He, the Living, the Self-Sustaining (al-Ḥayy al-Qayyūm), and I repent to Him' — three times — Allah forgives his sins, even if they were like the foam of the sea."

And it is recommended to multiply supplication (duʿāʾ) throughout the entire day of Friday, from the break of dawn to sunset, hoping to coincide with the hour of response (sāʿat al-ijābah). For there is disagreement concerning it among many opinions: it is said it is after the break of dawn and before sunrise; it is said after sunrise; it is said after the sun's declension (zawāl); it is said after the afternoon prayer (ʿaṣr); and other opinions are mentioned.

The correct — rather, the sound view which admits no other — is what is established in "Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim," on the authority of Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī, from the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that it is between the Imam's sitting upon the pulpit (minbar) and the completion of the prayer with the salutation (taslīm).

(Chapter on What One Says When the Sun Rises)

We have transmitted in the Book of Ibn al-Sunnī, with a weak chain of transmission, on the authority of Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: When the sun rose, the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would say: "Praise be to Allah who has clothed us this day with His well-being, and brought the sun from its rising place. O Allah, I rise bearing witness to You with what You have witnessed for Yourself, and what Your angels, the bearers of Your Throne, and all Your creation have witnessed — that You are Allah, there is no god but You, the Upholder of justice (al-Qāʾim bi al-Qisṭ), there is no god but You, the Mighty, the Wise. Write my testimony after the testimony of Your angels and the people of knowledge. O Allah, You are Peace (al-Salām), and from You is peace, and to You returns peace. I ask You, O Possessor of Majesty and Honor (Dhā al-Jalāl wa al-Ikrām), to respond to our supplication, to grant us our desire, and to enrich us from those of Your creation whom You have enriched us from. O Allah, set right for me my religion, which is the safeguard of my affair; set right for me my worldly life, in which is my livelihood; and set right for me my Hereafter, to which is my final return."

We have transmitted therein, on the authority of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, may Allah be pleased with him, as a statement stopped at him (mawqūf ʿalayhi), that he appointed someone to watch for the rising of the sun for him. When he informed him of its rising, he said: "Praise be to Allah who has bestowed this upon us."

chapters.title_en: Section 35 — On the Remembrances of the Sun's Rising, the Post-Zawāl Hours, the Afternoon, the Maghrib Adhān, the Witr Prayer, and the Remembrances Before Sleep
chapters.arabic_text:
اليوم وأقالنا فيه من عثراتنا.

| (باب ما يقول إذا استقلت الشمس) 
# (1)

| 243 - 
# روينا في كتاب ابن السني، عن عمرو بن عبسة رضي الله عنه، عن رسول الله

صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " ما تستقل الشمس فيبقى شئ من خلق الله تعالى إلا

سبح الله عز وجل وحمده إلا ما كان من الشيطان وأعتاء بني آدم، فسألت عن

أعتى بني آدم فقال: شرار الخلق " (2) .

| (باب ما يقول بعد زوال الشمس إلى العصر)
# قد تقدم إذا لبس ثوبه، وإذا خرج من بيته، وإذا دخل الخلاء، وإذا خرج منه،

وإذا توضأ، وإذا قصد المسجد، وإذا وصل بابه، وإذا صار فيه، وإذا سمع المؤذن

والمقيم، وما بين الأذان والإقامة، وما يقوله إذا أراد القيام للصلاة، وما

يقوله في الصلاة من أولها إلى آخرها، وما يقوله بعدها، وهذا كله يشترك فيه

جميع الصلوات.
# ويستحب الإكثار من الأذكار وغيرها من العبادات عقب الزوال.

| 244 - 
# لما روينا في كتاب الترمذي عن عبد الله بن السائب رضي الله عنه، " أن

رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يصلي أربعا بعد أن تزول الشمس قبل الظهر،

وقال: إنها ساعة تفتح فيها أبواب السماء فأحب أن يصعد لي فيها عمل صالح "

قال الترمذي: حديث حسن.
# ويستحب كثرة الأذكار بعد وظيفة الظهر لعموم قول الله تعالى: (وسبح بحمد

ربك بالعشي والإبكار) قال أهل اللغة: العشي من زوال الشمس إلى غروبها.
# قال الإمام أبو منصور الأزهري: العشي عند العرب: ما بين أن تزول الشمس

إلى أن تغرب.

| (باب ما يقوله بعد العصر إلى غروب الشمس) 
# قد تقدم ما يقوله بعد الظهر والعصر كذلك، ويستحب الإكثار من الأذكار في

العصر استحبابا متأكدا، فإنها الصلاة الوسطى على قول جماعات من السلف

والخلف، وكذلك تستحب زيادة الاعتناء بالأذكار في الصبح، فهاتان الصلاتان

أصح ما قيل في الصلاة الوسطى، ويستحب الإكثار من الأذكار بعد العصر، وآخر

النهار أكثر، قال الله تعالى: (فسبح بحمد ربك قبل طلوع الشمس وقبل غروبها)

[طه: 130] وقال تعالى: (وسبح بحمد ربك بالعشي والإبكار) .
# وقال الله تعالى: (واذكر ربك في نفسك تضرعا وخيفة ودون الجهر من القول

بالغدو والآصال) .
# [غافر: 55] وقال تعالى: (يسبح له فيها بالغدو والآصال رجال لا تلهيهم

تجارة ولا بيع عن ذكر الله) .
# [النور: 36] وقد تقدم أن الآصال ما بين العصر والمغرب.

| 245 - 
# وروينا في كتاب ابن السني بإسناد ضعيف عن أنس رضي الله عنه، قال: قال

رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " لأن أجلس مع قوم يذكرون الله عز وجل من

صلاة العصر إلى أن تغرب الشمس، أحب إلي من أن أعتق ثمانية من ولد إسماعيل

".

| (باب ما يقوله إذا سمع أذان المغرب)

| 246 - 
# روينا في سنن أبي داود، والترمذي، عن أم سلمة رضي الله عنها قالت: علمني

رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن أقول عند أذان المغرب: " اللهم هذا إقبال

ليلك وإدبار نهارك وأصوات دعاتك فاغفر لي " (1) .

| (باب ما يقوله بعد صلاة المغرب)
# قد تقدم قريبا أنه يقول عقيب كل الصلوات الأذكار المتقدمة، ويستحب أن

يزيد فيقول بعد أن يصلي سنة المغرب.

| 247 - 
# ما رويناه في كتاب ابن السني، عن أم سلمة رضي الله عنها قالت: كان رسول

الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا انصرف من صلاة المغرب يدخل فيصلي ركعتين، ثم

يقول فيما يدعو: " يا مقلب ثبت قلوبنا على دينك ".

| 248 - 
# وروينا في كتاب الترمذي، عن عمارة بن شبيب، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله

عليه وسلم: " من قال: لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، له الملك وله الحمد

يحيي ويميت وهو على كل شئ قدير عشر  مرات على أثر المغرب، بعث الله تعالى له

مسلحة يتكفلونه (2) من الشيطان حتى يصبح، وكتب الله له بها عشر حسنات

موجبات، ومحا عنه عشر سيئات موبقات، وكانت له بعدل عشر رقاب مؤمنات ".
# قال الترمذي: لا نعرف لعمارة بن شبيب سماعا من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم.
# قلت: وقد رواه النسائي في كتاب " عمل اليوم والليلة " من طريقين.
# أحدهما: هكذا، والثاني عن عمارة عن رجل من الأنصار.
# قال الحافظ أبو القاسم بن عساكر: هذا الثاني هو الصواب.
# قلت: قوله: " مسلحة " بفتح الميم وإسكان السين المهملة وفتح اللام

وبالحاء المهملة: وهم الحرس.

| (باب ما يقرؤه في صلاة الوتر وما يقوله بعدها)
# السنة لمن أوتر بثلاث ركعات، أن يقرأ في الأولى بعد الفاتحة: (سبح اسم

ربك الأعلى) ، وفي الثانية (قل يا أيها الكافرون) وفي الثالثة: (قل هو الله

أحد) والمعوذتين، 
# فإن نسي (سبح) في الأولى، أتى بها مع (قل يا أيها الكافرون) في الثانية،

وكذا إن نسي في الثانية (قل يا أيها الكافرون) أتى بها في الثالثة مع (قل

هو الله أحد) والمعوذتين.

| 249 - 
# وروينا في سنن أبي داود، والنسائي، وغيرهما بالإسناد الصحيح، عن أبي بن

كعب رضي الله عنه قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا سلم في الوتر

قال: " سبحان الملك القدوس ".
# وفي رواية النسائي وابن السني: " سبحان الملك القدوس " ثلاث مرات.

| 250 - 
# وروينا في سنن أبي داود، والترمذي، والنسائي، عن علي رضي الله عنه، أن

النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقول في آخر وتره: " اللهم إني أعوذ برضاك من

سخطك، وأعوذ بمعافاتك من عقوبتك، وأعوذ بك منك، لا أحصي ثناء عليك أنت كما

أثنيت على نفسك " قال الترمذي: حديث حسن.

| (باب ما يقول إذا أراد النوم واضطجع على فراشه)
# قال الله تعالى: (إن في خلق السموات والأرض واختلاف الليل والنهار لآيات

لأولي الألباب.
# الذين يذكرون الله قياما وقعودا وعلى جنوبهم ... ) [آل عمران: 190] .
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ز-و-ل (z-w-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Cessation, departure, decline; the sun's departure from its meridian zenith (zawāl).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Temporal transition marking the shift from the forenoon to the afternoon; a divinely-ordained boundary for prayer times.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for the sun's physical declination; metaphorical (majāz) for the passing of a state or season of divine mercy.
- Sībawayh Rule: Ẓarf (Adverbial Accusative) — temporal adverbs like "عند" (at the time of) govern the accusative, indicating the precise moment of an action's occurrence.
chapters.translation:
I say: And may He grant us and you success, and may He pardon us and you for our stumbles.

| (Chapter: What One Says When the Sun Rises High)

| 243 -
We narrated in the Book of Ibn al-Sunnī, on the authority of ʿAmr ibn ʿAbasah (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him), who said: "The sun does not rise high, leaving any of Allah's creation remaining, except that it glorifies Allah (ʿazza wa jall) and praises Him — save what is of the devil and the most obstinate of the children of Adam." I asked about the most obstinate of the children of Adam, and he said: "The worst of creation."

| (Chapter: What One Says After the Sun's Zawāl Until the ʿAṣr)
There has already preceded [the mention of] what one says when donning his garment, when leaving his house, when entering the privy, when exiting it, when performing ablution, when heading to the mosque, when reaching its door, when entering it, when hearing the mu'adhdhin and the muqīm, and what is between the adhān and the iqāmah, and what one says when intending to stand for prayer, and what one says in the prayer from its beginning to its end, and what one says after it — and all of this is shared by all the prayers.
And it is recommended (mustaḥabb) to multiply remembrances (adhkār) and other acts of worship immediately following the zawāl.

| 244 -
For we narrated in the Book of al-Tirmidhī, on the authority of ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Sā'ib (may Allah be pleased with him), "that the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) used to pray four [rakʿāt] after the sun's zawāl before the ẓuhr, and he said: 'It is an hour in which the gates of heaven are opened, and I love that a righteous deed of mine ascend therein.'" Al-Tirmidhī said: A ḥasan ḥadīth.
And it is recommended to multiply remembrances after the ẓuhr obligation, due to the generality of Allah's saying (Exalted is He): {«وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ بِالْعَشِيِّ وَالْإِبْكَارِ»} ("And glorify the praise of your Lord in the evening and the morning"). The people of language said: al-ʿashiyy is from the sun's zawāl to its setting.
Imam Abū Manṣūr al-Azharī said: Al-ʿashiyy among the Arabs is what is between the sun's zawāl and its setting.

| (Chapter: What One Says After the ʿAṣr Until the Sun's Setting)
There has already preceded what one says after the ẓuhr, and likewise the ʿaṣr. And it is recommended to multiply remembrances in the ʿaṣr with an emphatic recommendation (istiḥbāban mu'akkadan), for it is the middle prayer (al-ṣalāt al-wusṭā) according to the statement of many of the Salaf and the Khalaf. Likewise, it is recommended to increase attention to remembrances in the ṣubḥ — for these two prayers are the most sound of what has been said regarding the middle prayer. And it is recommended to multiply remembrances after the ʿaṣr, and the end of the day is even more so. Allah (Exalted is He) said: {«فَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ وَقَبْلَ غُرُوبِهَا»} ("So glorify the praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting") [Ṭāhā: 130]. And He said (Exalted is He): {«وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ بِالْعَشِيِّ وَالْإِبْكَارِ»} ("And glorify the praise of your Lord in the evening and the morning").
And Allah (Exalted is He) said: {«وَاذْكُرْ رَبَّكَ فِي نَفْسِكَ تَضَرُّعًا وَخِيفَةً وَدُونَ الْجَهْرِ مِنَ الْقَوْلِ بِالْغُدُوِّ وَالْآصَالِ»} ("And remember your Lord within yourself, in supplication and fear, and without loudness of speech, in the mornings and the evenings") [Ghāfir: 55]. And He said (Exalted is He): {«يُسَبِّحُ لَهُ فِيهَا بِالْغُدُوِّ وَالْآصَالِ رِجَالٌ لَا تُلْهِيهِمْ تِجَارَةٌ وَلَا بَيْعٌ عَنْ ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ»} ("Men whom neither commerce nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah, glorifying Him therein in the mornings and the evenings") [al-Nūr: 36]. And it has already preceded that al-āṣāl is what is between the ʿaṣr and the maghrib.

| 245 -
And we narrated in the Book of Ibn al-Sunnī with a weak chain (isnād ḍaʿīf), on the authority of Anas (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "That I sit with a people who remember Allah (ʿazza wa jall) from the ʿaṣr prayer until the sun sets is more beloved to me than freeing eight of the descendants of Ismāʿīl."

| (Chapter: What One Says When Hearing the Maghrib Adhān)

| 246 -
We narrated in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd and al-Tirmidhī, on the authority of Umm Salamah (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) taught me to say at the adhān of the maghrib: "O Allah, this is the coming of Your night, the departure of Your day, and the voices of Your callers — so forgive me."

| (Chapter: What One Says After the Maghrib Prayer)
There has already preceded, recently, that one says after all the prayers the remembrances mentioned earlier. And it is recommended that one add, saying after he prays the sunnah of the maghrib:

| 247 -
What we narrated in the Book of Ibn al-Sunnī, on the authority of Umm Salamah (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him), when he departed from the maghrib prayer, would enter and pray two rakʿāt, then say in his supplication: "O Turner of hearts, establish our hearts upon Your religion."

| 248 -
