- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of 'Aṭf (Coordination) and Conditional Clauses (Jumal Shartiyyah) — The text employs coordinated phrases (e.g., 'the last half is better than the first') and conditional constructions ('if he sleeps... then he recites') requiring precise temporal and logical linkage in translation.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that the most virtuous recitation outside of prayer is recitation at night, and the latter half of the night is superior to the former half. Recitation between the Maghrib and ʿIshā' prayers is beloved (maḥbūbah).

As for daytime recitation, the most virtuous is that which occurs after the Dawn Prayer (Ṣalāt al-Ṣubḥ). There is no disapproval (karāhah) in recitation at any time whatsoever, nor during the times in which prayer is prohibited.

As for what Ibn Abī Dāwūd (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated from Muʿādh ibn Rifāʿah (may Allah have mercy on him), from his shaykhs, that they disapproved of recitation after the ʿAṣr prayer, saying, 'It is the study of the Jews' — this is unacceptable (ghayr maqbūl), and it has no foundation (lā aṣla lahu).

Among the days, one should choose: Friday (al-Jumuʿah), Monday (al-Ithnayn), and Thursday (al-Khamīs), and the Day of ʿArafah. Among the ten-day periods (al-aʿshār): the first ten days of Dhū al-Ḥijjah and the last ten days of Ramaḍān. Among the months: Ramaḍān.

[CHAPTER] On the Etiquettes of the Completion (Khatm) and What Pertains to It:

It has already been mentioned that the completion (khatm) for the reciter alone is recommended (yustaḥabb) to be performed within prayer.

As for one who completes the Qur'an outside of prayer — such as a group who complete it together — it is recommended that their completion occur at the beginning of the night or the beginning of the day, as previously mentioned.

It is recommended to fast on the day of completion, unless it coincides with a day on which the Sacred Law (al-Sharʿ) has prohibited fasting.

It is authentically established (ṣaḥḥa) from Ṭalḥah ibn Muṣarrif, al-Musayyab ibn Rāfiʿ, and Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit — the Kūfan Successors (al-tābiʿīn), may Allah have mercy on them all — that they would begin the morning of the day on which they completed the Qur'an in a state of fasting.

It is recommended to attend the gathering of completion (majlis al-khatm), both for the one who recites and for the one who does not master recitation.

306 — We have narrated in the Two Ṣaḥīḥs (al-Ṣaḥīḥayn): {«That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded the menstruating women to go out on the Day of ʿĪd to witness the good and the supplication of the Muslims»}.

307 — We have narrated in the Musnad of al-Dārimī, from Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both), that he would appoint a man to watch over another man reciting the Qur'an; when he intended to complete it, he would inform Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both), and he would attend that (completion).

308 — Ibn Abī Dāwūd narrated with two authentic chains (isnādayn ṣaḥīḥayn), from Qatādah — the noble Successor, the Imām, the companion of Anas (may Allah be pleased with him) — who said: 'When Anas ibn Mālik (may Allah be pleased with him) completed the Qur'an, he would gather his family and supplicate.'

309 — He narrated with authentic chains, from al-Ḥakam ibn ʿUtaybah — with a tā' with two dots above, then a tā' with two dots below, then a bā' with one dot — the noble Successor, the Imām, who said: 'Mujāhid and ʿAbadah ibn Abī Lubābah sent word to me, saying: "We have sent to you because we intended to complete the Qur'an, and supplication is answered (mustajāb) at the completion of the Qur'an."'

310 — He narrated with his authentic chain, from Mujāhid, who said: 'They would gather at the completion of the Qur'an, saying: "Indeed, mercy descends at the Qur'an."' — i.e., mercy descends.

[CHAPTER]:
It is recommended to supplicate (duʿā') after the completion (khatmah) with a strongly emphasized recommendation (istiḥbāban muta'akkidan shadīdan), due to what we have previously mentioned.

We have narrated in the Musnad of al-Dārimī, and from Ḥumayd al-Aʿraj (may Allah have mercy on him), who said: 'Whoever recites the Qur'an and then supplicates, four thousand angels say Āmīn to his supplication.'

One should be persistent (mulīḥ) in supplication, and should supplicate for important matters and comprehensive words (al-kalimāt al-jāmiʿah). The greater part of it, or all of it, should concern the affairs of the Hereafter (umūr al-ākhirah), the affairs of the Muslims, the righteousness of their ruler (sulṭān) and all those in authority over their affairs, their success (tawfīq) in acts of obedience, their protection (ʿiṣmah) from acts of disobedience, their mutual cooperation upon righteousness and piety (al-birr wa al-taqwā), their establishment of the truth and their unity upon it, and their victory over the enemies of the religion and all other opponents. I have alluded to some of these matters in my book "Ādāb al-Qur'ān" (Etiquettes of the Qur'an), and I have mentioned therein concise supplications for whoever wishes to transmit them from it.

When one finishes the completion (khatmah), it is recommended to begin another recitation immediately connected to the completion, for the Salaf (the righteous predecessors) deemed this recommended.

311 — They adduced as evidence for this the ḥadīth of Anas (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: {«"The best of deeds are the setting out (al-ḥall) and the arrival (al-riḥlah)." It was said: "And what are they?" He said: "The opening of the Qur'an and its completion."»}

[CHAPTER] On the One Who Sleeps Through His Regular Portion (Ḥizb) and Customary Devotional Assignment (Wazīfah):

We have narrated in "Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim," from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: {«"Whoever sleeps through his ḥizb of the night, or through part of it, and then recites it between the Dawn Prayer (Ṣalāt al-Fajr) and the Noon Prayer (Ṣalāt al-Ẓuhr), it is written for him as if he had recited it in the night."»}

[CHAPTER] On the Command to Maintain the Qur'an (Taʿahhud) and the Warning Against Exposing It to Forgetfulness:

313 — We have narrated in the Two Ṣaḥīḥs of al-Bukhārī and Muslim, from Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: {«"Maintain this Qur'an (taʿāhadū), for by the One in Whose hand is the soul of Muḥammad, it is more prone to escape than a camel from its tether."»}

314 — We have narrated in their Two Ṣaḥīḥs, from Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both), that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: {«"The example of the companion of the Qur'an is like the example of a tethered camel: if he maintains it, he holds it fast; and if he releases it, it goes away."»}

315 — We have narrated in the book of Abū Dāwūd and al-Tirmidhī, from Anas (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: {«"The rewards of my nation were presented to me, even the speck of dust (al-qadhāh) that a man removes from the mosque. And the sins of my nation were presented to me, and I did not see a sin greater than a sūrah of the Qur'an or an āyah that a man was given and then forgot it."»} Al-Tirmidhī commented on it.

316 — We have narrated in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd and the Musnad of al-Dārimī, from Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: {«"Whoever recites the Qur'an and then forgets it, will meet Allah Almighty on the Day of Resurrection as a leper (ajdham)."»}

[CHAPTER] On Matters and Etiquettes That the Reciter Must Attend To:

These are very numerous indeed. We will mention from them some brief portions (aṭrāf), omitting the evidences due to their well-knownness and out of fear of tedious prolongation.

The first thing one is commanded with is: sincerity (ikhlāṣ) in his recitation, that he intends thereby Allah, Glorified and Exalted, and that he does not intend by it to attain anything other than that. He must conduct himself with proper adab (etiquette) toward the Qur'an, and bring to his mind that he is whispering in intimate conversation (munājāh) with Allah, Glorified and Exalted, and reciting His Book. He should recite in the state of one who sees Allah, for if he does not see Him, then Allah Almighty indeed sees him.

[CHAPTER]:
When he intends to recite, he should clean his mouth with the toothstick (siwāk) and other means. The preferred choice for the siwāk is to use a twig of the arāk tree, and it is permissible to use other twigs, and with al-saʿd (a fragrant plant), al-ushnān (a cleansing herb), a rough cloth, and other things that clean.

Regarding its attainment with a rough finger, there are three opinions (wujūh) among the Shāfiʿī companions: the most well-known among them is that it is not (sufficient).

chapters.title_en: Section 42 — On the Etiquette of the Toothstick (Siwāk), the Manner of Qur'anic Recitation, and Related Matters
chapters.arabic_text:
يحصل، والثاني: يحصل، والثالث: يحصل إن لم يجد
# غيرها، ولا يحصل إن وجد.
# ويستاك عرضا مبتدئا بالجانب الأيمن من فمه، وينوي به الإتيان بالسنة.
# قال بعض أصحابنا: يقول عند السواك: " اللهم بارك لي فيه يا أرحم الراحمين

" ويستاك في ظاهر الأسنان وباطنها، ويمر السواك على أطراف أسنانه وكراسي

أضراسه، وسقف حلقه إمرارا لطيفا، ويستاك بعود متوسط، لا شديد اليبوسة،

# ولا شديد اللين، فإن اشتد يبسه لينه بالماء.
# أما إذا كان فمه نجسا بدم أو غيره، فإنه يكره له قراءة القرآن قبل غسله،

وهل يحرم؟ فيه وجهان.
# أصحهما: لا يحرم، وسبقت المسألة أول الكتاب، وفي هذا الفصل بقايا تقدم

ذكرها في الفصول التي قدمتها في أول الكتاب.
# [فصل] :
# ينبغي للقارئ أن يكون شأنه الخشوع، والتدبر، والخضوع، فهذا هو المقصود

المطلوب، وبه تنشرح الصدور وتستنير القلوب، ودلائله أكثر من أن تحصر، وأشهر

من أن تذكر.
# وقد بات جماعة من السلف يتلو الواحد منهم الآية واحدة ليلة كاملة أو معظم

ليلة يتدبرها عند القراءة.
# وصعق جماعة منهم، ومات جماعات منهم.
# ويستحب البكاء والتباكي لمن لا يقدر على البكاء، فإن البكاء عند القراءة

صفة العارفين (1) وشعار عباد الله الصالحين، قال الله تعالى: (ويخرون

للأذقان يبكون ويزيدهم خشوعا) [الإسراء: 109] وقد ذكرت آثارا كثيرة وردت في

ذلك في " التبيان في آداب حملة القرآن ".
# قال السيد الجليل صاحب الكرامات والمعارف، والمواهب واللطائف، إبراهيم
# الخواص رضي الله عنه: دواء القلب خمسة أشياء: قراءة القرآن  بالتدبر،

وخلاء البطن، وقيام الليل، والتضرع عند السحر، ومجالسة الصالحين.
# [فصل] :
# قراءة القرآن في المصحف أفضل من القراءة من حفظه (2) ، هكذا قاله

أصحابنا، وهو مشهور عن السلف رضي الله عنهم، وهذا ليس على إطلاقه، بل إن

كان القارئ من حفظه يحصل له من التدبر والتفكر وجمع القلب والبصر أكثر مما

يحصل من المصحف، فالقراءة من الحفظ أفضل، وإن استويا، فمن المصحف أفضل،

وهذا مراد السلف.
# [فصل] :
# جاءت آثار بفضيلة رفع الصوت بالقراءة، وآثار بفضيلة الإسرار.
# قال العلماء: والجمع بينهما أن الإسرار أبعد من الرياء، فهو أفضل في حق

من يخاف ذلك، 
# فإن لم يخف الرياء، فالجهر أفضل، بشرط أن لا يؤذي غيره من مصل، أو نائم

أو غيرهما.
# ودليل فضيلة الجهر، أن العمل فيه أكبر، لأنه يتعدى نفعه إلى غيره، ولأنه

يوقظ قلب القارئ، ويجمع همه إلى الفكر، ويصرف سمعه إليه، ولأنه يطرد النوم

ويزيد في النشاط، ويوقظ غيره من نائم وغافل، وينشطه، فمتى حضره شئ من هذه

النيات فالجهر أفضل.
# [فصل] :
# ويستحب تحسين الصوت بالقراءة وتزيينها (1) ما لم يخرج عن حد القراءة

بالتمطيط، فإن أفرط حتى زاد حرفا أو أخفى حرفا، هو حرام (2) .
# وأما القراءة بالألحان، فهي على ما ذكرناه إن أفرط، فحرام، وإلا فلا،
# والأحاديث بما ذكرناه في تحسين الصوت كثيرة مشهورة في الصحيح وغيره ; وقد

ذكرت في آداب القراء قطعة منها.
# [فصل] :
# ويستحب للقارئ إذا ابتدأ من وسط السورة أن يبتدئ من أول الكلام المرتبط

بعضه بعض، وكذلك إذا وقف يقف على المرتبط وعند انتهاء الكلام، ولا يتقيد في

الابتداء ولا في الوقف بالأجزاء والأحزاب والأعشار، فإن كثيرا منها في وسط

الكلام المرتبط، ولا يغتر الإنسان بكثرة الفاعلين لهذا الذي نهينا عنه ممن

لا يراعي هذه الآداب، وامتثل ما قاله السيد الجليل أبو علي الفضيل بن عياض

رحمه الله عنه: لا تستوحش طرق الهدى لقلة أهلها، ولا تغتر بكثرة السالكين

الهاكين، ولهذا المعنى قال العلماء: قراءة سورة بكمالها أفضل من قراءة

قدرها من سورة طويلة، لأنه قد  يخفى الارتباط على كثير من الناس أو أكثرهم

في بعض الأحوال والمواطن.
# [فصل] :
# ومن البدع المنكرة ما يفعله كثيرون من جهلة المصلين بالناس التراويح من

# قراءة سورة (الأنعام) بكمالها في الركعة الأخيرة منها في الليلة السابعة،

معتقدين أنها مستحبة، زاعمين أنها نزلت جملة واحدة، فيجمعون في فعلهم هذا

أنواعا من
# المنكرات، منها: اعتقاد أنها مستحبة، ومنها: إيهام العوام ذلك، ومنها:

تطويل الركعة الثانية على الأولى، ومنها: التطويل على المأمومين، ومنها:

هذرمة القراءة، ومنها: المبالغة في تخفيف الركعات قبلها.
# [فصل] :

| 317 - 
# يجوز أن يقول: سورة البقرة، وسورة آل عمران، وسورة النساء، وسورة

العنكبوت، وكذلك الباقي، ولا كراهة في ذلك، وقال بعض السلف: يكره ذلك،

وإنما يقال: السورة التي تذكر فيها البقرة، والتي يذكر فيها النساء، وكذلك

الباقي، والصواب الأول، وهو قول جماهير علماء المسلمين من سلف الأمة

وخلفها، والأحاديث فيه عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أكثر من أن تحصر،

وكذلك عن الصحابة فمن بعدهم، وكذلك لا يكره أن يقال: هذه قراءة أبي عمرو،

وقراءة ابن كثير وغيرهما، هذا هو المذهب الصحيح المختار الذي عليه عمل

السلف والخلف من غير إنكار، وجاء عن إبراهيم النخعي رحمه الله أنه قال:

كانوا يكرهون [أن يقال:] سنة فلان، وقراءة فلان، والصواب: ما قدمناه.
# [فصل] :
# يكره أن يقول: نسيت آية كذا، أو سورة كذا، بل يقول: أنسيتها أو أسقطتها.

| 318 - 
# روينا في " صحيحي البخاري ومسلم " عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه، قال: قال

رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " لا يقول أحدكم: نسيت آية كذا وكذا، بل هو

نسي ".
# وفي رواية في الصحيحين أيضا: " بئسما لأحدهم أن يقول: نسيت آية كيت وكيت

بل هو نسي ".

| 319 - 
# وروينا في " صحيحيهما " عن عائشة رضي الله عنها، " أن النبي صلى الله

  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A physical purification ritual (ṭahārah) symbolizing spiritual cleansing, tied to prophetic practice (sunnah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) action of mechanical cleansing; metaphorical (majāz) extension to spiritual refinement.

chapters.translation:
I say: The first [matter]: it is attained. The second: it is attained. The third: it is attained if one finds no alternative, and it is not attained if one does find one.

One should use the toothstick (siwāk) horizontally, beginning with the right side of the mouth, intending thereby to perform the prophetic practice (sunnah). Some of our companions (aṣḥābunā) said: One says at the time of the toothstick: "O Allah, bless me in it, O Most Merciful of the merciful."

One uses the toothstick on the outer and inner surfaces of the teeth, passing it gently over the tips of the teeth, the molars, and the roof of the mouth with a delicate motion. One should use a medium-sized stick—neither excessively dry nor excessively soft—and if it becomes too dry, one softens it with water.

As for when one's mouth is impure (najis) due to blood or other matter, it is disliked (makrūh) for him to recite the Qur'an before washing it. Is it forbidden (ḥarām)? There are two opinions (wajhān) on this. The more correct of the two: it is not forbidden. This matter has already preceded at the beginning of the book, and in this section there remain remnants whose mention has preceded in the sections I presented at the start of the book.

[Section]:

It behooves the reciter that his state be one of humility (khushūʿ), reflection (tadabbur), and submissiveness (khudūʿ)—for this is the intended and sought-after goal. Through it, hearts expand and souls are illuminated. Its proofs are too numerous to enumerate and too famous to mention.

A group of the pious predecessors (salaf) would spend the night—one of them reciting a single verse for an entire night or most of the night—reflecting upon it during recitation. A group of them were struck unconscious, and many of them died [from the intensity of their emotion].

It is recommended to weep, and to feign weeping (tabākī) for one who cannot weep, for weeping during recitation is the attribute of the knowers of God (ʿārifīn) and the emblem of God's righteous servants. God Most High said: {«And they fall down on their chins weeping, and it increases them in humility»} [Al-Isrāʾ 17:109]. I have mentioned many reports (āthār) concerning this in "Al-Tibyān fī Ādāb Ḥamalat al-Qurʾān."

The noble master, possessor of miracles (karāmāt) and spiritual knowledges (maʿārif), of divine gifts and subtleties—Ibrāhīm al-Khawwāṣ, may God be pleased with him—said: The cure for the heart consists of five things: reciting the Qur'an with reflection, emptying the belly, night prayer (qiyām al-layl), supplication (taḍarruʿ) at dawn, and sitting with the righteous.

[Section]:

Reciting the Qur'an from the muṣḥaf (the written codex) is superior to reciting from memory. Thus said our companions, and it is well-known from the pious predecessors, may God be pleased with them. But this is not absolute; rather, if the reciter from memory attains more reflection, contemplation, focus of heart, and visual presence than he would from the muṣḥaf, then recitation from memory is superior. If the two are equal, then [recitation] from the muṣḥaf is superior. This is the intended meaning of the predecessors.

[Section]:

Reports have come regarding the virtue of raising the voice in recitation, and reports regarding the virtue of lowering it (isrār). The scholars said: The reconciliation between them is that lowering the voice is further from ostentation (riyāʾ), so it is superior for one who fears that. But if one does not fear ostentation, then raising the voice (jahr) is superior, on the condition that it does not harm another—whether one praying, sleeping, or otherwise.

The proof of the virtue of raising the voice is that the act therein is greater, because its benefit extends to others; because it awakens the reciter's heart, gathers his attention toward thought, and directs his hearing to it; because it repels sleep and increases vigor; and because it awakens others—whether sleeping or heedless—and energizes them. So whenever any of these intentions is present, raising the voice is superior.

[Section]:

It is recommended to beautify the voice in recitation and adorn it, as long as one does not exceed the bounds of recitation through excessive elongation (tamṭīṭ). If one overdoes it—such that it adds a letter or conceals a letter—it is forbidden (ḥarām). As for reciting with melodies (alḥān), it is as we have mentioned: if one exceeds [proper bounds], it is forbidden; otherwise, it is not.

The hadiths concerning what we have mentioned about beautifying the voice are numerous and well-known in the Ṣaḥīḥ and other collections; I have mentioned a portion of them in "Ādāb al-Qurrāʾ."

[Section]:

It is recommended for the reciter, when beginning from the middle of a sūrah, to begin from the start of a connected discourse—parts of which are linked to one another. Likewise, when stopping, he should stop at a connected point and at the completion of speech. He should not be bound in beginning or stopping by the juzʾ, ḥizb, or ʿushr divisions, for many of these fall in the middle of connected discourse. One should not be deceived by the multitude of those who do that which we have forbidden—those who do not observe these etiquettes. One should emulate what the noble master Abū ʿAlī al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ, may God have mercy on him, said: "Do not feel lonely on the paths of guidance due to the fewness of their travelers, and do not be deceived by the multitude of those who walk in ruin." For this meaning, the scholars said: Reciting a complete sūrah is superior to reciting its equivalent length from a long sūrah, because the connection may be hidden from many people—or most of them—in certain states and situations.

[Section]:

Among the reprehensible innovations (bidaʿ munkarah) is what many ignorant prayer leaders (juhhal al-muṣallīn) do during the Tarāwīḥ prayer: reciting the entire Sūrat al-Anʿām in the final rakʿah on the seventh night, believing it to be recommended, claiming that it was revealed all at once. In this act of theirs, they combine several types of objectionable things, including: their belief that it is recommended; their deluding the common people with that; lengthening the second rakʿah over the first; burdening the followers (maʾmūmīn) with excessive length; hasty and slurred recitation (hadhramah); and excessive shortening of the preceding rakʿahs.

[Section]:

317 — It is permissible to say: "Sūrat al-Baqarah," "Sūrat Āl ʿImrān," "Sūrat al-Nisāʾ," "Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt," and likewise the rest—there is no dislike (karāhah) in that. Some of the predecessors said: That is disliked; rather, one should say: "The sūrah in which the cow is mentioned," "the one in which women are mentioned," and likewise the rest. The correct view is the first, and it is the saying of the majority of Muslim scholars—from the predecessors (salaf) and successors (khalaf) of this ummah. The hadiths concerning this from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, are too numerous to count, and likewise from the Companions and those after them. Likewise, it is not disliked to say: "This is the recitation (qirāʾah) of Abū ʿAmr," "the recitation of Ibn Kathīr," and others. This is the correct and chosen school (madhhab) upon which the practice of the predecessors and successors proceeded without disapproval. It has come from Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī, may God have mercy on him, that he said: "They used to dislike saying: 'The sunnah of so-and-so' and 'the recitation of so-and-so.'" The correct view is what we have presented.

[Section]:

It is disliked to say: "I forgot such-and-such a verse" or "such-and-such a sūrah." Rather, one should say: "I was made to forget it" (ansītuhā) or "I dropped it" (asqaṭtuhā).

318 — We have narrated in the two Ṣaḥīḥs of al-Bukhārī and Muslim, on the authority of Ibn Masʿūd, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Let none of you say: 'I forgot such-and-such a verse.' Rather, he was made to forget." In another narration in the two Ṣaḥīḥs: "How bad it is for one of them to say: 'I forgot such-and-such a verse.' Rather, he was made to forget."

319 — And we have narrated in their two Ṣaḥīḥs, on the authority of ʿĀʾishah, may God be pleased with her, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace...

chapters.title_en: Section 43 — On the Etiquette of Qur'anic Recitation and the Virtues of Specific Surahs; The Book of Praise of Allah
chapters.arabic_text:
عليه وسلم سمع رجلا يقرأ، فقال: " رحمه الله، لقد أذكرني آية كنت أسقطتها

".
# وفي رواية في الصحيح: " كنت أنسيتها " (1) . 
# [فصل] :
# اعلم أن آداب القارئ والقراءة لا يمكن استقصاؤها في أقل من مجلدات، ولكنا

أردنا الإشارة إلى  بعض مقاصدها المهمات بما ذكرناه من هذه الفصول

المختصرات، وقد تقدم في الفصول السابقة في أول الكتاب شئ من آداب الذاكر

والقارئ، وتقدم أيضا في أذكار الصلاة جمل من الآداب المتعلقة بالقراءة، وقد

قدمنا الحوالة على كتاب " التبيان في آداب حملة القرآن " لمن أراد مزيدا،

وبالله التوفيق، وهو حسبي ونعم الوكيل.
# [فصل] :
# اعلم أن قراءة القرآن آكد الأذكار كما قدمنا، فينبغي المداومة عليها، فلا

يخلي عنها يوما وليلة، ويحصل له أصل القراءة بقراءة الآيات القليلة.

| 320 - 
# وقد روينا في كتاب ابن السني، عن أنس رضي الله عنه، أن رسول الله صلى

الله عليه وسلم قال: " من قرأ في يوم وليلة خمسين آية لم يكتب من الغافلين،

ومن قرأ مائة آية كتب من القانتين، ومن قرأ مائتي آية لم يحاجه القرآن يوم

القيامة، ومن قرأ خمسمائة كتب له قنطار من الأجر " وفي رواية (1) : " من

قرأ أربعين آية " بدل " خمسين " وفي رواية " عشرين " وفي رواية عن أبي

هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " من قرأ عشر

آيات لم يكتب من الغافلين " (2) وجاء في الباب أحاديث كثيرة بنحو هذا.
# وروينا أحاديث كثيرة في قراءة سور في اليوم والليلة، منها: يس، وتبارك

الملك، والواقعة، والدخان.

| 321 - 
# فعن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " من قرأ

(يس) في يوم وليلة ابتغاء وجه الله غفر له " (3) .

| 322 - 
# وفي رواية له: " من قرأ سورة (الدخان) في ليلة أصبح مغفورا له " (4) .

| 323 - 
# وفي رواية عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه، سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

يقول: " من قرأ سورة (الواقعة) في كل ليلة لم تصبه فاقة " (1) .

| 324 - 
# وعن جابر رضي الله عنه: " كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا ينام كل

ليلة حتى يقرأ (آلم تنزيل) الكتاب، و ((تبارك) الملك " (2) .

| 325 - 
# وعن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه، أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " من قرأ

في ليلة (إذا زلزلت الأرض) كانت له  كعدل نصف القرآن، ومن قرأ (يا أيها

الكافرون) كانت له كعدل ربع القرآن، ومن قرأ قل (هو الله أحد) كانت له كعدل

ثلث القرآن " (3) .

| 326 - 
# وفي رواية: " من قرأ آية الكرسي، وأول (حم) عصم ذلك اليوم من كل سوء "

(4) .
# والأحاديث بنحو ما ذكرنا كثيرة، وقد أشرنا إلى المقاصد، والله أعلم

بالصواب، وله الحمد والنعمة، وبه التوفيق والعصمة.

| كتاب حمد الله تعالى
# قال الله تعالى: (قل الحمد لله وسلام على عباده الذين اصطفى) [النمل: 59]

وقال الله تعالى: (وقل الحمد لله سيريكم آياته) [النمل: 93] وقال تعالى:

(وقل الحمد لله الذي لم يتخذ ولدا) [الإسراء: 111] وقال تعالى: (لئن شكرتم

لأزيدنكم) [إبراهيم: 7] وقال تعالى: (فاذكروني أذكركم واشكروا لي ولا

تكفرون) [البقرة: 152] والآيات المصرحة بالأمر بالحمد والشكر وبفضلهما

كثيرة معروفة.

| 327 - 
# وروينا في " سنن أبي داود "، " وابن ماجه "، و " مسند أبي عوانة

الإسفراييني " المخرج على " صحيح مسلم " رحمهم الله، عن أبي هريرة رضي الله

عنه، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: " كل أمر ذي بال لا يبدأ

فيه بالحمد لله فهو أقطع ". 
# وفي رواية: " بحمد الله ".
# وفي رواية: " بالحمد فهو أقطع ".
# وفي رواية: " كل كلام لا يبدأ فيه بالحمد لله فهو أجذم ".
# وفي رواية: " كل أمر ذي بال لا يبدأ فيه ببسم الله الرحمن الرحيم (1) فهو

أقطع ".
# روينا هذه الألفاظ كلها في كتاب " الأربعين " للحافظ عبد القادر الرهاوي،

وهو حديث حسن، وقد روي موصولا كما ذكرنا، وروي مرسلا، ورواية الموصول جيدة

الإسناد،
# وإذا روي الحديث موصولا ومرسلا، فالحكم للاتصال عند جمهور العلماء، لأنها

زيادة ثقة، وهي مقبولة عند الجماهير، ومعى " ذي بال ": أي: له حال يهتم به،

ومعنى أقطع: أي ناقص قليل البركة، وأجذم: بمعناه، وهو بالذال المعجمة

وبالجيم.
# قال العلماء: فيستحب البداءة بالحمد لله لكل مصنف، ودارس، ومدرس، وخطيب،

وخاطب، وبين يدي سائر الأمور المهمة.
# قال الشافعي رحمه الله: أحب أن يقدم المرء بين يدي خطبته وكل أمر طلبه:

حمد الله تعالى، والثناء عليه سبحانه وتعالى، والصلاة على رسول الله صلى

الله عليه وسلم.
# [فصل] :
# اعلم أن الحمد مستحب في ابتداء كل أمر ذي بال كما سبق، كما يستحب بعد

الفراغ من الطعام والشراب، والعطاس، وعند خطبة المرأة - وهو طلب زواجها -

وكذا عند عقد النكاح، وبعد الخروج من الخلاء، وسيأتي بيان هذه المواضع في

أبوابها بدلائلها، وتفريع مسائلها إن شاء الله تعالى، وقد سبق بيان ما يقال

بعد الخروج من الخلاء في بابه، ويستحب في ابتداء الكتب المصنفة كما سبق،

وكذا في ابتداء دروس المدرسين، وقراءة الطالبين، سواء قرأ حديثا أو فقها أو

غيرهما، وأحسن العبارات في ذلك: الحمد لله رب العالمين.
# [فصل] :
# حمد الله تعالى ركن في خطبة الجمعة وغيرها، لا يصح شئ منها إلا به، وأقل

الواجب: الحمد لله، والأفضل أن يزيد من الثناء، وتفصيله معروف في كتب

الفقه.
# ويشترط كونها بالعربية.
# [فصل] :
# يستحب أن يختم دعاءه بالحمد لله رب العالمين، وكذلك يبتدئه بالحمد لله،

قال الله تعالى: (وآخر دعواهم أن الحمد لله رب العالمين) [يونس: 10] وأما
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ذ-ك-ر (dhakara)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Remembrance, mention, recollection; the opposite of forgetfulness (nisyān)
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Dhikr as the heart's presence with Allah, encompassing verbal praise, supplication, and Qur'anic recitation — the highest form being the Qur'an itself
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — verbal mention; metaphorical (majāz) — internalized remembrance manifesting in obedience
- Root: ح-م-د (ḥamida)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Praise accompanied by gratitude; commendation of beauty and excellence
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ḥamd as the acknowledgment of Allah's absolute perfection and beneficence, distinct from mere shukr (gratitude for specific favors)
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — verbal laudation; metaphorical — the state of the servant wholly oriented toward the Praised One
- Root: ق-ر-أ (qara'a)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To read, recite, gather letters into coherent speech
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Tilāwah — following the Qur'an's commands through recitation and compliance
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — vocal articulation; metaphorical — contemplative engagement with meaning
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-jawāb) — The prophetic reports employ conditional clauses (man qara'a... kataba lahu) where the protasis specifies the action and the apodosis the reward, indicating causal connection between deed and divine recompense.
chapters.translation:
...upon him be peace, heard a man reciting, so he said: "May Allah have mercy upon him. He has reminded me of a verse I had dropped."

# In another narration in the Ṣaḥīḥ: "I had forgotten it."

# [Section]:
Know that the etiquettes of the reciter and of recitation cannot be exhaustively covered in less than multiple volumes. However, we intended to indicate some of its important objectives through what we have mentioned in these abridged sections. Already in the preceding sections at the beginning of the Book, some etiquettes of the one who remembers (al-dhākir) and the reciter have been presented, and likewise in the remembrances of prayer (adhkār al-ṣalāh), a number of etiquettes pertaining to recitation have been given. We have already referred to the book "Al-Tibyān fī Ādāb Ḥamalat al-Qur'ān" for whoever desires more. And with Allah is success; He is sufficient for me, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.

# [Section]:
Know that the recitation of the Qur'an is the most emphatic of all remembrances (ākad al-adhkār), as we have previously stated. Therefore, one should persist in it continuously, never abandoning it any day or night. The essential reward of recitation is attained by reciting even a few verses.

| 320 —
We have narrated in the book of Ibn al-Sunnī, on the authority of Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Whoever recites fifty verses in a day and night will not be recorded among the heedless (al-ghāfilīn). Whoever recites one hundred verses will be recorded among the devoutly obedient (al-qānitīn). Whoever recites two hundred verses, the Qur'an will not argue against him on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever recites five hundred verses, a qinṭār of reward will be recorded for him." In one narration: "Whoever recites forty verses" instead of "fifty," and in another narration "twenty." And in a narration from Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, he said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Whoever recites ten verses will not be recorded among the heedless." Many similar hadiths have come on this topic.

We have also narrated many hadiths concerning the recitation of specific surahs in the day and night, among them: Yā Sīn, Tabārak al-Mulk, al-Wāqiʿah, and al-Dukhān.

| 321 —
Thus, on the authority of Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him: "Whoever recites (Yā Sīn) in a day and night seeking the Face of Allah, he will be forgiven."

| 322 —
And in another narration from him: "Whoever recites Surah (al-Dukhān) in a night, he will wake up forgiven."

| 323 —
And in a narration from Ibn Masʿūd, may Allah be pleased with him: I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, say: "Whoever recites Surah (al-Wāqiʿah) every night, poverty will never afflict him."

| 324 —
And from Jābir, may Allah be pleased with him: "The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, would not sleep any night until he recited (Alif Lām Mīm Tanzīl) — the Book — and (Tabārak) al-Mulk."

| 325 —
And from Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Whoever recites at night (Idhā Zulzilat al-Arḍ), it will be for him equivalent to half of the Qur'an. Whoever recites (Yā Ayyuhā al-Kāfirūn), it will be for him equivalent to a quarter of the Qur'an. Whoever recites Qul (Huwa Allāhu Aḥad), it will be for him equivalent to a third of the Qur'an."

| 326 —
And in another narration: "Whoever recites the Verse of the Throne (Āyat al-Kursī) and the beginning of (Ḥā Mīm), he will be protected that day from every evil."

The hadiths similar to what we have mentioned are numerous, and we have indicated the essential objectives. And Allah knows best what is correct, and to Him belongs praise and grace, and through Him is success and protection.

---

# The Book of Praise of Allah the Exalted

Allah the Exalted said: {«Say: Praise be to Allah, and peace upon His servants whom He has chosen»} [al-Naml: 59]. And Allah the Exalted said: {«And say: Praise be to Allah; He will show you His signs»} [al-Naml: 93]. And the Exalted said: {«And say: Praise be to Allah, who has not taken a son»} [al-Isrā': 111]. And the Exalted said: {«If you are grateful, I will surely increase you»} [Ibrāhīm: 7]. And the Exalted said: {«So remember Me; I will remember you. And be grateful to Me and do not deny Me»} [al-Baqarah: 152]. The verses explicitly commanding praise (ḥamd) and gratitude (shukr), and their virtue, are numerous and well-known.

| 327 —
We have narrated in the "Sunan" of Abū Dāwūd, and Ibn Mājah, and the "Musnad" of Abū ʿAwānah al-Isfarāyīnī — arranged upon "Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim" — may Allah have mercy upon them, on the authority of Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, that he said: "Every matter of importance (dhū bāl) that does not begin with praise of Allah (al-ḥamdu lillāh) is severed (aqṭaʿ)."

In another narration: "With praise of Allah (bi-ḥamdillāh)."
In another narration: "With praise (bi-al-ḥamd), it is severed."
In another narration: "Every speech that does not begin with praise of Allah is maimed (ajdham)."
In another narration: "Every matter of importance that does not begin with In the Name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful (bismillāh al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm) is severed."

We have narrated all these wordings in the book "Al-Arbaʿīn" of the Ḥāfiẓ ʿAbd al-Qādir al-Rahāwī. This is a ḥasan hadith. It has been narrated with continuous chain (mawṣūl) as we have mentioned, and also with interrupted chain (mursal). The continuous narration has a sound chain of transmission.

When a hadith is narrated both continuously and interruptedly, the ruling is given to the continuous chain according to the majority of scholars (jumhūr al-ʿulamā'), because it constitutes an addition by a trustworthy narrator, which is accepted by the majority. The meaning of "dhū bāl" is: a matter that has a state one is concerned about. The meaning of "aqṭaʿ" is: deficient, having little blessing. And "ajdham" carries the same meaning; it is with the dotted dhāl and with jīm.

The scholars said: It is recommended (mustaḥabb) to begin with praise of Allah for every author, student, teacher, preacher, orator, and before all other important matters.

Al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah have mercy upon him, said: I love that a person place before his sermon and every matter he seeks: praise of Allah the Exalted, extolling Him — glorified and exalted be He — and sending prayers upon the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him.

# [Section]:
Know that praise (ḥamd) is recommended at the beginning of every matter of importance, as has preceded. Likewise, it is recommended after finishing from food and drink, after sneezing, at the proposal of a woman — that is, seeking her hand in marriage — and likewise at the conclusion of the marriage contract, and after leaving the lavatory. The explanation of these places will come in their respective chapters with their evidences and subsidiary rulings, if Allah the Exalted wills. The explanation of what is said after leaving the lavatory has already preceded in its chapter. It is also recommended at the beginning of authored books, as has preceded, and likewise at the beginning of teachers' lessons and students' recitations — whether reciting hadith, jurisprudence, or other than that. The best expression in this regard is: "Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds (al-ḥamdu lillāhi Rabb al-ʿālamīn)."

# [Section]:
Praise of Allah the Exalted is a pillar (rukn) in the Friday sermon and other sermons; none of them is valid without it. The minimum obligatory is: "Praise be to Allah (al-ḥamdu lillāh)." The better practice is to add more extolling, and its detailed treatment is well-known in the books of jurisprudence.

It is a condition that it be in Arabic.

# [Section]:
It is recommended to conclude one's supplication with "Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds," and likewise to begin it with "Praise be to Allah." Allah the Exalted said: {«And the last of their call will be: Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds»} [Yūnus: 10]. And as for...
