# Al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned a disconnected (munqaṭiʿ) ḥadīth, from a man who complained to the Prophet ﷺ of poverty, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Perhaps you revile the wind."
# Al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah have mercy on him, said: It is not befitting for anyone to revile the winds, for they are an obedient creation of Allah the Exalted, and a troop from His troops; He makes them a mercy and a punishment whenever He wills.

| (Chapter: What to say when a shooting star falls)

| 520 -
# We narrated in the book of Ibn al-Sunnī, on the authority of Ibn Masʿūd, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: We were commanded not to follow the shooting star with our eyes when it falls, and to say at that time: "Mā shā' Allāh, lā quwwata illā billāh" (What Allah wills — there is no power except with Allah).

| (Chapter: On refraining from pointing at and looking at the shooting star and lightning)
# In it is the aforementioned ḥadīth in the preceding chapter.

| 521 -
# Al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated in "al-Umm" with his chain, from one who is not accused [of untrustworthiness], on the authority of ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: When any of you sees lightning or rain-bearing clouds (al-wadaq), let him not point at it, but let him describe it and characterize it.
# Al-Shāfiʿī said: The Arabs have never ceased to disapprove of it.

| (Chapter: What to say when hearing thunder)

| 522 -
# We narrated in the book of al-Tirmidhī with a weak chain (isnād ḍaʿīf), on the authority of Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when he heard the sound of thunder and thunderbolts, would say: "O Allah, do not kill us with Your wrath, and do not destroy us with Your punishment, and grant us well-being before that."

| 523 -
# We narrated with a sound chain in "al-Muwaṭṭa'", on the authority of ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Zubayr, may Allah be pleased with them both, that when he heard thunder he would abandon conversation and say: "Glory be to Him whom the thunder glorifies with His praise, and the angels [glorify] out of fear of Him."

| 524 -
# Imām al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated in "al-Umm" with his sound chain, on the authority of Ṭāwūs, the venerable Imām of the Tābiʿūn, may Allah have mercy on him, that he would say upon hearing thunder: "Glory be to Him to Whom [all things] glorify."
# Al-Shāfiʿī said: It is as if he intends the saying of Allah the Exalted: {«ويسبح الرعد بحمده»} [al-Raʿd: 13].

| 525 -
# They mentioned on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: We were with ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, on a journey, and thunder, lightning, and hail struck us. Kaʿb said to us: "Whoever says upon hearing thunder, three times: 'Glory be to Him whom the thunder glorifies with His praise, and the angels out of fear of Him,' will be protected from that thunder." We said it, and we were protected.

| (Chapter: What to say when rain descends)

| 526 -
# We narrated in "Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī" on the authority of ʿĀ'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when he saw rain, would say: "O Allah, [send] a beneficial copious rain (ṣayyiban nāfiʿan)."

| 527 -
# We narrated in "Sunan Ibn Mājah," and he said therein: "O Allah, [send] a beneficial copious rain" — two or three times.

| 528 -
# Al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated in "al-Umm" with his chain, a mursal ḥadīth, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Seek the response to supplication at the meeting of armies, and at the establishment of prayer."

| (Chapter: What to say after the rain has fallen)

| 529 -
# We narrated in the two Ṣaḥīḥs of al-Bukhārī and Muslim, on the authority of Zayd ibn Khālid al-Juhanī, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ led us in the dawn prayer (ṣalāt al-ṣubḥ) at al-Ḥudaybiyyah, following a rain that had fallen during the night. When he finished, he turned to the people and said: "Do you know what your Lord said?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "He said: 'This morning, among My servants are those who believe in Me and those who disbelieve [in Me]. As for the one who says: "We were given rain by the bounty of Allah and His mercy" — that one believes in Me and disbelieves in the star [as a cause]. As for the one who says: "We were given rain by such-and-such a lunar mansion (naw')" — that one disbelieves in Me and believes in the star.'"
# I say: Al-Ḥudaybiyyah is well-known; it is a well near Makkah, less than one stage (marḥalah) away. It is permissible to lighten the second yā' or to double it; the lightening is the correct and preferred [pronunciation], and it is the saying of al-Shāfiʿī and the scholars [of the Hijaz].

chapters.title_en: Section 67 — On the Language of Rain, the Prayer for Rain, and Adhkar for Tarawih, Need, and Tasbih Prayers
chapters.arabic_text:
اللغة، والتشديد قول ابن وهب وأكثر المحدثين.
# والسماء هنا: المطر.
# وإثر بكسر الهمزة وإسكان الثاء، ويقال بفتحهما لغتان.
# قال العلماء: إن قال مسلم: مطرنا بنوء كذا،
# مريدا أن النوء هو الموجد والفاعل المحدث للمطر، صار كافرا مرتدا بلا شك،

وإن قاله مريدا أنه علامة لنزول المطر، فينزل المطر عند هذه العلامة،

ونزوله بفعل الله تعالى وخلقه سبحانه، لم يكفر.
# واختلفوا في كراهته، والمختار أنه مكروه، ولأنه من ألفاظ الكفار، وهذا

ظاهر الحديث، ونص عليه الشافعي رحمه الله في " الأم " وغيره، والله أعلم.
# ويستحب أن يشكر الله سبحانه وتعالى على هذه النعمة، أعني نزول المطر.

| (باب ما يقوله إذا كثر المطر وخيف منه الضرر)

| 530 - 
# روينا في " صحيحي البخاري ومسلم " عن أنس رضي الله عنه، قال: دخل رجل

المسجد يوم جمعة، ورسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قائم يخطب، فقال: يارسول

الله هلكت 
# الأموال وانقطعت السبل، فادع الله يغيثنا (1) ، فرفع رسول الله صلى الله

عليه وسلم يديه ثم قال: " اللهم أغثنا، اللهم أغثنا "، قال أنس: ولا والله،

ما نرى في السماء من سحاب ولا قزعة (2) ، وما بينا وبين سلع - يعني الجبل

المعروف بقرب المدينة - من بيت ولا دار، فطلعت من ورائه سحابة مثل الترس،

فلما توسطت السماء انتشرت ثم أمطرت، فلا والله ما رأينا الشمس سبتا (3) ،

ثم دخل رجل من ذلك  الباب في الجمعة المقبلة ورسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

قائم يخطب، قال: يا رسول الله هلكت الأموال وانقطعت السبل، فادع الله

يمسكها (4) عنا، فرفع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يديه ثم قال: " اللهم

حوالينا ولا علينا، والظراب وبطون الأودية ومنابت الشجر، فانقلعت وخرجنا

نمشي في الشمس " هذا حديث لفظه فيهما، إلا أن في رواية البخاري: " اللهم

اسقنا " بدل " أغثنا " وما أكثر فوائده (6) ، وبالله التوفيق.

| (باب أذكار صلاة التراويح)
# اعلم أن صلاة التراويح سنة باتفاق العلماء، وهي عشرون ركعة، يسلم من كل
# ركعتين، وصفة نفس الصلاة كصفة باقي الصلوات على ما تقدم بيانه، ويجئ فيها

جميع الأذكار المتقدمة كدعاء الافتتاح، وإستكمال الأذكار الباقية، واستيفاء

التشهد، والدعاء بعده، وغير ذلك مما تقدم، وهذا وإن كان ظاهرا معروفا،

فإنما نبهت عليه لتساهل أكثر الناس فيه، وحذفهم أكثر الأذكار، والصواب ما

سبق.
# وأما القراءة فالمختار الذي قاله الأكثرون وأطبق الناس على العمل به أن

تقرأ الختمة بكمالها في التراويح جميع الشهر، فيقرأ في كل ليلة نحو جزء من

ثلاثين جزءا، ويستحب أن يرتل القراءة ويبينها، وليحذر من التطويل عليهم

بقراءة أكثر من جزء، * 
# وليحذر كل الحذر مما اعتاده جهلة أئمة كثير من المساجد من قراءة سورة

الأنعام بكمالها في الركعة الأخيرة في الليلة السابعة من شهر رمضان، زاعمين

أنها نزلت جملة، وهذه بدعة قبيحة وجهالة ظاهرة مشتملة على مفاسد كثيرة، وقد

أوضحتها في كتاب التبيان في آداب حملة القرآن " وبالله التوفيق.

| (باب أذكار صلاة الحاجة)

| 531 - 
# روينا في كتاب الترمذي وابن ماجه، عن عبد الله بن أبي أوفى رضي الله

عنهما، قال: قال: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " من كانت له حاجة إلى

الله تعالى أو إلى أحد من بني آدم فليتوضأ وليحسن الوضوء، ثم ليصل ركعتين،

ثم ليثن على الله عز وجل، وليصل على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ثم ليقل: لا

إله إلا الله الحليم الكريم، سبحان الله رب العرش العظيم، الحمد لله رب

العالمين، أسألك موجبات رحمتك، وعزائم  مغفرتك، والغنيمة من كل بر، والسلامة

من كل إثم، لا تدع لي ذنبا إلا غفرته، ولا هما إلا فرجته، ولا حاجة هي لك

رضا إلا قضيتها يا أرحم الراحمين ".
# قال الترمذي: في إسناده مقال (1) .
# قلت: ويستحب أن يدعو بدعاء الكرب، وهو: اللهم آتنا في الدنيا حسنة وفي

الآخرة حسنة وقنا عذاب النار، لما قدمناه عن " الصحيحين " فيهما.

| 532 - 
# وروينا في كتاب الترمذي، وابن ماجه، عن عثمان بن حنيف رضي الله عنه، أن

رجلا ضرير البصر أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: ادع الله تعالى أن

يعافيني، قال: " إن شئت دعوت، وإن شئت صبرت فهو خير لك، قال فادعه، فأمره

أن يتوضأ فيحسن وضوءه ويدعو بهذا الدعاء: اللهم إني أسألك وأتوجه إليك

بنبيك محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم نبي الرحمة، يا محمد إني توجهت بك إلى ربي

في حاجتي هذه لتقضى لي، اللهم فشفعه في " قال الترمذي: حديث حسن صحيح.

| باب أذكار المتعلقة بالزكاة

| 533 - 
# روينا في كتاب الترمذي عنه قال: قد روي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم غير

حديث في صلاة التسبيح، لا يصح منه كبير شئ (2) .
# قال: وقد رأى ابن المبارك وغير واحد من 
# أهل العلم صلاة التسبيح، وذكروا الفضل فيه.
# قال الترمذي: حدثنا أحمد بن عبدة، قال: حدثنا أبو وهب، قال: سألت عبد

الله بن المبارك عن الصلاة التي يسبح فيها، قال: يكبر ثم يقول: سبحانك

اللهم وبحمدك، تبارك اسمك وتعالى جدك ولا إله غيرك، ثم يقول خمس عشرة مرة:

سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إله إلا الله والله أكبر، ثم يتعوذ ويقرأ بسم

الله الرحمن الرحيم وفاتحة الكتاب، وسورة، ثم يقول عشر مرات: سبحان الله،

والحمد لله، ولا إله إلا الله والله أكبر، ثم يركع فيقولها عشرا، ثم يرفع

رأسه فيقولها عشرا، ثم يسجد فيقولها عشرا، ثم يرفع رأسه فيقولها عشرا، ثم

يسجد الثانية فيقولها عشرا، يصلي أربع ركعات على هذا، فذلك خمس وسبعون

تسبيحة في كل ركعة، يبدأ بخمس عشرة تسبيحة، ثم يقرأ، ثم  يسبح عشرا، فإن صلى

ليلا، فأحب إلي أن يسلم في ركعتين، وإن صلى نهارا، فإن شاء سلم، وإن شاء لم
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ن-و-أ (n-w-')
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A star's setting or rising; a celestial station (manzil) used in pre-Islamic Arabian weather prognostication.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The created sign (ʿalāmah) versus the false attribution of causal agency (taʾthīr) to celestial bodies — a boundary of tawḥīd.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for the star itself; metaphorical (majāz) when linked to rain causation, which must be rejected.
- Root: غ-و-ث (gh-w-th)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To seek relief from distress; a cry for divine succor.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Istighāthah as supplication for rain (istisqāʾ) — an act of servitude acknowledging Allah's sole power over provision.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical rescue; metaphorical for spiritual and agricultural relief.
- Root: ت-ر-و-ي-ح (t-r-w-y-ḥ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To give rest, comfort; derived from rāḥah (rest).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Tarāwīḥ as the night prayer of Ramadan, named for the respite between its units (taslīmāt).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical rest; metaphorical for the spiritual ease attained through prolonged worship.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — The phrase "يعني الجبل المعروف بقرب المدينة" functions as explanatory apposition, clarifying "سلع" without altering its syntactic case.
chapters.translation:
I say: Regarding the language [of the term "al-nawʾ"], the tashdīd [of the letter wāw] is the statement of Ibn Wahb and the majority of the ḥadīth scholars. And "al-samāʾ" here means rain. And "ithr" — with a kasrah on the hamzah and sukūn on the thāʾ — and it is also said with a fatḥah on both, being two dialects.

The scholars said: If a Muslim says, "We were given rain by such-and-such a nawʾ," intending that the nawʾ is the originator, the agent, and the cause that brings the rain into existence, he becomes a disbeliever and an apostate without any doubt. But if he says it intending that it is merely a sign for the descent of rain — so that rain descends at the time of this sign, while its descent is by the act of Allah, the Exalted, and His creation, glorified be He — then he does not disbelieve. They differed concerning its disapproval (karāhah), and the chosen position is that it is disapproved, because it is from the expressions of the disbelievers, and this is apparent from the ḥadīth. Al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah have mercy on him, explicitly stated this in "Al-Umm" and other works. And Allah knows best.

It is recommended to thank Allah, glorified and exalted be He, for this blessing — I mean the descent of rain.

| (Chapter: What to Say When Rain Abounds and Harm Is Feared from It)

| 530 —
We narrated in the two Ṣaḥīḥs of al-Bukhārī and Muslim, on the authority of Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: A man entered the mosque on a Friday while the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was standing delivering the sermon. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, the wealth has perished and the roads have been cut off, so supplicate Allah to give us rain." The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, raised his hands, then said: "O Allah, give us rain! O Allah, give us rain!" Anas said: "By Allah, we did not see in the sky any cloud or patch of cloud, and between us and Salʿ — meaning the well-known mountain near Medina — there was no house or dwelling. Then a cloud like a shield appeared from behind it. When it reached the middle of the sky, it spread out, and then it rained. By Allah, we did not see the sun for a week. Then a man entered from that same door the following Friday while the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was standing delivering the sermon. He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, the wealth has perished and the roads have been cut off, so supplicate Allah to withhold it from us.' The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, raised his hands, then said: 'O Allah, around us and not upon us — upon the hills, the bottoms of the valleys, and the places where trees grow.' So the cloud lifted, and we went out walking in the sun." This is the wording of the ḥadīth in both [collections], except that in the narration of al-Bukhārī, "O Allah, give us to drink" (Allāhumma asqinā) appears in place of "give us rain" (agḥithnā). And how numerous are its benefits! And with Allah is success.

| (Chapter: Adhkar of the Tarawih Prayer)

Know that the Tarawih prayer is a Sunnah by the consensus of the scholars. It is twenty rakʿahs, with the taslīm after every two rakʿahs. The description of the prayer itself is like the description of the rest of the prayers, as previously explained. All the previously mentioned adhkar apply to it — such as the opening supplication (duʿāʾ al-istiftāḥ), the completion of the remaining adhkar, the full recitation of the tashahhud, the supplication after it, and other matters previously mentioned. Although this is apparent and well-known, I have only drawn attention to it because most people are negligent in it and omit most of the adhkar. The correct course is what has preceded.

As for the recitation, the chosen view — which the majority have stated and upon which the people have unanimously acted — is that the entire Qurʾān (khatmah) should be completed in the Tarawih over the whole month. Thus, approximately one-thirtieth (juzʾ) is recited each night. It is recommended to recite with measured pace (tartīl) and clarity. And one should beware of prolonging upon them by reciting more than one juzʾ.

And one must be extremely cautious of what the ignorant imams of many mosques have accustomed themselves to — reciting Sūrat al-Anʿām in its entirety in the final rakʿah of the seventh night of Ramadan, claiming that it was revealed all at once. This is an ugly innovation (bidʿah) and manifest ignorance, comprising many corruptions. I have clarified this in the book "Al-Tibyān fī Ādāb Ḥamalat al-Qurʾān." And with Allah is success.

| (Chapter: Adhkar of the Prayer of Need)

| 531 —
We narrated in the books of al-Tirmidhī and Ibn Mājah, on the authority of ʿAbdullāh ibn Abī Awfā, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Whoever has a need from Allah, the Exalted, or from any of the children of Adam, let him perform ablution and perfect his ablution, then pray two rakʿahs, then praise Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and send blessings upon the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, then say: 'There is no god but Allah, the Forbearing, the Generous. Glory be to Allah, Lord of the Mighty Throne. Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds. I ask You for the causes of Your mercy, and the resolutions of Your forgiveness, and the gain from every righteousness, and safety from every sin. Do not leave for me any sin except that You forgive it, nor any worry except that You relieve it, nor any need that is pleasing to You except that You fulfill it, O Most Merciful of the merciful.'"

Al-Tirmidhī said: In its chain there is some discussion (maqāl).

I say: It is recommended to supplicate with the supplication of distress (duʿāʾ al-karb), which is: "O Allah, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire," due to what we have previously narrated from the two Ṣaḥīḥs concerning it.

| 532 —
And we narrated in the books of al-Tirmidhī and Ibn Mājah, on the authority of ʿUthmān ibn Ḥunayf, may Allah be pleased with him, that a man who was blind in his sight came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and said: "Supplicate Allah, the Exalted, to heal me." He said: "If you wish, I will supplicate; and if you wish, you may be patient, and that is better for you." He said: "Then supplicate." So he commanded him to perform ablution, perfect his ablution, and supplicate with this supplication: "O Allah, I ask You and I turn to You through Your Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, the Prophet of mercy. O Muhammad, I have turned through you to my Lord concerning this need of mine so that it may be fulfilled for me. O Allah, accept his intercession for me." Al-Tirmidhī said: A ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ ḥadīth.

| Chapter: Adhkar Related to the Prayer of Tasbīḥ

| 533 —
We narrated in the book of al-Tirmidhī, on his authority, who said: It has been narrated from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, more than one ḥadīth concerning the prayer of tasbīḥ, none of which is authentically established (lā yaṣiḥḥu minhu kabīr shayʾ).

He said: And Ibn al-Mubārak and more than one of the people of knowledge saw [the validity of] the prayer of tasbīḥ, and they mentioned the virtue in it.

Al-Tirmidhī said: Ḥaddathanā Aḥmad ibn ʿAbadah, who said: Ḥaddathanā Abū Wahb, who said: I asked ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mubārak about the prayer in which one glorifies [Allah]. He said: He says the takbīr, then says: "Glory be to You, O Allah, and with Your praise; blessed be Your name, and exalted be Your majesty, and there is no god other than You." Then he says fifteen times: "Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah, and there is no god but Allah, and Allah is Greater." Then he seeks refuge [in Allah] and recites "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful," and the Opening of the Book (Fātiḥah), and a sūrah. Then he says ten times: "Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah, and there is no god but Allah, and Allah is Greater." Then he bows (rukūʿ) and says it ten times. Then he raises his head and says it ten times. Then he prostrates and says it ten times. Then he raises his head and says it ten times. Then he prostrates a second time and says it ten times. He prays four rakʿahs in this manner. That totals seventy-five tasbīḥāt in each rakʿah. He begins with fifteen tasbīḥāt, then recites, then glorifies ten times. If he prays at night, then it is more beloved to me that he makes the taslīm after two rakʿahs. And if he prays during the day, then if he wishes, he makes the taslīm, and if he wishes, he does not.

chapters.title_en: Section 68 — On the Remembrances Related to the Prayer of Tasbīḥ and the Alms-Tax (Zakāh)
chapters.arabic_text:
يسلم (1) .
# وفي رواية عن عبد الله بن المبارك أنه قال: يبدأ في الركوع: سبحان ربي

العظيم، وفي السجود: سبحان ربي الأعلى ثلاثا، ثم يسبح التسبيحات، وقيل لابن

المبارك: إن سها في هذه الصلاة، هل يسبح في سجدتي السهو عشرا عشرا؟ قال:

لا، إنما هي ثلاثمائة تسبيحة.

| 534 - 
# وروينا في كتاب الترمذي، وابن ماجه، عن أبي رافع رضي الله عنه، قال: قال

رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم للعباس: يا عم ألا أصلك ألا أحبوك ألا أنفعك؟

" قال: بلى يا رسول الله، قال: " يا عم صل أربع ركعات تقرأ في كل ركعة

بفاتحة القرآن وسورة، فإذا انقضت القراءة، فقل: الله أكبر والحمد لله

وسبحان الله خمس عشرة مرة قبل أن تركع، ثم اركع فقلها عشرا ثم ارفع رأسك،

فقلها عشرا، ثم اسجد، فقلها عشرا، ثم ارفع رأسك، فقلها عشرا قبل أن تقوم،

فتلك خمس وسبعون في كل ركعة، وهي ثلاثمائة 
# في أربع ركعات، فلو كانت ذنوبك مثل رمل عالج غفرها الله تعالى لك "، قال:

يا رسول الله من يستطيع أن يقولها في يوم؟ قال: " إن لم تستطع أن تقولها في

يوم فقلها في جمعة، فإن لم تستطع أن تقولها في جمعة فقلها في شهر، فلم يزل

يقول له حتى قال: قلها في سنة " قال الترمذي: هذا حديث غريب.
# قلت: قال الإمام أبو بكر بن العربي في كتابه " الأحوذي في شرح الترمذي ":

حديث أبي رافع هذا ضعيف ليس له أصل في الصحة ولا في الحسن، قال: وإنما ذكره

الترمذي لينبه عليه لئلا يغتر به، قال: وقول ابن المبارك ليس بحجة، هذا

كلام أبي بكر بن العربي.
# وقال العقيلي: ليس في صلاة التسبيح حديث يثبت، وذكر أبو الفرج بن الجوزي

أحاديث صلاة التسبيح وطرقها، ثم ضعفها كلها وبين ضعفها، ذكره في كتابه في

الموضوعات (1) .
# وبلغنا عن الإمام الحافظ أبي الحسن الدارقطني رحمه الله  أنه قال: أصح شئ

في فضائل السور، فضل: (قل هو الله أحد) وأصح شئ في فضائل الصلوات فضل صلاة

التسبيح، وقد ذكرت هذا الكلام مسندا في كتاب " طبقات الفقهاء " في ترجمة

أبي الحسن علي بن عمر الدارقطني، ولا يلزم من هذه العبارة أن يكون حديث

صلاة التسبيح صحيحا، فإنهم يقولون: هذا أصح ما جاء في الباب، وإن كان

ضعيفا، ومرادهم أرجحه وأقله ضعفا (2) .
# قلت: وقد نص جماعة من أئمة أصحابنا على استحباب صلاة التسبيح هذه، منهم
# أبو محمد البغوي وأبو المحاسن الروياني.
# قال الروياني في كتابه " البحر " في آخر " كتاب الجنائز " منه: اعلم أن

صلاة التسبيح مرغب فيها، يستحب أن يعتادها في كل حين، ولا يتغافل عنها،

قال: هكذا قال عبد الله بن المبارك وجماعة من العلماء.
# قال: وقيل لعبد الله بن المبارك: إن سها في صلاة التسبيح، أيسبح في سجدتي

السهو عشرا عشرا؟ قال: لا، وإنما هي ثلاثمائة تسبيحة، وإنما ذكرت هذا

الكلام في سجود السهو، وإن كان قد تقدم لفائدة لطيفة، وهي أن مثل هذا

الإمام إذا حكى هذا ولم ينكره أشعر بذلك بأنه يوافقه، فيكثر القائل بهذا

الحكم، وهذا الروياني من فضلاء أصحابنا المطلعين، والله أعلم.

| (باب الأذكار المتعلقة بالزكاة)
# قال الله تعالى: (خذ من أموالهم صدقة تطهرهم وتزكيهم بها وصل عليهم)

[التوبة: 103] .

| 535 - 
# وروينا في (صحيحي البخاري ومسلم) عن عبد الله بن أبي أوفى رضي الله

عنهما، قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أتاه قوم بصدقة قال: "

اللهم صل عليهم " فأتاه أبو أوفى بصدقته فقال: " اللهم صل على آل أبي أوفى

".
# قال الشافعي والأصحاب رحمهم الله: الاختيار أن يقول: آخذ الزكاة لدافعها:

آجرك (1) الله فيما أعطيت، وجعله لك طهورا، وبارك لك فيما أبقيت، وهذا

الدعاء مستحب لقابض الزكاة، سواء كان الساعي أو الفقراء، وليس الدعاء بواجب

على المشهور من مذهبنا ومذهب غيرنا.
# وقال بعض أصحابنا: إنه واجب، لقول الشافعي: فحق على الوالي أن يدعو له،

ودليله ظاهر الأمر في الآية.
# قال العلماء: ولا  يستحب أن
# يقول في الدعاء: اللهم صل على فلان، والمراد بقوله تعالى: (وصل عليهم "

أي: ادع لهم.
# وأما قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: " اللهم صل عليهم عليهم " فقال لكون

لفظ الصلاة مختصا به، فله أن يخاطب به من يشاء بخلافنا نحن.
# قالوا: وكما لا يقال: محمد عز وجل وإن كان عزيزا جليلا، فكذا لا يقال:

أبو بكر، أو علي صلى الله عليه وسلم، بل يقال: رضي الله عنه، أو رضوان الله

عليه، وشبه ذلك، فلو قال: صلى الله عليه وسلم، فالصحيح الذي عليه جمهور

أصحابنا أنه مكروه كراهة تنزيه.
# وقال بعضهم: هو خلاف الأولى، ولا يقال: مكروه.
# وقال بعضهم: لا يجوز، وظاهره التحريم، ولا ينبغي أيضا في غير الأنبياء أن

يقال: عليه السلام، أو نحو ذلك إلا إذا كان خطابا أو جوابا، فإن الابتداء

بالسلام سنة، ورده واجب، ثم هذا كله في الصلاة، والسلام على غير الأنبياء

مقصودا.
# أما إذا جعل تبعا، فإنه جائز بلا خلاف، فيقال: اللهم صل على محمد وعلى

آله وأصحابه وأزواجه وذريته وأتباعه، لأن السلف لم يمتنعوا من هذا، بل قد

أمرنا به في التشهد وغيره، بخلاف الصلاة عليه منفردا، وقد قدمت ذكر هذا

الفصل مبسوطا في " كتاب الصلاة على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ".
# [فصل] :
# اعلم أن نية الزكاة واجبة، ونيتها تكون بالقلب كغيرها من العبادات،

ويستحب أن يضم إليه التلفظ باللسان، كما في غيرها من العبادات، فإن اقتصر

على لفظ 
# اللسان دون النية بالقلب، ففي صحته خلاف.
# الأصح أنه لا يصح، ولا يجب على دافع الزكاة إذا نوى أن يقول مع ذلك: هذه

زكاة، بل يكفيه الدفع إلى من كان من أهلها، ولو تلفظ بذلك لم يضره، والله
chapters.anchors:
- Root: س-ل-م (s-l-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root denotes safety, peace, and the act of greeting (salām); in ritual context, the closing salutation of prayer.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In worship, salām signifies the completion of devotion and the invocation of divine peace upon the congregation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — verbal greeting; metaphorical (majāz) — the concluding act of prayer as a symbol of spiritual security.
- Root: س-ب-ح (s-b-ḥ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning — to swim, float, or move freely; extended to glorification (tasbīḥ) as the soul's immersion in divine praise.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Theological nuance — declaring God's transcendence (tanzīh) above all imperfection; the phrase "Subḥāna Rabbī" is a formal acknowledgment of His absolute purity.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — the act of swimming; metaphorical — the soul's swift movement in glorifying God, as in the prescribed utterances in bowing and prostration.
- Root: ص-ل-و (ṣ-l-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root signifies supplication (duʿā'), blessing, and the act of prayer; in Quranic usage, it carries the sense of invoking divine mercy.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): For God, ṣalāh means mercy and praise; for angels, it is seeking forgiveness; for believers, it is supplication — a key distinction in the Prophet's exclusive right to "ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi."
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — prayer; metaphorical — the specific honor of invoking God's blessing upon the Prophet, which is not extended to others in independent form.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of ʿAṭf (Coordination) and Conditional Clauses (Shart) — The text employs conditional structures (e.g., "in lam tastaṭiʿ... fa-qulhā") requiring precise parsing of protasis and apodosis; also, the prohibition of independent ṣalāh on non-prophets is governed by the rule of taʿlīq (suspension) where the predicate is contextually restricted.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that the closing salutation (taslīm) is [performed] once.

In a narration from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak, he said: One begins in the bowing (rukūʿ) with: "Glory be to my Lord, the Magnificent" (Subḥāna Rabbī al-ʿAẓīm), and in the prostration (sujūd) with: "Glory be to my Lord, the Most High" (Subḥāna Rabbī al-Aʿlā) three times, then one adds the additional glorifications (tasbīḥāt). It was said to Ibn al-Mubārak: "If one errs in this prayer, does he glorify in the two prostrations of forgetfulness (sujūd al-sahw) ten by ten?" He said: "No, for it is only three hundred glorifications."

| 534 —
We have related in the Book of al-Tirmidhī and Ibn Mājah, from Abū Rāfiʿ (may God be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said to al-ʿAbbās: "O uncle, shall I not grant you, shall I not honor you, shall I not benefit you?" He said: "Yes, O Messenger of God." He said: "O uncle, pray four rakʿahs, reciting in each rakʿah the Opening of the Qurʾān (Fātiḥah) and a chapter (sūrah). When the recitation is concluded, say: 'God is Greater (Allāhu Akbar), praise be to God (al-Ḥamdu lillāh), and glory be to God (Subḥān Allāh)' fifteen times before you bow. Then bow and say it ten times, then raise your head and say it ten times, then prostrate and say it ten times, then raise your head and say it ten times before you stand. That is seventy-five in each rakʿah, and it is three hundred in four rakʿahs. If your sins were like the sand of ʿĀlij, God (Exalted is He) would forgive them for you." He said: "O Messenger of God, who can say this in a day?" He said: "If you cannot say it in a day, then say it in a Friday (week); if you cannot say it in a Friday, then say it in a month." He continued saying this to him until he said: "Say it in a year." Al-Tirmidhī said: This is a strange (gharīb) hadith.

I say: Imam Abū Bakr ibn al-ʿArabī said in his book "al-Aḥwadhī fī Sharḥ al-Tirmidhī": The hadith of Abū Rāfiʿ is weak (ḍaʿīf); it has no basis in authenticity (ṣiḥḥah) nor in goodness (ḥasan). He said: Al-Tirmidhī only mentioned it to draw attention to it, lest one be deceived by it. He said: The statement of Ibn al-Mubārak is not a proof (ḥujjah). This is the speech of Abū Bakr ibn al-ʿArabī.

Al-ʿUqaylī said: There is no hadith concerning the Prayer of Tasbīḥ that is established (yathbut). Abū al-Faraj ibn al-Jawzī mentioned the hadiths of the Prayer of Tasbīḥ and their chains, then declared all of them weak and clarified their weakness, as recorded in his book on fabricated narrations (al-Mawḍūʿāt).

It has reached us from the Imam, the Ḥāfiẓ, Abū al-Ḥasan al-Dāraquṭnī (may God have mercy on him) that he said: The most authentic thing concerning the virtues of the chapters (sūrahs) is the virtue of {«Qul Huwa Allāhu Aḥad»} (Say: He is God, the One), and the most authentic thing concerning the virtues of the prayers is the virtue of the Prayer of Tasbīḥ. I have mentioned this statement with its chain in the book "Ṭabaqāt al-Fuqahāʾ" in the biography of Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn ʿUmar al-Dāraquṭnī. This expression does not necessitate that the hadith of the Prayer of Tasbīḥ be authentic (ṣaḥīḥ), for they say: "This is the most authentic thing that has come in this chapter," even if it is weak, and their intent is that it is the most preponderant (arjaḥ) and the least weak.

I say: A group of the imams of our companions (the Shāfiʿīs) have explicitly stated the recommendation (istiḥbāb) of this Prayer of Tasbīḥ, among them Abū Muḥammad al-Baghawī and Abū al-Maḥāsin al-Rūyānī.

Al-Rūyānī said in his book "al-Baḥr" at the end of the "Book of Funerals" (Kitāb al-Janāʾiz): Know that the Prayer of Tasbīḥ is encouraged (muraghghab fīhā); it is recommended to habituate oneself to it at all times and not to be heedless of it. He said: Thus said ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak and a group of scholars.

He said: It was said to ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak: "If one errs in the Prayer of Tasbīḥ, does he glorify in the two prostrations of forgetfulness ten by ten?" He said: "No, for it is only three hundred glorifications." I have only mentioned this statement concerning the prostrations of forgetfulness, even though it has preceded, for a subtle benefit (fāʾidah laṭīfah): that when such an imam narrates this and does not reject it, it indicates that he agrees with it, thus increasing the number of those who hold this ruling. This al-Rūyānī is among the virtuous of our companions, the well-informed. And God knows best.

| Chapter on the Remembrances Related to the Alms-Tax (Zakāh)

God (Exalted is He) said: {«Khudh min amwālihim ṣadaqatan tuṭahhiruhum wa tuzakkīhim bihā wa ṣalli ʿalayhim»} (Take from their wealth a charity to purify them and sanctify them thereby, and pray upon them) [Al-Tawbah: 103].

| 535 —
We have related in the two Ṣaḥīḥs of al-Bukhārī and Muslim, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Awfā (may God be pleased with them both), who said: When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) was brought charity (ṣadaqah) by a people, he would say: "O God, pray upon them (Allāhumma ṣalli ʿalayhim)." Then Abū Awfā brought him his charity, and he said: "O God, pray upon the family of Abū Awfā (Allāhumma ṣalli ʿalā āli Abī Awfā)."

Al-Shāfiʿī and the companions (may God have mercy on them) said: The preferred choice (al-ikhtiyār) is that the one taking the zakāh should say to the one giving it: "May God reward you (ājaraka Allāh) for what you have given, and make it a purification (ṭuhūr) for you, and bless you in what you have retained." This supplication is recommended (mustaḥabb) for the one receiving the zakāh, whether he is the collector (al-sāʿī) or the poor recipient, and the supplication is not obligatory (wājib) according to the well-known (mashhūr) view of our school and the schools of others.

Some of our companions said: It is obligatory, due to the statement of al-Shāfiʿī: "It is incumbent upon the governor (al-wālī) to supplicate for him," and his evidence is the apparent command (ẓāhir al-amr) in the verse.

The scholars said: It is not recommended to say in the supplication: "O God, pray upon so-and-so (Allāhumma ṣalli ʿalā fulān)." The intent of His statement (Exalted is He): {«Wa ṣalli ʿalayhim»} (and pray upon them) is: supplicate for them (udʿu lahum).

As for the statement of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him): "O God, pray upon them (Allāhumma ṣalli ʿalayhim)," this is because the term prayer (ṣalāh) is exclusively specific to him, so he may address with it whomever he wishes, unlike us.

They said: Just as one does not say "Muḥammad, Exalted and Majestic (ʿazza wa jalla)" even though he is mighty and glorious, likewise one does not say "Abū Bakr, or ʿAlī, peace and blessings be upon him (ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam)," but rather one says: "May God be pleased with him (raḍiya Allāhu ʿanhu)," or "May the pleasure of God be upon him (riḍwān Allāhu ʿalayhi)," and similar expressions. If one were to say "peace and blessings be upon him (ṣallā Allāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam)," the correct view, upon which is the majority of our companions, is that it is disliked (makrūh) with a dislike of purification (karāhah tanzīh).

Some of them said: It is contrary to what is more proper (khilāf al-awlā), and it is not said to be disliked (makrūh).

Some of them said: It is not permissible (lā yajūz), and its apparent meaning is prohibition (taḥrīm). Likewise, it is not appropriate for other than the prophets to say "upon him be peace (ʿalayhi al-salām)" or similar, except when it is an address (khitāb) or a response (jawāb), for initiating the greeting (salām) is a Sunnah, and returning it is obligatory (wājib). Then all of this concerns prayer (ṣalāh) and greeting (salām) upon non-prophets when intended independently.

As for when it is made subordinate (tabaʿ), it is permissible without disagreement, so one says: "O God, pray upon Muḥammad and upon his family (ālihi), his companions (aṣḥābihi), his wives (azwājihi), his descendants (dhurriyyatihi), and his followers (atbāʿihi)," because the predecessors (al-salaf) did not refrain from this; rather, we have been commanded to do so in the tashahhud and elsewhere, unlike praying upon him independently. I have already mentioned this chapter in detail in the "Book of Prayer upon the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him)."

| Section (Faṣl):
Know that the intention (niyyah) for the zakāh is obligatory (wājibah), and its intention is made in the heart, like other acts of worship. It is recommended to combine with it verbal utterance (al-talfuẓ) by the tongue, as in other acts of worship. If one confines himself to the utterance of the tongue without the intention of the heart, there is disagreement (khilāf) concerning its validity.

The most correct view (al-aṣaḥḥ) is that it is not valid. It is not obligatory upon the one giving the zakāh, when he intends, to say along with that: "This is zakāh." Rather, it suffices him to hand it over to one who is among its eligible recipients (ahluhā). If he were to utter that, it would not harm him. And God knows best.

chapters.title_en: Section 69 — On Supplications for the Giver of Alms, the Seer of the New Moon, the Fasting Person, and the Night of Decree
chapters.arabic_text:
أعلم.
# [فصل] :
# يستحب لمن دفع زكاة، أو صدقة، أو نذرا، أو كفارة ونحو ذلك أن يقول: ربنا

تقبل منا إنك أنت السميع العليم، قد أخبر الله سبحانه وتعالى بذلك عن

إبراهيم وإسماعيل صلى الله عليهما وسلم، وعن امرأة عمران.

| كتاب أذكار الصيام

| (باب ما يقوله  إذا رأى الهلال، وما يقول إذا رأى القمر)

| 536 - 
# روينا في " مسند الدارمي " وكتاب الترمذي، عن طلحة بن عبيد الله رضي الله

عنه، أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا رأى الهلال قال: " اللهم أهله

علينا باليمن والإيمان والسلامة والإسلام ربي وربك الله " قال الترمذي:

حديث حسن.

| 537 - 
# وروينا في " مسند الدارمي " عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما، قال: كان رسول

الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا رأى الهلال قال: " الله أكبر، اللهم أهله

علينا بالأمن والإيمان والسلامة والإسلام، والتوفيق لما تحب وترضى، ربنا

وربك الله ".

| 538 - 
# وروينا في " سنن أبي داود " في " كتاب الأدب " عن قتادة، أنه بلغه، أن

نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا رأى الهلال قال: " هلال خير ورشد،

هلال خير ورشد، هلال خير ورشد، آمنت بالله الذي خلقك "، ثلاث مرات، ثم

يقول: " الحمد لله الذي ذهب بشهر كذا وجاء بشهر كذا ".
# وفي رواية عن قتادة " أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا رأى الهلال

صرف وجهه عنه " هكذا رواهما أبو داود مرسلين.
# وفي بعض نسخ أبي داود، قال أبو داود: ليس في هذا الباب عن النبي صلى الله

عليه وسلم حديث مسند صحيح (1) .

| 539 - 
# ورويناه في كتاب ابن السني، عن أبي سعيد الخدري، عن رسول الله صلى الله

عليه وسلم.

| 540 - 
# وأما رؤية القمر، فروينا في كتاب ابن السني، عن عائشة رضي الله عنها

# قالت: أخذ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بيدي، فإذا القمر حين طلع فقال:

" تعوذي بالله من شر هذا الغاسق (1) إذا وقب " (2) .

| 541 - 
# وروينا في " حلية الأولياء " بإسناد فيه ضعف، عن زياد النميري، عن أنس

رضي الله عنه، قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا دخل رجب قال: "

اللهم بارك لنا في رجب وشعبان وبلغنا رمضان ".
# ورويناه أيضا في كتاب ابن السني بزيادة (3) .

| (باب الأذكار المستحبة في الصوم)
# يستحب أن يجمع في نية الصوم بين القلب واللسان، كما قلنا في غيره من

العبادات، فإن اقتصر على  القلب كفاه، وإن اقتصر على اللسان لم يجزئه بلا

خلاف، والسنة إذا شتمه غيره، أو تسافه عليه في حال صومه أن يقول: " إني

صائم إني صائم " مرتين أو أكثر.

| 542 - 
# روينا في " صحيحي البخاري ومسلم " عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه، أن رسول

الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " الصيام جنة، فإذا صام أحدكم فلا يرفث ولا

يجهل، وإن امرؤ قاتله أو شاتمه فليقل: إني صائم، إني صائم، مرتين ".
# قلت: قيل: إنه يقول بلسانه، ويسمع الذي شاتمه لعله ينزجر، وقيل: يقوله

بقلبه لينكف عن المسافهة، ويحافظ على صيانة صومه، والأول أظهر.
# ومعنى شاتمه.
# شتمه متعرضا لمشاتمته، والله أعلم.

| 534 - 
# وروينا في كتابي الترمذي وابن ماجه، عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه، قال: قال

رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " ثلاثة لا ترد دعوتهم: الصائم حتى يفطر،

والإمام العادل، ودعوة المظلوم " قال الترمذي: حديث حسن. 
# قلت: هكذا الرواية " حتى " بالتاء المثناة فوق (1) .

| (باب ما يقول عند الإفطار)

| 544 - 
# روينا في سنن أبي داود، والنسائي، عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما، قال: كان

النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أفطر قال: " ذهب الظمأ، وابتلت العروق، وثبت

الأجر إن شاء الله تعالى " (2) .
# قلت: الظمأ مهموز الآخر مقصور: وهو العطش.
# قال الله تعالى: (ذلك بأنهم لا يصيبهم ظمأ) [التوبة: 120] وإنما ذكرت هذا

وإن كان ظاهرا، لأني رأيت من اشتبه عليه فتوهمه ممدودا.

| 545 - 
# وروينا في سنن أبي داود، عن معاذ بن زهرة، أنه بلغه، أن النبي صلى الله

عليه وسلم كان إذا أفطر قال: " اللهم لك صمت، وعلى رزقك أفطرت " هكذا رواه

مرسلا (3) .

| 546 - 
# وروينا في كتاب ابن السني، عن معاذ بن زهرة، قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله

عليه وسلم إذا أفطر قال: " الحمد لله الذي أعانني فصمت، ورزقني فأفطرت "

(4) .

| 547 - 
# وروينا في كتاب ابن السني عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما، قال: كان النبي

صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أفطر قال: " اللهم لك صمنا، وعلى رزقك أفطرنا،

فتقبل منا إنك أنت السميع  العليم " (5) .

| 548 - 
# وروينا في كتابي ابن ماجه، وابن السني، عن عبد الله بن أبي مليكة، عن عبد

الله بن عمرو بن العاص رضي الله عنهما، قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه

وسلم يقول: " إن للصائم عند فطره لدعوة ما ترد " قال ابن أبي مليكة: سمعت

عبد الله بن عمرو إذا أفطر
# يقول: " اللهم إني أسألك برحمتك التي وسعت كل شئ أن تغفر لي " (6) .

| (باب ما يقول إذا أفطر عند قوم)

| 549 - 
# روينا في سنن أبي داود وغيره بالإسناد الصحيح (1) ، عن أنس رضي الله عنه،

أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم جاء إلى سعد بن عبادة، فجاء بخبز وزيت، وهو

كذلك في نسخ الأذكار، ولكنه تصحيف، والصحيح أنه جاء بخبز وزبيب.
# فأكل، ثم قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: أفطر عندكم الصائمون، وأكل

طعامكم الأبرار وصلت عليكم الملائكة ".

| 550 - 
# وروينا في كتاب ابن السني عن أنس قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا

أفطر عند قوم دعا لهم فقال: " أفطر عندكم الصائمون ... " إلى آخره (2) .

| (باب ما يدعو به إذا صادف ليلة القدر)

| 551 - 
# روينا بالأسانيد الصحيحة في كتب الترمذي والنسائي وابن ماجه وغيرها عن
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To accept, receive, meet face-to-face; core sense of drawing near and taking in.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, 'acceptance (qabūl)' of an act by Allah denotes His turning to it with mercy and reward, distinct from mere 'recording (kitābah)'.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: physical reception; metaphorical (majāz): divine approval and reward for obedience.
- Root: ه-ل-ل (h-l-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The new moon (hilāl) — from 'to appear, to shine'; also 'to raise the voice' in talbiyah.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The crescent as a sign of appointed times (mawāqīt) for worship, linking cosmic order to divine law.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: the visible crescent; metaphorical: the advent of a blessed time.
- Root: ص-و-م (s-w-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To abstain, to refrain; originally from 'to be still/quiet' (as in the Quranic Maryam's vow).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Fasting (ṣawm) as comprehensive abstinence from appetites, a shield (junnah) against sin.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: abstention; metaphorical: guarding the tongue and limbs from transgression.
- Root: غ-س-ق (gh-s-q)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Intense darkness, the onset of night; also 'to overflow' (as in a wound).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The 'ghāsiq' in the Quranic verse refers to the moon when eclipsed or the night when dark — a time of hidden evil.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: the darkening; metaphorical: any harmful thing that emerges in darkness.
- Sībawayh Rule: 'Conditional and Command Sequence' (al-sharṭ wa al-jawāb) — In the hadith "If one of you fasts, let him not utter obscenity," the imperative (fa-lā yarfuth) is the apodosis of a conditional clause, indicating a binding obligation of restraint.
chapters.translation:
Know that it is recommended (mustaḥabb) for one who has paid the obligatory alms (zakāh), a voluntary charity (ṣadaqah), a vow (nadhr), an expiation (kaffārah), or the like, to say: "Our Lord, accept from us; indeed, You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing." Allah, Glorified and Exalted, has informed us of this from the words of Abraham and Ishmael (peace be upon them both), and from the wife of ʿImrān.

| The Book of Remembrances for Fasting

| (Chapter: What One Says Upon Seeing the New Moon, and What One Says Upon Seeing the Moon)

| 536 — We have related in the "Musnad of al-Dārimī" and the book of al-Tirmidhī, from Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbayd Allāh (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Prophet (peace be upon him), when he saw the new moon, said: "O Allah, bring it forth upon us with blessing (yumn), faith (īmān), safety (salāmah), and Islam (islām). My Lord and your Lord is Allah." Al-Tirmidhī said: A good (ḥasan) hadith.

| 537 — And we have related in the "Musnad of al-Dārimī" from Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), when he saw the new moon, said: "Allah is the Greatest (Allāhu akbar). O Allah, bring it forth upon us with security (amn), faith (īmān), safety (salāmah), and Islam (islām), and with success (tawfīq) for what You love and are pleased with. My Lord and your Lord is Allah."

| 538 — And we have related in the "Sunan of Abū Dāwūd" in the "Book of Etiquette" from Qatādah, that it reached him that the Prophet of Allah (peace be upon him), when he saw the new moon, said: "A crescent of goodness and guidance, a crescent of goodness and guidance, a crescent of goodness and guidance. I have believed in Allah who created you" — three times. Then he would say: "Praise be to Allah who has taken away such-and-such a month and brought such-and-such a month." And in another narration from Qatādah: "That the Prophet (peace be upon him), when he saw the new moon, turned his face away from it." Abū Dāwūd related both of these as disconnected (mursal) traditions. And in some copies of Abū Dāwūd, Abū Dāwūd said: "There is no sound connected (musnad) hadith from the Prophet (peace be upon him) on this chapter."

| 539 — And we have related it in the book of Ibn al-Sunnī, from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him).

| 540 — As for seeing the moon, we have related in the book of Ibn al-Sunnī, from ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) took my hand, and behold, the moon had just risen. He said: "Seek refuge with Allah from the evil of this darkening one (al-ghāsiq) when it sets" {«...»} (Quran 113:3).

| 541 — And we have related in the "Ḥilyat al-Awliyāʾ" with a chain containing weakness, from Ziyād al-Numayrī, from Anas (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), when Rajab entered, said: "O Allah, bless us in Rajab and Shaʿbān, and convey us to Ramaḍān." And we have also related it in the book of Ibn al-Sunnī with an addition.

| (Chapter: The Recommended Remembrances in Fasting)

It is recommended to combine in the intention (niyyah) for fasting both the heart and the tongue, as we have stated regarding other acts of worship. If one confines himself to the heart, it suffices him; but if he confines himself to the tongue, it does not suffice him, without disagreement. The Sunnah, when another person insults him or behaves foolishly toward him during his fast, is to say: "I am fasting, I am fasting" — twice or more.

| 542 — We have related in the two Ṣaḥīḥs of al-Bukhārī and Muslim, from Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Fasting is a shield (junnah). So when one of you fasts, let him not utter obscenity (rafath) nor act ignorantly. And if a man fights him or insults him, let him say: 'I am fasting, I am fasting' — twice." I say: It has been said that he says it with his tongue, and the one who insulted him hears it, perhaps he will be deterred. And it has been said that he says it in his heart, to restrain himself from foolishness and to preserve the sanctity of his fast. The first is more apparent (aẓhar). And the meaning of "insulted him" (shātamahu): he reviled him, exposing himself to mutual reviling. And Allah knows best.

| 534 — And we have related in the two books of al-Tirmidhī and Ibn Mājah, from Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Three whose supplication is not rejected: the fasting person until he breaks his fast, the just ruler (imām ʿādil), and the supplication of the oppressed (maẓlūm)." Al-Tirmidhī said: A good (ḥasan) hadith. I say: Thus is the narration — "until" (ḥattā) with a tāʾ with two dots above.

| (Chapter: What One Says Upon Breaking the Fast)

| 544 — We have related in the "Sunan of Abū Dāwūd" and al-Nasāʾī, from Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him), when he broke his fast, said: "The thirst has gone, the veins have become moist, and the reward is established, if Allah wills." I say: "Al-ẓamaʾ" (thirst) is with a hamzah at the end and is shortened (maqṣūr): it is thirst. Allah the Exalted said: {«...»} (Quran 9:120) — "That is because they are not afflicted by thirst." I have only mentioned this, although it is apparent, because I have seen one for whom it was ambiguous, and he imagined it to be lengthened (mamdūd).

| 545 — And we have related in the "Sunan of Abū Dāwūd," from Muʿādh ibn Zuhrah, that it reached him that the Prophet (peace be upon him), when he broke his fast, said: "O Allah, for You I have fasted, and upon Your provision I have broken my fast." Thus he related it as disconnected (mursal).

| 546 — And we have related in the book of Ibn al-Sunnī, from Muʿādh ibn Zuhrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), when he broke his fast, said: "Praise be to Allah who aided me, so I fasted, and provided for me, so I broke my fast."

| 547 — And we have related in the book of Ibn al-Sunnī, from Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him), when he broke his fast, said: "O Allah, for You we have fasted, and upon Your provision we have broken our fast. So accept from us; indeed, You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing."

| 548 — And we have related in the two books of Ibn Mājah and Ibn al-Sunnī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Mulaykah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) say: "Indeed, for the fasting person, at the time of his breaking his fast, there is a supplication that is not rejected." Ibn Abī Mulaykah said: I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, when he broke his fast, say: "O Allah, I ask You by Your mercy which encompasses all things, that You forgive me."

| (Chapter: What One Says When Breaking the Fast at a People's Gathering)

| 549 — We have related in the "Sunan of Abū Dāwūd" and others with a sound chain (isnād ṣaḥīḥ), from Anas (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Prophet (peace be upon him) came to Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah, and he brought bread and oil — and thus it is in the copies of the "Adhkār," but it is a scribal error (taṣḥīf); the correct version is that he brought bread and raisins. He ate, then the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "The fasting people have broken their fast with you, the righteous have eaten your food, and the angels have prayed for blessings upon you."

| 550 — And we have related in the book of Ibn al-Sunnī, from Anas, who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him), when he broke his fast at a people's gathering, supplicated for them and said: "The fasting people have broken their fast with you..." to the end of it.

| (Chapter: What One Supplicates With When He Encounters the Night of Decree)

| 551 — We have related with sound chains (asānīd ṣaḥīḥah) in the books of al-Tirmidhī, al-Nasāʾī, Ibn Mājah, and others, from...

chapters.title_en: Section 70 — Supplications for Laylat al-Qadr, Iʿtikāf, and the Rites of Hajj
chapters.arabic_text:
عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت: قلت: يارسول الله إن علمت ليلة القدر ما أقول

فيها؟ قال: " قولي: اللهم إنك عفو تحب العفو فاعف عني " قال الترمذي: حديث

حسن صحيح.
# قال أصحابنا رحمهم الله: يستحب أن يكثر فيها من هذا الدعاء، ويستحب قراءة

القرآن وسائر الأذكار والدعوات المستحبة في المواطن الشريفة، وقد سبق

بيانها مجموعة ومفرقة.
# قال الشافعي رحمه الله: أستحب أن يكون اجتهاده في يومها كاجتهاده في
# ليلتها، هذا نصه، ويستحب أن يكثر فيها من الدعوات بمهمات المسلمين، فهذا

شعار الصالحين وعباد الله العارفين، وبالله التوفيق.

| (باب الأذكار في الاعتكاف)
# يستحب أن يكثر فيه من تلاوة القرآن وغيره من الأذكار.

| كتاب أذكار الحج
# اعلم أن أذكار الحج ودعواته كثيرة لا تنحصر، ولكن نشير إلى المهم من

مقاصدها، والأذكار التي فيها على ضربين: أذكار في سفره،  وأذكار في نفس

الحج.
# فأما التي في سفره، فنؤخرها لنذكرها في أذكار الأسفار إن شاء الله تعالى.
# وأما التي في نفس الحج فنذكرها على ترتيب عمل الحج إن شاء الله تعالى،

وأحذف الأدلة والأحاديث في 
# أكثرها خوفا من طول الكتاب، وحصول السآمة على مطالعه، فإن هذا الباب طويل

جدا، فلهذا أسلك فيه الاختصار إن شاء الله تعالى.
# فأول ذلك: إذا أراد الإحرام اغتسل وتوضأ ولبس إزاره ورداءه (1) ، وقد

قدمنا ما يقوله المتوضئ والمغتسل، وما يقول إذا لبس الثوب، ثم يصلي ركعتين،

وتقدمت أذكار الصلاة، ويستحب أن يقرأ في الركعة الأولى بعد الفاتحة (قل يا

أيها الكافرون) وفي الثانية (قل هو الله أحد) فإذا فرغ من الصلاة استحب أن

يدعو بما شاء، وتقدم ذكر جمل من الدعوات والأذكار خلف الصلاة، فإذا أراد

الإحرام نواه بقلبه.
# ويستحب أن يساعد بلسانه قلبه (2) ، فيقول: نويت الحج وأحرمت به لله عز

وجل، لبيك اللهم لبيك ... إلى آخر التلبية.
# والواجب نية القلب، واللفظ سنة، فلو اقتصر على القلب أجزأه، ولو اقتصر

على اللسان لم يجزئه.
# قال الإمام أبو الفتح سليم بن أيوب الرازي: لو قال يعني بعد هذا: اللهم

لك أحرم نفسي وشعري وبشري ولحمي ودمي، كان حسنا (3) .
# وقال غيره: يقول أيضا: اللهم إني نويت الحج فأعني عليه وتقبله مني، ويلبي

فيقول:

| 552 - 
# لبيك اللهم لبيك، لبيك لا شريك لك لبيك، إن الحمد والنعمة لك والملك، لا

شريك لك، هذه تلبية رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، ويستحب أن يقول في أول

تلبية يلبيها: لبيك اللهم بحجة، إن كان أحرم بحجة، أو لبيك بعمرة، إن كان

أحرم بها، ولا يعيد ذكر الحج والعمرة فيما يأتي بعد ذلك من التلبية على

المذهب الصحيح المختار.
# واعلم أن التلبية سنة لو تركها صح حجه وعمرته ولا شئ عليه، لكن فاتته

الفضيلة العظيمة والاقتداء برسول الله صلى الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، هذا هو

الصحيح من مذهبنا ومذهب جماهير العلماء، وقد أوجبها بعض أصحابنا، واشترطها

لصحة الحج بعضهم، والصواب الأول،  لكن 
# تستحب المحافظة عليها للاقتداء برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، وللخروج

من الخلاف، والله أعلم.
# وإذا أحرم عن غيره قال: نويت الحج وأحرمت به لله تعالى عن فلان، لبيك

اللهم
# عن فلان ... إلى آخر ما يقوله من يحرم عن نفسه.
# [فصل] :
# ويستحب أن يصلي على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بعد التلبية، وأن يدعو

لنفسه ولمن أراد بأمور الآخرة والدنيا، ويسأل الله تعالى رضوانه والجنة،

ويستعيذ به من النار، ويستحب الإكثار من التلبية، ويستحب ذلك في كل حال

قائما، وقاعدا، وماشيا، وراكبا، ومضطجعا، ونازلا، وسائرا، ومحدثا، وجنبا،

وحائضا، وعند تجدد الأحوال وتغايرها زمانا ومكانا، وغير ذلك، كإقبال الليل

والنهار، وعند الأسحار، واجتماع الرفاق، وعند القيام والقعود، والصعود

والهبوط، والركوب والنزول، وأدبار الصلوات، وفي المساجد كلها، والأصح أنه

لا يلبي في حال الطواف والسعي، لأن لهما أذكارا مخصوصة.
# ويستحب أن يرفع صوته بالتلبية بحيث لا يشق عليه، وليس للمرأة رفع الصوت،

لأن صوتها يخاف الافتتان به.
# ويستحب أن يكرر التلبية كل مرة ثلاث مرات فأكثر، ويأتي بها متوالية لا

يقطعها بكلام لا غيره.
# وإن سلم عليه إنسان رد السلام، ويكره السلام عليه في هذه الحالة.

| 553 - 
# وإذا رأى شيئا فأعجبه قال: لبيك إن العيش عيش الآخرة، اقتداء برسول الله

صلى الله عليه وسلم (1) .
# واعلم أن التلبية لا تزال مستحبة حتى يرمي جمرة العقبة يوم النحر أو يطوف

طواف الإفاضة إن قدمه عليها، فإذا بدأ بواحد منهما قطع التلبية مع أول

شروعه فيه، واشتغل بالتكبير.
# قال الإمام الشافعي رحمه الله: ويلبي المعتمر حتى يستلم الركن.
# [فصل] :
# فإذا وصل المحرم إلى حرم مكة زاده الله شرفا، أستحب له أن يقول: اللهم

# هذا حرمك وأمنك فحرمني على النار، وأمني من عذابك يوم تبعث عبادك،

واجعلني من أوليائك وأهل طاعتك، ويدعو بما أحب (1) .
# [فصل] :
# فإذا دخل مكة ووقع بصره على الكعبة ووصل المسجد، استحب له أن يرفع يديه

ويدعو، فقد جاء أنه يستجاب دعاء المسلم عند رؤية الكعبة، ويقول: اللهم زد

هذا البيت  تشريفا وتعظيما وتكريما ومهابة، وزد من شرفه وكرمه ممن حجه أو

اعتمره تشريفا وتكريما وتعظيما وبرا.
# ويقول: اللهم أنت السلام ومنك السلام، حينا ربنا بالسلام، ثم يدعو بما

شاء من خيرات الآخرة والدنيا، ويقول عند دخول المسجد ما قدمناه في أول

الكتاب في جميع المساجد.

| فصل في أذكار الطواف
# يستحب أن يقول عند استلام الحجر الأسود وعند ابتداء الطواف أيضا: بسم

الله والله أكبر، اللهم إيمانا بك وتصديقا بكتابك، ووفاء بعهدك واتباعا
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ف-و (ʿ-f-w)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To pardon, to efface, to leave unpunished; the root denotes obliteration of a fault as if it never existed.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Divine ʿAfw is the erasure of sin entirely, distinct from maghfirah which covers; it implies the removal of the very trace of transgression.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally of God's absolute pardon; metaphorically of a man's magnanimity in overlooking an offense.
- Root: ن-و-ي (n-w-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Intent, purpose, resolution of the heart; the core meaning is direction of the will toward an aim.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In worship, niyyah is the distinguishing factor that elevates a mere act to an act of obedience; it is the seat of sincerity (ikhlāṣ).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal in the heart; the verbal utterance is a metaphorical extension, not the reality of intention.
- Root: ل-ب-ي (l-b-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: From labba bi-l-makān, to remain, to abide; the talbiyah expresses perpetual readiness and presence in response to a call.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The pilgrim's response to God's summons, signifying unwavering compliance and the abandonment of all other allegiances.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literally "I am here"; rhetorically, it is the answer of the servant to the divine command, repeated for emphasis and devotion.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ) — The Prophet's instruction "If you know Laylat al-Qadr, what should I say?" is answered by a direct imperative (qūlī), showing that the response to a conditional inquiry is a command, not a narrative.
chapters.translation:
I say: ʿĀʾishah, may God be pleased with her, said: "I said: O Messenger of God, if I know which night is Laylat al-Qadr, what should I say in it?" He said: "Say: O God, You are Pardoning (ʿAfuww), You love pardon, so pardon me." Al-Tirmidhī said: A good and authentic hadith (ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ).

Our companions, may God have mercy on them, said: It is recommended (mustaḥabb) to multiply this supplication during that night, and it is recommended to recite the Qurʾān and all the other remembrances (adhkār) and supplications that are recommended in noble stations. Their exposition has already preceded, both collectively and individually.

Al-Shāfiʿī, may God have mercy on him, said: I recommend that one's striving (ijtihād) during its day be like one's striving during its night. This is his very text (naṣṣ). And it is recommended to multiply therein supplications concerning the important affairs of the Muslims, for this is the distinguishing mark (shiʿār) of the righteous and of God's knowing servants. And with God is success (tawfīq).

| (Chapter on Remembrances during Iʿtikāf)

It is recommended to multiply therein the recitation of the Qurʾān and other remembrances.

| The Book of Hajj Remembrances

Know that the remembrances of Hajj and its supplications are numerous and cannot be encompassed. But we shall point to the important ones among their purposes. The remembrances contained therein are of two kinds: remembrances during one's journey, and remembrances during the Hajj itself.

As for those during the journey, we shall defer them and mention them in the remembrances of travels, God willing.

As for those during the Hajj itself, we shall mention them according to the order of the Hajj rites, God willing. And I shall omit the evidences and hadiths in most of them, out of fear of the book's length and the onset of weariness upon its reader, for this chapter is extremely long. For this reason, I pursue brevity therein, God willing.

The first of that: When one intends to enter the state of iḥrām, he performs the major ablution (ghusl), performs the minor ablution (wuḍūʾ), and dons his waist-wrapper (izār) and cloak (ridāʾ). We have already presented what the one performing ablution and the one performing ghusl say, and what one says when donning a garment. Then he prays two units (rakʿatān). The remembrances of prayer have already preceded. It is recommended to recite in the first unit after the Fātiḥah {«قُلْ يَا أَيُّهَا الْكَافِرُونَ»} ("Say: O disbelievers") and in the second {«قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ»} ("Say: He is God, the One"). When he finishes the prayer, it is recommended that he supplicate with whatever he wishes. A collection of supplications and remembrances following the prayer has already been mentioned.

When he intends to enter iḥrām, he resolves it in his heart. It is recommended that his tongue assist his heart, and he says: "I intend the Hajj and I enter iḥrām for it for God, Mighty and Majestic. Here I am, O God, here I am (labbayka Allāhumma labbayk)..." to the end of the talbiyah.

The obligatory (wājib) is the intention of the heart, and the utterance is Sunnah. If one confines himself to the heart, it suffices him. If one confines himself to the tongue, it does not suffice him.

Imam Abū al-Fatḥ Sulaym ibn Ayyūb al-Rāzī said: If one says after this — meaning: "O God, to You I consecrate my soul, my hair, my skin, my flesh, and my blood" — it is good.

Another said: One also says: "O God, I have intended the Hajj, so assist me in it and accept it from me." Then he raises his voice in the talbiyah, saying:

| 552 —

"Here I am, O God, here I am. Here I am, You have no partner, here I am. Indeed, all praise, grace, and sovereignty are Yours. You have no partner." This is the talbiyah of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. It is recommended that one say at the first talbiyah he utters: "Here I am, O God, for a Hajj" if he has entered iḥrām for Hajj, or "Here I am for an ʿUmrah" if he has entered iḥrām for it. He does not repeat the mention of Hajj or ʿUmrah in what follows thereafter of the talbiyah, according to the sound and chosen position (al-madhhab al-ṣaḥīḥ al-mukhtār).

Know that the talbiyah is Sunnah. If one abandons it, his Hajj and ʿUmrah are valid and nothing is due upon him, but he has missed the great virtue and the emulation of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. This is the sound position in our school (madhhab) and the position of the majority of scholars (jumhūr al-ʿulamāʾ). Some of our companions made it obligatory, and some made it a condition for the validity of Hajj. The correct view is the first. However, it is recommended to maintain it for emulation of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to exit from disagreement (khilāf). And God knows best.

If one enters iḥrām on behalf of another, he says: "I intend the Hajj and I enter iḥrām for it for God, Most High, on behalf of so-and-so. Here I am, O God, on behalf of so-and-so..." to the end of what the one who enters iḥrām for himself says.

[Section]:

It is recommended to send blessings upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, after the talbiyah, and to supplicate for oneself and for whomever one wishes regarding the affairs of the Hereafter and this world. One asks God, Most High, for His good pleasure (riḍwān) and Paradise, and seeks refuge with Him from the Fire. It is recommended to multiply the talbiyah, and this is recommended in every state: standing, sitting, walking, riding, lying down, descending, traveling, in a state of minor impurity (ḥadath), in major impurity (janābah), and during menstruation (ḥayḍ). It is also recommended at the renewal of states and their variation in time and place, and other occasions, such as the coming of night and day, at the dawn hours (asḥār), at the gathering of companions, upon standing and sitting, ascending and descending, mounting and dismounting, after the obligatory prayers, and in all mosques. The soundest view (al-aṣaḥḥ) is that one does not recite the talbiyah during the ṭawāf and the saʿy, for they have their own specific remembrances.

It is recommended to raise one's voice in the talbiyah to a degree that does not cause hardship upon oneself. A woman does not raise her voice, for there is fear of temptation (fitnah) in her voice.

It is recommended to repeat the talbiyah three times or more on each occasion, and to utter it consecutively, not interrupting it with speech or anything else. If someone greets him with salām, he returns the greeting. It is disliked (makrūh) to greet him in this state.

| 553 —

If he sees something that pleases him, he says: "Here I am, indeed, true life is the life of the Hereafter," in emulation of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

Know that the talbiyah remains recommended until one casts the pebbles at the Jamrat al-ʿAqabah on the Day of Sacrifice (yawm al-naḥr), or performs the ṭawāf al-ifāḍah if he has brought it forward before it. If he begins with either of the two, he ceases the talbiyah with the commencement of that act, and occupies himself with the takbīr.

Imam al-Shāfiʿī, may God have mercy on him, said: The one performing ʿUmrah continues the talbiyah until he touches the Corner (al-rukn).

[Section]:

When the muḥrim arrives at the sacred precinct of Mecca — may God increase it in honor — it is recommended for him to say: "O God, this is Your sacred sanctuary (ḥaram) and Your place of security, so make me forbidden to the Fire, and secure me from Your punishment on the Day You resurrect Your servants, and make me among Your friends (awliyāʾ) and the people of Your obedience." And he supplicates with whatever he loves.

[Section]:

When he enters Mecca and his sight falls upon the Kaʿbah and he reaches the Mosque, it is recommended for him to raise his hands and supplicate, for it has come that the supplication of a Muslim is answered upon seeing the Kaʿbah. He says: "O God, increase this House in honor, veneration, dignity, and awe, and increase those who honor it and venerate it — among those who perform Hajj to it or ʿUmrah — in honor, veneration, dignity, and righteousness."

And he says: "O God, You are Peace (Salām) and from You is peace. Make us live, our Lord, in peace." Then he supplicates with whatever he wishes of the good of the Hereafter and this world. And upon entering the Mosque, he says what we have presented at the beginning of the book regarding all mosques.

| Section on the Remembrances of Ṭawāf

It is recommended to say upon touching the Black Stone and also at the commencement of the ṭawāf: "In the name of God, and God is Greatest. O God, in faith in You, and in affirmation of Your Book, and in fulfillment of Your covenant, and in following the Sunnah of Your Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace."

chapters.title_en: Section 71 — Supplications During the Circumambulation (Ṭawāf), at the Multazam, the Ḥijr, and Within the Kaʿbah
chapters.arabic_text:
لسنة نبيك صلى الله عليه وسلم.
# ويستحب أن يكرر هذا الذكر عند محاذاة الحجر الأسود في كل طوفة، ويقول في

رمله في الأشواط الثلاثة: " اللهم اجعله حجا مبرورا وذنبا مغفورا، وسعيا

مشكورا " (2) .
# ويقول في الأربعة الباقية من أشواظا لطواف: " اللهم اغفر وارحم، واعف عما

تعلم وأنت الأعز الأكرم، اللهم ربنا آتنا في الدنيا حسنة وفي الآخرة حسنة

وقنا عذاب النار ".
# قال الشافعي رحمه الله: أحب ما يقال في الطواف: اللهم ربنا آتنا في

الدنيا 
# حسنة ... إلى آخره، قال: وأحب أن يقال في كله، ويستحب أن يدعو فيما بين

طوافه بما أحب من دين ودنيا، ولو دعا واحد وأمن جماعة فحسن.
# وحكي عن الحسن رحمه الله أن الدعاء يستجاب هنالك في خمسة عشر موضعا: في

الطواف، وعند الملتزم، وتحت الميزاب، وفي البيت، وعند زمزم، وعلى الصفا

والمروة، وفي المسعى، وخلف المقام، وفي عرفات، وفي المزدلفة، وفي منى، وعند

الجمرات الثلاث، فمحروم من لا يجتهد في الدعاء فيها.
# ومذهب الشافعي وجماهير أصحابه أنه يستحب قراءة القرآن في الطواف لأنه

موضع ذكر.
# وأفضل الذكر قراءة القرآن.
# واختار أبو عبد الله الحليمي من كبار أصحاب الشافعي أنه لا يستحب قراءة

القرآن فيه، والصحيح هو الأول.
# قال أصحابنا: والقراءة أفضل من الدعوات غير المأثورة، وأما المأثورة فهي

أفضل من القراءة على الصحيح.
# وقيل: القراءة أفضل منها.
# قال الشيخ أبو محمد الجويني رحمه الله: يستحب أن يقرأ في أيام الموسم

ختمة في طوافه فيعظم أجرها (1) ، والله أعلم.
# ويستحب إذا فرغ من الطواف ومن صلاة  ركعتي الطواف أن يدعو بما أحب، ومن

الدعاء المنقول فيه: اللهم أنا عبدك وابن عبدك أتيتك بذنوب كثيرة (2)

وأعمال سيئة وهذا مقام العائذ بك من النار فاغفر لي إنك أنت الغفور الرحيم

".

| فصل في الدعاء الملتزم
# ، وهو ما بين الكعبة والحجر الأسود: وقد قدمنا أنه يستجاب فيه الدعاء.
# ومن الدعوات المأثورة: " اللهم لك الحمد حمدا يوافي نعمك، ويكافئ مزيدك،

أحمدك بجميع محامدك ما علمت منها وما لم أعلم على جميع نعمك ما علمت منها

وما لم أعلم، وعلى كل حال، اللهم صل وسلم على محمد وعلى آل محمد، اللهم

أعذني من الشيطان الرجيم، وأعذني من كل سوء، وقنعني بما رزقتني وبارك لي

فيه، اللهم اجعلني من أكرم وفدك عليك، وألزمني سبيل الاستقامة حتى ألقاك يا

رب العالمين، ثم يدعو بما أحب (3) .

| [فصل] : في الدعاء في الحجر، 
# بكسر الحاء وإسكان الجيم، وهو محسوب من البيت.
# وقد قدمنا أنه يستجاب الدعاء فيه.
# ومن الدعاء المأثور فيه: يا رب أتيتك من شقة بعيدة مؤملا معروفك فأنلني

معروفا من معروفك تغنيني به عن معروف من سواك يا معروفا بالمعروف " (1) .

| فصل في الدعاء في البيت
# : وقد قدمنا أنه يستجاب الدعاء فيه.
# وروينا في كتاب النسائي عن أسامة بن زيد رضي الله عنهما " أن رسول الله

صلى الله عليه وسلم لما دخل البيت أتى ما استقبل من دبر الكعبة فوضع وجهه

وخده عليه، وحمد الله تعالى وأثنى عليه وسأله واستغفره، ثم انصرف إلى كل

ركن من أركان الكعبة، فاستقبله بالتكبير والتهليل والتسبيح والثناء على

الله عز وجل والمسألة، والاستغفار، ثم خرج " (2) .
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ط و ف (ṭ-w-f)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To go around, encircle; the act of circumambulating a sacred precinct.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ritual encircling of the Kaʿbah as an act of devotional obedience (ṭāʿah), symbolizing the soul's orientation toward the Divine Center.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical circling; metaphorical (majāz) for encompassing divine mercy in supplication.
- Root: ل ز م (l-z-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To cling, adhere, be inseparable; the Multazam as the place of clinging to the House of God.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Persistence in supplication (duʿāʾ) as spiritual adhesion to divine mercy.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical clinging; metaphorical for steadfastness (istiqāmah) in obedience.
- Root: ح ج ر (ḥ-j-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To forbid, enclose; the Ḥijr as the enclosed semicircular wall of the Kaʿbah.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The sacred enclosure counted as part of the House (bayt), a locus of answered prayer.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal architectural term; metaphorical for divine protection (iḥjār) from sin.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional-Answer Construction (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — The phrase "إذا فرغ... أن يدعو" employs a temporal conditional where the protasis governs the apodosis, requiring the subjunctive mood in the verb of supplication, as in classical periodic structure.
chapters.translation:
I say: It is recommended (yustaḥabbu) to repeat this remembrance when aligning with the Black Stone (al-Ḥajar al-Aswad) in every circuit (ṭawfah), and one says during the rapid pacing (ramal) in the first three circuits: "O Allah, make it an accepted pilgrimage (ḥajjan mabrūran), a forgiven sin (dhanban maghfūran), and a praiseworthy endeavor (saʿyan mashkūran)."

And one says in the remaining four circuits of the circumambulation: "O Allah, forgive and have mercy, and pardon what You know, for You are the Most Mighty, the Most Generous. O Allah, our Lord, give us in this world good, and in the Hereafter good, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire."

Al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah have mercy on him, said: The most beloved thing to be said during the circumambulation is: "O Allah, our Lord, give us in this world good..." to the end of the verse. He said: And I love that it be said throughout the entire ṭawāf. And it is recommended that one supplicate between his circuits with whatever he wishes of religious or worldly matters. And if one person supplicates and a group says 'Amen,' that is excellent.

It is narrated from al-Ḥasan, may Allah have mercy on him, that supplication is answered there in fifteen places: during the circumambulation, at the Multazam, beneath the water-spout (al-Mīzāb), inside the House (al-Bayt), at Zamzam, upon al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, in the course (al-Masʿā), behind the Station of Abraham (Maqām Ibrāhīm), at ʿArafāt, at Muzdalifah, at Minā, and at the three stone-pillars (al-Jamarāt). Deprived indeed is the one who does not strive earnestly in supplication in these places.

The school of al-Shāfiʿī and the majority of his companions holds that it is recommended to recite the Qurʾān during the circumambulation, because it is a place of remembrance (dhikr). And the most excellent form of remembrance is the recitation of the Qurʾān.

Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥalīmī, one of the leading companions of al-Shāfiʿī, chose the view that reciting the Qurʾān therein is not recommended. The correct view is the first one.

Our companions said: Recitation (of the Qurʾān) is more excellent than non-transmitted supplications (al-duʿawāt ghayr al-maʾthūrah). As for transmitted supplications (al-maʾthūrah), they are more excellent than recitation according to the correct view. And it was said: Recitation is more excellent than them.

The Shaykh Abū Muḥammad al-Juwaynī, may Allah have mercy on him, said: It is recommended that one recite a complete recitation (khatmah) of the Qurʾān during his circumambulation in the days of the season (mawsim), so that its reward is magnified. And Allah knows best.

It is recommended, when one finishes the circumambulation and the prayer of the two units (rakʿatān) of the ṭawāf, that he supplicate with whatever he wishes. Among the transmitted supplications therein is: "O Allah, I am Your servant, the son of Your servant. I have come to You with many sins and evil deeds, and this is the station of the one seeking refuge with You from the Fire. So forgive me, for You are the Oft-Forgiving, the Most Merciful."

SECTION ON SUPPLICATION AT THE MULTAZAM
It is the space between the Kaʿbah and the Black Stone. We have already mentioned that supplication therein is answered. Among the transmitted supplications: "O Allah, to You is all praise — a praise that befits Your blessings and equals Your abundant increase. I praise You with all Your praises, those I know and those I do not know, for all Your blessings, those I know and those I do not know, and in every state. O Allah, send blessings and peace upon Muḥammad and upon the family of Muḥammad. O Allah, protect me from the accursed Satan, and protect me from every evil, and make me content with what You have provided me, and bless me therein. O Allah, make me among the most honored of Your guests before You, and bind me to the path of uprightness (sabīl al-istiqāmah) until I meet You, O Lord of the worlds." Then he supplicates with whatever he wishes.

SECTION ON SUPPLICATION AT THE ḤIJR
With a kasrah on the ḥāʾ and a sukūn on the jīm — it is counted as part of the House (al-Bayt). We have already mentioned that supplication therein is answered. Among the transmitted supplications therein: "O Lord, I have come to You from a distant land, hoping for Your favor. So grant me a favor from Your favors, by which You enrich me from the favor of anyone other than You. O You who are known for beneficence (maʿrūf)."

SECTION ON SUPPLICATION INSIDE THE HOUSE (AL-BAYT)
We have already mentioned that supplication therein is answered. We have narrated in the book of al-Nasāʾī, on the authority of Usāmah ibn Zayd, may Allah be pleased with them both, that "the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when he entered the House, he came to what faced him of the back of the Kaʿbah, placed his face and cheek upon it, praised Allah Almighty, extolled Him, asked of Him, and sought His forgiveness. Then he turned to every corner of the Kaʿbah's corners, facing each with the takbīr, the tahlīl, the tasbīḥ, praise of Allah Almighty, supplication, and seeking forgiveness. Then he departed."

chapters.title_en: Section on the Remembrances of the Saʿy (Ritual Pacing), and the Supplications for Departure from Mecca to ʿArafāt
chapters.arabic_text:
# فصل في أذكار السعي: وقد تقدم أنه يستجاب الدعاء فيه، والسنة أن يطيل

القيام على الصفا، ويستقبل الكعبة، فيكبر ويدعو فيقول: الله أكبر، الله

أكبر، الله أكبر، ولله الحمد، الله أكبر على ما هدانا، والحمد لله على ما

أولانا، لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، له الملك وله الحمد يحيي ويميت،

بيده الخير، وهو على كل شئ قدير،
# لا إله إلا الله، أنجز  وعده، ونصر عبده، وهزم الأحزاب وحده، لا إله إلا

الله، ولا نعبد إلا إياه، مخلصين له الدين ولو كره الكافرون، اللهم إنك

قلت: ادعوني أستجب لكم، وإنك لا تخلف الميعاد، وإني أسألك كما هديتني

للإسلام أن لا تنزعه مني حتى تتوفاني وأنا مسلم ".
# ثم يدعو بخيرات الدنيا والآخرة، ويكرر هذا لذكر والدعاء ثلاث مرات، ولا

يلبي، وإذا وصل إلى المروة رقى عليها وقال الأذكار والدعوات التي قالها على

الصفا (3) .

| 555 - 
# وروينا عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما أنه كان يقول على الصفا: اللهم

# اعصمنا بدينك وطواعيتك وطواعية رسولك صلى الله عليه وسلم، وجنبنا حدودك،

اللهم اجعلنا نحبك ونحب ملائكتك وأنبياءك ورسلك، ونحب عبادك الصالحين،

اللهم حببنا إليك وإلى ملائكتك وإلى أنبيائك ورسلك، وإلى عبادك الصالحين،

اللهم يسرنا لليسرى، وجنبنا العسرى، واغفر لنا في الآخرة والأولى، واجعلنا

من أئمة المتقين.
# ويقول في ذهابه ورجوعه بين الصفا والمروة: رب اغفر وارحم وتجاوز عما تعلم

إنك أنت الأعز الأكرم، اللهم آتنا في الدنيا حسنة وفي الآخرة حسنة وقنا

عذاب النار (1) .

| ومن الأدعية المختارة في السعي وفي كل مكان

| 556 - 
# " اللهم يا مقلب القلوب ثبت قلبي على دينك ".

| 557 - 
# " اللهم إني أسألك موجبات رحمتك، وعزائم مغفرتك والسلامة من كل إثم،

والفوز بالجنة، والنجاة من النار ".

| 558 - 
# " اللهم إني أسألك الهدى والتقى والعفاف والغنى ".

| 559 - 
# " اللهم أعني على ذكرك وشكرك وحسن عبادتك ".

| 560 - 
# " اللهم إني أسألك من الخير كله ما علمت منه وما لم أعلم، وأعوذ بك من

الشر كله ما علمت منه وما لم أعلم، وأسألك الجنة وما قرب إليها من قول أو

عمل، وأعوذ بك من النار وما قرب إليها من قول أو عمل ".
# ولو قرأ القرآن كان أفضل.
# وينبغي أن يجمع بين هذه الأذكار والدعوات والقرآن، فإن أراد الاقتصار أتى

بالمهم.

# فصل في الأذكار التي يقولها في خروجه من مكة إلى عرفات: يستحب إذا خرج من

مكة متوجها إلى منى أن يقول: اللهم إياك أرجو، ولك أدعو، فبلغني صالح أملي،

واغفر لي  ذنوبي، وامنن علي بما مننت به على أهل طاعتك إنك على كل شئ قدير

(2) .
# وإذا سار من منى إلى عرفة استحب أن يقول: اللهم إليك توجهت، ووجهك

# الكريم أردت، فاجعل ذنبي مغفورا، وحجي مبرورا، وارحمني ولا تخيبني إنك

على كل شئ قدير (1) .
# ويلبي ويقرأ القرآن، ويكثر من سائر الأذكار والدعوات، ومن قوله: اللهم

آتنا في الدنيا حسنة وفي الآخرة حسنة وقنا عذاب النار.
chapters.anchors:
- Root: س-ع-ي (sa-ʿa-ya)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of exertion, striving, or rapid walking; in ritual context, the pacing between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Denotes purposeful endeavor in worship, distinct from mere locomotion; carries the nuance of devotional pursuit.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical striving; metaphorical (majāz) for spiritual earnestness in supplication.
- Root: د-ع-و (da-ʿa-wa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Calling, invoking, or summoning; the act of beseeching.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological terms, the servant’s humble petition to Allah, premised on His promise of response.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for vocal call; metaphorical for heartfelt reliance and entreaty.
- Root: ذ-ك-ر (dha-ka-ra)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Mention, remembrance, or recollection.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The conscious invocation of Allah, both verbal and inward, as a pillar of devotional practice.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for utterance; metaphorical for steadfast mindfulness of the Divine.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Conditional Clauses (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — For the phrase «ادعوني أستجب لكم», the imperative serves as the condition and the future verb as its apodosis, indicating a guaranteed response.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that it has preceded that supplication is answered during the Saʿy, and the Sunnah is to prolong the standing upon al-Ṣafā, facing the Kaʿbah, then to magnify (Allah) and supplicate, saying: “Allah is Greatest, Allah is Greatest, Allah is Greatest, and to Allah belongs all praise. Allah is Greatest for what He has guided us, and praise be to Allah for what He has bestowed upon us. There is no deity but Allah alone, with no partner; to Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs all praise; He gives life and causes death; in His hand is all good, and He is over all things Omnipotent. There is no deity but Allah; He fulfilled His promise, aided His servant, and alone defeated the confederates. There is no deity but Allah, and we worship none but Him, devoting religion sincerely to Him, even if the disbelievers detest it. O Allah, You have said: {«ادعوني أستجب لكم»} (“Call upon Me; I will respond to you”), and You do not break Your promise. I ask You, just as You guided me to Islam, not to strip it from me until You take me unto Yourself while I am a Muslim.” Then he supplicates for the good of this world and the Hereafter, and repeats this remembrance and supplication three times, and he does not perform the talbiyah. When he reaches al-Marwah, he ascends upon it and recites the remembrances and supplications he recited upon al-Ṣafā.
