- Root: أ-ن-س (ʾ-n-s)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Familiarity, sociability, companionship; the opposite of estrangement (waḥshah)
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The psychological comfort and intimacy that dispels solitude; used theologically for the soul's repose in divine remembrance
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of "finding comfort in company"; metaphorically extended to the purpose of greeting as a social bond
- Root: خ-ص-ص (kh-ṣ-ṣ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To single out, to distinguish, to allocate exclusively
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Particularization (takhṣīṣ) as opposed to generalization (taʿmīm); in legal theory, the specification of a general command
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal "cutting off" a portion; metaphorically, singling out individuals from a group
- Root: ر-د-د (r-d-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To return, to repel, to give back
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The obligatory response (radd) to a greeting as a reciprocal act of justice and courtesy
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal "turning back" something; metaphorically, the verbal reciprocation of salām
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause with Implied Protasis (al-sharṭ al-muḍmar) — The phrase "if he intended to reply to all of them" governs the legal consequence without requiring explicit repetition of the condition in each clause.
chapters.translation:
I say — and Allah grants success:

**Section:**
Al-Mutawallī said: When a man encounters a group and wishes to single out a portion of them with the greeting, this is disapproved (makrūh), because the very purpose of the greeting is mutual familiarity (muʾānasah) and affection (ulfah). In singling out some, there is estrangement (īḥāsh) for the rest, and perhaps it becomes a cause for enmity.

**Section:**
When one walks frequently through the marketplace or well-trodden streets and similar places where many encounters occur, the Chief Judge (Qāḍī al-Quḍāh) al-Māwardī mentioned that the greeting here is only given to some people and not others. He said: For if he greeted everyone he met, he would be occupied from every important matter, and he would depart from customary practice (al-ʿurf). He said: By this greeting, one intends only one of two things: either the acquisition of affection (iktisāb wudd), or the repulsion of something disliked (istidfāʿ makrūh).

**Section:**
Al-Mutawallī said: When a group greets a man, and he says, "And upon you be peace" (wa-ʿalaykum al-salām), intending to reply to all of them, the obligation of replying falls from him with respect to all of them — just as if he prayed over multiple funeral biers at once, the obligation of prayer over all of them is thereby discharged.

**Section:**
Al-Māwardī said: When a person enters upon a small group whom a single greeting encompasses, he limits himself to one greeting directed to all of them. Anything beyond that, in singling out some of them, is merely courteous embellishment (adab). It suffices that one of them replies; whoever among them adds more, that is adab. He said: But if it is a large gathering in which a single greeting does not spread, such as a mosque or a crowded assembly, then the sunnah of greeting is that the entrant initiates it at his first entry when he beholds the people. He thereby fulfills the sunnah of greeting with respect to all who hear him, and the obligation of sufficiency (farḍ kifāyah) of replying falls upon all who hear him. If he intends to sit among them, the sunnah of greeting drops from him with respect to those remaining whom he did not reach with his greeting. But if he intends to sit among those further away who did not hear his earlier greeting, then there are two positions (wajhān) among our companions:
The first: That the sunnah of greeting has already been attained by his greeting to the first ones, because they are a single assembly (jamʿ wāḥid). Thus, if he repeated the greeting upon them, it would be merely adab. On this position, whichever of the mosque's people replied to him, the obligation of sufficiency is discharged from all of them.
The second position: That the sunnah of greeting remains incumbent for those whom his earlier greeting did not reach, if he intends to sit among them. On this position, the obligation of replying to the earlier greeting is not discharged from the first ones by the reply of the later ones.

**Section:**
It is recommended (mustaḥabb), when one enters his house, to greet even if there is no one in it, and to say: "Peace be upon us and upon Allah's righteous servants" (al-salāmu ʿalaynā wa-ʿalā ʿibādillāhi al-ṣāliḥīn).
We have already presented at the beginning of the book the explanation of what one says upon entering his house.
Likewise, when one enters a mosque or another person's house in which there is no one, it is recommended to greet and to say: "Peace be upon us and upon Allah's righteous servants. Peace be upon you, O people of the house, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings" (al-salāmu ʿalaynā wa-ʿalā ʿibādillāhi al-ṣāliḥīn, al-salāmu ʿalaykum ahl al-bayt wa-raḥmatullāhi wa-barakātuh).

**Section:**
When one is sitting with a people and then rises to depart from them, the sunnah is to greet them.

**739 —**
We have related in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd, al-Tirmidhī, and others, with sound chains of transmission, on the authority of Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: {«When one of you arrives at a gathering, let him greet; and when he wishes to rise, let him greet. The first is not more worthy than the last.»} Al-Tirmidhī said: A ḥasan (good) hadith.
I say: The apparent meaning of this hadith is that the group is obligated to reply to the greeting of this person who greeted them and then parted from them. The two Imāms, al-Qāḍī Ḥusayn and his companion Abū Saʿd al-Mutawallī, said: The custom of some people has been to greet upon parting from a group, and this is a supplication (duʿāʾ) whose response is recommended but not obligatory, because the greeting (taḥiyyah) is only at the time of meeting, not at the time of departure. This is their statement. The Imām Abū Bakr al-Shāshī al-Akhīr, one of our companions, rejected this and said: This is corrupt (fāsid), because the greeting is a sunnah at departure just as it is a sunnah at sitting, and this hadith supports it. What al-Shāshī said is the correct view.

**Section:**
When one passes by a single person or more, and it dominates his assumption (ghalaba ʿalā ẓannihi) that if he greets, the other will not reply — whether due to the arrogance of the one passed by, or his negligence of the passer or of the greeting, or for some other reason — he should still greet and not abandon it for this assumption. For the greeting is commanded, and the passer is commanded to greet; he is not commanded to secure a reply. Moreover, the one passed by may be mistaken in the assumption about him and may actually reply.
As for the statement of one who has no verification: "The passer's greeting is a cause for the acquisition of sin upon the one passed by" — this is manifest ignorance and evident stupidity. For the legally commanded acts are not dropped from the one commanded by such fancies. If we were to look to this corrupt fancy, we would abandon the enjoining of good and forbidding of evil (al-amr bi-l-maʿrūf wa-l-nahy ʿan al-munkar) upon one who commits a wrong while ignorant of its being wrong, and it dominates our assumption that he will not be deterred by our words — for our forbidding him and informing him of its ugliness would be a cause for his sin if he does not desist. There is no doubt that we do not abandon forbidding on account of such a thing. The parallels to this are many and well-known. And Allah knows best.
It is recommended for one who greets a person, makes him hear the greeting, and thereby obligates the reply upon him with its conditions, yet the other does not reply — that he absolve him of it, saying: "I absolve you of my right to the reply of the greeting" (abraʾtuhu min ḥaqqī fī radd al-salām), or "I have made you lawful of it" (jaʿaltuhu fī ḥill minhu), and similar expressions. He should utter this verbally, for thereby the right of this human being is dropped. And Allah knows best.

**740 —**
We have related in the book of Ibn al-Sunnī, on the authority of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Shibl al-Ṣaḥābī, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: {«Whoever answers the greeting, it is for him; and whoever does not answer, then he is not of us.»}
It is recommended for one who greets a person and the other does not reply, to say to him with a gentle expression: "The reply to the greeting is obligatory, so it behooves you to reply to me so that the obligation falls from you." And Allah knows best.

**(Chapter on Seeking Permission — Bāb al-Istiʾdhān)**
Allah, the Exalted, said: {«O you who believe, do not enter houses other than your own until you seek familiarity (tastaʾnisū) and greet their inhabitants»} [al-Nūr: 27]. And the Exalted said: {«And when the children among you reach...»}

chapters.title_en: Section 104 — On the Etiquette of Seeking Permission to Enter (Ādāb al-Istidhān)
chapters.arabic_text:
منكم الحلم فليستأذنوا كما استأذن الذين من قبلهم) [النور: 59] .

| 741 - 
# وروينا في " صحيحي البخاري ومسلم " عن أبي موسى الأشعري رضي الله عنه

قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " الاستئذان ثلاث، فإن أذن لك وإلا

فارجع ".
# ورويناه في " الصحيحين " أيضا عن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه وغيره عن

النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم.
# وروينا في " صحيحيهما " عن سهل بن سعد رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله

صلى الله عليه وسلم: " إنما جعل الاستئذان من أجل البصر ".
# وروينا الاستئذان ثلاثا من جهات كثيرة.
# والسنة أن يسلم ثم يستأذن، فيقوم عند الباب بحيث لا ينظر إلى من في

داخله، ثم يقول: السلام عليكم، أأدخل؟ فإن لم يجبه أحد، قال ذلك ثانيا

وثالثا، فإن لم يجبه أحد انصرف.

| 742 - 
# وروينا في " سنن أبي داود " بإسناد صحيح عن ربعي بن حراش، بكسر الحاء

المهملة وآخره شين معجمة، التابعي الجليل قال: حدثنا رجل من بني عامر "

استأذن على 
# النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو في بيت فقال: أألج؟ فقال رسول الله صلى

الله عليه وسلم لخادمه: " اخرج إلى هذا فعلمه الاستئذان، فقل له: قل:

السلام عليكم، أأدخل؟ فسمعه الرجل فقال: السلام عليكم، أأدخل؟ بفأذن له

النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فدخل ".

| 734 - 
# وروينا في " سنن أبي داود والترمذي " عن كلدة بن الحنبل الصحابي رضي الله

عنه قال: " أتيت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فدخلت عليه ولم أسلم، فقال

النبي: ارجع فقل: السلام عليكم أأدخل؟ " قال الترمذي: حديث حسن.
# قلت: كلدة، بفتح الكاف واللام.
# والحنبل، بفتح الحاء المهملة وبعدها نون ساكنة ثم باء موحدة ثم لام.
# وهذا الذي ذكرناه من تقديم السلام على الاستئذان هو الصحيح.
# وذكر الماوردي فيه ثلاثة أوجه، أحدها هذا، والثاني تقديم الاستئذان على

السلام، والثالث: وهو اختياره، إن وقعت عين المستأذن على صاحب المنزل قبل

دخوله قدم السلام، وإن لم تقع عليه عينه، قدم الاستئذان.
# وإذا استأذن ثلاثا فلم يؤذن له وظن أنه لم يسمع، فهل يزيد عليها؟ حكى

الإمام أبو بكر بن العربي المالكي فيه ثلاثة مذاهب، أحدها: يعيده، والثاني:

لا يعيده، والثالث: إن كان بلفظ الاستئذان المتقدم لم يعده، وإن كان بغيره

أعاده، قال: والأصح أنه لا يعيده بحال، وهذا الذي صححه هو
# الذي تقتضيه السنة (1) ، والله أعلم.

# فصل:
# وينبغي إذا استأذن على إنسان بالسلام أو بدق الباب، فقيل له: من أنت؟ أن

يقول: فلان بن فلان، أو فلان الفلاني، أو فلان المعروف بكذا، أو ما أشبه

ذلك، بحيث يحصل التعريف التام به، ويكره أن يقتصر على قوله: أنا، أو

الخادم، أو بعض الغلمان، أو بعض المحبين، وما أشبه ذلك.

| 744 - 
# روينا في " صحيحي البخاري ومسلم " في حديث الإسراء المشهور (2) ، قال

رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " " ثم صعد بي جبريل إلى السماء الدنيا

فاستفتح (3) ، فقيل: من هذا؟ 
# قال: جبريل، قيل: ومن معك؟ قال: محمد، ثم صعد بي إلى السماء الثانية

والثالثة وسائرهن، ويقال في باب كل سماء: من هذا؟ فيقول: جبريل ".

| 745 - 
# وروينا في " صحيحيهما " في حديث أبي موسى لما جلس النبي صلى الله عليه

وسلم على بئر البستان (1) وجاء أبو بكر فاستأذن، فقال: من؟ قال: أبو بكر،

ثم جاء عمر فاستأذن، فقال: من: قال عمر، ثم عثمان كذلك.

| 746 - 
# وروينا في " صحيحيهما " أيضا عن جابر رضي الله عنه قال: " أتيت النبي صلى

الله عليه وسلم فدققت الباب، فقال: من ذا؟ فقلت: أنا، فقال: أنا أنا؟ كأنه

كرهها ".
chapters.anchors:
- Root: أ-ذ-ن (ʾ-dh-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is 'to listen, to hear, to give ear'; from it derives 'permission' (idhn) as an act of granting leave after hearing a request.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In sacred law, istidhān is the formal request for entry, a divinely instituted social protocol preserving the sanctity of private dwellings (ḥurumāt) and the gaze (baṣar).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) sense is 'seeking leave'; metaphorical (majāz) extension applies to seeking access to hearts or honor, but here it remains strictly literal in the juristic context.
- Root: س-ل-م (s-l-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root denotes safety, soundness, and freedom from defect; the greeting 'al-salāmu ʿalaykum' invokes divine protection.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The greeting is a verbal covenant of security (amān) between believers, preceding any intimate approach.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: 'peace be upon you'; metaphorical: the greeting as a key that unlocks the door of social intercourse.
- Root: ب-ص-ر (b-ṣ-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Denotes sight, perception, and insight; here it refers to the physical eye (ʿayn) and its accidental glance.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The rationale for istidhān is the protection of the gaze from unlawful exposure to what lies within private quarters.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: the organ of vision; metaphorical: spiritual discernment — but the ḥadīth employs the literal sense.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Taqdīm wa Taʾkhīr (Fronting and Delaying) — In the phrase "السلام عليكم أأدخل؟", the greeting is fronted as a necessary preliminary (istiʾnāf) before the interrogative request, establishing a sequential syntactic order that mirrors the legal priority.
chapters.translation:
I say — Know that the Almighty has said: {«...so let them ask permission as those before them did»} [al-Nūr: 59].

| 741 —
We have related in the two Ṣaḥīḥs of al-Bukhārī and Muslim, on the authority of Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Seeking permission is three times; if permission is granted to you, then enter, otherwise return."
We have also related it in the two Ṣaḥīḥs on the authority of Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, may God be pleased with him, and others, from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.
We have related in their two Ṣaḥīḥs, on the authority of Sahl ibn Saʿd, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Seeking permission was only instituted for the sake of the gaze."
We have related the threefold seeking of permission from many chains of transmission.
The Sunnah is that one gives the greeting (salām) and then seeks permission. He stands at the door in a position where he cannot see those within, then says: "Peace be upon you; may I enter?" If no one answers him, he repeats this a second and third time. If no one answers him after that, he departs.

| 742 —
We have related in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd, with a sound chain, on the authority of Ribʿī ibn Ḥirāsh — with kasrah on the unpointed ḥāʾ and its final letter being an unpointed shīn — the noble Tābiʿī, who said: A man from the tribe of Banū ʿĀmir narrated to us: "He sought permission to enter upon the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was in a house, and said: 'Shall I enter (a-alij)?' The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to his servant: 'Go out to this man and teach him the etiquette of seeking permission. Say to him: Say: Peace be upon you; may I enter?' The man heard him and said: 'Peace be upon you; may I enter?' Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, granted him permission, and he entered."

| 734 —
We have related in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd and al-Tirmidhī, on the authority of Kaladah ibn al-Ḥanbal, the Companion, may God be pleased with him, who said: "I came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and entered upon him without giving the greeting. The Prophet said: 'Return and say: Peace be upon you; may I enter?'" Al-Tirmidhī said: This is a good (ḥasan) ḥadīth.
I say: Kaladah is with fatḥah on the kāf and the lām. Al-Ḥanbal is with fatḥah on the unpointed ḥāʾ, followed by a silent nūn, then an unpointed bāʾ, then a lām.
What we have mentioned — the precedence of the greeting over the request for permission — is the correct position. Al-Māwardī mentioned three opinions on this matter: the first is this one; the second is giving precedence to the request for permission over the greeting; the third — which is his own choice — is that if the eye of the one seeking permission falls upon the owner of the house before his entry, he gives the greeting first; but if his eye does not fall upon him, he gives the request for permission first.
If one seeks permission three times and is not granted it, and he suspects that he was not heard, should he exceed that number? The Imām Abū Bakr ibn al-ʿArabī al-Mālikī reported three schools on this: the first holds that he repeats it; the second holds that he does not repeat it; the third holds that if he used the same wording of the previous request, he does not repeat it, but if he used different wording, he repeats it. He said: The most correct view is that he does not repeat it under any circumstance. This is what he deemed sound, and it is what the Sunnah requires — and God knows best.

A Sub-Section:
It is proper that when one seeks permission upon a person by greeting or by knocking on the door, and it is said to him: "Who are you?", he should say: "So-and-so, son of so-and-so," or "So-and-so of such-and-such tribe," or "So-and-so known by such-and-such," or something similar, such that full identification is achieved. It is disliked (makrūh) for him to restrict himself to saying: "It is I," or "The servant," or "One of the boys," or "One of your loved ones," and the like.

| 744 —
We have related in the two Ṣaḥīḥs of al-Bukhārī and Muslim, in the well-known ḥadīth of the Night Journey, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Then Gabriel ascended with me to the lowest heaven and asked for it to be opened. It was said: 'Who is this?' He said: 'Gabriel.' It was said: 'And who is with you?' He said: 'Muhammad.' Then he ascended with me to the second heaven, the third, and the rest of them. At the gate of each heaven it is said: 'Who is this?' And he says: 'Gabriel.'"

| 745 —
We have related in their two Ṣaḥīḥs, in the ḥadīth of Abū Mūsā, that when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sat at the well of the garden, Abū Bakr came and sought permission, and he said: "Who?" He said: "Abū Bakr." Then ʿUmar came and sought permission, and he said: "Who?" He said: "ʿUmar." Then ʿUthmān did likewise.

| 746 —
We have related in their two Ṣaḥīḥs as well, on the authority of Jābir, may God be pleased with him, who said: "I came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and knocked on the door. He said: 'Who is it?' I said: 'It is I.' He said: 'I, I?' — as if he disliked it."

chapters.title_en: Section on a Person Describing Himself by What He Is Known By, and Related Matters on Greetings
chapters.arabic_text:
# فصل:
# ولا بأس أن يصف نفسه بما يعرف إذا لم يعرفه المخاطب بغيره، وإن كان
# فيه صورة تبجيل له، بأن يكني نفسه، أو يقول: أنا المفتي فلان، أو القاضي،

أو الشيخ فلان، أو ما أشبه ذلك.

| 747 - 
# روينا في " صحيحي البخاري ومسلم " عن أم هانئ بنت أبي طالب رضي الله

عنها، واسمها فاختة على المشهور، وقيل: فاطمة، وقيل هند، قالت: " أتيت

النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يغتسل وفاطمة تستره فقال: " من هذه؟ فقلت:

أنا أم هانئ ".

| 748 - 
# وروينا في " صحيحيهما " عن أبي ذر رضي الله عنه، واسمه  جندب، وقيل: برير

بضم الباء تصغير بر، قال: خرجت ليلة من الليالي فإذا رسول الله صلى الله

عليه وسلم يمشي وحده، فجعلت أمشي في ظل القمر، فالتفت فرآني فقال: " من

هذا؟ " فقلت: أبو ذر ".

| 749 - 
# وروينا في " صحيح مسلم " عن أبي قتادة الحارث بن ربعي رضي الله عنه في

حديث الميضأة المشتمل على معجزات كثيرة لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وعلى

جمل من فنون العلم، قال فيه أبو قتادة: " فرفع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

رأسه فقال: من هذا؟ قلت: أبو قتادة ".
# قلت: ونظائر هذا كثيرة، وسببه الحاجة، وعدم إرادة الافتخار.

| 750 - 
# ويقرب من هذا ما رويناه في " صحيح مسلم " عن أبي هريرة رصي الله عنه -

واسمه عبد الرحمن بن صخر على الأصح - قال: قلت: يا رسول الله ادع الله أن

يهدي 
# أم أبي هريرة ... " وذكر الحديث ... إلى أن قال: " فرجعت فقلت: يا رسول

الله قد استجاب الله دعوتك وهدى أم أبي هريرة.

| (باب في مسائل تتفرع على السلام)

# مسألة: قال أبو سعد المتولي: التحية عند الخروج من الحمام، بأن يقال له:

طاب حمامك، لا أصل لها، ولكن روي أن عليا رضي الله عنه قال لرجل خرج من

الحمام: طهرت فلا نجست.
# قلت: هذا المحل لم يصح فيه شئ، ولو قال إنسان لصاحبه على سبيل المودة

والمؤالفة واستجلاب الود: أدام الله لك النعيم، ونحو ذلك من الدعاء فلا بأس

به.

# مسألة: إذا ابتدأ المار الممرور عليه، فقال: صبحك الله بالخير، أو

بالسعادة، أو قواك الله، أو لا أوحش الله منك، أو غير ذلك من الألفاظ التي

يستعملها الناس في العادة، لم يستحق جوابا، لكن لو دعا له قباله ذلك كان

حسنا، إلا أن يترك جوابه بالكلية زجرا له في تخلفه وإهماله السلام وتأديبا

له ولغيره في الاعتناء بالابتداء بالسلام.
chapters.anchors:
- Root: و-ص-ف (wa-ṣa-fa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To describe, characterize, attribute a quality; core sense of depicting an attribute (ṣifah) of a thing.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, ṣifah relates to attributing qualities to entities; here, self-description for identification, not self-praise.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) self-identification for recognition; metaphorical (majāz) would be self-glorification, which is not intended.
- Root: ك-ن-ي (k-n-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To use a kunyah (teknonym, e.g., Abū X); a form of respectful indirect naming.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A social convention of honorific address; permissible when needed for clarity.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage in address; metaphorical extension to any respectful self-reference.
- Root: ت-ح-ي-ة (t-ḥ-y-h)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Greeting, salutation; from ḥayāh (life), wishing life/vitality.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Islamic law, the prescribed greeting is salām; other forms are customary (ʿādah) and not legislated.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: wishing life; metaphorical: any benevolent invocation.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — When the author says "أو القاضي، أو الشيخ فلان" (or the judge, or Shaykh so-and-so), the alternatives are explanatory appositives, not syntactic conjunctions requiring separate predicates; the conditional clause governs all.
chapters.translation:
Section: There is no harm in a person describing himself by what he is known by, if the addressee does not know him otherwise, even if it contains a form of veneration for himself — such as using his kunyah, or saying: "I am the Muftī so-and-so," or "the judge," or "the Shaykh so-and-so," or similar to that.

| 747 - We have related in the two Ṣaḥīḥs of al-Bukhārī and Muslim, on the authority of Umm Hāniʾ bint Abī Ṭālib — may Allah be pleased with her — and her name is Fākhitah according to the well-known view, and it was said: Fāṭimah, and it was said: Hind — she said: "I came to the Prophet — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — while he was bathing, and Fāṭimah was screening him. He said: 'Who is this?' I said: 'I am Umm Hāniʾ.'"

| 748 - And we have related in their two Ṣaḥīḥs, on the authority of Abū Dharr — may Allah be pleased with him — and his name is Jundab, and it was said: Burayr, with the ḍammah on the bāʾ, a diminutive of Barr — he said: "I went out one night, and behold, the Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — was walking alone. I began to walk in the moonlight. He turned and saw me, and said: 'Who is this?' I said: 'Abū Dharr.'"

| 749 - And we have related in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, on the authority of Abū Qatādah al-Ḥārith ibn Ribʿī — may Allah be pleased with him — in the ḥadīth of the water vessel (al-mīḍāʾah), which comprises many miracles of the Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — and a number of branches of knowledge. Abū Qatādah said therein: "The Prophet — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — raised his head and said: 'Who is this?' I said: 'Abū Qatādah.'"

I say: And parallels to this are many, and its cause is need, and the absence of any intention of self-glorification.

| 750 - And close to this is what we have related in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, on the authority of Abū Hurayrah — may Allah be pleased with him — and his name is ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ṣakhr according to the most correct view — he said: "I said: O Messenger of Allah, supplicate Allah to guide the mother of Abū Hurayrah..." and he mentioned the ḥadīth... until he said: "So I returned and said: O Messenger of Allah, Allah has answered your supplication and guided the mother of Abū Hurayrah."

| (Chapter on Matters that Branch off from the Greeting)

Question: Abū Saʿd al-Mutawallī said: The greeting upon leaving the bathhouse — that one says to him: "May your bath be pleasant (ṭāba ḥammāmuka)" — has no basis [in the Sunnah]. However, it is related that ʿAlī — may Allah be pleased with him — said to a man who had left the bathhouse: "You have become purified, so may you not become impure (ṭahurta fa-lā tanjus)."

I say: Nothing authentic has been established in this matter. But if a person says to his companion, by way of affection, amity, and drawing closeness of love: "May Allah perpetuate for you bliss," or similar supplications, there is no harm in it.

Question: If the passer-by initiates [the greeting] upon the one being passed, saying: "May Allah give you a good morning with goodness," or "with happiness," or "May Allah strengthen you," or "May Allah not make you lonely," or other expressions that people customarily use, he does not deserve a reply. However, if the other supplicates for him in return for that, it is good. Except that he may leave answering him entirely as a rebuke to him for his negligence and abandonment of the salām, and as discipline for him and others in attending to initiating the greeting.

chapters.title_en: Section 106 — On Kissing the Hand of Another, the Cheek of a Child, and Related Matters
chapters.arabic_text:
# فصل:
# إذا أراد تقبيل يد غيره، إن كان ذلك لزهده وصلاحه أو علمه أو شرفه

وصيانته أو نحو ذلك من الأمور الدينية، لم يكره، بل يستحب، وإن كان لغناه

ودنياه  وثروته وشوكته ووجاهته عند أهل الدنيا ونحو ذلك، فهو مكروه شديد

الكراهة.
# وقال المتولي من أصحابنا: لا يجوز فأشار إلى أنه حرام.

| 751 - 
# روينا في سنن أبي داود عن زارع رضي الله عنه، وكان في وفد عبد القيس قال:

" فجعلنا نتبادر من رواحلنا فنقبل يد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ورجله ".
# قلت: زارع بزاي في أوله وراء بعد الألف على لفظ زارع الحنطة وغيرها.

| 752 - 
# وروينا في سنن أبي داود أيضا عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما قصة قال فيها: "

فدنونا: يعني من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقبلنا يده.
# وأما تقبيل الرجل خد ولده الصغير، وأخيه، وقبلة غير خده من أطرافه ونحوها

على وجه الشفقة والرحمة واللطف ومحبة القرابة، فسنة.
# والأحاديث فيه كثيرة صحيحة مشهورة، وسواء الولد الذكر والأنثى، وكذلك

قبلته ولد صديقه وغيره من صغار الأطفال
# على هذا الوجه.
# وأما التقبيل بالشهوة، فحرام بالاتفاق.
# وسواء في ذلك الولد وغيره، بل النظر إليه بالشهوة حرام بالاتفاق على

القريب والأجنبي.
# 

| 753 - 
# وروينا في " صحيحي البخاري ومسلم " عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: " قبل

النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم الحسن بن علي رضي الله عنهما وعنده الأقرع بن

حابس التميمي، فقال الأقرع: إن لى عشرة من الولد ما قبلت منهم أحدا، فنظر

إليه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم (1) ثم قال: من لا يرحم لا يرحم " (2) .

| 754 - 
# وروينا في " صحيحيهما " عن عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت " قدم ناس من

الأعراب على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، فقالوا: تقبلون صبيانكم؟

فقالوا: نعم، قالوا: لكنا والله ما نقبل، فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه

وسلم: أو أملك أن كان الله تعالى نزع منكم الرحمة؟ " هذا لفظ إحدى

الروايات، وهو مروي بألفاظ.

| 755 - 
# وروينا في " صحيح البخاري " وغيره عن أنس رضي الله عنه قال: " أخذ رسول

الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ابنه إبراهيم فقبله وشمه ".

| 756 - 
# وروينا في سنن أبي داود عن البراء بن عازب رضي الله عنهما (3) قال: دخلت

مع أبي  بكر رضي الله عنه أول ما قدم المدينة، فإذا عائشة ابنته رضي الله

عنها مضطجعة قد أصابتها حمى، فأتاها أبو بكر فقال: كيف أنت يا بنية؟ وقبل

خدها.

| 757 - 
# وروينا في كتب الترمذي والنسائي وابن ماجه بالأسانيد الصحيحة (4) عن

صفوان بن عسال الصحابي رضي الله عنه - وعسال بفتح العين وتشديد السين

المهملتين - 
# قال: قال يهودي لصاحبه: " اذهب بنا إلى هذا النبي، فأتيا رسول الله صلى

الله عليه وسلم فسألاه عن تسع آيات بينات ... فذكر الحديث ... إلى قوله:

فقبلوا يده ورجله، وقالا: نشهد أنك نبي (1) .

| 758 - 
# وروينا في سنن أبي داود بالإسناد الصحيح المليح (2) عن إياس بن دغفل قال:

رأيت أبا نضرة قبل خد الحسن بن علي رضي الله عنهما.
# قلت: أبو نضرة بالنون والضاد المعجمة: اسمه المنذر بن مالك بن قطعة،

تابعي ثقة.
# ودغفل، بدال مهملة مفتوحة ثم غين معجمة ساكنة ثم فاء مفتوحة ثم لام.

| 759 - 
# وعن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما أنه كان يقبل ابنه سالما ويقول: اعجبوا من

شيخ يقبل شيخا (3) .
# وعن سهل بن عبد الله التستري السيد الجليل أحد أفراد زهاد الأمة وعبادها

رضي الله عنه أنه كان يأتي أبا داود السجستاني ويقول: أخرج لي لسانك الذي

تحدث به حديث
# رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لأقبله، فيقبله.
# وأفعال السلف في هذا الباب أكثر من أن تحصر، والله أعلم.
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To receive, meet, face; to kiss (as an act of drawing near or greeting); derived from the notion of "coming before" or "facing" another.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In religious contexts, kissing (taqbīl) is an embodied act of veneration (taʿẓīm) or affection (shafaqah), contingent upon the intention (niyyah) of the agent.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — physical contact of lips; metaphorical (majāz) — an expression of honor or love, hence its ruling shifts with the underlying motive.
- Root: ر-ح-م (r-ḥ-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Mercy, compassion, tenderness; from raḥim (womb), signifying innate, protective affection.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Raḥmah as a divine attribute and a human moral virtue; its absence is a privation of natural human disposition.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — the quality of compassion; metaphorical — the divine decree stripping it from a heart.
- Root: ك-ر-ه (k-r-h)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Dislike, aversion, abhorrence.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Karāhah as a legal category (makrūh) — that which is discouraged but not punishable, distinct from taḥrīm (prohibition).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — personal distaste; technical — a jurisprudential grading of actions.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-jazāʾ) — The protasis (in khāna... ) governs the apodosis (lam yukrah... ), with the ruling determined by the nature of the cause (sabab) stated in the condition; also, the use of fa- (as in fa-huwa makrūh) for immediate consequence and emphasis.
chapters.translation:
**Section 106**

**On kissing the hand of another — if it is for his asceticism, righteousness, knowledge, or noble lineage, and his safeguarding, or similar religious matters, it is not disliked; rather, it is recommended (mustaḥabb). But if it is for his wealth, worldly status, riches, power, and prestige among the people of this world, and the like, then it is severely disliked (makrūh karāhah shadīdah).**

**Al-Mutawallī, one of our companions (i.e., of the Shāfiʿī school), said: It is not permissible (lā yajūz), indicating that he deemed it unlawful (ḥarām).**

| 751 —
We narrated in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd, on the authority of Zāriʿ (may Allah be pleased with him) — and he was among the delegation of ʿAbd al-Qays — who said: "We hastened from our mounts and kissed the hand of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) and his foot."
I say: Zāriʿ is with a zāy at its beginning and a rāʾ after the alif, on the pattern of the word for a sower of wheat and other crops (zāriʿ).

| 752 —
We also narrated in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd, on the authority of Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both), a story in which he said: "We drew near — meaning to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) — and kissed his hand."

**As for a man kissing the cheek of his young child, or his brother, or kissing other than the cheek — such as the limbs — out of compassion, mercy, gentleness, and love of kinship, it is a Sunnah (established practice). The hadiths concerning this are numerous, authentic, and well-known. It is the same whether the child is male or female. Likewise, one may kiss the child of a friend or any other young child in this manner.**

**As for kissing with lust (shahwah), it is unlawful (ḥarām) by consensus (ittifāq). This applies equally to one's own child and others; indeed, even looking at such a person with lust is unlawful by consensus, whether the person is a close relative or a stranger.**

| 753 —
We narrated in the two Ṣaḥīḥs of al-Bukhārī and Muslim, on the authority of Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) kissed al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with them both) while al-Aqraʿ ibn Ḥābis al-Tamīmī was with him. Al-Aqraʿ said: 'I have ten children, and I have never kissed any one of them.' The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) looked at him, then said: {«He who does not show mercy will not be shown mercy»}."

| 754 —
We narrated in the two Ṣaḥīḥs, on the authority of ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: "Some Bedouins came to the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) and said: 'Do you kiss your children?' They replied: 'Yes.' The Bedouins said: 'But we, by Allah, do not kiss.' The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: {«Can I help it if Allah has stripped mercy from your hearts?»} This is the wording of one of the narrations, and it is transmitted with several wordings."

| 755 —
We narrated in the Ṣaḥīḥ of al-Bukhārī and others, on the authority of Anas (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) took his son Ibrāhīm, kissed him, and smelled him."

| 756 —
We narrated in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd, on the authority of al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: "I entered with Abū Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) when he first arrived in Madīnah, and there was ʿĀʾishah, his daughter (may Allah be pleased with her), lying down, stricken with fever. Abū Bakr came to her and said: 'How are you, my little daughter?' And he kissed her cheek."

| 757 —
We narrated in the books of al-Tirmidhī, al-Nasāʾī, and Ibn Mājah, with authentic chains of transmission, on the authority of Ṣafwān ibn ʿAssāl, the Companion (may Allah be pleased with him) — and ʿAssāl is with a fatḥah on the ʿayn and a shaddah on the sīn, both unpointed letters — who said: "A Jew said to his companion: 'Come, let us go to this Prophet.' So they came to the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) and asked him about nine clear signs... and he mentioned the hadith... until his saying: 'Then they kissed his hand and his foot, and said: We bear witness that you are a Prophet.'"

| 758 —
We narrated in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd, with an authentic and excellent chain of transmission, on the authority of Iyās ibn Daghfal, who said: "I saw Abū Naḍrah kiss the cheek of al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with them both)."
I say: Abū Naḍrah — with a nūn and a pointed ḍād — his name is al-Mundhir ibn Mālik ibn Qiṭʿah, a trustworthy Successor (tābiʿī thiqah). And Daghfal — with an unpointed dāl, fatḥah, then a pointed ghayn, sukūn, then a fāʾ, fatḥah, then a lām.

| 759 —
And on the authority of Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both), that he used to kiss his son Sālim and say: "Marvel at an old man kissing an old man."
And on the authority of Sahl ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Tustarī — the noble master, one of the unique ascetics and worshippers of this Ummah (may Allah be pleased with him) — that he used to come to Abū Dāwūd al-Sijistānī and say: "Put out your tongue with which you narrate the hadith of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) so that I may kiss it," and he would kiss it.
**The deeds of the Salaf (righteous predecessors) in this matter are too numerous to be enumerated. And Allah knows best.**

chapters.title_en: Section 107 — On Kissing the Deceased for Blessing, Embracing, and the Handshake (Muṣāfaḥah)
chapters.arabic_text:
# فصل:
# ولا بأس بتقبيل وجه الميت الصالح للتبرك، ولا بتقبيل الرجل وجه صاحبه إذا

قدم من سفر ونحوه.

| 760 - 
# روينا في " صحيح البخاري " عن عائشة رضي الله عنها في الحديث الطويل في

وفاة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قالت: " دخل أبو بكر رضي الله عنه فكشف

عن وجه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ثم أكب عليه فقبله، ثم بكى " (4) .

| 761 - 
# وروينا في كتاب الترمذي عن عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت: " قدم زيد بن

# حارثة المدينة ورسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في بيتي، فأتاه فقرع الباب،

فقام إليه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يجر ثوبه،  فاعتنقه وقبله " قال

الترمذي: حديث حسن.
# وأما المعانقة وتقبيل الوجه لغير الطفل ولغير القادم من سفر ونحوه،

فمكروهان، نص على كراهتهما أبو محمد البغوي وغيره من أصحابنا.
# 761 م - ويدل على الكراهة ما رويناه في كتابي الترمذي وابن ماجه عن أنس

رضي
# الله عنه قال: " قال رجل: يا رسول الله! الرجل منا يلقى أخاه أو صديقه

أينحني له؟ قال: لا، قال: أفيلتزمه ويقبله؟ قال: لا، قال: فيأخذه بيده

ويصافحه؟ قال: نعم " قال الترمذي: حديث حسن.
# قلت: وهذا الذي ذكرناه في التقبيل والمعانقة، وأنه لا بأس به عند القدوم

من سفر ونحوه، ومكروه كراهة تنزيه في غيره، هو في غير الأمرد الحسن الوجه،

فأما الأمرد الحسن، فيحرم بكل حال تقبيله، سواء قدم من سفر أم لا.
# والظاهر أن معانقته كتقبيله، أو قريبة من تقبيله، ولا فرق في هذا بين أن

يكون المقبل والمقبل رجلين صالحين أو فاسقين، أو أحدهما صالحا، فالجميع

سواء.
# والمذهب الصحيح عندنا تحريم النظر إلى الأمرد الحسن، ولو كان بغير شهوة،

وقد أمن الفتنة، فهو حرام كالمرأة لكونه في معناها

| فصل في المصافحة
# : اعلم أنها سنة مجمع عليها عند التلاقي.

| 762 - 
# روينا في " صحيح البخاري " عن قتادة قال: قلت لأنس رضي الله عنه: أكانت

المصافحة في أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم؟ قال: نعم.

| 763 - 
# وروينا في " صحيحي البخاري ومسلم " في حديث كعب بن مالك رضي الله عنه في

قصة توبته قال: فقام إلي طلحة بن عبيد الله رضي الله عنه يهرول، حتى صافحني

وهنأني (1) .

| 764 - 
# وروينا بالإسناد الصحيح في سنن أبي داود عن أنس رضي الله عنه قال: " لما

جاء أهل اليمن، قال لهم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " قد جاءكم أهل

اليمن وهم أول من جاء بالمصافحة ". 

| 765 - 
# وروينا في سنن أبي داود والترمذي وابن ماجه عن البراء رضي الله عنه قال:
# قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " ما من مسلمين يلتقيان فيتثافحان إلا

غفر لهما قبل أن يتفرقا ".

| 766 - 
# وروينا في كتابي الترمذي  وابن ماجه عن أنس رضي الله عنه قال: " قال رجل:

يا رسول الله! الرجل منا يلقى أخاه أو صديقه أينحني له؟ ، قال: لا، قال:

أفيلتزمه ويقبله؟ قال: لا، قال: فيأخذ بيده ويصافحه؟ قال: نعم " قال

الترمذي: حديث حسن.
# وفي الباب أحاديث كثيرة.

| 767 - 
# وروينا في " موطأ الإمام مالك " رحمه الله عن عطاء بن عبد الله الخراساني

قال: قال لي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " تصافحوا يذهب الغل، وتهادوا

تحابوا وتذهب الشحناء ".
# قلت: هذا حديث مرسل (1) .
# واعلم أن هذه المصافحة مستحبة عند كل لقاء، وأما ما اعتاده الناس من

المصافحة بعد صلاتي الصبح والعصر، فلا أصل له في الشرع على هذا الوجه، ولكن

لا بأس به، فإن أصل المصافحة سنة، وكونهم حافظوا عليها في بعض الأحوال،

وفرطوا فيها في كثير من الأحوال أو أكثرها، لا يخرج ذلك البعض عن كونه من

المصافحة التي ورد الشرع بأصلها.
# وقد ذكر الشيخ الإمام أبو محمد عبد السلام رحمه الله في كتابه " القواعد

" أن البدع على خمسة أقسام: واجبة، ومحرمة، ومكروهة، ومستحبة، ومباحة.
# قال: ومن أمثلة البدع المباحة: المصافحة عقب الصبح والعصر، والله أعلم.
# قلت: وينبغي أن يحترز من مصافحة الأمرد الحسن الوجه، فإن النظر إليه حرام

كما قدمنا في الفصل الذي قبل هذا، وقد قال أصحابنا: كل من حرم النظر إليه

حرم مسه، بل المس أشد، فإنه يحل النظر إلى الأجنبية إذا أراد أن يتزوجها.
# وفي حال البيع والشراء والأخذ والعطاء ونحو ذلك، ولا يجوز مسها في شئ من

ذلك، والله أعلم.
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To meet face-to-face; to receive; to kiss (taqbīl) as an act of direct frontal encounter.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Denotes acceptance (qubūl) and veneration; kissing a sacred object or person is an act of seeking blessing (tabarruk), not worship.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical contact of lips; metaphorical (majāz) for acceptance of deeds by Allah.
- Root: ع-ن-ق (ʿ-n-q)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The neck; muʿānaqah — to embrace, encircling the neck.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Physical expression of affection and brotherhood; contextually regulated by custom (ʿurf) and legal rank (ḥukm).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical embrace; no metaphorical extension in legal discourse.
- Root: ص-ف-ح (ṣ-f-ḥ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The side of the face; muṣāfaḥah — the joining of palms in greeting.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A covenantal gesture of reconciliation and removal of rancor (ghill).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the physical act; metaphorical for peace and pardon (ṣafḥ).
- Root: م-ر-د (m-r-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Hairlessness; amrad — a beardless youth.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal discourse, a person whose beauty poses fitnah (temptation); ruled analogically to a woman (ajnabiyyah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical state; metaphorical for the danger of seduction.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — The phrase "أو قريبة من تقبيله" (or close to kissing him) functions as an appositive qualifier, softening the categorical ruling on embracing the amrad to a near-equivalence, not absolute identity, preserving juristic precision.
chapters.translation:
Section: There is no harm in kissing the face of a righteous deceased person for the purpose of seeking blessing (tabarruk), nor in a man kissing the face of his companion when he arrives from a journey or the like.

| 760 —
We have related in "Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī" on the authority of ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, in the lengthy ḥadīth concerning the death of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said: "Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, entered, uncovered the face of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, then bent over him and kissed him, then wept."

| 761 —
And we have related in the book of al-Tirmidhī on the authority of ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: "Zayd ibn Ḥārithah arrived in Madīnah while the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was in my house. He came to him and knocked at the door. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, rose to him, dragging his garment, embraced him and kissed him." Al-Tirmidhī said: A ḥasan ḥadīth.

As for embracing (muʿānaqah) and kissing the face — other than in the case of a child or one arriving from a journey or the like — both are disliked (makrūh). Abū Muḥammad al-Baghawī and others of our companions have explicitly stated their disapproval.

| 761m —
Evidence for the disapproval is what we have related in the two books of al-Tirmidhī and Ibn Mājah on the authority of Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "A man said: O Messenger of Allah! When one of us meets his brother or his friend, should he bow to him? He said: No. He said: Should he embrace him and kiss him? He said: No. He said: Should he take his hand and shake it? He said: Yes." Al-Tirmidhī said: A ḥasan ḥadīth.

I say: What we have mentioned concerning kissing and embracing — that there is no harm in it upon arrival from a journey or the like, and that it is disliked with a disapproval of tanzīh (avoidance, not prohibition) in other cases — applies only to other than a beardless youth of handsome face (al-amrad al-ḥasan al-wajh). As for the beardless handsome youth, kissing him is unlawful (ḥarām) in every case, whether he has arrived from a journey or not. And the apparent position is that embracing him is like kissing him, or close to it. There is no difference in this matter between whether the kisser and the kissed are two righteous men, two wicked men, or one righteous and one wicked — all are the same.

The correct school (al-madhhab al-ṣaḥīḥ) in our view is the prohibition of looking at a beardless handsome youth, even without lust, and even if fitnah (temptation) is deemed secure. It is unlawful just as looking at a woman is unlawful, because he falls under her meaning (fī maʿnāhā).

Section on the Handshake (Muṣāfaḥah):
Know that it is a Sunnah upon which there is consensus (ijmāʿ) at the time of meeting.

| 762 —
We have related in "Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī" on the authority of Qatādah, who said: I said to Anas, may Allah be pleased with him: Was the handshake practiced among the companions of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace? He said: Yes.

| 763 —
And we have related in the two "Ṣaḥīḥs" of al-Bukhārī and Muslim in the ḥadīth of Kaʿb ibn Mālik, may Allah be pleased with him, concerning the story of his repentance, who said: "Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbaydillāh, may Allah be pleased with him, rose to me, hurrying, until he shook my hand and congratulated me."

| 764 —
And we have related with a sound chain (al-isnād al-ṣaḥīḥ) in the "Sunan" of Abū Dāwūd on the authority of Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "When the people of Yemen came, the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to them: 'The people of Yemen have come to you, and they are the first to come with the handshake.'"

| 765 —
And we have related in the "Sunan" of Abū Dāwūd, al-Tirmidhī, and Ibn Mājah on the authority of al-Barāʾ, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: "There are no two Muslims who meet and shake hands, except that they are forgiven before they part."

| 766 —
And we have related in the two books of al-Tirmidhī and Ibn Mājah on the authority of Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "A man said: O Messenger of Allah! When one of us meets his brother or his friend, should he bow to him? He said: No. He said: Should he embrace him and kiss him? He said: No. He said: Should he take his hand and shake it? He said: Yes." Al-Tirmidhī said: A ḥasan ḥadīth. And in this chapter there are many ḥadīths.

| 767 —
And we have related in the "Muwaṭṭaʾ" of Imām Mālik, may Allah have mercy on him, on the authority of ʿAṭāʾ ibn ʿAbdillāh al-Khurāsānī, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to me: "Shake hands, and rancor (ghill) will depart; exchange gifts, and you will love one another, and enmity (shahṇāʾ) will depart."

I say: This is a mursal ḥadīth (a tradition with an omitted link in the chain).

Know that this handshake is recommended (mustaḥabb) at every meeting. As for what people have accustomed themselves to — the handshake after the two prayers of dawn (ṣubḥ) and afternoon (ʿaṣr) — this has no basis in the Sacred Law (sharʿ) in that specific manner, but there is no harm in it. For the origin of the handshake is Sunnah, and the fact that people have maintained it in some situations while neglecting it in many or most situations does not remove that particular instance from being part of the handshake whose origin the Sacred Law has established.

The Shaykh Imām Abū Muḥammad ʿAbd al-Salām, may Allah have mercy on him, has mentioned in his book "al-Qawāʿid" that innovations (bidaʿ) are of five categories: obligatory (wājibah), unlawful (muḥarramah), disliked (makrūhah), recommended (mustaḥabbah), and permissible (mubāḥah). He said: Among the examples of permissible innovation is the handshake immediately after dawn and afternoon prayers. And Allah knows best.

I say: One should be cautious of shaking hands with a beardless handsome youth, for looking at him is unlawful, as we have established in the preceding section. Our companions have said: Whoever it is unlawful to look at, it is unlawful to touch; indeed, touching is more severe. For it is permissible to look at an unrelated woman (ajnabiyyah) when one intends to marry her, and in the context of buying, selling, taking, giving, and the like — but it is not permissible to touch her in any of these matters. And Allah knows best.

chapters.arabic_text:
# فصل:
# ويستحب مع المصافحة، البشاشة بالوجه، والدعاء بالمغفرة وغيرها.

| 761 - 
# روينا في " صحيح مسلم " عن أبي ذر رضي الله عنه قال: قال لي
# رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " لا تحقرن من المعروف شيئا، ولو أن تلقى

أخاك بوجه طليق " (2) . 

| 769 - 
# وروينا في كتاب ابن السني عن البراء بن عازب رضي الله عنهما قال: قال

رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " إن المسلمين إذا التقيا فتصافحا وتكاشرا

بود ونصيحة تناثرت خطاياهما  بينهما ".
# وفي رواية: " إذا التقى المسلمان فتصافحا وحمدا الله تعالى واستغفرا، غفر

الله عز وجل لهما ".

| 770 - 
# وروينا فيه (2) عن أنس رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "

ما من عبدين متحابين في الله، يستقبل أحدهما صاحبه فيصافحه، فيصليان على

النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إلا لم يتفرقا حتى تغفر ذنوبهما ما تقدم منها وما

تأخر ".

| 771 - 
# وروينا فيه عن أنس أيضا، قال: ما أخذ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بيد

رجل ففارقه حتى قال: " اللهم آتنا في الدنيا حسنة وفي الآخرة حسنة وقنا

عذاب النار ".

# فصل:
# ويكره حني الظهر في كل حال لكل أحد (3) ، ويدل عليه ما قدمنا في الفصلين

المتقدمين من حديث أنس، وقوله: " أينحني له؟ قال: لا " وهو حديث حسن كما

ذكرناه، ولم يأت له معارض، فلا مصير إلى مخالفته، ولا يغتر بكثرة من يفعله

ممن ينسب إلى علم أو صلاح وغيرهما من خصال الفضل، فإن الاقتداء إنما يكون

برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، قال الله تعالى: (وما آتاكم الرسول فخذوه

(4) وما نهاكم عنه فانتهوا) 
# [الحشر: 7] وقال تعالى: (فليحذر الذين يخالفون عن أمره أن تصيبهم فتنة أو

يصيبهم عذاب أليم) [النور: 63] .
# وقد قدمنا في " كتاب الجنائز " عن الفضيل بن عياض رضي الله عنه ما معناه:

اتبع طرق الهدى، ولا يضرك قلة السالكين، وإياك وطرق الضلالة، ولا تغتر

بكثرة الهالكين، وبالله التوفيق.

# فصل:
# وأما إكرام الداخل بالقيام، فالذي نختاره أنه مستحب لمن كان فيه فضيلة

ظاهرة من علم أو صلاح أو شرف أو ولاية مصحوبة بصيانة، أوله ولادة أو رحم مع

سن ونحو ذلك، ويكون هذا القيام للبر والإكرام والاحترام، لا للرياء

والإعظام، وعلى هذا الذي اخترناه استمر عمل السلف والخلف، وقد جمعت في ذلك

جزءا جمعت فيه الأحاديث والآثار وأقوال السلف وأفعالهم الدالة على ما

ذكرته، ذكرت فيه ما خالفها، وأوضحت الجواب عنه، فمن أشكل عليه من ذلك شئ

ورغب في مطالعة ذلك الجزء
# رجوت أن يزول إشكاله إن شاء الله تعالى،  والله أعلم.
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ب-ش-ش (bashasha)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to be cheerful, to greet with a radiant and open countenance"; al-bishr is the gladness that appears on the face.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, bashāshah denotes the outward manifestation of inward amity (ulfah) and sincerity (nuṣḥ), a praiseworthy trait of the believer's character.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — a physical brightness of the face; metaphorical (majāz) — the spiritual disposition of warmth and welcome that the face reveals.
- Root: ح-ن-ي (ḥanā)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To bend, curve, or bow the back; ḥaniyya is the bending of the spine in humility or servility.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Kalām, bowing (ḥanī) is a bodily posture of veneration; its permissibility depends on intent — if directed toward a creature in a manner reserved for worship, it is prohibited.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — physical curvature; metaphorical — abasement of the self before another, which is censured except toward Allah.
- Root: ق-و-م (qāma)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To stand, rise, or arise; qiyām is the act of standing upright.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Qiyām in social contexts is an honorific gesture; its ruling hinges on the presence of a praiseworthy attribute (faḍīlah) in the one honored, and the purity of the intention behind the act.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — rising from a seated position; metaphorical — the elevation of esteem and reverence (ikrām) for a person of merit.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Coordination) — In the phrase "البشاشة بالوجه، والدعاء بالمغفرة" the conjunction (wāw) coordinates two verbal nouns (maṣdars) governed by the same implicit verb (yustaḥabbu), indicating that both actions are equally recommended. Also, the Rule of Ḥāl (Circumstantial Clause) — "بوجه طليق" functions as a ḥāl describing the state of the subject when meeting, requiring the accusative in classical parsing.
chapters.translation:
**Section: On the Recommendation of Cheerfulness of Countenance and Supplication for Forgiveness Alongside the Handshake**

I say: It is recommended, alongside the handshake, to greet with a cheerful face and to supplicate for forgiveness and other blessings.

**761** — We have related in *Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim*, on the authority of Abū Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said to me: "Do not belittle any act of goodness, even if it be that you meet your brother with a cheerful countenance."

**769** — And we have related in the book of Ibn al-Sunnī, on the authority of al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Verily, when two Muslims meet and shake hands, and exchange mutual affection and sincere counsel, their sins fall away between them." In another narration: "When two Muslims meet and shake hands, and praise Allah the Exalted and seek His forgiveness, Allah the Mighty and Majestic forgives them both."

**770** — And we have related therein, on the authority of Anas (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), who said: "There are no two servants who love each other for the sake of Allah, and one of them meets his companion and shakes his hand, and they both send blessings upon the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), except that they do not part until their sins — both past and future — are forgiven."

**771** — And we have related therein, also on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) never took a man's hand and parted from him without saying: "O Allah, grant us in this world goodness, and in the Hereafter goodness, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire."

**Section: On the Disapproval of Bowing the Back in All Circumstances for Everyone**

I say: It is disapproved (makrūh) to bow the back in every situation, for every person. This is indicated by what we have already presented in the two preceding sections, namely the ḥadīth of Anas, and his saying: "Should he bow to him? He said: No." This is a ḥasan (good) ḥadīth, as we have mentioned, and no opposing report has come to contradict it. Therefore, there is no recourse to opposing it. And let no one be deceived by the multitude of those who practice it, even among those attributed to knowledge, piety, or other virtuous qualities — for emulation is only of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him). Allah the Exalted said: {«وما آتاكم الرسول فخذوه وما نهاكم عنه فانتهوا»} ["And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you, abstain from it"] (al-Ḥashr: 7). And He the Exalted said: {«فليحذر الذين يخالفون عن أمره أن تصيبهم فتنة أو يصيبهم عذاب أليم»} ["So let those who oppose his command beware, lest a trial befall them or a painful punishment strike them"] (al-Nūr: 63). And we have already presented in the *Book of Funerals*, on the authority of al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ (may Allah be pleased with him), the meaning of his words: Follow the paths of guidance, and let not the scarcity of travelers harm you; and beware of the paths of misguidance, and be not deceived by the multitude of the perishing. And with Allah is the success.

**Section: On Honoring the One Who Enters by Standing**

I say: As for honoring the one who enters by standing up (qiyām), what we choose is that it is recommended (mustaḥabb) for one who possesses a manifest virtue — whether of knowledge, piety, nobility, or a position of authority accompanied by integrity — or for one who has a tie of lineage or kinship, combined with age and the like. This standing should be for the sake of kindness, honor, and reverence, not for ostentation (riyāʾ) or self-aggrandizement. Upon this choice of ours, the practice of the predecessors (salaf) and successors (khalaf) has continued. I have compiled on this matter a separate treatise in which I gathered the ḥadīths, the reports (āthār), the sayings of the predecessors, and their actions that indicate what I have mentioned. I also mentioned therein what contradicts them, and I clarified the answer to it. So whoever finds any of this problematic and wishes to examine that treatise, I hope that his difficulty will be resolved, Allah the Exalted willing. And Allah knows best.

# فصل:
# يستحب استحبابا متأكدا: زيارة الصالحين، والإخوان، والجيران، والأصدقاء،

والأقارب، وإكرامهم، وبرهم، وصلتهم، وضبط ذلك يختلف باختلاف أحوالهم

ومراتبهم وفراغهم.
# وينبغي أن تكون زيارته لهم على وجه لا يكرهونه، وفي وقت يرتضونه.
# والأحاديث والآثار في هذا كثيرة مشهورة.

| 772 - 
# ومن أحسنها ما رويناه في " صحيح مسلم " عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن

النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم " أن رجلا زار أخا له في قرية أخرى، فأرصد الله

تعالى على مدرجته ملكا (1) ، فلما أتى عليه قال: أين تريد؟ قال: أريد أخا

لي في هذه القرية، قال: هل لك عليه من نعمة تربها؟ قال: لا، غير أني أحببته

في الله تعالى، قال: فإني رسول الله إليك بأن الله تعالى قد أحبك كما

أحببته فيه ".
# قلت: مدرجته بفتح الميم والراء والجيم: طريقه.
# ومعنى تربها: أي تحفظها وتراعيها وتربيها كما يربي الرجل ولده.

| 773 - 
# وروينا في كتابي الترمذي وابن ماجه عن أبي هريرة أيضا قال: قال

# رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " من عاد مريضا، أو زار أخا له في الله

تعالى، ناداه مناد بأن طبت وطاب ممشاك، وتبوأت من الجنة منزلا " (1) .
# ، [فصل في استحباب طلب الإنسان من صاحبه الصالح أن يزوره، وأن يكثر من

زيارته] .

| 774 - 
# روينا في " صحيح البخاري " عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: قال النبي

صلى الله عليه وسلم
# لجبريل صلى الله عليه وسلم: " ما يمنعك أن تزورنا أكثر مما تزورنا؟ فنزلت

(وما نتنزل إلا بأمر ربك، له ما بين أيدينا وما خلفنا) [مريم: 64] .

| (باب تشميت العاطس وحكم التثاؤب)

| 775 - 
# روينا في " صحيح البخاري " عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله

عليه وسلم قال: " إن الله تعالى يحب العطاس، ويكره التثاؤب، فإذا عطس أحدكم

وحمد الله تعالى، كان حقا على كل مسلم سمعه أن يقول له: يرحمك الله.
# وأما التثاؤب، فإنما هو من الشيطان، فإذا تثاءب أحدكم، فليرده ما استطاع،

فإن أحدكم إذا تثاءب ضحك منه الشيطان ".
# قلت: قال العلماء: معناه: أن العطاس  سببه محمود، وهو خفة الجسم التي تكون

لقلة الأخلاط وتخفيف الغذاء، وهو أمر مندوب إليه، لأنه يضعف الشهوة ويسهل

الطاعة، والتثاؤب بضد ذلك، والله أعلم.

| 776 - 
# وروينا في " صحيح البخاري " عن أبي هريرة أيضا عن النبي صلى الله عليه

وسلم قال: " إذا عطس أحدكم فليقل: الحمد لله، وليقل له أخوه أو صاحبه:

يرحمك الله، فإذا قال له: يرحمك الله، فليقل: يهديكم الله ويصلح بالكم "

قال العلماء: بالكم: أي شأنكم.

| 777 - 
# وروينا في " صحيحي البخاري ومسلم " عن أنس رضي الله عنه قال: " عطس رجلان

عند النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم " فشمت أحدهما، ولم يشمت الآخر، فقال الذي لم

يشمته: عطس فلان فشمته، وعطست فلم تشمتني، فقال: هذا حمد الله تعالى، وإنك

لم تحمد الله تعالى ".

| 778 - 
# وروينا في " صحيح مسلم " عن أبي موسى الأشعري رضي الله عنه قال: (1) وهو

حديث حسن شواهده.
# (*)
# 
# سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: " إذا عطس أحدكم فحمد الله

تعالى فشمتوه، فإن لم يحمد الله فلا تشمتوه ".

| 779 - 
# وروينا في " صحيحيهما " عن البراء رضي الله عنه قال: " أمرنا رسول الله

صلى الله عليه وسلم بسبع، ونهانا عن سبع: أمرنا بعيادة المريض، واتباع

الجنازة، وتشميت العاطس، وإجابة الداعي، ورد السلام، ونصر المظلوم، وإبرار

القسم " (1) .
# وروينا في " صحيحيهما " عن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "

حق المسلم على المسلم خمس: رد السلام، وعيادة المريض، واتباع الجنائز،

وإجابة الدعوة وتشميت العاطس ".
# وفي رواية لمسلم " حق المسلم على المسلم ست: إذا لقيته فسلم عليه، وإذا

دعاك فأجبه، وإذا استنصحك فانصح له، وإذا عطس فحمد الله تعالى فشمته، وإذا

مرض فعده، وإذا مات فاتبعه ".
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ز-و-ر (z-w-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to incline, to turn toward, to visit" — a deliberate act of approaching another, whether physically or in intent.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, ziyārah denotes a pious act of drawing near to a fellow believer for the sake of Allah, not for worldly benefit — a form of qurbah (devotional approach).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) = physical visitation; metaphorical (majāz) = spiritual inclination or seeking favor. Here, the literal sense is primary, but the intent (niyyah) elevates it to worship.
- Root: ع-ط-س (ʿ-ṭ-s)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root denotes "sneezing" — a sudden, involuntary expulsion of breath, linked to bodily lightness and health.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The act is a sign of divine favor (lightness of body), thus praiseworthy; its opposite, yawning (tathāʾub), stems from heaviness and is attributed to Satan.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal = the physical act; metaphorical = the spiritual state it reflects (gratitude vs. negligence).
- Root: ش-م-ت (sh-m-t)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to rejoice at another's misfortune" — but in Islamic usage, it is inverted to mean "to pray for mercy upon the sneezer," a lexical shift from blame to blessing.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technically, it is the prescribed response (tashmīt) to a believer's praise of Allah, transforming a natural event into a communal act of supplication.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal = rejoicing; metaphorical (majāz) = the ritual blessing, as the root is repurposed by sacred law (sharʿ).
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Imperative Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-jazāʾ) — The phrase "if one of you sneezes and praises Allah, it is incumbent upon every Muslim who hears him to say..." uses a conditional clause (sharṭ) with an implied imperative (jazāʾ), governing the legal obligation (wujūb) in the apodosis.
chapters.translation:
I say: It is highly recommended (mustaḥabb taʾakkud) to visit the righteous, brothers, neighbors, friends, and relatives, and to honor them, treat them with kindness, and maintain ties with them. The precise manner of this varies according to their differing conditions, ranks, and availability. One should visit them in a manner they do not dislike, and at a time they approve of. The hadiths and reports on this matter are numerous and well-known.

| 772 — Among the finest of these is what we have related in "Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim," on the authority of Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him): "A man visited his brother in another village. Allah the Exalted stationed an angel on his path. When he came upon him, the angel said: 'Where do you intend to go?' He replied: 'I intend to visit a brother of mine in this village.' The angel said: 'Do you have any favor from him that you seek to preserve?' He said: 'No, except that I love him for the sake of Allah the Exalted.' The angel said: 'Then I am a messenger from Allah to you, informing you that Allah the Exalted loves you just as you love him for His sake.'"

I say: His word "madratihi" (مدرجته) — with the fatḥah on the mīm, rāʾ, and jīm — means "his path." The meaning of "tarubbuhā" (تربها) is: you preserve it, care for it, and nurture it, just as a man nurtures his child.

| 773 — We have related in the two books of al-Tirmidhī and Ibn Mājah, also on the authority of Abū Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever visits a sick person, or visits a brother of his for the sake of Allah the Exalted, a caller calls out to him: 'You have been purified, and your walking is purified, and you have taken up a dwelling in Paradise.'"

[Section on the recommendation for a person to ask his righteous companion to visit him, and to increase his visits to him.]

| 774 — We have related in "Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī," on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said to Gabriel (peace be upon him): "What prevents you from visiting us more often than you do?" Then the verse was revealed: {«And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord; to Him belongs what is before us and what is behind us»} [Maryam: 64].

(Chapter on Blessing the Sneezer and the Ruling on Yawning)

| 775 — We have related in "Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī," on the authority of Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), who said: "Indeed, Allah the Exalted loves sneezing and dislikes yawning. So if one of you sneezes and praises Allah the Exalted, it is incumbent upon every Muslim who hears him to say to him: 'May Allah have mercy on you.' As for yawning, it is from Satan. So if one of you yawns, let him suppress it as much as he can, for when one of you yawns, Satan laughs at him."

I say: The scholars have said: Its meaning is that sneezing has a praiseworthy cause — namely, the lightness of the body that results from a reduction of humors and the lightening of food intake. This is a commendable matter, because it weakens desire and facilitates obedience. Yawning is the opposite of that. And Allah knows best.

| 776 — We have related in "Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī," also on the authority of Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), who said: "If one of you sneezes, let him say: 'Praise be to Allah' (al-ḥamdu lillāh), and let his brother or companion say to him: 'May Allah have mercy on you' (yarḥamuka Allāh). And when he says to him: 'May Allah have mercy on you,' let him reply: 'May Allah guide you and set your affairs right' (yahdīkum Allāh wa yuṣliḥ bālakum)." The scholars said: "Bālakum" (بالكم) means "your affair" (shaʾnakum).

| 777 — We have related in the two "Ṣaḥīḥs" of al-Bukhārī and Muslim, on the authority of Anas (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "Two men sneezed in the presence of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him). He blessed one of them and did not bless the other. The one who was not blessed said: 'So-and-so sneezed and you blessed him, but I sneezed and you did not bless me.' He said: 'This one praised Allah the Exalted, but you did not praise Allah the Exalted.'"

| 778 — We have related in "Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim," on the authority of Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) say: "If one of you sneezes and praises Allah the Exalted, then bless him. But if he does not praise Allah, then do not bless him." (This is a hadith with sound supporting witnesses.)

| 779 — We have related in the two "Ṣaḥīḥs," on the authority of al-Barāʾ (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) commanded us to do seven things and forbade us from seven: He commanded us to visit the sick, follow funeral processions, bless the sneezer, accept invitations, return greetings of peace, support the oppressed, and fulfill oaths." We have also related in the two "Ṣaḥīḥs," on the authority of Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), who said: "The right of a Muslim upon a Muslim is five: returning the greeting of peace, visiting the sick, following funeral processions, accepting invitations, and blessing the sneezer." In a narration of Muslim: "The right of a Muslim upon a Muslim is six: When you meet him, greet him with peace; when he invites you, accept; when he seeks your counsel, advise him sincerely; when he sneezes and praises Allah, bless him; when he falls ill, visit him; and when he dies, follow his funeral."

chapters.title_en: Section 110 — On Sneezing, Praising Allah, and the Response of Blessing (Tashmīt)
chapters.arabic_text:
# فصل:
# اتفق العلماء على أنه يستحب للعاطس أن يقول عقب عطاسه: الحمد لله، فلو

قال: الحمد لله رب العالمين كان أحسن، ولو قال: الحمد لله على كل حال كان

أفضل.

| 780 - 
# روينا في سنن أبي داود وغيره بإسناد صحيح عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن

النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " إذا  عطس أحدكم فليقل: الحمد لله على كل

حال، وليقل أخوه أو صاحبه: يرحمك الله، ويقول هو: يهديكم الله ويصلح بالكم

".

| 781 - 
# وروينا في كتاب الترمذي عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما " أن رجلا عطس إلى

جنبه فقال: الحمد لله والسلام على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، فقال ابن

عمر: وأنا أقول: الحمد لله والسلام على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، وليس

هكذا علمنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، علمنا أن نقول: الحمد لله على كل

حال " (2) .
# قلت: ويستحب لكل من سمعه أن يقول له: يرحمك الله، أو يرحمكم الله، أو

# رحمك الله، أو رحمكم الله.
# ويستحب للعاطس بعد ذلك أن يقول: يهديكم الله ويصلح بالكم، أو يغفر الله

لنا ولكم 782 - وروينا في " موطأ مالك " عنه عن نافع عن ابن عمر رضي الله

عنهما أنه قال: إذا عطس أحدكم فقيل له: يرحمك الله، يقول: يرحمنا الله

وإياكم، ويغفر الله لنا ولكم (1) .
# وكل هذا سنة ليس فيه شئ واجب، قال أصحابنا: والتشميت وهو قوله: يرحمك

الله، سنة على الكفاية، لو قاله بعض الحاضرين أجزأ عنهم، ولكن الأفضل أن

يقوله كل واحد منهم لظاهر قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم في الحديث الصحيح الذي

قدمناه: 783 - " كان حقا على كل مسلم سمعه أن يقول له: يرحمك الله " وهذا

الذي ذكرناه من استحباب التشميت هو مذهبنا.
# واختلف أصحاب مالك في وجوبه، فقال القاضي عبد الوهاب: هو سنة، ويجزئ

تشميت واحد من الجماعة كمذهبنا، وقال ابن مزين: يلزم كل واحد منهم، واختاره

ابن العربي المالكي.

# فصل:
# إذا لم يحمد العاطس لا يشمت، للحديث المتقدم، وأقل الحمد والتشميت وجوابه

أن يرفع صوته بحيث يسمع صاحبه.

# فصل:
# إذا قال العاطس لفظا آخر غير " الحمد لله " لم يستحق التشميت.

| 784 - 
# روينا في سنن أبي داود والترمذي عن سالم بن عبيد الأشجعي الصحابي رضي

الله تعالى (2) عنه قال: " بينا نحن عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذ

عطس رجل من القوم، فقال: السلام عليكم، فقال  رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

وعليك وعلى أمك (3) ، ثم قال: إذا عطس أحدكم فليحمد الله تعالى، فذكر بعض

المحامد، وليقل له من عنده: يرحمك الله،
# وليرد - يعني عليهم - يغفر الله لنا ولكم " (4) .

# فصل:
# إذا عطس في صلاته يستحب أن يقول: الحمد لله، ويسمع نفسه، هذا 
# مذهبنا.
# ولأصحاب مالك ثلاثة أقوال.
# أحدها هذا، واختاره ابن العربي! والثاني: يحمد في نفسه، والثالث قاله

سحنون: لا يحمد جهرا ولا في نفسه.

# فصل:
# السنة إذا جاءه العطاس أن يضع يده أو ثوبه أو نحو ذلك على فمه، وأن يخفض

صوته.

| 785 - 
# روينا في سنن أبي داود والترمذي عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: " كان

الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا عطس وضع يده أو ثوبه على فمه، وخفض أو غض بها

صوته - شك الراوي أي اللفظين قال - قال الترمذي: حديث صحيح.

| 786 - 
# وروينا في كتاب ابن السني عن عبد الله بن الزبير رضي الله عنهما قال: قال

رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " إن الله عز وجل يكره رفع الصوت بالتثاؤب

والعطاس " (1) .

| 787 - 
# وروينا فيه عن أم سلمة رضي الله عنها قالت: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه

وسلم يقول: " التثاؤب الرفيع والعطسة الشديدة من الشيطان ".
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ح-م-د (ḥ-m-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of praise (ḥamd) as deliberate, conscious commendation of the praised one's excellence, contrasted with mere thanks (shukr) which is a response to benefit.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, ḥamd is the acknowledgment of Allah's absolute perfection and beneficence, encompassing both praise for His essence and gratitude for His acts.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — verbal praise; metaphorical (majāz) — the state of being praiseworthy (maḥmūd) itself. Here, the phrase "al-ḥamdu lillāh" is literal speech act, not metaphorical.
- Root: ش-م-ت (sh-m-t)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Root denotes joy at another's misfortune (shamātah); in Islamic legal usage, it is inverted to mean supplicating mercy for the sneezer, a technical transference.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The term tashmīt in the Sunnah is a prayer for divine mercy and well-being, not the pre-Islamic sense of gloating.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Here it is a technical (sharʿī) usage, distinct from its lexical origin — a clear case of naql (transference) from literal to revealed terminology.
- Root: ع-ط-س (ʿ-ṭ-s)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The act of sneezing (ʿuṭās), a natural bodily reflex; root also carries sense of sudden expulsion of air.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In prophetic guidance, sneezing is treated as a sign of divine favor, hence the command to praise; yawning (tathāʾub) is associated with Satanic influence.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — the physical act; metaphorical — the occasion for spiritual response (ḥamd and duʿāʾ).
- Root: ي-س-ر (y-s-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Ease and facility; in the phrase "yashmitu" (to respond), the root here is not used, but the related concept of facilitation appears in "yuṣliḥ" (to set right).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The supplication "yuṣliḥu bālakum" (may Allah set right your state) implies holistic rectification of one's affairs, both worldly and religious.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — repairing or mending; metaphorical — spiritual and moral correction.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Command (Ṣīghat al-Amr) and Conditional Clause (Jumlat al-Sharṭ): The prophetic statements "If one of you sneezes, let him say..." employ the imperative (fiʿl amr) after a conditional (idhā), indicating recommended (mandūb) rather than obligatory action, as context and scholarly consensus (ijmāʿ) confirm.
chapters.translation:
I say: The scholars are unanimously agreed that it is recommended (mustaḥabb) for the one who sneezes to say, immediately after his sneeze: "Praise be to Allah" (al-ḥamdu lillāh). If he says: "Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds" (al-ḥamdu lillāhi rabbi al-ʿālamīn), that is more excellent. And if he says: "Praise be to Allah in every circumstance" (al-ḥamdu lillāhi ʿalā kulli ḥāl), that is most virtuous.

| 780 — We have related in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd and others, with a sound chain of transmission (isnād ṣaḥīḥ), on the authority of Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), that he said: {«If one of you sneezes, let him say: "Praise be to Allah in every circumstance," and let his brother or companion say to him: "May Allah have mercy on you" (yarḥamuka Allāh), and let him respond: "May Allah guide you and set right your state" (yahdīkumu Allāh wa yuṣliḥa bālakum»)}.

| 781 — And we have related in the book of al-Tirmidhī, on the authority of Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both), that a man sneezed beside him and said: "Praise be to Allah, and peace be upon the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him)." Ibn ʿUmar said: "I too say: 'Praise be to Allah, and peace be upon the Messenger of Allah,' but this is not how the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) taught us. He taught us to say: 'Praise be to Allah in every circumstance.'"

I say: It is recommended (mustaḥabb) for everyone who hears him to say to him: "May Allah have mercy on you" (yarḥamuka Allāh), or "May Allah have mercy on you all" (yarḥamkumu Allāh), or "May Allah have mercy on you" (raḥimaka Allāh), or "May Allah have mercy on you all" (raḥimakumu Allāh). And it is recommended for the sneezer, after that, to say: "May Allah guide you and set right your state" (yahdīkumu Allāh wa yuṣliḥa bālakum), or "May Allah forgive us and you" (yaghfiru Allāhu lanā wa lakum).

| 782 — And we have related in the Muwaṭṭaʾ of Mālik, from him (Mālik), from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both), that he said: "When one of you sneezes and it is said to him: 'May Allah have mercy on you,' let him say: 'May Allah have mercy on us and you, and may Allah forgive us and you.'"

All of this is Sunnah (recommended practice); none of it is obligatory (wājib). Our companions (the Shāfiʿīs) said: The tashmīt — that is, one's saying: "May Allah have mercy on you" — is a Sunnah of sufficiency (sunnah ʿalā al-kifāyah). If some of those present say it, it suffices on behalf of all, but it is more virtuous for each one of them to say it, due to the apparent meaning of his saying (peace and blessings be upon him) in the sound ḥadīth we have already presented: | 783 — {«It is a right upon every Muslim who hears him to say to him: "May Allah have mercy on you"»}. This that we have mentioned — the recommendation of tashmīt — is our school (madhhab).

The companions of Mālik differed concerning its obligation. Al-Qāḍī ʿAbd al-Wahhāb said: It is a Sunnah, and the tashmīt of one from the group suffices, just as in our school. Ibn Muzayn said: It is incumbent upon each one of them. And Ibn al-ʿArabī al-Mālikī chose this latter view.

Section: If the sneezer does not praise Allah, he is not to be given tashmīt, due to the aforementioned ḥadīth. And the minimum of the praise (ḥamd), the tashmīt, and its response is that one raise one's voice to the extent that one's companion can hear it.

Section: If the sneezer says some other phrase instead of "Praise be to Allah" (al-ḥamdu lillāh), he does not deserve the tashmīt.

| 784 — We have related in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd and al-Tirmidhī, on the authority of Sālim ibn ʿUbayd al-Ashjaʿī, the Companion (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "While we were with the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him), a man from the people sneezed and said: 'Peace be upon you' (al-salāmu ʿalaykum). The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: 'And upon you and upon your mother.' Then he said: 'When one of you sneezes, let him praise Allah — and he mentioned some of the praises — and let the one with him say to him: "May Allah have mercy on you," and let him respond — meaning to them — "May Allah forgive us and you."'"

Section: If one sneezes during the prayer (ṣalāh), it is recommended that he say: "Praise be to Allah" (al-ḥamdu lillāh), audible to himself only. This is our school (madhhab). The companions of Mālik have three opinions: One of them is this — and Ibn al-ʿArabī chose it. The second: He praises in his heart (fī nafsihi) without moving his tongue. The third — stated by Saḥnūn: He does not praise aloud nor in himself.

Section: It is the Sunnah, when a sneeze comes upon him, that he place his hand, or his garment, or something similar, over his mouth, and that he lower his voice.

| 785 — We have related in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd and al-Tirmidhī, on the authority of Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "When the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) sneezed, he would place his hand or his garment over his mouth, and he would lower or soften his voice with it" — the narrator doubted which of the two wordings he said. Al-Tirmidhī said: A sound ḥadīth (ḥadīth ṣaḥīḥ).

| 786 — And we have related in the book of Ibn al-Sunnī, on the authority of ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: {«Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, dislikes the raising of the voice in yawning and sneezing»}.

| 787 — And we have related therein, on the authority of Umm Salamah (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) say: {«The loud yawn and the violent sneeze are from Satan»}.

chapters.title_en: Section 111 — On Repeated Sneezing, the One Who Sneezes Without Praising Allah, Sneezing of a Jew, Yawning, and the Chapter on Praise
