# فصل:
# إذا تكرر العطاس من إنسان متتابعا، فالسنة أن يشمته لكل مرة إلى أن يبلغ

ثلاث مرات.

| 788 - 
# روينا في " صحيح مسلم " وسنن أبي داود والترمذي عن سلمة بن الأكوع رضي

الله عنه " أنه سمع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وعطس عنده رجل، فقال له:

يرحمك الله، ثم عطس أخرى، فقال له رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: الرجل

مزكوم " هذا لفظ رواية مسلم.
# وأما رواية أبي داود والترمذي فقالا: قال سلمة: " عطس رجل عند رسول الله

صلى الله عليه وسلم وأنا شاهد، فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: يرحمك

الله، ثم عطس الثانية أو الثالثة، فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

يرحمك الله، هذا رجل مزكوم " قال الترمذي: حديث حسن صحيح (2) . 

| 789 - 
# وأما  الذي رويناه في سنن أبي داود والترمذي عن عبيد الله بن رفاعة

الصحابي رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " يشمت

العاطس ثلاثا، فإن زاد، فإن شئت فشمته، وإن شئت فلا " فهو حديث ضعيف (1) ،

قال فيه الترمذي: حديث غريب، وإسناده مجهول. 

| 790 - 
# وروينا في كتاب ابن السني بإسناد فيه رجل لم أتحقق حاله (1) وباقي إسناده

صحيح عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

يقول: " إذا عطس أحدكم فليشمته جليسه، وإن زاد على ثلاثة فهو مزكوم، ولا

يشمت بعد ثلاث ".
# واختلف العلماء فيه، فقال ابن العربي المالكي: قيل: يقال له في الثانية:

إنك مزكوم، وقيل: يقال له في الثالثة، وقيل: في الرابعة، والأصح أنه في

الثالثة.
# قال: والمعنى فيه أنك لست ممن يشمت بعد هذا، لأن هذا الذي بك زكام ومرض،

لا خفة العطاس.
# فإن قيل: فإذا كان مرضا، فكان ينبغي أن يدعى له ويشمت، لأنه أحق بالدعاء

من غيره؟ فالجواب أنه يستحب أن يدعى له لكن غير دعاء العطاس المشروع، بل

دعاء المسلم للمسلم بالعافية والسلامة ونحو ذلك، ولا يكون من باب التشميت.

# فصل:
# إذا عطس ولم يحمد الله تعالى، فقد قدمنا أنه لا يشمت، وكذا لو حمد الله

تعالى ولم يسمعه الإنسان لا يشمته، فإن كانوا جماعة فسمعه بعضهم دون بعض،

فالمختار أنه يشمته من سمعه دون غيره.
# وحكى ابن العربي خلافا في تشميت الذين لم يسمعوا الحمد إذا سمعوا تشميت

صاحبهم، فقيل: يشمته، لأنه عرف عطاسه وحمده بتشميت غيره، وقيل: لا، لأنه لم

يسمعه.
# واعلم أنه إذا لم يحمد أصلا يستحب لمن عنده أن يذكره الحمد، هذا هو

المختار.
# وقد روينا في " معالم السنن " للخطابي نحوه عن الإمام الجليل إبراهيم

النخعي، وهو من باب النصيحة والأمر بالمعروف، والتعاون على البر والتقوى،

وقال ابن العربي: 
# لا يفعل هذا، وزعم أنه جهل من فاعله، وأخطأ في زعمه، بل الصواب استحبابه

لما ذكرناه، وبالله التوفيق.

# فصل فيما إذا عطس يهودي. 

| 791 - 
# روينا في سنن أبي داود والترمذي وغيرهما بالأسانيد الصحيحة عن أبي موسى

الأشعري رضي الله عنه قال: " كان اليهود يتعاطسون عند رسول الله صلى الله

عليه وسلم يرجون أن يقول لهم: يرحمكم الله (1) فيقول: يهديكم الله ويصلح

بالكم " (2) قال الترمذي: حديث حسن صحيح.

# فصل:

| 792 - 
# روينا في " مسند أبي يعلى الموصلي " عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه
# قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " من حدث حديثا فعطس عنده فهو حق

" كل إسناده ثقات متقنون إلا بقية بن الوليد فمختلف فيه، وأكثر الحفاظ

والأئمة يحتجون بروايته عن الشاميين، وقد روي هذا الحديث عن معاوية بن يحيى

الشامي (3) .

# فصل:
# إذا تثاءب، فالسنة أن يرده ما استطاع، للحديث الصحيح الذي قدمناه.

| 793 - 
# والسنة أن يضع يده على فيه، لما رويناه في " صحيح مسلم " عن أبي سعيد

الخدري رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " إذا تثاءب

أحدكم فليمسك بيده على فمه، فإن الشيطان يدخل ".
# قلت: وسواء كان التثاؤب في الصلاة أو خارجها، يستحب وضع اليد على الفم،

وإنما يكره للمصلي وضع يده على فمه في الصلاة إذا لم تكن حاجة كالتثاؤب

وشبهه، والله أعلم.

| (باب المدح)
# اعلم أن مدح الإنسان والثناء عليه بجميل صفاته قد يكون في حضور الممدوح،

وقد يكون بغير حضوره، فأما الذي في غير حضوره، فلا منع منه إلا أن يجازف

المادح ويدخل في الكذب، فيحرم عليه بسبب الكذب لا لكونه مدحا، ويستحب هذا

المدح الذي لا كذب فيه إذا ترتب عليه مصلحة ولم يجر إلى مفسدة بأن يبلغ

الممدوح فيفتتن به، أو غير ذلك.
# وأما المدح في وجه الممدوح فقد جاءت فيه أحاديث تقتضي إباحته أو

استحبابه، وأحاديثه تقتضي المنع منه.
# قال العلماء: وطريق الجمع بين الأحاديث أن يقال: إن كان الممدوح عنده

كمال إيمان، وحسن يقين، ورياضة نفس، ومعرفة تامة، بحيث لا يفتتن، ولا يغتر

بذلك، ولا تلعب به نفسه، فليس بحرام ولا مكروه، وإن خيف عليه شئ من هذه

الأمور،  كره مدحه كراهة شديدة.
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ش م ت (sh-m-t)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To invoke mercy upon a sneezer; the core sense is supplicating for the removal of what is disliked.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A legislated prayer (duʿāʾ) of mercy for the believer who has praised Allah; tied to the etiquette of brotherhood.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally for the verbal formula; metaphorically extended to any act of well-wishing toward a fellow Muslim.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ) — The repeated sneeze is governed by a conditional construction (idhā... fa-), where the protasis sets the legal occasion and the apodosis states the ruling, repeated per occurrence up to the limit of three.
chapters.translation:
**Chapter: If a person sneezes repeatedly in succession, the Sunnah is to invoke mercy upon him (tashmīt) each time until it reaches three times.**

| 788 —
We narrated in "Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim" and the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd and al-Tirmidhī, on the authority of Salamah ibn al-Akwaʿ (may Allah be pleased with him): "That he heard the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) — and a man sneezed in his presence — so he said to him: 'May Allah have mercy on you (yarḥamuka Allāh).' Then he sneezed again, so the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said to him: 'This man is afflicted with a cold (mazkūm).'" This is the wording of the narration of Muslim.
As for the narration of Abū Dāwūd and al-Tirmidhī, they both said: Salamah said: "A man sneezed in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) while I was witnessing, so the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: 'May Allah have mercy on you.' Then he sneezed a second or third time, so the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: 'May Allah have mercy on you. This is a man afflicted with a cold.'" Al-Tirmidhī said: A ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ ḥadīth.

| 789 —
As for what we narrated in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd and al-Tirmidhī, on the authority of ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Rifāʿah, the Companion (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The sneezer is invoked with mercy three times; if he exceeds that, then if you wish, invoke mercy upon him, and if you wish, do not" — this is a weak ḥadīth (ḍaʿīf). Al-Tirmidhī said concerning it: A gharīb ḥadīth, and its chain contains an unknown (majhūl) narrator.

| 790 —
And we narrated in the book of Ibn al-Sunnī with a chain containing a man whose condition I have not verified, while the rest of its chain is sound (ṣaḥīḥ), on the authority of Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) say: "When one of you sneezes, let his companion invoke mercy upon him; and if he exceeds three, then he is afflicted with a cold, and no invocation of mercy is made after three."
The scholars differed concerning this. Ibn al-ʿArabī al-Mālikī said: It was said: One says to him on the second [sneeze]: "You are afflicted with a cold." And it was said: One says it on the third. And it was said: On the fourth. The most correct (al-aṣaḥḥ) is that it is on the third.
He said: The meaning therein is: "You are not one upon whom invocation of mercy is made after this, for what afflicts you is a cold and an illness, not the lightness of sneezing."
If it is said: "Since it is an illness, then it would be fitting to supplicate for him and invoke mercy upon him, for he is more deserving of supplication than others?" The answer is: It is recommended (mustaḥabb) to supplicate for him, but not with the legislated supplication of sneezing (tashmīt). Rather, it is the supplication of a Muslim for a Muslim for well-being (ʿāfiyah) and safety and the like of that, and it does not fall under the category of tashmīt.

**Chapter: If one sneezes and does not praise Allah the Exalted, we have already stated that no invocation of mercy is made upon him. Likewise, if he praises Allah the Exalted but a person does not hear him, no invocation of mercy is made upon him. If they are a group and some of them hear him while others do not, then the chosen position (al-mukhtār) is that the one who heard him invokes mercy upon him, not the others.**
Ibn al-ʿArabī related a difference of opinion concerning the invocation of mercy by those who did not hear the praise (taḥmīd) when they hear the tashmīt of their companion. It was said: They invoke mercy upon him, because they came to know of his sneeze and his praise through the tashmīt of another. And it was said: No, because they did not hear him.
Know that if he does not praise [Allah] at all, it is recommended for the one present with him to remind him of the praise (taḥmīd). This is the chosen position (al-mukhtār).
We have narrated in "Maʿālim al-Sunan" of al-Khaṭṭābī something similar to this, on the authority of the noble Imām Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī. This falls under the category of sincere counsel (naṣīḥah), enjoining good (al-amr bi-l-maʿrūf), and cooperation upon righteousness and piety (al-taʿāwun ʿalā al-birr wa-l-taqwā). Ibn al-ʿArabī said: "One should not do this," and he claimed it is ignorance on the part of the one who does it. He erred in his claim. Rather, the correct view is that it is recommended (istihbāb), for what we have mentioned. And with Allah is the success (tawfīq).

**Chapter: Concerning when a Jew sneezes.**

| 791 —
We narrated in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd and al-Tirmidhī and others, with sound chains (asānīd ṣaḥīḥah), on the authority of Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "The Jews used to sneeze in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him), hoping that he would say to them: 'May Allah have mercy on you (yarḥamkum Allāh).' So he would say: 'May Allah guide you and set right your condition (yahdīkum Allāh wa yuṣliḥ bālakum).'" Al-Tirmidhī said: A ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ ḥadīth.

**Chapter:**

| 792 —
We narrated in the "Musnad of Abū Yaʿlā al-Mawṣilī," on the authority of Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever relates a narration and someone sneezes in his presence, it is true (ḥaqq)." All of its chain consists of trustworthy, precise narrators (thiqāt mutqanūn), except Baqiyyah ibn al-Walīd, concerning whom there is disagreement. Most of the ḥuffāẓ and Imāms adduce his narration from the Syrians (al-Shāmiyyīn) as evidence. This ḥadīth has also been narrated from Muʿāwiyah ibn Yaḥyā al-Shāmī.

**Chapter: If one yawns, the Sunnah is to suppress it as much as one is able, due to the sound ḥadīth we have already presented.**

| 793 —
And the Sunnah is to place one's hand over one's mouth, due to what we narrated in "Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim," on the authority of Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "When one of you yawns, let him hold his hand over his mouth, for indeed the devil (al-shayṭān) enters."
I say: It is the same whether the yawning occurs in prayer or outside of it — it is recommended (mustaḥabb) to place the hand over the mouth. It is only disliked (makrūh) for the one praying to place his hand over his mouth in prayer when there is no need, such as yawning and the like of it. And Allah knows best.

**(Chapter on Praise [al-Madḥ])**
Know that a person's praising (madḥ) and commending (thanāʾ) him for his beautiful attributes may occur in the presence of the one praised, and it may occur in his absence. As for that which occurs in his absence, there is no prohibition against it, except that if the praiser exaggerates (yujāzif) and falls into falsehood (kadhib), then it becomes forbidden (yaḥrum) upon him due to the falsehood, not because it is praise. This praise which contains no falsehood is recommended (mustaḥabb) when a benefit (maṣlaḥah) results from it and it does not lead to a corruption (mafsadah), such as the one praised being informed of it and thus becoming seduced (yuftatan) by it, or other than that.
As for praise in the face of the one praised, there have come narrations (aḥādīth) that indicate its permissibility (ibāḥah) or recommendation (istihbāb), and narrations that indicate prohibition (manʿ) from it.
The scholars said: The way of reconciling (al-jamʿ) between the narrations is to say: If the one praised possesses completeness of faith (kamāl īmān), sound certainty (ḥusn yaqīn), discipline of the soul (riyāḍat nafs), and complete knowledge (maʿrifah tāmmah), such that he is not seduced, nor deceived by that, nor does his soul play with him — then it is neither forbidden (ḥarām) nor disliked (makrūh). But if any of these matters is feared concerning him, then his praise is severely disliked (yukrah karāhiyah shadīdah).

chapters.title_en: Section 112 — On the Prohibition of Excessive Praise (Madḥ) and the Permissibility of Praising When There is a Religious Benefit

| 794 - 
# فمن أحاديث المنع ما رويناه في " صحيح مسلم " عن المقداد رضي الله عنه "

أن رجلا جعل يمدح عثمان رضي الله عنه، فعمد المقداد فجثا على ركبتيه، فجعل

يحثو في وجهه الحصباء (1) ، فقال له عثمان: ما شأنك؟ فقال: إن رسول الله

صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " إذا رأيتم المداحين فاحثوا في وجوههم التراب ".

| 795 - 
# وروينا في " صحيحي البخاري ومسلم " عن أبي موسى الأشعري رضي الله عنه

قال: سمع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم رجلا يثني على رجل ويطريه في المدحة

فقال: أهلكتم أو قطعتم ظهر الرجل ".
# قلت: قوله يطريه، بضم الياء وإسكان الطاء المهملة وكسر الراء وبعدها ياء

مثناة تحت.
# والإطراء: المبالغة في المدح ومجاوزة الحد، وقيل: هو المدح.

| 796 - 
# وروينا في " صحيحيهما " عن أبي بكرة رضي الله عنه " أن رجلا ذكر عند

النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فأثنى عليه رجل خيرا، فقال النبي صلى الله عليه

وسلم: ويحك قطعت عنق صاحبك - يقوله 
# مرارا - إن كان أحدكم مادحا أخاه لا محالة فليقل: أحسب كذا وكذا إن كان

يرى أنه كذلك، وحسيبه الله ولا يزكني على الله أحدا ".
# وأما أحاديث الإباحة فكثيرة لا تنحصر، ولكن نشير إلى أطراف منها.

| 797 - 
# فمنها قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم في الحديث الصحيح لأبي بكر رضي الله عنه:

" ما ظنك باثنين الله ثالثهما؟ ".

| 798 - 
# وفي الحديث الآخر: " لست منهم " أي لست من الذين يسبلون أزرهم خيلاء.

| 799 - 
# وفي الحديث الآخر " يا أبا بكر لا تبك، إن أمن الناس علي في صحبته وماله

أبو بكر، ولو كنت متخذا من أمتي خليلا لاتخذت أبا بكر خليلا ".

| 800 - 
# وفي الحديث الآخر: " أرجو أن تكون منهم " أي من الذين يدعون من جميع

أبواب الجنة لدخولها.

| 801 - 
# وفي الحديث الآخر " ائذن له وبشره بالجنة " 802 - وفي الحديث الآخر "

اثبت أحد فإنما عليك نبي وصديق وشهيدان ".

| 803 - 
# وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " دخلت الجنة فرأيت قصرا، فقلت: لمن

هذا؟ قالوا: لعمر، فأردت أن أدخله، فذكرت  غيرتك، فقال عمر رضي الله عنه:

بأبي وأمي يا رسول الله، أعليك أغار؟ ".

| 804 - 
# وفي الحديث الآخر: " يا عمر ما لقيك الشيطان سالكا مجالا إلا سلك مجالا

غير فجك ".

| 805 - 
# وفي الحديث الآخر: " افتح لعثمان وبشره بالجنة ".

| 806 - 
# وفي الحديث الآخر قال لعلي: " أنت مني وأنا منك ".

| 807 - 
# وفي الحديث الآخر قال لعلي: " أما ترضى أن تكون مني بمنزلة هارون من

موسى؟ ".

| 808 - 
# وفي الحديث الآخر قال لبلال: " سمعت دف نعليك في الجنة ".

| 809 - 
# وفي الحديث الآخر قال لأبي بن كعب: " ليهنأك (1) العلم أبا المنذر ".

| 810 - 
# وفي الحديث الآخر قال لعبد الله بن سلام: " أنت على الإسلام حتى تموت ".

| 811 - 
# وفي الحديث الآخر قال للأنصاري: " ضحك الله عز وجل، أو عجب من فعالكما ".

| 812 - 
# وفي الحديث الآخر قال للأنصار: " أنتم من أحب الناس إلي ".

| 813 - 
# وفي الحديث الآخر قال لأشج عبد القيس: " إن فيك خصلتين يحبهما الله تعالى

ورسوله: الحلم والأناة ".
# وكل هذه الأحاديث التي أشرت إليها في الصحيح مشهورة، فلهذا لم أضفها،

ونظائر ما ذكرناه من مدحه صلى الله عليه وسلم في الوجه كثيرة.
# وأما مدح الصحابة والتابعين فمن بعدهم من العلماء والأئمة الذين يقتدى

بهم رضي الله عنهم أجمعين فأكثر من أن تحصر، والله أعلم.
# قال أبو حامد الغزالي في آخر " كتاب الزكاة " من " الإحياء ": إذا تصدق

إنسان بصدقة، فينبغي للآخذ منه أن ينظر، فإن كان الدافع ممن يحب الشكر

عليها ونشرها فينبغي للآخذ أن يخفيها لأن قضاء حقه أن لا ينصره على الظلم،

وطلبه الشكر ظلم، وإن علم من حاله أنه لا يحب الشكر ولا يقصده فينبغي أن

يشكره ويظهر صدقته.
# وقال سفيان الثوري رحمه الله: من عرف نفسه لم يضره مدح الناس.
# قال أبو حامد الغزالي بعد أن ذكر ما سبق في أول الباب: فدقائق هذه

المعاني ينبغي أن يلحظها من يراعي قلبه، فإن أعمال الجوارح مع إهمال هذه

الدقائق ضحكة للشيطان لكثرة التعب وقلة النفع، ومثل هذا العلم هو الذي

يقال: إن تعلم مسألة منه  أفضل من عبادة سنة، إذ بهذا العلم تحيا عبادة

العمر، وبالجهال به تموت عبادة العمر وبالجهل به تموت عبادة العمر وتتعطل،

وبالله التوفيق.

| (باب مدح الإنسان نفسه وذكر محاسنه)
# قال الله تعالى: (فلا تزكوا أنفسكم) [النجم: 32] اعلم أن ذكر محاسن نفسه

ضربان: مذموم ; ومحبوب، فالمذموم أن يذكره للافتخار وإظهار الارتفاع

والتميز على
# الأقران وشبه ذلك، والمحبوب أن يكون فيه مصلحة دينية، وذلك بأن يكون آمرا

بمعروف، أو ناهيا عن منكر، أو ناصحا أو مشيرا بمصلحة، أو معلما، أو مؤدبا،

أو واعظا، أو مذكرا، أو مصلحا بين اثنين، أو يدفع عن نفسه شرا، أو نحو ذلك،

فيذكر
# 
# محاسنه ناويا بذلك أن يكون هذا أقرب إلى قبول قوله واعتماد ما يذكره، أو

أن هذا الكلام الذي أقوله لا تجدونه عند غيري فاحتفظوا به، أو نحو ذلك، وقد
chapters.anchors:
- Root: م-د-ح (m-d-ḥ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is to praise, commend, or eulogize; the act of describing someone's good qualities.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, madḥ is distinct from shukr (gratitude); madḥ is verbal commendation regardless of prior benefit, while shukr is a response to a specific favor.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage refers to genuine commendation; metaphorical (majāz) usage appears in the prophetic prohibition where "throwing dust in the faces" of excessive praisers is a figurative expression of rebuke and humiliation.
- Root: ط-ر-ي (ṭ-r-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The verb aṭrā (يطري) means to exceed the bounds in praise, to exaggerate commendation.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technically, iṭrāʾ is the blameworthy excess in praise that approaches falsehood or flattery.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Distinguishes between permissible praise (within limits) and iṭrāʾ, which is the rhetorical hyperbole that "cuts the back" of the praised one — a metaphor for causing spiritual harm or arrogance.
- Root: ز-ك-ي (z-k-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To purify, to declare someone pure or righteous; tazkiyah means self-justification or declaring oneself free from fault.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The Quranic prohibition {«فلا تزكوا أنفسكم»} (Q 53:32) forbids self-praise as an act of self-purification before God, since only God knows the true state of hearts.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is purification; metaphorical sense in the verse is claiming purity for oneself, which is blameworthy unless done for a clear religious benefit.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — The phrase "إن كان أحدكم مادحا أخاه لا محالة فليقل" employs a conditional clause with an implied apodosis, and the exceptive "لا محالة" (unavoidably) governs the permissive command, requiring careful parsing of the legal ruling's scope.
chapters.translation:
I say: Among the hadiths of prohibition is what we narrated in "Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim" on the authority of al-Miqdād, may God be pleased with him:

That a man began to praise ʿUthmān, may God be pleased with him, so al-Miqdād deliberately knelt upon his knees and began to scoop up pebbles and throw them in his face. ʿUthmān said to him: "What is the matter with you?" He replied: "Indeed, the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'When you see those who excessively praise, throw dust in their faces.'"

| 795 —
And we narrated in the two "Ṣaḥīḥs" of al-Bukhārī and Muslim, on the authority of Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, heard a man praising another man and exceeding the bounds in his commendation, so he said: "You have destroyed him — or you have cut the man's back."

I say: His statement "yuṭrīhi" (يطريه) — with a ḍammah on the yāʾ, a sukūn on the unpointed ṭāʾ, a kasrah on the rāʾ, followed by a dotted yāʾ (tāʾ marbūṭah form).
And al-iṭrāʾ (الإطراء): is exaggeration in praise and transgressing its bounds; and it is said: it is simply praise [in its blameworthy excess].

| 796 —
And we narrated in the two "Ṣaḥīḥs" on the authority of Abū Bakrah, may God be pleased with him: That a man was mentioned in the presence of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and another man praised him well, so the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Woe to you! You have cut the neck of your companion" — he repeated this several times — "If one of you must praise his brother unavoidably, let him say: 'I consider him to be such-and-such, if he indeed sees him to be so — and God is his reckoner — and I do not declare anyone pure before God.'"

As for the hadiths of permissibility, they are numerous and cannot be enumerated, but I shall point to some of their aspects.

| 797 —
Among them is his statement, peace and blessings be upon him, in the authentic hadith to Abū Bakr, may God be pleased with him: "What do you think of two, the third of whom is God?"

| 798 —
And in the other hadith: "I am not of them" — meaning, I am not of those who drag their garments out of arrogance.

| 799 —
And in the other hadith: "O Abū Bakr, do not weep. Indeed, the most gracious of people to me in his companionship and his wealth is Abū Bakr. And were I to take an intimate friend (khalīl) from my nation, I would have taken Abū Bakr as an intimate friend."

| 800 —
And in the other hadith: "I hope that you will be of them" — meaning, of those who will be called from all the gates of Paradise to enter it.

| 801 —
And in the other hadith: "Permit him and give him glad tidings of Paradise."

| 802 —
And in the other hadith: "Stand firm, O Uḥud, for upon you are a Prophet, a Ṣiddīq, and two martyrs."

| 803 —
And the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "I entered Paradise and saw a palace. I said: 'To whom does this belong?' They said: 'To ʿUmar.' I wanted to enter it, but I remembered your jealousy (ghayrah)." So ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, said: "May my father and mother be your ransom, O Messenger of God — would I be jealous of you?"

| 804 —
And in the other hadith: "O ʿUmar, Satan never meets you traversing a path except that he takes a path other than your path."

| 805 —
And in the other hadith: "Open for ʿUthmān and give him glad tidings of Paradise."

| 806 —
And in the other hadith, he said to ʿAlī: "You are from me, and I am from you."

| 807 —
And in the other hadith, he said to ʿAlī: "Are you not pleased to be from me in the station of Hārūn from Mūsā?"

| 808 —
And in the other hadith, he said to Bilāl: "I heard the sound of your sandals in Paradise."

| 809 —
And in the other hadith, he said to Ubayy ibn Kaʿb: "May knowledge be a source of delight to you, O Abā al-Mundhir."

| 810 —
And in the other hadith, he said to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām: "You shall remain upon Islam until you die."

| 811 —
And in the other hadith, he said to the Anṣārī: "God, the Mighty and Majestic, laughed — or marveled — at your deed."

| 812 —
And in the other hadith, he said to the Anṣār: "You are among the most beloved of people to me."

| 813 —
And in the other hadith, he said to Ashajj ʿAbd al-Qays: "Indeed, in you are two qualities which God, the Exalted, and His Messenger love: forbearance (ḥilm) and deliberateness (anāh)."

All these hadiths to which I have pointed are well-known in the Ṣaḥīḥ collections, and for this reason I did not append their full chains. And the parallels of what we have mentioned of his praise, peace and blessings be upon him, to one's face are numerous.

As for the praise of the Companions, the Followers (Tābiʿūn), and those after them from the scholars and the imams who are followed — may God be pleased with them all — it is more than can be enumerated. And God knows best.

Abū Ḥāmid al-Ghazālī said at the end of the "Book of Zakāh" from the "Iḥyāʾ": When a person gives a charity, the recipient should consider: if the giver is one who loves to be thanked for it and to have it publicized, then the recipient should conceal it, because fulfilling his right is not to assist him in injustice — and his seeking thanks is an injustice. But if he knows from his state that he does not love thanks nor intends it, then he should thank him and publicize his charity.

And Sufyān al-Thawrī, may God have mercy on him, said: Whoever knows his own soul, the praise of people does not harm him.

Abū Ḥāmid al-Ghazālī said, after mentioning what preceded at the beginning of the chapter: The subtleties of these meanings should be observed by whoever watches over his heart. For the deeds of the limbs, with the neglect of these subtleties, are a laughingstock for Satan — due to the abundance of toil and the scarcity of benefit. And this kind of knowledge is that of which it is said: Learning one issue of it is better than a year of worship — for by this knowledge the worship of a lifetime is enlivened, and by ignorance of it the worship of a lifetime dies and becomes void. And with God is the success.

(Section on a Person Praising Himself and Mentioning His Own Virtues)

God, the Exalted, said: {«فلا تزكوا أنفسكم»} (So do not declare yourselves pure) [Q 53:32].

Know that mentioning one's own virtues is of two types: blameworthy and beloved. The blameworthy is when one mentions them for pride, to display elevation and distinction over one's peers, and the like. The beloved is when there is a religious benefit in it — such as when one is commanding good, forbidding evil, giving sincere counsel, advising toward a benefit, teaching, disciplining, preaching, reminding, reconciling between two people, or repelling harm from oneself, or the like. In such cases, one mentions his virtues intending thereby that this will be more conducive to the acceptance of his words and reliance upon what he states — or that this statement which I utter you will not find with anyone other than me, so preserve it — or the like. And [this is permissible].

chapters.title_en: Section 113 — On Praiseworthy Self-Description and Laudatory Addresses (Bāb fī Masāʾil Tataʿallaqu bi-mā Taqaddam)
chapters.arabic_text:
جاء في هذا المعنى ما لا يحصى من النصوص، كقول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:

814 - " أنا النبي لا كذب ".

| 815 - 
# " أنا سيد ولد آدم ".
# " أنا أول من تنشق عنه الأرض ".
# " أنا أعلمكم بالله وأتقاكم ".

| 816 - 
# " إني أبيت عند ربي ".
# وأشباهه كثيرة، وقال يوسف صلى الله عليه وسلم: " (اجعلني على خزائن الأرض

إني حفيظ عليم) [يوسف: 55] وقال شعيب صلى الله عليه وسلم: (ستجدني إن شاء

الله من الصالحين) [القصص: 27] .

| 817 - 
# وقال عثمان رضي الله عنه حين حصر ما رويناه في " صحيح البخاري " أنه قال:

ألستم تعلمون أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " من جهز جيش العسرة

(1) فله الجنة؟ فجهزتهم، ألستم تعلمون أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

قال: من حفر بئر رومة (2) فله الجنة، فحفرتها؟ فصدقوه بما قال ".

| 818 - 
# وروينا في " صحيحيهما " عن سعد بن أبي وقاص رضي الله عنه أنه قال حين

شكاه أهل الكوفة إلى عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه وقالوا: لا يحسن يصلي،

فقال سعد: والله إني لأول رجل من العرب رمى بسهم في سبيل الله تعالى، ولقد

كنا نغزو مع
# رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ... وذكر  تمام الحديث.

| 819 - 
# وروينا في " صحيح مسلم " عن علي رضي الله عنه قال: " والذي فلق الحبة

وبرأ النسمة، إنه لعهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إلي أنه لا يحبني إلا مؤمن

ولا يبغضني إلا منافق ".
# قلت: برأ مهموز معناه: خلق، والنسمة: النفس.

| 820 - 
# وروينا في " صحيحيهما "، عن أبي وائل قال: خطبنا ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه

فقال: " والله لقد أخذت من في رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) بضعا وسبعين

سورة، ولقد علم أصحاب رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) أني من أعلمهم بكتاب

الله تعالى، وما أنا بخيرهم، ولو أعلم أن أحدا أعلم مني لرحلت إليه ".

| 821 - 
# وروينا في " صحيح مسلم " عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أنه سئل عن البدنة

إذا أزحفت (1) فقال: على الخبير سقطت - يعني نفسه - ... وذكر تمام الحديث.
# ونظائر هذا كثيرة لا تنحصر، وكلها محمولة على ما ذكرنا، وبالله التوفيق.

| (باب في مسائل تتعلق بما تقدم)

# مسألة: يستحب إجابة من ناداك: " لبيك وسعديك " أو " لبيك " وحدها، ويستحب

أن يقول لمن ورد عليه: مرحبا، وأن يقول لمن أحسن إليه أو رأى منه فعلا

جميلا: حفظك الله، وجزاك الله خيرا، وما أشبهه، ودلائل هذا من الحديث

الصحيح كثيرة مشهورة.

# مسألة: ولا بأس بقوله للرجل الجليل في علمه أو صلاحه أو نحو ذلك: جعلني

الله فداك، أو فداك أبي وأمي وما أشبهه، ودلائل هذا من الحديث الصحيح كثيرة

مشهورة حذفتها اختصارا.
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ح-ف-ظ (ḥ-f-ẓ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To guard, preserve, retain; vigilance in keeping something safe from loss or corruption.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, ḥifẓ denotes divine preservation of revelation and the believer’s custodianship of sacred knowledge.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — physical guarding; metaphorical (majāz) — intellectual retention and moral fidelity.
- Root: خ-ب-ر (kh-b-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Knowledge of a matter’s inner reality; one who is expert (khabīr) through direct acquaintance.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Khabar as reported information; khabīr as the one possessing certain, tested knowledge — applied to God and to qualified scholars.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — news conveyed; metaphorical — the expert’s authoritative judgment, as in “upon the expert you have fallen” (ʿalā al-khabīr saqaṭt).
- Root: ن-س-م (n-s-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Breath, soul, living being; nasamah as the individual creature endowed with spirit.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Nasamah denotes the rational soul in its creaturely origin, distinct from rūḥ in emphasizing embodied life.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — breathing entity; metaphorical — every human person as a responsible agent.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — When the Prophet (ﷺ) says “I am the master of the sons of Adam,” the following clauses (“I am the first from whom the earth will split,” etc.) function as explicative appositions, each reinforcing the same laudatory import without implying rivalry or vainglory.
chapters.translation:
Know that concerning this meaning — namely, the permissibility of a person mentioning his own praiseworthy qualities when there is a sound religious purpose — there have come texts beyond enumeration, such as the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ):

814 — “I am the Prophet; there is no falsehood.”

815 — “I am the master of the sons of Adam.” And: “I am the first from whom the earth will be split open.” And: “I am the most knowing of you concerning God, and the most God-fearing of you.”

816 — “Indeed, I spend the night with my Lord.” And similar reports are numerous. And Joseph (upon him be peace) said: {«اجعلني على خزائن الأرض إني حفيظ عليم»} [Yūsuf: 55] — “Appoint me over the treasuries of the earth; indeed, I am a knowledgeable guardian.” And Shuʿayb (upon him be peace) said: {«ستجدني إن شاء الله من الصالحين»} [Al-Qaṣaṣ: 27] — “You will find me, if God wills, among the righteous.”

817 — And ʿUthmān (may God be pleased with him) said, at the time he was besieged, that which we have related in “Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī”: He said: “Do you not know that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: ‘Whoever equips the army of distress (jaysh al-ʿusrah) shall have Paradise’? So I equipped them. Do you not know that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: ‘Whoever digs the well of Rūmah shall have Paradise’? So I dug it.” And they affirmed the truth of what he said.

818 — And we have related in the two “Ṣaḥīḥs” (of al-Bukhārī and Muslim), on the authority of Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ (may God be pleased with him), that he said when the people of Kūfah complained of him to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb (may God be pleased with him) and said: “He does not pray well” — Saʿd said: “By God, I am the first man among the Arabs who shot an arrow in the path of God the Exalted, and indeed we used to go on raids with the Messenger of God (ﷺ)…” — and he mentioned the rest of the ḥadīth.

819 — And we have related in “Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim,” on the authority of ʿAlī (may God be pleased with him), that he said: “By Him who splits the seed and creates the soul (nasamah), it is indeed the covenant of the Prophet (ﷺ) to me that none loves me except a believer, and none hates me except a hypocrite.” I say: “barāʾa” (with hamzah) means “He created,” and “al-nasamah” means “the soul.”

820 — And we have related in the two “Ṣaḥīḥs,” on the authority of Abū Wāʾil, who said: Ibn Masʿūd (may God be pleased with him) addressed us and said: “By God, I have taken from the mouth of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) seventy-odd sūrahs, and the companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) indeed knew that I am the most knowledgeable of them concerning the Book of God the Exalted, and I am not the best of them. And if I knew that anyone was more knowledgeable than I, I would have traveled to him.”

821 — And we have related in “Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim,” on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās (may God be pleased with them both), that he was asked about a sacrificial camel (badanah) that had become lame (uzḥifat), and he said: “Upon the expert you have fallen” — meaning himself — and he mentioned the rest of the ḥadīth.

And parallels to this are many, not to be confined, and all of them are to be interpreted according to what we have mentioned — namely, that such self-praise is permissible when it serves a religious interest, such as establishing a proof, encouraging good, or repelling harm — and with God is the success.

[Section on Questions Related to What Has Preceded]

Question: It is recommended (mustaḥabb) to answer the one who calls you with “Labbayka wa-saʿdayk” (Here I am at your service, and at your happiness) or “Labbayk” alone. And it is recommended to say to the one who comes to you: “Marḥaban” (Welcome), and to say to the one who has done good to you or from whom you have seen a beautiful act: “Ḥafiẓaka Allāh” (May God preserve you), and “Jazāka Allāh khayran” (May God reward you with good), and the like of that. And the evidences for this from the authentic ḥadīth are many and well-known.

Question: And there is no harm in one’s saying to a man of eminence in his knowledge, or his righteousness, or the like of that: “Jaʿalanī Allāhu fidāk” (May God make me your ransom), or “Fidāka abī wa-ummī” (May my father and mother be your ransom), and the like of that. And the evidences for this from the authentic ḥadīth are many and well-known, which I have omitted for the sake of brevity.

chapters.title_en: Section 114 — On Women's Speech with Non-Mahram Men, and the Etiquette of Proposing Marriage
chapters.arabic_text:
# مسألة: إذا احتاجت المرأة إلى كلام غير المحارم في بيع أو شراء، أو غير

ذلك من المواضع التي يجوز لها كلامه فيها، فينبغي أن تفخم عبارتها وتغلظها

ولا تلينها مخافة من طمعه فيها.
# قال الإمام أبو الحسن الواحدي من أصحابنا في كتابه " البسيط ": قال

أصحابنا: المرأة مندوبة إذا خاطبت الأجانب إلى الغلظة في المقالة، لأن ذلك

أبعد من الطمع في الريبة، وكذلك إذا خاطبت محرما عليها بالمصاهرة، ألا ترى

أن الله تعالى أوصى أمهات المؤمنين وهن محرمات على التأبيد بهذه الوصية،

فقال تعالى: (يا نساء النبي لستن  كأحد من النساء إن اتقيتن فلا تخضعن

بالقول فيطمع الذي في قلبه مرض) [الأحزاب: 32] 
# قلت: هذا الذي ذكره الواحدي من تغليظ صوتها، كذا قاله أصحابنا.
# قال الشيخ إبراهيم المروزي من أصحابنا، طريقها في تغليظه أن تأخذ ظهر

كفها بفيها وتجيب كذلك، والله أعلم.
# وهذا الذي ذكره الواحدي من أن المحرم بالمصاهرة كالأجنبي في هذا ضعيف

وخلاف المشهور عند أصحابنا، لأنه كالمحرم بالقرابة في جواز النظر والخلوة.
# وأما أمهات المؤمنين، فإنهن أمهات في تحريم نكاحهن ووجوب احترامهن فقط،

ولهذا يحل نكاح بناتهن، والله أعلم.

| كتاب أذكار النكاح وما يتعلق به

| (باب ما يقوله من جاء يخطب امرأة من أهلها لنفسه أو لغيره)
# يستحب أن يبدأ الخاطب بالحمد لله والثناء عليه والصلاة على رسول الله

(صلى الله عليه وسلم) ويقول: أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له،

وأشهد أن محمدا عبده ورسوله، جئتكم راغبا في فتاتكم فلانة، أو في كريمتكم

فلانة بنت فلان أو نحو ذلك.

| 822 - 
# روينا في " سنن أبي داود وابن ماجه " وغيرهما، عن أبي هريرة رضي الله

عنه، عن رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) قال: " كل كلام " وفي بعض الروايات

" كل أمر لا يبدأ فيه بالحمد لله فهو أجذم " وروي " أقطع " وهما بمعنى، هذا

حديث حسن (1) .
# وأجذم بالجيم والذال المعجمة ومعناه: قليل البركة.

| 823 - 
# وروينا في " سنن أبي داود والترمذي " عن أبي هريرة عن النبي (صلى الله

عليه وسلم) قال: " كل خطبة ليس فيها تشهد فهي كاليد الجذماء " قال الترمذي:

حديث حسن.

| (باب عرض الرجل بنته وغيرها ممن) إليه تزويجها على أهل الفضل والخير ليتزوجوها)

| 824 - 
# روينا في " صحيح البخاري " أن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه لما توفي زوج

بنته حفصة رضي الله عنهما قال: لقيت عثمان فعرضت عليه حفصة فقلت: إن شئت

# أنكحتك حفصة بنت عمر، فقال: سأنظر في أمري (1) ، فلبثت ليالي ثم لقيني

فقال: قد بدا لي أن لا أتزوج يومي هذا، قال عمر: فلقيت أبا بكر الصديق رضي

الله عنه، فقلت:  إن شئت أنكحتك حفصة بنت عمر، فصمت أبو بكر رضي الله عنه

... وذكر تمام
chapters.anchors:
- Root: غ ل ظ (gh-l-ẓ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Coarseness, thickness, severity; the opposite of softness and delicacy in both physical and verbal substance.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological discourse, denotes firmness of address that repels base inclination, aligning with the Quranic command to avoid seductive softening (takhḍīʿ).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical roughness; metaphorical (majāz) for speech stripped of allure, functioning as a protective barrier.
- Root: خ ض ع (kh-ḍ-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Submissiveness, lowering, yielding; in speech, a pliant or compliant tone.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The Quranic prohibition (takhḍaʿna) targets any vocal inflection that awakens desire in the diseased-hearted — a moral-legal category, not mere etiquette.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: physical bowing; metaphorical: verbal capitulation to lustful expectation.
- Root: م ه ر (m-h-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Dower, skill, or kinship by marriage (muṣāharah) — affinity established through wedlock.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal theology, muṣāharah creates permanent prohibition of marriage (ḥurmat al-muṣāharah) but does not equate to blood-kinship in all rulings.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: marriage-tie; metaphorical extension: the legal fiction of "motherhood" for the Prophet's wives — restricted to prohibition and reverence, not general mahram-status.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional-Exceptive Construction (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — The verse «فلا تخضعن بالقول فيطمع الذي في قلبه مرض» employs a conditional protasis (in ittaqaytunna) followed by a jussive apodosis, where the exception of the Mothers of the Believers from general female address is governed by the restrictive clause "inn ittaqaytunna," parsed as a legal qualifier limiting the scope of the command.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that the question arises: when a woman has need to speak with non-mahram men — whether in buying, selling, or any other situation where such speech is permissible for her — then it behooves her to make her expression firm and coarse, and not to soften it, out of fear of his coveting her.

The Imām Abū al-Ḥasan al-Wāḥidī, one of our companions (may Allah have mercy on him), said in his book "Al-Basīṭ": Our companions said: a woman is encouraged, when addressing unrelated men (ajānib), to employ harshness in her speech, because that is more remote from any hope of illicit desire. Likewise, when she addresses one who is mahram to her by marriage-alliance (muṣāharah). Do you not see that Allah Most High enjoined the Mothers of the Believers — who are forbidden in marriage to all men perpetually — with this very injunction, saying: {«يا نساء النبي لستن كأحد من النساء إن اتقيتن فلا تخضعن بالقول فيطمع الذي في قلبه مرض»} [O wives of the Prophet, you are not like anyone among women. If you fear Allah, then be not soft in speech, lest he in whose heart is disease should covet] (Al-Aḥzāb: 32).

I say: This which al-Wāḥidī mentioned — regarding the coarsening of her voice — is exactly what our companions stated.

Shaykh Ibrāhīm al-Marwazī, one of our companions, said: her method in coarsening it is that she places the back of her hand to her mouth and answers in that manner. And Allah knows best.

Now, this which al-Wāḥidī mentioned — that the mahram by marriage-alliance is like a stranger (ajnabī) in this matter — is weak and contrary to the well-known position (mashhūr) of our companions, because he is like a mahram by blood-kinship in the permissibility of looking and of seclusion (khalwah).

As for the Mothers of the Believers, they are "mothers" only in the prohibition of marrying them and the obligation of revering them — and for this reason, it is lawful to marry their daughters. And Allah knows best.

[Book of the Remembrances of Marriage and What Pertains to It]

[Chapter: What One Says Who Comes to Propose Marriage to a Woman from Her Family, for Himself or for Another]

It is recommended that the suitor begin with praise of Allah (al-ḥamdu lillāh) and extolling Him, and sending prayers upon the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him), and say: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, and I bear witness that Muḥammad is His servant and His Messenger. I have come to you desiring your daughter [or: your noble one] so-and-so, daughter of so-and-so" — or something of that sort.

| 822 —

We have related in the "Sunan of Abū Dāwūd" and "Ibn Mājah" and others, on the authority of Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him), that he said: "Every speech" — and in some narrations, "Every matter that does not begin with praise of Allah is maimed (ajdham)" — and it is also narrated as "cut off (aqṭaʿ)," and both mean the same. This is a good (ḥasan) ḥadīth.

"Ajdham" is with jīm and dhāl (unpointed), and its meaning is: of little blessing.

| 823 —

And we have related in the "Sunan of Abū Dāwūd" and "Al-Tirmidhī," on the authority of Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), that he said: "Every sermon (khuṭbah) in which there is no tashahhud is like a maimed hand." Al-Tirmidhī said: a good (ḥasan) ḥadīth.

[Chapter: A Man Offering His Daughter or Other Female Under His Guardianship in Marriage to People of Virtue and Goodness, That They Might Marry Her]

| 824 —

We have related in "Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī" that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb (may Allah be pleased with him), when her husband died, offered his daughter Ḥafṣah (may Allah be pleased with both of them) in marriage. He said: I met ʿUthmān and offered Ḥafṣah to him, saying: "If you wish, I will marry you to Ḥafṣah bint ʿUmar." He said: "I will consider my affair." Then I waited several nights, and then he met me and said: "It has occurred to me that I will not marry at this time." ʿUmar said: Then I met Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq (may Allah be pleased with him) and said: "If you wish, I will marry you to Ḥafṣah bint ʿUmar." Abū Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) remained silent... and he mentioned the rest of the narration.

chapters.title_en: Section 115 — On What is Said at the Contracting of Marriage, Its Sermon, and What is Said to the Spouse
chapters.arabic_text:
# الحديث.

| (باب ما يقوله عند عقد النكاح)
# يستحب أن يخطب بين يدي العقد خطبة تشتمل على ما ذكرناه في الباب الذي قبل

هذا، وتكون أطول من تلك، وسواء خطب العاقد أو غيره.

| 825 - 
# وأفضلها ما روينا في سنن أبي داود والترمذي والنسائي وابن ماجه وغيرها

بالأسانيد الصحيحة عن عبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال: علمنا رسول الله

(صلى الله عليه وسلم) خطبة الحاجة: " الحمد لله نستعينه ونستغفره ونعوذ به

من شرور أنفسنا، من يهد الله فلا مضل له، ومن يضلل فلا هادي له، وأشهد أن

لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن محمدا عبده ورسوله، (يا أيها

الناس اتقوا ربكم الذي خلقكم من نفس واحدة وخلق منها زوجها، وبث منهما

رجالا كثيرا ونساء، واتقوا الله الذي تساءلون به والأرحام، إن الله كان

عليكم رقيبا) [النساء: 1] ، (يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا الله حق تقاته ولا

تموتن إلا وأنتم مسلمون) [آل عمران: 102] ، (يا أيها الذين آمنوا اتقوا

الله وقولوا قولا سديدا.
# يصلح لكم أعمالكم، ويغفر لكم ذنوبكم، ومن يطع الله ورسوله فقد فاز فوزا

عظيما) [الأحزاب: 71] هذا لفظ إحدى روايات أبي داود وفي رواية له أخرى بعد

قوله ورسوله " أرسله بالحق بشيرا ونذيرا بين يدي الساعة، من يطع الله

ورسوله فقد رشد، ومن يعصهما فإنه لا يضر إلا نفسه ولا يضر الله شيئا " قال

الترمذي: حديث حسن.
# قال أصحابنا: ويستحب أن يقول مع هذا: أزوجك على ما أمر الله به من إمساك

بمعروف أو تسريح بإحسان.
# وأقل هذه الخطبة: الحمد لله، والصلاة على رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم)

، أوصي بتقوى الله.
# والله أعلم. 
# واعلم أن هذه الخطبة سنة، لو لم يأت بشئ منها صح النكاح باتفاق العلماء.
# وحكي عن داود الظاهري رحمه الله أنه قال: لا يصح، ولكن العلماء المحققون

لا يعدون خلاف داود خلافا معتبرا، ولا ينخرق الإجماع بمخالفته، والله أعلم. 
# وأما الزوج، فالمذهب المختار أنه لا يخطب بشئ، بل إذا قال له الولي:

زوجتك فلانة.
# يقول متصلا به: قبلت تزويجها، وإن شاء قال: قبلت نكاحها، فلو قال: الحمد

لله والصلاة على رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) قبلت، صح النكاح، ولم يضر

هذا الكلام بين الإيجاب والقبول، لأنه فصل يسير له تعلق بالعقد.
# وقال بعض أصحابنا: يبطل به النكاح، وقال بعضهم: لا يبطل بل يستحب أن يأتي

به، والصواب ما قدمناه أنه لا يأتي به ولو خالف فأتى به لا يبطل النكاح،

والله أعلم.

| (باب ما يقال للزوج بعد عقد النكاح)

| 826 - 
# السنة أن يقال له: بارك الله لك، أو بارك الله عليك، وجمع بينكما في خير.
# ويستحب أن يقال لكل واحد من الزوجين: بارك الله لكل واحد منكما في صاحبه،

وجمع بينكما في خير.

| 827 - 
# روينا في " صحيحي البخاري ومسلم " عن أنس رضي الله عنه، أن النبي (صلى

الله عليه وسلم) قال لعبد الرحمن بن عوف رضي الله عنه حين أخبره أنه تزوج:

" بارك الله لك ".

| 828 - 
# وروينا في " الصحيح " أيضا أنه (صلى الله عليه وسلم) قال لجابر رضي الله

عنه حين أخبره أنه تزوج: " بارك الله عليك ".

| 829 - 
# وروينا بالأسانيد الصحيحة في سنن أبي داود والترمذي وابن ماجه وغيرها
# عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه، أن النبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم) كان إذا رفأ

الإنسان، إذا تزوج قال: " بارك الله لك، وبارك عليك، وجمع بينكما في خير "

قال الترمذي: حديث حسن صحيح.

# فصل:
# ويكره أن يقال له بالرفاء والبنين، وسيأتي دليل كراهته إن شاء الله تعالى

في " كتاب حفظ اللسان " في آخر الكتاب (1) .
# والرفاء بكسر الراء وبالمد: وهو الاجتماع.

| (باب ما يقول الزوج إذا دخلت عليه امرأته ليلة الزفاف)
# يستحب أن يسمي الله تعالى ويأخذ بناصيتها (1) أول ما يلقاها ويقول: بارك

الله لكل واحد منا في صاحبه.

| 830 - 
# ويقول معه: ما رويناه بالأسانيد الصحيحة (2) في سنن أبي داود وابن ماجه

وابن السني وغيرها عن عمرو بن شعيب عن  أبيه عن جده رضي الله عنه عن النبي

(صلى الله عليه وسلم) قال: " إذا تزوج أحدكم امرأة، أو اشترى خادما فليقل:

اللهم إني أسألك خيرها وخير ما جبلتها عليه (3) ، وأعوذ بك من شرها وشر ما

جبلتها ما جبلتها عليه.
# وإذا اشترى بعيرا فليأخذ بذروة سنامه وليقل مثل ذلك " وفي رواية: " ثم

ليأخذ بناصيتها وليدع بالبركة في المرأة والخادم ".

| (باب ما يقال للرجل بعد دخول أهله عليه)

| 831 - 
# روينا في " صحيح البخاري " وغيره عن أنس رضي الله عنه قال: " بنى رسول

الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) بزينب رضي الله عنها، فأولم بخبز ولحم.." وذكر

الحديث في " صفة الوليمة وكثرة من دعي إليها " ثم قال: فخرج رسول الله (صلى

الله عليه وسلم) فانطلق إلى حجرة عائشة
# فقال: " السلام عليكم أهل البيت ورحمة الله وبركاته، فقالت: وعليك السلام

ورحمة الله، كيف وجدت أهلك؟ بارك الله لك، فتقرى (4) حجر نسائه كلهن يقول
chapters.anchors:
- Root: خ ط ب (kha-ṭa-ba)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To address, deliver an oration; the act of public speech (khuṭbah) aimed at persuasion and solemn declaration.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In sacred usage, the khuṭbah is a formal invocation of divine praise and exhortation, framing a covenantal act (ʿaqd) within the ethos of taqwā.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — a spoken address; metaphorical (majāz) — the marriage sermon as a symbolic gateway to lawful union, not a constitutive pillar.
- Root: ز و ج (z-w-j)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Pairing, coupling; the spouse as a counterpart (zawj) completing a dyad.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The marital bond as a divinely ordained pairing (nikāḥ), reflecting the cosmic pairing in creation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — the act of marriage; metaphorical — the union as a "garment" (libās) of mutual intimacy, per Quranic imagery.
- Root: ر ف أ (r-f-ʾ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To join, reconcile, bring together; al-rafāʾ denotes harmony and union.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In marriage context, a prayer for concord and blessing, not mere festivity.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — physical joining; metaphorical — the verbal benediction seeking divine consolidation of the pair.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Conjunction (al-ʿaṭf) and Sequentiality (al-tartīb) — The phrase "قبلت تزويجها" (I accept her marriage) must follow the offer (ījāb) without substantive interruption; a brief, contract-related pause (faṣl yasīr) is syntactically and legally tolerated, as it does not sever the speech-act continuum.
chapters.translation:
I say: It is recommended (mustaḥabb) that before the contracting of marriage, a sermon (khuṭbah) be delivered which includes what we have mentioned in the preceding chapter, and that it be lengthier than that one. It is equal whether the one contracting the marriage delivers it or someone else.

825 — The most excellent of these sermons is what we have related in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd, al-Tirmidhī, al-Nasāʾī, Ibn Mājah, and others, with sound chains of transmission (asānīd ṣaḥīḥah), from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) taught us the sermon of need (khuṭbat al-ḥājah): "Praise be to God; we seek His aid and His forgiveness, and we seek refuge in Him from the evils of our own souls. Whomsoever God guides, none can lead astray, and whomsoever He leads astray, none can guide. And I bear witness that there is no god but God alone, with no partner, and I bear witness that Muḥammad is His servant and His Messenger. {O mankind, fear your Lord who created you from a single soul and created from it its mate, and dispersed from both of them many men and women. And fear God, through whom you ask one another, and the wombs. Indeed, God is ever over you an Observer} [al-Nisāʾ: 1]. {O you who have believed, fear God as He should be feared and do not die except as Muslims} [Āl ʿImrān: 102]. {O you who have believed, fear God and speak a right word — He will amend for you your deeds and forgive you your sins. And whoever obeys God and His Messenger has certainly attained a great attainment} [al-Aḥzāb: 71]." This is the wording of one of the narrations of Abū Dāwūd. In another of his narrations, after his saying "and His Messenger," [it adds]: "He sent him with the truth as a bearer of good tidings and a warner before the Hour. Whoever obeys God and His Messenger has been rightly guided, and whoever disobeys them harms only himself and harms God not at all." Al-Tirmidhī said: This is a good (ḥasan) hadith.

Our companions (aṣḥābunā) said: It is recommended to add to this: "I marry you to her upon what God has commanded — retention with honor or release with kindness." The minimum of this sermon is: "Praise be to God, and blessings upon the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), and I enjoin the fear of God." And God knows best.

Know that this sermon is a sunnah; if one were to omit any part of it, the marriage remains valid by the consensus of the scholars (ijmāʿ). It has been related from Dāwūd al-Ẓāhirī, may God have mercy on him, that he said: It is not valid. But the verifying scholars do not count the dissent of Dāwūd as a considered dissent, nor is the consensus breached by his opposition. And God knows best.

As for the husband, the chosen position (al-madhhab al-mukhtār) is that he should not deliver any sermon. Rather, when the guardian (walī) says to him: "I have married you to so-and-so," he should say, immediately connected to it: "I accept her marriage" (qabiltu tazwījahā). And if he wishes, he may say: "I accept her wedlock" (qabiltu nikāḥahā). If he were to say: "Praise be to God and blessings upon the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), I accept," the marriage is valid, and this speech between the offer (ījāb) and acceptance (qabūl) does no harm, because it is a brief separation (faṣl yasīr) connected to the contract. Some of our companions said: It invalidates the marriage. Others said: It does not invalidate, rather it is recommended to utter it. The correct view is what we have stated — that he should not utter it, but if he violates this and utters it, the marriage is not invalidated. And God knows best.

[Chapter: On What is Said to the Husband After the Contracting of Marriage]

826 — The sunnah is to say to him: "May God bless you" (bāraka Allāhu laka), or "May God bless you" (bāraka Allāhu ʿalayka), and "May He bring you both together in goodness." It is recommended to say to each of the two spouses: "May God bless each of you in his companion, and bring you both together in goodness."

827 — We have related in the two Ṣaḥīḥs of al-Bukhārī and Muslim, from Anas, may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, may God be pleased with him, when he informed him that he had married: "May God bless you" (bāraka Allāhu laka).

828 — We have also related in the Ṣaḥīḥ that he (peace and blessings be upon him) said to Jābir, may God be pleased with him, when he informed him that he had married: "May God bless you" (bāraka Allāhu ʿalayka).

829 — We have related with sound chains of transmission in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd, al-Tirmidhī, Ibn Mājah, and others, from Abū Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), when he congratulated a person upon his marriage, would say: "May God bless you, and bless you, and bring you both together in goodness." Al-Tirmidhī said: This is a good and sound (ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ) hadith.

A Section (faṣl): It is disliked (makrūh) to say to him "with harmony and sons" (bil-rafāʾ wal-banīn). The evidence for its dislike will come, God willing, in the "Book of Guarding the Tongue" at the end of this work. Al-rafāʾ, with a kasrah on the rāʾ and a lengthened alif, means: union and coming together.

[Chapter: On What the Husband Says When His Wife Enters Upon Him on the Wedding Night]

It is recommended that he mention God, may He be exalted, and take hold of her forelock (nāṣiyah) at the first moment of meeting her, and say: "May God bless each of us in his companion."

830 — And he should say along with this what we have related with sound chains of transmission in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd, Ibn Mājah, Ibn al-Sunnī, and others, from ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb, from his father, from his grandfather, may God be pleased with him, from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), who said: "When one of you marries a woman, or purchases a servant, let him say: 'O God, I ask You for her goodness and the goodness of what You have created her upon, and I seek refuge in You from her evil and the evil of what You have created her upon.' And when he purchases a camel, let him take hold of the top of its hump and say the like of that." In another narration: "Then let him take hold of her forelock and pray for blessing upon the woman and the servant."

[Chapter: On What is Said to a Man After His Wife Enters Upon Him]

831 — We have related in the Ṣaḥīḥ of al-Bukhārī and others, from Anas, may God be pleased with him, who said: "The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) consummated his marriage with Zaynab, may God be pleased with her, and gave a wedding feast (walīmah) with bread and meat..." — and he mentioned the hadith concerning the description of the feast and the multitude of those invited — then he said: "Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) went out and departed to the chamber of ʿĀʾishah and said: 'Peace be upon you, O people of the household, and the mercy of God and His blessings.' She said: 'And upon you be peace and the mercy of God. How did you find your wife? May God bless you.' Then he went around to all his wives' chambers, saying the same."

| 832 - 
# روينا في " صحيحي البخاري ومسلم " عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما من طرق

كثيرة عن النبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم) قال: " لو أن أحدكم إذا أتى أهله قال:

بسم الله اللهم جنبنا 
# الشيطان وجنب الشيطان ما رزقتنا فقضي بينهما ولد لم يضره " وفي رواية

للبخاري " لم يضره شيطان أبدا ".

| (باب ملاعبة الرجل امرأته وممازحته لها ولطف عبارته معها)

| 833 - 
# روينا في " صحيحي البخاري ومسلم " عن جابر رضي الله عنه قال: قال لي رسول

الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) : " تزوجت بكرا أم ثيبا؟ قلت: تزوجت ثيبا، قال:

هلا تزوجت بكرا تلاعبها وتلاعبك ".

| 834 - 
# وروينا في كتاب الترمذي وسنن النسائي عن عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت: قال

رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم:) " أكمل المؤمنين إيمانا أحسنهم خلقا

وألطفهم لاهله " (1) .

| (باب بيان أدب الزوج مع أصهاره في الكلام)
# اعلم أنه يستحب للزوج أن لا يخاطب أحدا من أقارب زوجته بلفظ فيه ذكر جماع

النساء، أو تقبيلهن، أو معانقتهن، أو  غير ذلك من أنواع الاستمتاع بهن، أو

ما يتضمن ذلك أو يستدل به عليه أو يفهم منه.

| 835 - 
# روينا في " صحيحي البخاري ومسلم " عن علي رضي الله عنه قال: " كنت رجلا

مذاء (2) فاستحييت أن أسأل رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) لمكان ابنته

مني، فأمرت المقداد فسأله ".

| (باب ما يقال عند الولادة وتألم المرأة بذلك)
# ينبغي أن يكثر من دعاء الكرب الذي قدمناه.

| 836 - 
# وروينا في كتاب ابن السني عن فاطمة رضي الله عنها " أن رسول الله (صلى

الله عليه وسلم) لما دنا ولادها أمر أم سلمة وزينب بنت جحش أن يأتيا فيقرآ

عندها آية الكرسي، و (إن ربكم الله..) إلى آخر الآية (3) [الاعراف: 54]

ويعوذاها بالمعوذتين ".
# (4) *

| (باب الأذان في أذن المولود)

| 837 - 
# روينا في سنن أبي داود والترمذي وغيرهما عن أبي رافع رضي الله عنه مولى

رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) قال: " رأيت رسول الله (صلى الله عليه

وسلم) أذن في أذن الحسين بن علي حين ولدته فاطمة بالصلاة رضي الله عنهم "

قال الترمذي: حديث حسن صحيح.
# قال جماعة من أصحابنا: يستحب أن يؤذن في أذنه اليمنى ويقيم الصلاة في

أذنه اليسرى.

| 838 - 
# وقد روينا في كتاب ابن السني عن الحسين بن علي رضي الله عنهما قال: قال

رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) : " من ولد له مولود فأذن في أذنه اليمنى،

وأقام في أذنه اليسرى لم تضره أم الصبيان " (1) .

| (باب الدعاء عند تحنيك الطفل)

| 839 - 
# روينا بالإسناد الصحيح في سنن أبي داود، عن عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت: "

كان رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) يؤتى بالصبيان فيدعو لهم ويحنكهم " وفي

رواية: فيدعو لهم بالبركة ".

| 840 - 
# وروينا في " صحيحي البخاري ومسلم " عن أسماء بنت أبي بكر رضي الله عنهما

قالت: " حملت بعبد الله بن الزبير بمكة، فأتيت المدينة فنزلت قباء، فولدت

بقباء، ثم أتيت به النبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم) ، فوضعه في حجره ثم دعا

بتمرة فمضغها ثم تفل في فيه، فكان أول شئ دخل جوفه ريق رسول  الله (صلى الله

عليه وسلم) ، ثم حنكه بالتمرة، ثم دعا له وبارك عليه ".

| 841 - 
# وروينا في " صحيحهما " عن أبي موسى الأشعري رضي الله عنه قال: " ولد لي

غلام، فأتيت به النبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم) فسماه إبراهيم، وحنكه بتمرة،

ودعا له بالبركة " هذا لفظ البخاري ومسلم، إلا قوله: " ودعا له بالبركة "

فإنه للبخاري خاصة.

| كتاب الأسماء

| (باب تسمية المولود)
# السنة أن يسمى المولود في اليوم السابع من ولادته أو يوم الولادة.

| 842 - 
# فأما استحبابه يوم السابع، فلما رويناه في كتاب الترمذي عن عمرو بن *

# شعيب عن أبيه عن جده " أن النبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم) أمر بتسمية المولود

يوم سابعه، ووضع الأذى عنه، والعق " قال الترمذي: حديث حسن (1) .

| 843 - 
# وروينا في سنن أبي داود والترمذي والنسائي وابن ماجه وغيرهما بالأسانيد

الصحيحة عن سمرة بن جندب رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم)

قال: " كل غلام رهينة بعقيقته تذبح عنه يوم سابعه، ويحلق، ويسمى " قال

الترمذي: حديث حسن صحيح.

| 844 - 
# وأما يوم الولادة فلما رويناه في الباب المتقدم من حديث أبي موسى.

| 845 - 
# وروينا في صحيح مسلم " وغيره عن أنس رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله

(صلى الله عليه وسلم) : " ولد لي الليلة غلام فسميته باسم أبي: إبراهيم

(صلى الله عليه وسلم) ".

| 846 - 
# وروينا في " صحيحي البخاري ومسلم " عن أنس قال: " ولد لأبي طلحة غلام،

فأتيت به النبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم) فحنكه، وسماه عبد الله ".

| 847 - 
# وروينا في " صحيحيهما " عن سهل بن سعد الساعدي رضي الله عنه قال: " أتي

chapters.anchors:
- Root: ج-ن-ب (j-n-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To be removed, distanced, set apart; side or flank (jānib).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In supplication, "jannibnā" denotes a plea for divine distancing from evil—an act of seeking protection (istiʿādha) through God's agency.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in spatial removal; metaphorical (majāz) in spiritual or demonic exclusion.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ) — The protasis (law an aḥadakum) with apodosis (lam yaḍurruhu) governs the semantic outcome; the particle "law" indicates hypothetical unrealized condition.

- Root: ر-ه-ن (r-h-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Pledge, collateral, security held against a debt.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The newborn is "held in pledge" (rahīna) for the ʿaqīqah—a ritual obligation whose fulfillment releases the child from spiritual liability.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal in financial transactions; metaphorical here—the child's well-being is conceptually bound to the sacrificial rite.
- Sībawayh Rule: Predicate of Inherence (al-Khabar) — "kullu ghulāmin rahīnatun" employs a nominal sentence where the predicate is a metaphorically extended noun, requiring the listener to grasp the implied comparison.

- Root: ح-ن-ك (ḥ-n-k)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To chew, masticate; the palate (ḥanak); to rub the palate of an infant with chewed dates.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A Prophetic act of blessing (baraka) symbolically transferring the sunna of the Messenger into the child's first nourishment.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal action (chewing and placing in mouth); metaphorical—the "first thing entering the stomach" is the blessed saliva of the Prophet, signifying spiritual initiation.
- Sībawayh Rule: Transitive Verb with Object (al-Mafʿūl bihi) — "ḥannakahu bi-tamra" shows the instrument (bā' of accompaniment) modifying the verbal action.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that the rulings pertaining to intimate relations, the etiquette of playfulness with one's wife, and the proper conduct of speech with in-laws are established upon Prophetic guidance. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) taught his community the supplication to be uttered at the moment of intercourse, as a shield against the harm of Satan.

Section: What is Said at Intercourse

832 - We have related in the two Ṣaḥīḥs of al-Bukhārī and Muslim, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās (may God be pleased with them both), through numerous chains of transmission, that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "If any of you, when he approaches his wife, says: 'In the name of God, O God, distance us from Satan and distance Satan from what You have provided us'—then if a child is decreed for them from that union, Satan will not harm him." In a narration of al-Bukhārī: "No Satan will ever harm him."

Section: On a Man's Playfulness with His Wife, His Jesting with Her, and His Gentle Speech Towards Her

833 - We have related in the two Ṣaḥīḥs of al-Bukhārī and Muslim, on the authority of Jābir (may God be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said to me: "Have you married a virgin or a previously married woman?" I said: "I have married a previously married woman." He said: "Why did you not marry a virgin, so that you might play with her and she with you?"

834 - And we have related in the book of al-Tirmidhī and the Sunan of al-Nasā'ī, on the authority of ʿĀ'isha (may God be pleased with her), who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "The most complete of believers in faith is the one with the best character and the most gentle with his family."

Section: Explaining the Etiquette of the Husband in Speech with His In-Laws

Know that it is recommended (mustaḥabb) for the husband not to address any of his wife's relatives with any expression that mentions intercourse with women, or kissing them, or embracing them, or any other kind of intimate enjoyment with them—nor anything that implies such, or alludes to it, or may be understood from it.

835 - We have related in the two Ṣaḥīḥs of al-Bukhārī and Muslim, on the authority of ʿAlī (may God be pleased with him), who said: "I was a man who frequently emitted prostatic fluid (madhy), and I felt ashamed to ask the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) because of the position of his daughter with me. So I commanded al-Miqdād to ask him."

Section: What is Said at the Time of Birth and When a Woman Experiences Its Pain

One should frequently recite the supplication for distress (duʿā' al-karb) which we have previously mentioned.

836 - And we have related in the book of Ibn al-Sunnī, on the authority of Fāṭimah (may God be pleased with her), "that when the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) approached the time of her delivery, he commanded Umm Salamah and Zaynab bint Jaḥsh to come and recite at her side the Āyat al-Kursī, and {«Indeed, your Lord is God...»} to the end of the verse {«[al-Aʿrāf: 54]»}, and to seek refuge for her with the two Muʿawwidhatān (the two chapters of refuge, al-Falaq and al-Nās)."

Section: The Adhān in the Ear of the Newborn

837 - We have related in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd, al-Tirmidhī, and others, on the authority of Abū Rāfiʿ (may God be pleased with him), the freed slave of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), who said: "I saw the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) pronounce the adhān in the ear of al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī when Fāṭimah gave birth to him—the adhān of prayer (may God be pleased with them all)." Al-Tirmidhī said: A ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ ḥadīth.

A group of our companions (the Shāfiʿī jurists) said: It is recommended to pronounce the adhān in his right ear and the iqāmah in his left ear.

838 - And we have related in the book of Ibn al-Sunnī, on the authority of al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī (may God be pleased with them both), who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever has a child born to him, and pronounces the adhān in his right ear and the iqāmah in his left ear, the 'mother of boys' (umm al-ṣibyān, i.e., the female jinn afflicting children) will not harm him."

Section: The Supplication at the Tahnīk of an Infant

839 - We have related with a sound chain of transmission in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd, on the authority of ʿĀ'isha (may God be pleased with her), who said: "The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) used to have the infants brought to him, and he would supplicate for them and perform tahnīk upon them." In another narration: "He would supplicate for them with blessing."

840 - And we have related in the two Ṣaḥīḥs of al-Bukhārī and Muslim, on the authority of Asmā' bint Abī Bakr (may God be pleased with them both), who said: "I conceived ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr in Mecca. I came to Medina and alighted at Qubā', and gave birth there. Then I brought him to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), who placed him in his lap. Then he called for a date, chewed it, and placed some of it in the child's mouth. The first thing that entered his stomach was the saliva of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). Then he performed tahnīk with the date, then supplicated for him and blessed him."

841 - And we have related in the two Ṣaḥīḥs, on the authority of Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī (may God be pleased with him), who said: "A boy was born to me, and I brought him to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him). He named him Ibrāhīm, performed tahnīk upon him with a date, and supplicated for him with blessing." This is the wording of al-Bukhārī and Muslim, except for his statement "and supplicated for him with blessing"—for that is specific to al-Bukhārī.

The Book of Names

Section: Naming the Newborn

The sunna is to name the newborn on the seventh day after his birth, or on the day of birth itself.

842 - As for the recommendation of the seventh day, it is due to what we have related in the book of al-Tirmidhī, on the authority of ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb, from his father, from his grandfather, "that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) commanded that the newborn be named on his seventh day, that the harm be removed from him, and that the ʿaqīqah be performed." Al-Tirmidhī said: A ḥasan ḥadīth.

843 - And we have related in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd, al-Tirmidhī, al-Nasā'ī, Ibn Mājah, and others, with sound chains of transmission, on the authority of Samurah ibn Jundub (may God be pleased with him), that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Every boy is held in pledge for his ʿaqīqah; it is slaughtered on his behalf on his seventh day, his head is shaved, and he is named." Al-Tirmidhī said: A ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ ḥadīth.

844 - As for the day of birth, it is due to what we have related in the preceding section, from the ḥadīth of Abū Mūsā.

845 - And we have related in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim and others, on the authority of Anas (may God be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "A boy was born to me tonight, and I named him after my father: Ibrāhīm (peace be upon him)."

846 - And we have related in the two Ṣaḥīḥs of al-Bukhārī and Muslim, on the authority of Anas, who said: "A boy was born to Abū Ṭalḥah. I brought him to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), who performed tahnīk upon him and named him ʿAbd Allāh."

847 - And we have related in the two Ṣaḥīḥs, on the authority of Sahl ibn Saʿd al-Sāʿidī (may God be pleased with him), who said: "Al-Mundhir ibn Abī Usayd was brought to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) when he was born. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) placed him on his thigh while Abū Usayd was sitting. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) became distracted..."

عليه وسلم) بشئ بين يديه، فأمر أبو أسيد بابنه فاحتمل من على فخذ النبي

(صلى الله عليه وسلم) ، فأقلبوه، فاستفاق النبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم) فقال:

أين الصبي؟ فقال أبو أسيد: أقلبناه يا رسول الله، قال: ما اسمه؟ قال:  فلان،

قال: لا، ولكن اسمه المنذر، فسماه يومئذ المنذر ".
# قلت: قوله لهي، بكسر الهاء وفتحها لغتان: الفتح لطئ، والكسر لباقي العرب،

وهو الفصيح المشهور، ومعناه: انصرف عنه، وقيل اشتغل بغيره، وقيل نسيه،

وقوله استفاق: أي ذكره، وقوله فأقلبوه: أي ردوه إلى منزلهم.

| (باب تسمية السقط)
# (2) يستحب تسميته، فإن لم يعلم أذكر هو أو أنثى، سمي باسم يصلح للذكر

والأنثى، كأسماء، وهند، وهنيدة، وخارجة، وطلحة، وعميرة، وزرعة، ونحو ذلك.
# قال الإمام البغوي:

| 848 - 
# يستحب تسمية السقط لحديث ورد فيه (1) ، وكذا قاله غيره من أصحابه.
# قال أصحابنا: ولو مات المولود قبل تسميته استحب تسميته (2) .

| (باب استحباب تحسين الاسم)

| 849 - 
# روينا في سنن أبي داود بالإسناد الجيد (3) عن أبي الدرداء رضي الله عنه

قال: قال رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) : " إنكم تدعون يوم القيامة

بأسمائكم وأسماء آبائكم فأحسنوا أسماءكم ".

| (باب بيان أحب الأسماء إلى الله عز وجل)

| 850 - 
# روينا في " صحيح مسلم " عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما قال: قال رسول الله

(صلى الله عليه وسلم) : " إن أحب أسمائكم إلى الله عز وجل عبد الله وعبد

الرحمن ".

| 851 - 
# وروينا في " صحيحي البخاري ومسلم " عن جابر رضي الله عنه قال: ولد لرجل

منا غلام فسماه القاسم، فقلنا: لا نكنيك أبا القاسم ولا كرامة، فأخبر النبي

(صلى الله عليه وسلم) فقال: " سم ابنك عبد الرحمن ".

| 852 - 
# وروينا في سنن أبي داود والنسائي وغيرهما عن أبي وهيب الجشمي الصحابي رضي

الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) : " تسموا بأسماء

الأنبياء، وأحب الأسماء إلى الله تعالى: عبد الله وعبد الرحمن، وأصدقها:

حارث وهمام، وأقبحها: حرب ومرة " (4) .

| (باب استحباب التهنئة وجواب المهنأ)

| 853 - 
# يستحب تهنئة المولود له، قال أصحابنا: ويستحب أن يهنأ بما جاء عن الحسين

رضي الله عنه أنه علم إنسانا التهنئة فقال: قل: بارك الله لك في الموهوب

لك، وشكرت الواهب، وبلغ أشده، ورزقت بره.
# ويستحب أن يرد على المهنئ فيقول: بارك الله لك، وبارك عليك، وجزاك الله

خيرا، ورزقك الله مثله،  أو أجزل الله ثوابك، ونحو هذا.

| (باب النهي عن التسمية بالأسماء المكروهة)

| 854 - 
# روينا في " صحيح مسلم " عن سمرة بن جندب رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله

(صلى الله عليه وسلم) : " لا تسمين غلامك يسارا، ولا رباحا، ولا نجاحا، ولا

أفلح، فإنك تقول أثم هو؟ فلا يكون، فتقول: لا، إنما هن أربع فلا تزيدون علي

".

| 855 - 
# وروينا في سنن أبي داود وغيره من رواية جابر، وفيه أيضا النهي عن تسميته

بركة.

| 856 - 
# وروينا في " صحيحي البخاري ومسلم " عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن النبي

(صلى الله عليه وسلم) قال: " إن أخنع اسم عند الله تعالى رجل تسمى ملك

الأملاك ".
# وفي رواية " أخنى " بدل " أخنع ".
# وفي رواية لمسلم " أغيظ رجل عند الله يوم القيامة وأخبثه رجل كان يسمى

ملك الأملاك، لا ملك إلا الله " قال العلماء: معنى أخنع وأخنى: أوضع وأذل

وأرذل.
# وجاء في الصحيح عن سفيان بن عيينة قال: ملك الأملاك مثل شاهان شاه.

| (باب ذكر الإنسان من يتبعه من ولد أو غلام أو متعلم أو نحوهم باسم قبيح ليؤدبه ويزجره عن القبيح ويروض نفسه)

| 857 - 
# روينا في كتاب ابن السني عن عبد الله بن بسر المازني الصحابي رضي الله

عنه - وهو بضم الباء الموحدة وإسكان السين المهملة - قال: " بعثتني أمي إلى

رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) بقطف من عنب، فأكلت منه قبل أن أبلغه إياه،

فلما جئت به أخذ بأذني وقال: يا غدر " (1) .

| 858 - 
# وروينا في " صحيحي البخاري ومسلم " عن عبد الرحمن بن أبي بكر الصديق رضي

الله عنهما في حديثه الطويل المشتمل على كرامة ظاهرة للصديق رضي الله عنه

(1) ، ومعناه: أن الصديق رضي الله عنه ضيف جماعة وأجلسهم في منزله وانصرف

إلى رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) فتأخر رجوعه، فقال عند رجوعه:

أعشيتموهم؟ قالوا: لا، فأقبل على ابنه عبد الرحمن فقال: يا غنثر، فجدع (2)

وسب (3) .
# قلت: قوله: غنثر، بغين معجمة مضمومة، ثم نون ساكنة ثم تاء مثلثة مفتوحة

ومضمومة ثم نون ساكنة ثم ثاء  مثلثة مفتوحة ومضمومة ثم راء، ومعناه: يا

لئيم، وقوله:
# فجدع، وهو بالجيم والدال المهملة، ومعناه: دعا عليه بقطع الأنف ونحوه،

والله أعلم.

| (باب نداء من لا يعرف اسمه)
# ينبغي أن ينادى بعبارة لا يتأذى بها، ولا يكون فيها كذب ولا ملق (4) ولا

ملق ": كقولك: يا أخي (5) يا فقيه، يا فقير، يا سيدي، يا هذا، يا صاحب

الثوب الفلاني أو النعل الفلاني أو الفرس أو الجمل، أو السيف أو الرمح، وما

أشبه هذا على حسب حال المنادى والمنادي.
chapters.anchors:
- Root: س-ق-ط (sa-qa-ṭa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To fall, to drop; al-siqṭ is that which falls from the womb before viability.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A theological-legal term for a fetus expelled dead before the full term; its naming is a sunnah of honor, not a ritual necessity.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical falling; metaphorical (majāz) extended to the miscarriage event itself.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — The explanatory clause "أي ذكره" (i.e., he remembered him) functions as apposition to clarify the verb "استفاق" without altering its grammatical case.
chapters.translation:
I say: His statement "لَهِيَ" — with kasrah on the hāʾ and fatḥah on it — are two dialects: the fatḥah is the dialect of Ṭayyiʾ, and the kasrah is that of the rest of the Arabs, and it is the eloquent and well-known one. Its meaning is: "turn away from him"; and it was said: "occupy oneself with something else"; and it was said: "forget him." His statement "فَاسْتَفَاقَ" (he regained consciousness) means: he remembered him. His statement "فَأَقْلَبُوهُ" (they turned him over) means: they returned him to their dwelling.

| (Chapter: On Naming the Miscarried Infant)

It is recommended (mustaḥabb) to name him. If it is not known whether it is male or female, he is given a name suitable for both male and female, such as Asmāʾ, Hind, Hunaydah, Khārijah, Ṭalḥah, ʿUmayrah, Zurʿah, and the like.

Imam al-Baghawī said:

848 — It is recommended to name the miscarried infant due to a ḥadīth reported concerning that, and likewise said other companions of his (i.e., of the Shāfiʿī school).

Our companions (the Shāfiʿī jurists) said: And if a newborn dies before being named, it is recommended to name him.

| (Chapter: On the Recommendation of Beautifying the Name)

849 — We reported in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd with a good chain (al-isnād al-jayyid) on the authority of Abū al-Dardāʾ, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وسلم) said: {«إِنَّكُمْ تُدْعَوْنَ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ بِأَسْمَائِكُمْ وَأَسْمَاءِ آبَائِكُمْ فَأَحْسِنُوا أَسْمَاءَكُمْ»} — "You will be called on the Day of Resurrection by your names and the names of your fathers, so beautify your names."

| (Chapter: On Clarifying the Most Beloved Names to Allah, Mighty and Majestic)

850 — We reported in "Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim" on the authority of Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وسلم) said: {«إِنَّ أَحَبَّ أَسْمَائِكُمْ إِلَى اللهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ عَبْدُ اللهِ وَعَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ»} — "The most beloved of your names to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, are ʿAbd Allāh and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān."

851 — And we reported in the two Ṣaḥīḥs of al-Bukhārī and Muslim on the authority of Jābir, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: A man among us had a boy born to him, and he named him al-Qāsim. We said: "We will not address you by the kunyah Abū al-Qāsim, and no honor for you." So the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) was informed, and he said: {«سَمِّ ابْنَكَ عَبْدَ الرَّحْمَنِ»} — "Name your son ʿAbd al-Raḥmān."

852 — And we reported in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd, al-Nasāʾī, and others, on the authority of Abū Wahb al-Jushamī, the Companion, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وسلم) said: {«تَسَمَّوْا بِأَسْمَاءِ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ، وَأَحَبُّ الْأَسْمَاءِ إِلَى اللهِ تَعَالَى: عَبْدُ اللهِ وَعَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ، وَأَصْدَقُهَا: حَارِثٌ وَهَمَّامٌ، وَأَقْبَحُهَا: حَرْبٌ وَمُرَّةُ»} — "Name yourselves with the names of the prophets. The most beloved of names to Allah Most High are ʿAbd Allāh and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān; the truest of them are Ḥārith and Hammām; and the ugliest of them are Ḥarb and Murrah."

| (Chapter: On the Recommendation of Congratulating and the Response to the One Who Congratulates)

853 — It is recommended to congratulate the one to whom a child is born. Our companions said: It is recommended to congratulate with what has come from al-Ḥusayn, may Allah be pleased with him, that he taught a person the congratulation and said: Say: "Bāraka Allāhu laka fī al-mawhūbi laka, wa shakarta al-wāhiba, wa balagha ashuddahu, wa ruziqta birrahu" — "May Allah bless you in what He has gifted you, and may you thank the Giver, and may he reach his full strength, and may you be granted his piety."

And it is recommended that the one congratulated respond to the congratulator, saying: "Bāraka Allāhu laka, wa bāraka ʿalayka, wa jazāka Allāhu khayran, wa razaqaka Allāhu mithlahu" — "May Allah bless you, and bless upon you, and may Allah reward you with good, and may Allah grant you the like of it" — or "Ajjala Allāhu thawābaka" — "May Allah make your reward abundant" — and the like.

| (Chapter: On the Prohibition of Naming with Disliked Names)

854 — We reported in "Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim" on the authority of Samurah ibn Jundub, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وسلم) said: {«لَا تُسَمِّيَنَّ غُلَامَكَ يَسَارًا، وَلَا رَبَاحًا، وَلَا نَجَاحًا، وَلَا أَفْلَحَ، فَإِنَّكَ تَقُولُ أَثَمَّ هُوَ؟ فَلَا يَكُونُ، فَتَقُولُ: لَا، إِنَّمَا هُنَّ أَرْبَعٌ فَلَا تَزِيدُونَ عَلَيَّ»} — "Do not name your boy Yasār, nor Rabāḥ, nor Najāḥ, nor Aflaḥ, for you will say: 'Is he there?' and he will not be, and you will say: 'No.' Indeed, they are but four, so do not add to me."

855 — And we reported in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd and others from the narration of Jābir, and in it also is the prohibition of naming him Barakah.

856 — And we reported in the two Ṣaḥīḥs of al-Bukhārī and Muslim on the authority of Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) who said: {«إِنَّ أَخْنَعَ اسْمٍ عِنْدَ اللهِ تَعَالَى رَجُلٌ تَسَمَّى مَلِكَ الْأَمْلَاكِ»} — "The most despicable name in the sight of Allah Most High is a man who calls himself King of Kings."

In another narration, "أَخْنَى" (akhnā) instead of "أَخْنَعَ" (akhnaʿ).

In a narration of Muslim: {«أَغْيَظُ رَجُلٍ عِنْدَ اللهِ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ وَأَخْبَثُهُ رَجُلٌ كَانَ يُسَمَّى مَلِكَ الْأَمْلَاكِ، لَا مَلِكَ إِلَّا اللهُ»} — "The most enraging man to Allah on the Day of Resurrection and the most wicked of them is a man who was called King of Kings; there is no king but Allah."
