The scholars said: The meaning of "akhnaʿ" and "akhnā" is: the lowest, the most humiliated, and the most contemptible.

And it came in the Ṣaḥīḥ on the authority of Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah who said: "King of Kings" is like "Shāhān Shāh."

| (Chapter: On a Man Mentioning One Who Follows Him — Whether a Child, a Servant, a Student, or the Like — with an Ugly Name in Order to Discipline Him, Deter Him from the Ugly, and Train His Own Soul)

857 — We reported in the book of Ibn al-Sunnī on the authority of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Busr al-Māzinī, the Companion, may Allah be pleased with him — and it is with ḍammah on the bāʾ (muwahḥadah) and sukūn on the sīn (muhmalah) — who said: "My mother sent me to the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وسلم) with a cluster of grapes, and I ate from it before I delivered it to him. When I came to him with it, he took hold of my ear and said: 'Yā Ghadar' — 'O treacherous one.'"

858 — And we reported in the two Ṣaḥīḥs of al-Bukhārī and Muslim on the authority of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, may Allah be pleased with them both, in his long ḥadīth which includes a manifest miracle (karāmah) for al-Ṣiddīq, may Allah be pleased with him. Its meaning is: that al-Ṣiddīq hosted a group and seated them in his dwelling, then departed to the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وسلم), and his return was delayed. Upon his return he said: "Have you fed them?" They said: "No." So he turned to his son ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and said: "Yā Ghant̲ar" — then he "jadaʿa" (rebuked him harshly) and "sabba" (insulted him).

I say: His statement "غَنْثَر" — with a ḍammah on the ghayn (muʿjamah), then a sukūn on the nūn, then a fatḥah and ḍammah on the tāʾ (muthallathah), then a sukūn on the nūn, then a fatḥah and ḍammah on the thāʾ (muthallathah), then a rāʾ — and its meaning is: "O base one." And his statement "فَجَدَعَ" — with the jīm and the dāl (muhmalah) — its meaning is: he supplicated against him for the cutting off of the nose and the like. And Allah knows best.

| (Chapter: On Addressing One Whose Name Is Not Known)

One should address him with an expression by which he is not harmed, and in which there is neither falsehood nor flattery (malq) nor sycophancy (malaq) — such as saying: "O my brother," "O jurist (faqīh)," "O poor one (faqīr)," "O my master (sayyidī)," "O this one (yā hādhā)," "O owner of such-and-such garment, or such-and-such sandal, or horse, or camel, or sword, or spear," and whatever resembles this, according to the state of the one addressed and the one addressing.

chapters.title_en: Section 118 — On the Prohibition of a Child, Student, or Disciple Calling His Father, Teacher, or Shaykh by Name; and the Recommendation of Changing Names to Better Ones
chapters.arabic_text:
| 859 - 
# وقد روينا في سنن أبي داود والنسائي وابن ماجه بإسناد حسن عن بشير بن

معبد المعروف بابن الخصاصية رضي الله عنه قال: " بينما أنا أماشي (6) النبي

(صلى الله عليه وسلم) نظر فإذا رجل يمشي بين القبور عليه نعلان فقال: يا

صاحب السبتيتين (7) ويحك ألق سبتيتيك.." وذكر تمام الحديث.
# قلت: النعال السبتية بكسر السين: التي لا شعر عليها.

| 860 - 
# وروينا في كتاب ابن السني عن جارية الأنصاري الصحابي رضي الله عنه -

# وهو بالجيم - قال: " كنت عند النبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم) وكان إذا لم

يحفظ اسم الرجل قال: " يا بن عبد الله ".

| (باب نهي الولد والمتعلم والتلميذ أن ينادي أباه ومعلمه وشيخه باسمه)

| 861 - 
# روينا في كتاب ابن السني عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه: " أن النبي (صلى

الله عليه وسلم) رأى رجلا معه غلام، فقال للغلام: من هذا؟ قال: أبي، قال:

فلا تمش أمامه، ولا تستسب له، ولا تجلس قبله، ولا تدعه باسمه ".
# قلت: معنى لا تستسب له: أي لا تفعل فعلا يتعرض فيه لأن يسبك أبوك زجرا لك

تأديبا على فعلك القبيح.

| 862 - 
# وروينا فيه عن السيد الجليل العبد الصالح المتفق على صلاحه عبيد الله بن

زحر؟ - بفتح الزاي وإسكان الحاء المهملة - رضي الله عنه قال: يقال من

العقوق أن تسمي أباك باسمه، وأن تمشي أمامه في طريق.

| باب استحباب تغيير الاسم إلى أحسن منه
# 862 م - فيه حديث سهل به سعد الساعدي المذكور في باب تسمية المولود في

قصة المنذر  بن أبي أسيد.

| 863 - 
# روينا في " صحيحي البخاري ومسلم " عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه " أن زينب

كان اسمها برة، فقيل: تزكي نفسها، فسماها رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) "

زينب ".

| 864 - 
# وفي " صحيح مسلم " عن زينب بنت أبي سلمة رضي الله عنها قالت سميت برة،

فقال رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) : " سموها زينب، قالت: ودخلت عليه

زينب بنت جحش واسمها برة، فسما ها زينب ".

| 865 - 
# وفي " صحيح مسلم " أيضا عن ابن عباس قال: " كانت جويرية اسمها برة، فحول

رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) اسمها جويرية، وكان يكره أن يقال خرج من

عند برة ".

| 866 - 
# وروينا في " صحيح البخاري " عن سعيد بن المسيب بن حزن عن أبيه، أن أباه

جاء إلى النبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم) فقال: " ما اسمك؟ قال: حزن، فقال: أنت

سهل، قال: لا أغير اسما سمانيه أبي، قال ابن المسيب: فما زالت الحزونة فينا

بعد ". 
# قلت: الحزونة: غلظ الوجه وشي من القساوة.

| 867 - 
# وروينا في " صحيح البخاري مسلم " عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما " أن النبي

(صلى الله عليه وسلم) غير اسم عاصية، وقال: " أنت جميلة ".
# وفي رواية لمسلم أيضا: " أن ابنة لعمر كان يقال لها عاصية، فسماها رسول

الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) جميلة ".

| 868 - 
# وروينا في سنن أبي داود " بإسناد حسن، عن أسامة بن أخدري الصحابي رضي

الله عنه - وأخدري بفتح الهمزة والدال المهملة وإسكان الخاء المعجمة بينهما

- " أن رجلا يقال له أصرم كان في النفر الذين أتوا رسول الله (صلى الله

عليه وسلم) ، فقال رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) : ما اسمك؟ قال: أصرم،

قال: " بل أنت زرعة ".

| 869 - 
# وروينا في سنن أبي داود والنسائي وغيرهما عن أبي شريح هانئ الحارثي

الصحابي رضي الله عنه " أنه لما وفد إلى رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) مع

قومه سمعهم يكنونه بأبي الحكم، فدعاه رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) فقال:

إن الله هو الحكم " وإليه الحكم، فلم تكنى أبا الحكم؟ فقال: إن قومي  إذا

اختلفوا في شئ أتوني فحكمت بينهم، فرضي كلا الفريقين، فقال رسول الله (صلى

الله عليه وسلم) : ما أحسن هذا، فما لك من الولد؟ قال: لي شريح، ومسلم،

وعبد الله، قال: فمن أكبرهم؟ قلت: شريح، قال: فأنت أبو شريح " (1) .
# قال أبو داود: وغير النبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم) اسم العاصي، وعزيز،

وعتلة، عتلة، وشيطان، والحكم، وغراب، وحباب، وشهاب، فسماه هاشما، وسمى حربا

سلما، وسمى المضطجع المنبعث، وأرضا يقال لها عقرة سماها خضرة، وشعب الضلالة

سماه شعب الهدى، وبنو الزينة سماهم بني الرشدة، وسمى بني مغوية بني رشدة.
# قال أبو داود: تركت أسانيدها للاختصار.
# قلت: عتلة بفتح العين المهملة وسكون التاء المثناة فوق، قاله ابن ماكولا،

قال: وقال عبد الغني: عتلة: يعني بفتح التاء أيضا، قال: وسماه النبي (صلى

الله عليه وسلم) عتبة، وهو عتبة بن عبد السلمي.

| (باب جواز ترخيم الاسم إذا لم يتأذ بذلك صاحبه)

| 870 - 
# روينا في الصحيح من طرق كثيرة " أن رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) رخم

أسماء جماعة من الصحابة، فمن ذلك قوله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) لأبي هريرة رضي

الله عنه: يا أبا هر " وقوله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) لعائشة رضي الله عنها "

يا عائش " ولأنجشة رضي الله عنه " ياأنجش "

| 871 - 
# وفي كتاب ابن السني أن النبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم) قال لأسامة: يا أسيم "

وللمقدتم " يا قديم ".
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ن-ع-ل (na-ʿa-la)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The sandal (naʿl) and its plural (niʿāl); a covering for the foot, specifically the sole.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The term denotes the physical foot-covering; in prophetic discourse, it carries a practical admonitory nuance regarding ritual purity and humility before the dead.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for the footwear itself; metaphorical (majāz) extension is absent here — the command to remove them is literal, tied to the sanctity of the graveyard.
- Root: ع-ق-ق (ʿa-q-q)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Severance, cutting off; filial disobedience (ʿuqūq) as a severing of the bond of dutifulness.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Theological-ethical term for the rupture of the commanded tie of birr (piety toward parents); it is a major sin in the Qur'anic moral framework.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal root meaning of splitting; metaphorically applied to the moral breach between child and parent.
- Root: غ-ي-ر (gh-y-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To alter, transform, or exchange one thing for another.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In prophetic practice, taḥwīl al-ism (changing a name) signifies a spiritual re-orientation — replacing an inauspicious or blameworthy designation with a praiseworthy one.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal act of substitution; rhetorically, it underscores the prophetic authority to redefine identity through language.
- Root: ر-خ-م (r-kh-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Softness, tenderness; in grammar, tarakhīm is the apocopated or abbreviated form of a name (e.g., Yā Abā Hura for Abū Hurayrah).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Not a theological term; its application here is purely linguistic and social — a mark of intimacy and affection.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal softening of the name's form; metaphorically, it signals endearment and familiarity, permissible when no offense is caused.
- Sībawayh Rule: Al-Tarakhīm (Apocopation) — The dropping of the final syllable or letters of a proper noun in vocative address (al-nidāʾ), a recognized syntactic license in Arabic; also, the rule of ʿaṭf al-bayān (explicative apposition) for clarifying name variants in chains of transmission.
chapters.translation:
859 — We have related in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd, al-Nasāʾī, and Ibn Mājah, with a sound chain of transmission (isnād ḥasan), on the authority of Bashīr ibn Muʿbad, known as Ibn al-Khaṣāṣiyyah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "While I was walking alongside the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), he looked and saw a man walking between the graves wearing two sandals. He said: 'O wearer of the two sandals (ṣāḥib al-sibtayayn) — woe to you! Cast off your two sandals.'" And he mentioned the rest of the hadith.
I say: The sandals called sibtīyah — with a kasrah on the sīn — are those upon which there is no hair (i.e., made of tanned leather without fur).

860 — We have related in the book of Ibn al-Sunnī, on the authority of Jāriyah al-Anṣārī, the Companion (may Allah be pleased with him) — and it is with a jīm (i.e., Jāriyah, not Ḥāriyah) — who said: "I was with the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), and whenever he did not retain a man's name, he would say: 'O son of ʿAbd Allāh.'"

[Section on the Prohibition of a Child, Student, and Disciple Calling His Father, Teacher, and Shaykh by Name]

861 — We have related in the book of Ibn al-Sunnī, on the authority of Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him): "That the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) saw a man with a young boy, and he said to the boy: 'Who is this?' He said: 'My father.' He said: 'Then do not walk before him, do not cause him to be cursed (lā tastasibb lahu), do not sit before him, and do not call him by his name.'"
I say: The meaning of "lā tastasibb lahu" is: do not commit an act by which you expose yourself to your father being cursed as a rebuke to you, as a discipline for your ugly deed.

862 — We have related in it (i.e., Ibn al-Sunnī's book), on the authority of the noble master, the righteous servant, whose righteousness is unanimously agreed upon, ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Zahr — with a fatḥah on the zāy and a sukūn on the ḥāʾ (i.e., Zahr, not Zuhar) — may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "It is said that it is part of filial disobedience (ʿuqūq) that you call your father by his name, and that you walk before him on the road."

[Section on the Recommendation of Changing a Name to a Better One]

862m — In it (i.e., this section) is the hadith of Sahl ibn Saʿd al-Sāʿidī, already mentioned in the section on naming a newborn, in the story of al-Mundhir ibn Abī Usayd.

863 — We have related in the two Ṣaḥīḥs of al-Bukhārī and Muslim, on the authority of Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him): "That Zaynab's name was Barrah (i.e., 'the pious one'), and it was said: 'She praises herself (tuzakkī nafsahā),' so the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) named her Zaynab."

864 — And in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, on the authority of Zaynab bint Abī Salamah (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: "I was named Barrah, and the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: 'Name her Zaynab.' She said: 'And Zaynab bint Jaḥsh entered upon him, and her name was Barrah, so he named her Zaynab.'"

865 — And in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim as well, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "Juwayriyah's name was Barrah, so the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) changed her name to Juwayriyah, for he disliked that it be said: 'He came out from Barrah's (i.e., 'the pious one's') presence' — a phrasing that could imply self-praise."

866 — We have related in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, on the authority of Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib ibn Ḥazn, from his father, that his father came to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), who said: "What is your name?" He said: "Ḥazn (i.e., 'roughness')." He said: "Rather, you are Sahl (i.e., 'ease')." He said: "I will not change a name my father gave me." Ibn al-Musayyib said: "And roughness (al-ḥuzūnah) has remained among us ever since."
I say: Al-ḥuzūnah means harshness of countenance and a measure of hardness (of disposition).

867 — We have related in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī and Muslim, on the authority of Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both): "That the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) changed the name of ʿĀṣiyah (i.e., 'the disobedient one'), and said: 'You are Jamīlah (i.e., 'the beautiful one').'"
And in a narration also of Muslim: "That a daughter of ʿUmar was called ʿĀṣiyah, so the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) named her Jamīlah."

868 — We have related in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd, with a sound chain of transmission, on the authority of Usāmah ibn Ukhaydirī, the Companion (may Allah be pleased with him) — and Ukhaydirī is with a fatḥah on the hamzah and the dāl (unpointed), and a sukūn on the khāʾ (pointed) between them — "That a man called Aṣram (i.e., 'the cut-off one') was among the group who came to the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him), and the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: 'What is your name?' He said: 'Aṣram.' He said: 'Rather, you are Zurʿah (i.e., 'the sown one').'"

869 — We have related in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd, al-Nasāʾī, and others, on the authority of Abū Shurayḥ Hāniʾ al-Ḥārithī, the Companion (may Allah be pleased with him): "That when he came as a delegate to the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) with his people, he heard them calling him by the kunyah Abū al-Ḥakam (i.e., 'father of the judge'). The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) called him and said: 'Indeed, Allah is al-Ḥakam (the Judge), and to Him belongs the judgment (al-ḥukm). So why are you called Abū al-Ḥakam?' He said: 'When my people differ over a matter, they come to me, and I judge between them, and both parties are satisfied.' The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: 'How excellent is this! And what children do you have?' He said: 'I have Shurayḥ, Muslim, and ʿAbd Allāh.' He said: 'Who is the eldest among them?' I said: 'Shurayḥ.' He said: 'Then you are Abū Shurayḥ.'"
Abū Dāwūd said: "And the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) changed the names of al-ʿĀṣī (the disobedient), ʿAzīz, ʿAtalah, ʿAtalah, Shayṭān, al-Ḥakam, Ghurāb (crow), Ḥubāb (snake), and Shihāb (flame) — he named him Hāshim; and he named Ḥarb (war) Salam (peace); and he named al-Muḍṭajiʿ (the reclining one) al-Munbaʿith (the roused one); and a land called ʿAqirah he named Khaḍirah (green); and Shaʿb al-Ḍalālah (the valley of error) he named Shaʿb al-Hudā (the valley of guidance); and Banū al-Zaynah (the sons of adornment) he named Banū al-Rishdah (the sons of right guidance); and he named Banū Mughwiyah (the sons of seduction) Banū Rishdah (the sons of guidance)."
Abū Dāwūd said: "I have omitted their chains of transmission for the sake of brevity."
I say: ʿAtalah is with a fatḥah on the ʿayn (unpointed) and a sukūn on the tāʾ (with two dots above); this is what Ibn Mākūlā said. He said: And ʿAbd al-Ghanī said: ʿAtalah — meaning also with a fatḥah on the tāʾ. He said: And the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) named him ʿUtbah, and he is ʿUtbah ibn ʿAbd al-Sulamī.

[Section on the Permissibility of Apocopating (Tarakhīm) a Name When Its Owner Is Not Offended]

870 — We have related in the Ṣaḥīḥ (i.e., al-Bukhārī and Muslim) through many chains of transmission: "That the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) apocopated the names of a group of the Companions. Among that is his saying (peace and blessings be upon him) to Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him): 'Yā Abā Hur (O Abā Hur),' and his saying (peace and blessings be upon him) to ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her): 'Yā ʿĀʾish (O ʿĀʾish),' and to Anjashah (may Allah be pleased with him): 'Yā Anjash (O Anjash).'"

871 — And in the book of Ibn al-Sunnī: "That the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said to Usāmah: 'Yā Usaym (O Usaym),' and to al-Miqdād: 'Yā Qadīm (O Qadīm).'"

chapters.title_en: Section 119 — On the Prohibition of Nicknames Disliked by Their Bearer; On the Permissibility and Desirability of Beloved Nicknames; On Kunyahs and Related Rulings
chapters.arabic_text:
| (باب النهي عن الألقاب التي يكرهها صاحبها)
# قال الله تعالى: (ولا تنابزوا بالألقاب) [الحجرات: 11] واتفق العلماء على

تحريم تلقيب الإنسان بما يكره، سواء كان له صفة، كالأعمش، والأجلح،

والأعمى، والأعرج، والأحول، والأبرص، والأشج، والأصفر، والأحدب، والأصم،

والأزرق، والأفطس، والأشتر، والأثرم، والأقطع، والزمن، والمقعد، والأشل، أو

كان صفة لأبيه أو لأمه أو غير ذلك مما يكره.
# واتفقوا على جواز ذكره بذلك على جهة التعريف لمن لا يعرفه إلا بذلك،

ودلائل ما ذكرته كثرة مشهورة حذفتها اختصارا واستغناء بشهرتها.

| (باب جواز واستحباب اللقب الذي يحبه صاحبه)
# فمن ذلك أبو بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه، اسمه عبد الله بن  عثمان، لقبه

عتيق، هذا هو الصحيح الذي عليه جماهير العلماء من المحدثين وأهل السير

والتواريخ وغيرهم.
# وقيل اسمه عتيق، حكاه الحافظ أبو القاسم ابن عساكر في كتابه " الأطراف "،

والصواب
# الأول، واتفق العلماء على أنه لقب خير.
# واختلفوا في سبب تسميته عتيقا.

| 872 - 
# فروينا عن عائشة رضي الله عنها من أوجه أن رسول الله (صلى الله عليه

وسلم) قال: " أبو بكر عتيق الله من النار " وقال: فمن يومئذ سمي عتيقا (1)

.
# وقال مصعب بن الزبير وغيره من أهل النسب: سمي عتيقا لأنه لم يكن في نسبه

شئ يعاب به، وقيل غير ذلك، والله أعلم.

| 873 - 
# ومن ذلك أبو تراب لقب لعلي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه، وكنيته أبو

# الحسن: ثبت في الصحيح " أن رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) وجده نائما في

المسجد وعليه التراب، فقال: قم أبا تراب، قم أبا تراب " فلزمه هذا اللقب

الحسن الجميل.

| 874 - 
# وروينا هذا في " صحيحي البخاري ومسلم " عن سهل بن سعد، قال سهل: وكانت

أحب أسماء علي إليه، وإن كان ليفرح أن يدعى بها.
# هذا لفظ رواية البخاري.
# ومن ذلك ذو اليدين واسمه الخرباق - بكسر الخاء المعجمة وبالباء الموحدة

وآخره قاف - كان في يديه طول.

| 874 - 
# ثبت في الصحيح " أن رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) كان يدعوه ذا اليدين

" واسمه الخرباق، رواه البخاري بهذا اللفظ في أوائل كتاب البر والصلة ".

| (باب جواز الكنى واستحباب مخاطبة أهل الفضل بها)
# هذا الباب أشهر من أن نذكر فيه شيئا منقولا، فإن دلائله يشترك فيها

الخواص والعوام، والأدب أن يخاطب أهل الفضل ومن قاربهم بالكنية، وكذلك إن

كتب إليه رسالة، وكذا إن روى عنه رواية، فيقال: حدثنا الشيخ أو الإمام أبو

فلان، فلان بن فلان، وما أشبهه، والأدب أن لا يذكر الرجل كنيته في كتابه

ولا في غيره، إلا أن لا يعرف إلا بكنيته، أو كانت الكنية أشهر من اسمه.
# قال النحاس: إذا كانت الكنية أشهر، يكنى
# على نظيره ويسمى لمن فوقه، ثم يلحق: المعروف أبا فلان  أو بأبي فلان.

| (باب كنية الرجل بأكبر أولاده)
# كني نبينا محمد (صلى الله عليه وسلم) أبا القاسم بابنه القاسم وكان أكبر

بنيه.

| 875 - 
# وفي الباب حديث أبي شريح الذي قدمناه في باب استحباب تغيير الاسم إلى

أحسن منه.
# (باب كنية الرجل الذي له أولاد بغير أولاده)
# هذا الباب واسع لا يحصى من يتصف به، ولا بأس بذلك.
# (باب كنية من لم يولد له وكنية الصغير)

| 876 - 
# روينا في " صحيحي البخاري ومسلم " عن أنس رضي الله عنه قال: كان النبي

(صلى الله عليه وسلم) أحسن الناس خلقا، وكان لي أخ يقال له أبو عمير: قال

الراوي: أحسبه قال
# 
# فطيم - وكان النبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم) إذا جاءه يقول: " يا أبا عمير،

ما فعل النغير " (1) نغر كان يلعب به.

| 877 - 
# وروينا بالأسانيد الصحيحية في سنن أبي داود وغيره عن عائشة رضي الله عنها

أنها قالت: " يا رسول الله كل صواحبي لهن كنى، قال: فاكتني بابنك عبد الله

" قال الراوي: يعني عبد الله بن الزبير وهو ابن أختها أسماء بنت أبي بكر،

وكانت عائشة تكنى أم عبد الله.
# قلت: فهذا هو الصحيح المعروف.

| 878 - 
# وأما ما رويناه في كتاب ابن السني عن عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت: " أسقطت

من النبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم) سقطا فسماه عبد الله، وكناني بأم عبد الله "

فهو حديث ضعيف (2) ؟.
# وقد كان في الصحابة جماعات لهم كنى قبل أن يولد لهم، كأبي هريرة، وأنس

وأبي حمزة، وخلائق لا يحصون من الصحابة والتابعين فمن بعدهم، ولا كراهة في

ذلك، بل هو محبوب بالشرط السابق.

| (باب النهي عن التكني بأبي القاسم)

| 879 - 
# روينا في " صحيحي البخاري ومسلم " عن جماعة من الصحابة، منهم جابر، وأبو

هريرة رضي الله عنهما أن رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) قال: " سموا باسمي

ولا تكنوا بكنيتي ".
# قلت: اختلف العلماء في التكني بأبي القاسم على ثلاثة مذاهب: فذهب الشافعي

رحمه الله ومن وافقه إلى أنه لا يحل لأحد أن يتكنى أبا القاسم، سواء كان

اسمه محمدا  أو غيره، وممن روى هذا من أصحابنا عن الشافعي الأئمة الحفاظ

الثقات الأثبات الفقهاء المحدثون: أبو بكر البيهقي، وأبو محمد البغوي في
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ن-ب-ز (n-b-z)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To call someone by a name or epithet that mocks, derides, or stigmatizes; the act of branding with a disparaging label.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the Quranic context {«وَلَا تَنَابَزُوا بِالْأَلْقَابِ»}, it denotes mutual vilification through offensive epithets, a moral vice rooted in arrogance (kibr) and contempt for others.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — verbal designation; metaphorical (majāz) — the intent to degrade and humiliate, which is the effective cause of prohibition.
- Root: ل-ق-ب (l-q-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A title or appellation beyond the given name, often descriptive of a physical trait, lineage, or honorific.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Distinguished between blameworthy titles (dhamm) and praiseworthy ones (madḥ); the former are prohibited when disliked, the latter encouraged when beloved.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The rhetorical shift — a title used for identification (taʿrīf) is permissible even if the trait is negative, whereas using it for derision is forbidden.
- Root: ك-ن-ي (k-n-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To address someone by a teknonymic (kunyah) beginning with "Abū" (father of) or "Umm" (mother of), even without children.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A mark of honor and respect in Islamic social ethics, elevating the addressed person's dignity.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — paternal/maternal relation; metaphorical — a gesture of veneration, as seen in the Prophet's addressing young Anas's brother as "Abū ʿUmayr."
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — When listing multiple examples (e.g., physical traits like al-aʿmash, al-aʿraj), the nouns are in apposition to the generic category, each specifying a distinct instance without requiring repetition of the governing verb.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that the section on the prohibition of nicknames which their bearer dislikes is established by the saying of Allah the Exalted: {«وَلَا تَنَابَزُوا بِالْأَلْقَابِ»} [al-Ḥujurāt: 11]. The scholars are unanimously agreed upon the prohibition of labeling a person with something he dislikes, whether it be a description of him — such as the bleary-eyed (al-aʿmash), the bald (al-ajlaḥ), the blind (al-aʿmā), the lame (al-aʿraj), the squint-eyed (al-aḥwal), the leprous (al-abraṣ), the scarred (al-ashajj), the yellow-complexioned (al-aṣfar), the hunchbacked (al-aḥdab), the deaf (al-aṣamm), the blue-eyed (al-azraq), the flat-nosed (al-afṭas), the split-lidded (al-ashtar), the gap-toothed (al-athram), the amputee (al-aqṭaʿ), the chronically ill (al-zamin), the bedridden (al-maqʿad), the paralyzed-handed (al-ashal) — or whether it be a description of his father, his mother, or anything else that he dislikes.

They are also unanimously agreed upon the permissibility of mentioning him by such a description by way of identification (taʿrīf) for one who knows him only by that means. The evidences for what I have mentioned are numerous and well-known; I have omitted them for brevity and reliance upon their fame.

Then, the section on the permissibility and desirability of a nickname which its bearer loves. Among such examples is Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, may Allah be pleased with him — his name was ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUthmān, and his nickname was ʿAtīq. This is the correct view, upon which the majority of scholars among the ḥadīth specialists, the biographers, the historians, and others concur. It was also said that his name was ʿAtīq, as related by the ḥāfiẓ Abū al-Qāsim Ibn ʿAsākir in his book al-Aṭrāf, but the correct view is the first. The scholars are agreed that it was a good nickname. They differed, however, regarding the reason he was called ʿAtīq.

[872] We have related from ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, through multiple chains, that the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Abū Bakr is ʿAtīq (freed) by Allah from the Fire," and he said: "From that day he was named ʿAtīq." Muṣʿab ibn al-Zubayr and others among the genealogists said: He was named ʿAtīq because there was nothing in his lineage that could be reproached. Other opinions were also mentioned, and Allah knows best.

[873] Among such examples is Abū Turāb, a nickname for ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, whose kunyah was Abū al-Ḥasan. It is established in the Ṣaḥīḥ that the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) found him sleeping in the mosque with dust upon him, and said: "Rise, O Abū Turāb! Rise, O Abū Turāb!" Thus this beautiful and excellent nickname adhered to him.

[874] We have related this in both Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī and Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim from Sahl ibn Saʿd, who said: "And it was the most beloved of ʿAlī's names to him, and he would rejoice when called by it." This is the wording of al-Bukhārī's narration.

Among such examples is Dhū al-Yadayn (the long-handed), whose name was al-Khirbāq — with a kasrah on the khāʾ (unpointed), a bāʾ (single-pointed), and a final qāf — and he had elongation in his hands. [874] It is established in the Ṣaḥīḥ that the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) used to call him Dhū al-Yadayn, and his name was al-Khirbāq. Al-Bukhārī related this with this wording at the beginning of the Book of Righteousness and Ties of Kinship (Kitāb al-Birr wa al-Ṣilah).

Then, the section on the permissibility of kunyahs and the desirability of addressing people of virtue by them. This section is too well-known to require citing anything transmitted concerning it, for its evidences are shared by the elite and the common folk alike. The proper etiquette (adab) is to address people of virtue and those close to them in rank by their kunyah. Likewise, when writing a letter to such a person, and likewise when narrating from him, one should say: "We were told by the Shaykh or the Imām, Abū so-and-so, so-and-so ibn so-and-so," and the like. The proper etiquette is also that a man should not mention his own kunyah in his book or elsewhere, unless he is known only by his kunyah, or the kunyah is more famous than his name. Al-Naḥḥās said: When the kunyah is more famous, one is addressed by it, and the person's name is mentioned for those above him, then one adds: "known as Abū so-and-so" or "by Abū so-and-so."

Then, the section on a man's kunyah by his eldest son. Our Prophet Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him) was given the kunyah Abū al-Qāsim after his son al-Qāsim, who was his eldest son. [875] In this section is the ḥadīth of Abū Shurayḥ which we have already presented in the section on the desirability of changing one's name to something better.

Then, the section on a man's kunyah by other than his children when he has children. This section is vast — those who are described by it cannot be counted — and there is no harm in it.

Then, the section on the kunyah of one who has no child born to him, and the kunyah of a young child. [876] We have related in both Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī and Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) was the best of people in character. I had a brother called Abū ʿUmayr" — the narrator said: I think he said — "a weaned child (faṭīm). And whenever the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) came to him, he would say: 'O Abū ʿUmayr, what did the little bird (nughayr) do?'" — a bird he used to play with.

[877] We have related through sound chains in Sunan Abī Dāwūd and others from ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that she said: "O Messenger of Allah, all my companions have kunyahs." He said: "Then take a kunyah from your son ʿAbdullāh." The narrator said: meaning ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Zubayr, the son of her sister Asmāʾ bint Abī Bakr. And ʿĀʾishah was called Umm ʿAbdillāh. I say: This is the correct and well-known view.

[878] As for what we have related in the book of Ibn al-Sunnī from ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: "I miscarried from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) a fetus, and he named him ʿAbdullāh, and gave me the kunyah Umm ʿAbdillāh" — this is a weak ḥadīth. Among the Companions there were many groups who had kunyahs before any child was born to them, such as Abū Hurayrah, Anas, Abū Ḥamzah, and countless others among the Companions, the Followers, and those after them. There is no dislike in that; rather, it is beloved, subject to the previously mentioned condition.

Then, the section on the prohibition of taking the kunyah Abū al-Qāsim. [879] We have related in both Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī and Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim from a group of the Companions, among them Jābir and Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Name yourselves with my name, but do not use my kunyah."

I say: The scholars differed regarding the use of the kunyah Abū al-Qāsim, holding three schools of thought. Al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah have mercy on him, and those who agreed with him held that it is not lawful for anyone to take the kunyah Abū al-Qāsim, whether his name be Muḥammad or otherwise. Among those who related this from al-Shāfiʿī from our companions are the leading, trustworthy, established jurist-ḥadīth scholars: Abū Bakr al-Bayhaqī and Abū Muḥammad al-Baghawī, in [his book]...

chapters.title_en: Section 120 — On the Permissibility of Giving Kunyahs (Teknonyms) to Disbelievers, Innovators, and Sinners, and Related Matters
chapters.arabic_text:
كتابه " التهذيب " في أول " كتاب النكاح "، وأبو القاسم بن عساكر في "

تاريخ دمشق ".
# والمذهب الثاني مذهب مالك رحمه الله أنه يجوز التكني بأبي القاسم لمن

اسمه محمد ولغيره، ويجعل النهي خاصا بحياة رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم)

.
# والمذهب الثالث: لا يجوز لمن اسمه محمد، ويجوز لغيره.
# قال الإمام أبو القاسم الرافعي من أصحابنا: يشبه أن يكون هذا الثالث أصح،

لأن الناس لم يزالوا يكتنون به في جميع الأعصار من غير إنكار، وهذا الذي

قاله صاحب هذا المذهب فيه مخالفة ظاهرة للحديث. 
# وأما إطباق الناس على فعله مع أن في المتكنين به والمكنين الأئمة

الأعلام، وأهل الحل والعقد والذين يقتدى بهم في مهمات الدين ففيه تقوية

لمذهب مالك في جوازه مطلقا، ويكونون قد فهموا من النهي الاختصاص بحياته

(صلى الله عليه وسلم) كما هو مشهور من سبب النهي في تكني اليهود بأبي

القاسم ومناداتهم: يا أبا القاسم، للإيذاء، وهذا المعنى قد زال.
# والله أعلم.

| (باب جواز تكنية الكافر والمبتدع والفاسق إذا كان لا يعرف إلا بها أو خيف من ذكره باسمه فتنة)
# قال الله تعالى: (تبت يدا أبي لهب) واسمه عبد العزى، قيل: ذكر بكنيته

لأنه يعرف بها، وقيل: كراهة لاسمه حيث جعل عبدا للصنم.

| 880 - 
# وروينا في " صحيحي البخاري ومسلم " عن أسامة بن زيد رضي الله عنهما " أن

رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) ركب على حمار ليعود سعد بن عبادة رضي الله

عنه.." فذكر الحديث ومرور النبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم) على عبد الله بن أبي

سلول المنافق، ثم قال: فسار النبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم) حتى دخل على سعد بن

عبادة، فقال النبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم) : " أي سعد، ألم تسمع إلى ما قال

أبو حباب - يريد عبد الله بن أبي - قال: كذا وكذا ... " وذكر الحديث.
# قلت: تكرر في الحديث تكنية أبي طالب، واسمه عبد  مناف، وفي الصحيح " هذا

قبر أبي رغال " ونظائر هذا كثيرة، هذا كله إذا وجد الشرط الذي ذكرناه في

الترجمة، فإن لم يوجد، لم يزد على الاسم.

| 881 - 
# كما رويناه في " صحيحيهما " أن رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) كتب: " من

محمد عبد الله ورسوله إلى هرقل " فسماه باسمه، ولم يكنه ولا لقبه بلقب ملك

الروم وهو قيصر، ونظائر هذا كثيرة، وقد أمرنا بالإغلاظ عليهم، فلا ينبغي أن

نكنيهم ولا نرقق لهم عبارة، ولا نلين لهم قولا، ولا نظهر لهم ودا ولا

مؤالفة.

| باب جواز تكنية الرجل
# بأبي فلانة وأبي فلان والمرأة بأم فلان وأم فلانة اعلم أن هذا كله لا حجر

فيه، وقد تكنى جماعات من أفاضل سلف الأمة من الصحابة والتابعين فمن بعدهم

بأبي فلانة، فمنهم عثمان بن عفان رضي الله عنه له ثلاث كنى: أبو عمرو، وأبو

عبد الله، وأبو ليلى، ومنهم أبو الدرداء وزوجته أم الدرداء الكبرى
# 
# صحابية اسمها خيرة (1) وزوجته الأخرى أم الدرداء الصغرى اسمها هجيمة،

وكانت جليلة القدر، فقيهة فاضلة، موصوفة بالعقل الوافر، والفضل الباهر، وهي

تابعية.
# ومنهم أبو ليلى والد عبد الرحمن بن أبي ليلى، وزوجته أم ليلى، وأبو ليلى

وزوجته صحابيان.
# ومنهم أبو أمامة وجماعات من الصحابة.
# ومنهم أبو ريحانة، وأبو رمثة، وأبو ريمة، وأبو عمرة بشير بن عمرو، وأبو

فاطمة الليثي، قيل اسمه عبد الله بن أنيس، وأبو مريم الأزدي، وأبو رقية

تميم الداري، وأبو كريمة المقدام بن معد يكرب، وهؤلاء كلهم صحابة.
# ومن التابعين أبو عائشة مسروق الأجدع، وخلائق لا يحصون.
# قال السمعاني في " الأنساب " سمي مسروقا، لأنه سرقه إنسان وهو صغير ثم

وجد.

| 882 - 
# وقد ثبت في الأحاديث الصحيحة تكنية النبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم) أبا هريرة

بأبي هريرة.

| كتاب الأذكار المتفرقة
# اعلم أن هذا الكتاب أنثر فيه إن شاء الله تعالى أبوابا متفرقة من الأذكار

والدعوات يعظم الانتفاع بها إن شاء الله تعالى، وليس لها ضابط نلتزم

ترتيبها بسببه، والله الموفق.

| (باب استحباب حمد الله تعالى والثناء عليه عند  البشارة بما يسره)
# اعلم أنه يستحب لمن تجددت له نعمة ظاهرة، أو اندفعت عنه نقمة ظاهرة أن

يسجد شكرا لله تعالى، وأن يحمد الله تعالى، أو يثني عليه بما هو أهله،

والأحاديث والآثار في هذا كثيرة مشهورة.

| 883 - 
# روينا في " صحيح البخاري " عن عمرو بن ميمون في مقتل عمر بن الخطاب رضي

الله عنه في حديث الشورى الطويل، أن عمر رضي الله عنه أرسل ابنه عبد الله

إلى عائشة رضي الله عنها يستأ ذنها أن يدفن مع صاحبيه، فلما أقبل عبد الله

قال 
# عمر: ما لديك؟ قال: الذي تحب يا أمير المؤمنين، أذنت، قال: الحمدلله، ما

كان شئ أهم إلي من ذلك.

| (باب ما يقول إذا سمع صياح الديك ونهيق الحمار ونباح الكلب)

| 884 - 
# روينا في " صحيحي البخاري ومسلم " عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن النبي

(صلى الله عليه وسلم) قال: " إذا سمعتم نهاق الحمير فتعوذوا بالله من

الشيطان، فإنها رأت شيطانا، وإذا سمعتم صياح الديكة فاسألوا الله من فضله

فإنها رأت ملكا ".
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ك-ن-ي (k-n-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The root denotes concealment and covering; a kunyah (teknonym) is an honorific appellation derived from a child's name (e.g., Abū Qāsim, "father of Qāsim"), serving as a dignified form of address that veils the bearer's direct name.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological discourse, the kunyah functions as a marker of social respect and identity; its permissibility in addressing others is governed by intent (niyyah) and context, particularly regarding honorifics for those of differing faith or moral standing.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literally, the kunyah is a relational epithet; metaphorically (majāz), it extends to any appellation used to honor or identify, even when the named person lacks the nominal child—thus the Prophet's (ﷺ) kunyah "Abū al-Qāsim" is literal, while applying it to others is a metaphorical extension subject to juristic restriction.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — When multiple kunyahs are listed (e.g., "Abū ʿAmr, Abū ʿAbd Allāh, Abū Laylā" for ʿUthmān), each functions as an appositive clarifying the same referent, requiring precise nominal agreement in parsing.
chapters.translation:
I say: His book "Al-Tahdhīb" at the beginning of "The Book of Marriage," and Abū al-Qāsim ibn ʿAsākir in his "History of Damascus."

The second school is the school of Mālik, may Allah have mercy on him, that it is permissible to adopt the kunyah "Abū al-Qāsim" for one whose name is Muḥammad and for others, and he makes the prohibition specific to the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

The third school: It is not permissible for one whose name is Muḥammad, but it is permissible for others.

The Imām Abū al-Qāsim al-Rāfiʿī, one of our companions (Shāfiʿīs), said: It is likely that this third view is the most correct, because people have never ceased to adopt this kunyah in all ages without any disapproval. However, what the proponent of this school has said contains an apparent contradiction of the ḥadīth.

As for the consensus of the people upon doing so—while among those who adopted it and those who bestowed it are the eminent Imāms, the people of authority and binding counsel (ahl al-ḥall wa al-ʿaqd), and those who are emulated in the important matters of religion—this strengthens the school of Mālik regarding its absolute permissibility. They would have understood from the prohibition its specificity to his lifetime (ﷺ), as is well-known from the cause of the prohibition concerning the Jews' teknonym of "Abū al-Qāsim" and their calling out, "O Abū al-Qāsim," as a means of annoyance—and this meaning has ceased to exist.

And Allah knows best.

| Chapter on the Permissibility of Giving a Kunyah to a Disbeliever, an Innovator, and a Sinner, if He Is Known Only by It, or If Fear of Mentioning Him by His Name Would Cause Tribulation |

Allah the Exalted said: {«Perish the hands of Abū Lahab»} (Quran 111:1). His name was ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā. It is said: He was mentioned by his kunyah because he was known by it; and it is said: out of aversion to his name, since he was made a servant to the idol.

| 880 -
We have related in the two Ṣaḥīḥs of al-Bukhārī and Muslim, on the authority of Usāmah ibn Zayd, may Allah be pleased with them both, "that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) rode a donkey to visit Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah, may Allah be pleased with him..." — and he mentioned the ḥadīth, and the passing of the Prophet (ﷺ) by ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl, the hypocrite. Then he said: The Prophet (ﷺ) proceeded until he entered upon Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O Saʿd, did you not hear what Abū Ḥubāb said—meaning ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy—he said such-and-such..." — and he mentioned the ḥadīth.

I say: In the ḥadīth, the teknonym of Abū Ṭālib is repeated, and his name was ʿAbd Manāf. And in the Ṣaḥīḥ: "This is the grave of Abū Righāl." And similar examples are numerous. All of this is when the condition we mentioned in the chapter heading is present; if it is not present, then one should not go beyond the name.

| 881 -
As we have related in the two Ṣaḥīḥs, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wrote: "From Muḥammad, the servant of Allah and His Messenger, to Heraclius" — so he named him by his name, and did not give him a kunyah, nor did he address him by the title of the king of the Romans, which is Caesar. And similar examples are numerous. And we have been commanded to be harsh with them, so it is not befitting that we give them kunyahs, nor soften our expression toward them, nor soften our speech to them, nor show them affection or amity.

| Chapter on the Permissibility of a Man's Kunyah Being "Abū So-and-So (Female)" and "Abū So-and-So (Male)," and a Woman's "Umm So-and-So (Male)" and "Umm So-and-So (Female)" |

Know that all of this has no restriction upon it. Numerous groups of the virtuous predecessors (salaf) of this nation—from the Companions, the Followers, and those after them—adopted kunyahs like "Abū So-and-So (female)." Among them is ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, may Allah be pleased with him, who had three kunyahs: Abū ʿAmr, Abū ʿAbd Allāh, and Abū Laylā. Among them is Abū al-Dardāʾ and his wife Umm al-Dardāʾ al-Kubrā, a female Companion whose name was Khayrah. And his other wife, Umm al-Dardāʾ al-Ṣughrā, whose name was Hujaymah—she was of great standing, a jurist, virtuous, described as possessing abundant intellect and manifest excellence, and she was a Follower (tābiʿiyyah).

Among them is Abū Laylā, the father of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, and his wife Umm Laylā—Abū Laylā and his wife were both Companions.

Among them is Abū Umāmah and numerous groups of the Companions.

Among them is Abū Rayḥānah, Abū Rimthah, Abū Raymah, Abū ʿAmrah Bashīr ibn ʿAmr, Abū Fāṭimah al-Laythī (it is said his name was ʿAbd Allāh ibn Unays), Abū Maryam al-Azdī, Abū Ruqayyah Tamīm al-Dārī, and Abū Karīmah al-Miqdām ibn Maʿdīkarib—all of these were Companions.

And among the Followers is Abū ʿĀʾishah Masrūq ibn al-Ajdaʿ, and countless others.

Al-Samʿānī said in "Al-Ansāb": He was named Masrūq because a man stole him while he was young, and then he was found.

| 882 -
And it is established in the authentic ḥadīths that the Prophet (ﷺ) gave Abū Hurayrah the kunyah "Abū Hurayrah."

| The Book of Miscellaneous Remembrances |

Know that in this book I shall, Allah willing, spread out miscellaneous chapters of remembrances (adhkār) and supplications (daʿawāt), the benefit of which will be great, Allah willing. There is no single organizing principle by which I am bound to arrange them. And Allah is the Granter of success.

| Chapter on the Recommendation of Praising Allah the Exalted and Extolling Him upon Receiving Glad Tidings of What Brings Joy |

Know that it is recommended for one upon whom a manifest blessing has newly come, or from whom a manifest affliction has been repelled, to prostrate in gratitude to Allah the Exalted, and to praise Allah the Exalted, or to extol Him as He deserves. The ḥadīths and reports (āthār) concerning this are numerous and well-known.

| 883 -
We have related in the Ṣaḥīḥ of al-Bukhārī, on the authority of ʿAmr ibn Maymūn, concerning the killing of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, in the lengthy ḥadīth of the Shūrā (consultative council), that ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, sent his son ʿAbd Allāh to ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, to seek her permission to be buried with his two companions. When ʿAbd Allāh returned, ʿUmar said: "What do you have?" He said: "That which you love, O Commander of the Believers—she has given permission." He said: "Praise be to Allah (al-ḥamdu lillāh). Nothing was more important to me than that."

| Chapter on What One Says Upon Hearing the Crow of a Rooster, the Bray of a Donkey, and the Bark of a Dog |

| 884 -
We have related in the two Ṣaḥīḥs of al-Bukhārī and Muslim, on the authority of Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "When you hear the braying of donkeys, seek refuge with Allah from Satan, for they have seen a devil. And when you hear the crowing of roosters, ask Allah of His bounty, for they have seen an angel."

chapters.title_en: Section 121 — Remembrances Upon Hearing Dogs Barking, Seeing Fire, Rising from a Gathering, and Upon Anger
chapters.arabic_text:
| 885 - 
# وروينا في سنن أبي داود عن جابر بن عبد الله رضي الله عنهما قال: قال

رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) : " إذا سمعتم نباح الكلاب ونهيق الحمير

بالليل فتعوذوا بالله، فإنهن يرين ما لا ترون ".

| (باب ما يقول إذا رأى الحريق)

| 886 - 
# روينا في كتاب ابن السني عن عمرو بن شعيب عن أبيه عن جده رضي الله عنه

قال: قال رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) : " إذا رأيتم الحريق فكبروا، فإن

التكبير يطفئه ".
# ويستحب أن يدعو مع ذلك بدعاء الكرب وغيره مما قدمناه في " كتاب الأذكار

للأمور العارضات وعند العاهات والآفات ".

| (باب ما يقوله عند القيام من المجلس)

| 887 - 
# روينا في كتاب الترمذي وغيره عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول

الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم: " من جلس في مجلس فكثر فيه لغطه فقال قبل أن

يقوم من مجلسه ذلك:
# سبحانك اللهم وبحمدك، أشهد أن لا إله إلا أنت، أستغفرك وأتوب إليك، إلا

غفر له ما كان في مجلسه ذلك " قال الترمذي: حديث حسن صحيح.

| 888 - 
# وروينا في سنن أبي داود وغيره عن أبي برزة رضي الله عنه واسمه نضلة قال:

كان رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) يقول بأخرة إذا أراد أن يقوم من

المجلس: " سبحانك اللهم وبحمدك، أشهد أن لا إله إلا أنت، أستغفرك، وأتوب

إليك "، فقال رجل: يا رسول الله إنك لتقول قولا ما كنت تقوله فيما مضى،

قال: " ذلك كفارة لما يكون في المجلس " 
# ورواه الحاكم في " المستدرك " من رواية عائشة رضي الله عنها وقال: صحيح

الإسناد.
# قلت: قوله بأخرة، وهو بهمزة مقصورة مفتوحة وبفتح الخاء، ومعناه: في آخر

الأمر.

| 889 - 
# وروينا في " حلية الأولياء " عن علي رضي الله عنه قال: من أحب أن يكتال

بالمكيال الأوفى فليقل في آخر مجلسه أو حين يقول: سبحان ربك رب العزة عما

يصفون، وسلام على المرسلين، والحمد لله رب العالمين (1) .

| (باب دعاء الجالس في جمع لنفسه ومن معه)

| 890 - 
# روينا في كتاب الترمذي عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما قال: " قلما كان رسول

الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) يقوم من مجلس حتى يدعو بهؤلاء الدعوات لأصحابه:

" اللهم اقسم لنا من خشيتك (2) ما تحول به بيننا وبين معاصيك، ومن طاعتك ما

تبلغنا به جنتك، ومن اليقين ما تهون به علينا مصائب الدنيا، اللهم متعنا

بأسماعنا وأبصارنا وقوتنا ما أحييتنا، واجعله الوارث منا، واجعل ثأرنا على

من ظلمنا، وانصرنا على من عادانا ولا تجعل مصيبتنا في ديننا، ولا تجعل

الدنيا أكبر همنا ولا مبلغ علمنا، ولا تسلط علينا من لا يرحمنا " قال
# الترمذي: حديث حسن.

| (باب كراهة القيام من المجلس قبل أن يذكر الله تعالى)

| 891 - 
# روينا بالإسناد الصحيح في سنن أبي داود وغيره عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه

قال: قال رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) : " ما من قوم يقومون من مجلس لا

يذكرون الله تعالى فيه إلا قاموا عن مثل جيفة حمار وكان لهم حسرة ".

| 892 - 
# وروينا فيه عن أبي هريرة  أيضا عن رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) قال: "

من قعد مقعدا لم يذكر الله تعالى فيه كانت عليه من الله ترة، ومن اضطجع

مضجعا لا يذكر الله تعالى فيه كانت عليه من الله ترة ".
# قلت: ترة بكسر التاء وتخفيف الراء، ومعناه: نقص، وقيل تبعة، ويجوز أن

يكون حسرة كما في الرواية الأخرى.

| 893 - 
# وروينا في كتاب الترمذي عن أبي هريرة أيضا عن النبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم)

قال: " ما جلس قوم مجلسا لم يذكروا الله تعالى فيه، ولم يصلوا على نبيهم

فيه، إلا كان عليهم ترة، فإن شاء عذبهم، وإن شاء غفر لهم " قال الترمذي:

حديث حسن.

| (باب الذكر في الطريق)

| 894 - 
# روينا في كتاب ابن السني عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن النبي (صلى الله

عليه وسلم) قال: " ما من قوم جلسوا مجلسا لم يذكروا الله عز وجل فيه إلا

كانت عليهم ترة، وما سلك رجل طريقا لم يذكر الله عز وجل فيه إلا كانت عليه

ترة " (1) .

| 895 - 
# وروينا في كتاب ابن السني و " دلائل النبوة " للبيهقي عن أبي أمامة

الباهلي
# رضي الله عنه قال: " أتى رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) جبريل (صلى الله

عليه وسلم) وهو بتبوك فقال: يا محمد اشهد جنازة معاوية بن معاوية المزني،

فخرج رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) ، ونزل جبريل (عليه السلام) في سبعين

ألفا من الملائكة، فوضع جناحه الأيمن على الجبال فتواضعت، ووضع جناحه

الأيسر على الأرضين فتواضعت، حتى نظر إلى مكة والمدينة، فصلى عليه رسول

الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) وجبريل والملائكة (عليهم السلام) ، فلما فرغ

قال: يا جبريل بم بلغ معاوية هذه المنزلة؟ قال: بقراءته: قل هو الله أحد،

قائما وراكبا وماشيا " (2) .

| (باب ما يقول إذا غضب)
# قال الله تعالى: (والكاظمين الغيظ والعافين عن الناس ... ) الآية [آل

عمران: 134] وقال تعالى: (وإما ينزغنك من الشيطان نزغ فاستعذ بالله إنه هو

السميع العليم) [الاعراف: 199] .

| 896 - 
# وروينا في " صحيحي البخاري ومسلم " عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه أن رسول
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-و-ذ (ʿ-w-dh)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Seeking refuge, clinging to a protector; the act of entrusting oneself to a sheltering power.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, istiʿādhah denotes the believer's recourse to Allah as the sole sanctuary against unseen harms, both physical and spiritual.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — actual seeking of protection; metaphorical (majāz) — the verbal formula as a shield against evil.
- Root: ك-ب-ر (k-b-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Magnification, declaring greatness; the root conveys the idea of exceeding in size or rank.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Takbīr as the declaration of Allah's supremacy, a means of spiritual dominion over worldly calamities.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — proclaiming Allah's greatness; metaphorical — the takbīr's efficacy in extinguishing fire by divine decree.
- Root: ت-ر-ه (t-r-h)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Deficiency, loss, or a claim against someone; a state of incompleteness.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In eschatological context, tirah signifies a divine grievance or reckoning for neglected remembrance.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — a deficit; metaphorical — a burden of accountability (tabiʿah) or regret (ḥasrah).
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — The protasis (e.g., "if you hear") governs the apodosis ("seek refuge"), with the imperative serving as the response, indicating a causal and obligatory linkage.
chapters.translation:
I say: We have related in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd, on the authority of Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "When you hear the barking of dogs and the braying of donkeys at night, seek refuge with Allah, for they see what you do not see."

[Chapter: What One Says Upon Seeing a Fire]

| 886 —
We have related in the book of Ibn al-Sunnī, on the authority of ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb, from his father, from his grandfather (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "When you see a fire, then magnify Allah (say takbīr), for indeed the takbīr extinguishes it." And it is recommended to supplicate alongside that with the supplication of distress (duʿāʾ al-karb) and other such supplications which we have already presented in "The Book of Remembrances for Contingent Matters and Upon Afflictions and Calamities."

[Chapter: What One Says Upon Rising from a Gathering]

| 887 —
We have related in the book of al-Tirmidhī and others, on the authority of Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever sits in a gathering wherein much clamor occurs, and then says before rising from that gathering: 'Glory be to You, O Allah, and with Your praise; I bear witness that there is no god but You; I seek Your forgiveness and I repent to You' — except that he is forgiven for what occurred in that gathering." Al-Tirmidhī said: A ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ ḥadīth.

| 888 —
And we have related in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd and others, on the authority of Abū Barzah (may Allah be pleased with him) — and his name is Naḍlah — who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) used to say at the end (bi-ākhiratin) when he intended to rise from the gathering: "Glory be to You, O Allah, and with Your praise; I bear witness that there is no god but You; I seek Your forgiveness and I repent to You." A man said: O Messenger of Allah, you indeed say a saying which you did not used to say previously. He said: "That is an expiation for what occurs in the gathering." And al-Ḥākim related it in "Al-Mustadrak" from the narration of ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her), and he said: Its chain is ṣaḥīḥ.

I say: His saying "bi-ākhiratin" — it is with a shortened, open hamzah and with a fatḥah on the khāʾ — and its meaning is: at the end of the matter.

| 889 —
And we have related in "Ḥilyat al-Awliyāʾ" on the authority of ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: Whoever loves to be measured with the fullest measure, let him say at the end of his gathering, or at the time he says: {«Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of Might, above what they describe, and peace be upon the messengers, and praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds»} (Quran 37:180-182).

[Chapter: The Supplication of One Sitting in a Gathering for Himself and Those with Him]

| 890 —
We have related in the book of al-Tirmidhī, on the authority of Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: Rarely did the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) rise from a gathering until he supplicated with these supplications for his companions: "O Allah, apportion for us from Your fear that which will serve as a barrier between us and Your acts of disobedience, and from Your obedience that which will convey us to Your Paradise, and from certainty that which will make the calamities of this world easy upon us. O Allah, let us enjoy our hearing, our sight, and our strength as long as You keep us alive, and make it the inheritor from us, and make our vengeance upon those who wronged us, and grant us victory over those who are hostile to us, and do not make our calamity in our religion, and do not make this world our greatest concern nor the limit of our knowledge, and do not give authority over us to one who does not show us mercy." Al-Tirmidhī said: A ḥasan ḥadīth.

[Chapter: The Dislike of Rising from a Gathering Before Mentioning Allah (Exalted is He)]

| 891 —
We have related with a sound chain (al-isnād al-ṣaḥīḥ) in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd and others, on the authority of Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "No people rise from a gathering in which they do not mention Allah (Exalted is He) — except that they rise from the like of a donkey's carcass, and it will be a source of regret for them."

| 892 —
And we have related therein, on the authority of Abū Hurayrah as well, from the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him), who said: "Whoever sits in a sitting place in which he does not mention Allah (Exalted is He) — upon him is a tirah from Allah. And whoever lies down in a lying place in which he does not mention Allah (Exalted is He) — upon him is a tirah from Allah." I say: Tirah — with a kasrah on the tāʾ and a tashdīd-free rāʾ — and its meaning is: deficiency; and it is said: a liability (tabiʿah); and it is permissible that it be regret (ḥasrah), as in the other narration.

| 893 —
And we have related in the book of al-Tirmidhī, on the authority of Abū Hurayrah as well, from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), who said: "No people sit in a gathering in which they do not mention Allah (Exalted is He) and do not send blessings upon their Prophet therein — except that upon them is a tirah. Then if He wills, He punishes them, and if He wills, He forgives them." Al-Tirmidhī said: A ḥasan ḥadīth.

[Chapter: Remembrance on the Road]

| 894 —
We have related in the book of Ibn al-Sunnī, on the authority of Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), who said: "No people sit in a gathering in which they do not mention Allah (Mighty and Majestic is He) — except that upon them is a tirah. And no man traverses a road in which he does not mention Allah (Mighty and Majestic is He) — except that upon him is a tirah."

| 895 —
And we have related in the book of Ibn al-Sunnī and in "Dalāʾil al-Nubuwwah" of al-Bayhaqī, on the authority of Abū Umāmah al-Bāhilī (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) while he was at Tabūk, and said: O Muḥammad, attend the funeral prayer of Muʿāwiyah ibn Muʿāwiyah al-Muzanī. So the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) went out, and Gabriel (peace be upon him) descended with seventy thousand angels. He placed his right wing upon the mountains, and they became humbled, and he placed his left wing upon the earths, and they became humbled, until he looked upon Mecca and Medina. Then the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) prayed over him, along with Gabriel and the angels (peace be upon them). When he finished, he said: O Gabriel, by what did Muʿāwiyah attain this station? He said: By his recitation of {«Say: He is Allah, the One»} (Quran 112:1), standing, riding, and walking.

[Chapter: What One Says When Angry]
Allah (Exalted is He) said: {«And those who restrain anger and pardon the people...»} (Quran 3:134), and He (Exalted is He) said: {«And if an incitement from Satan provokes you, then seek refuge with Allah; indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing»} (Quran 7:199).

| 896 —
And we have related in the two Ṣaḥīḥs of al-Bukhārī and Muslim, on the authority of Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Messenger of...

chapters.title_en: Section 122 — On Anger, Its Remedy, and Related Matters
chapters.arabic_text:
الله  (صلى الله عليه وسلم) قال: " ليس الشديد بالصرعة، إنما الشديد الذي

يملك نفسه عند الغضب ".

| 897 - 
# وروينا في " صحيح مسلم " عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله

(صلى الله عليه وسلم) : " ما تعدون الصرعة فيكم؟ " قلنا: الذي لا تصرعه

الرجال، قال: " ليس بذلك، ولكنه الذي يملك نفسه عند الغضب " 
# قلت: الصرعة بضم الصاد وفتح الراء - وأصله الذي يصرع الناس كثيرا كالهمزة

واللمزة الذي يهمزهم (1) كثيرا.

| 898 - 
# وروينا في سنن أبي داود، والترمذي، وابن ماجه، عن معاذ بن أنس
# الجهني الصحابي رضي الله عنه، أن النبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم) قال: " من

كظم غيظا وهو قادر على أن ينفذه دعاه الله سبحانه وتعالى على رؤوس الخلائق

يوم القيامة حتى يخيره من الحور ما شاء " قال الترمذي: حديث حسن.

| 899 - 
# وروينا في " صحيحي البخاري ومسلم " عن سليمان بن صرد الصحابي رضي الله

عنه قال: كنت جالسا مع النبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم) ورجلان يستبان، وأحدهما

قد احمر وجهه، وانتفخت أوداجه، فقال رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) : "

إني لأعلم كلمة لو قالها لذهب عنه ما يجد، لو قال: أعوذ بالله من الشيطان

الرجيم، ذهب منه ما يجد، فقالوا له: أن النبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم) قال:

تعوذ بالله من الشيطان الرجيم، فقال: وهل بي من جنون؟ ".

| 900 - 
# ورويناه في كتابي أبي داود والترمذي بمعناه، من رواية عبد الرحمن بن أبي

ليلى، عن معاذ بن جبل رضي الله عنه، عن النبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم) (2) ،

قال الترمذي: هذا مرسل: يعني أن عبد الرحمن لم يدرك معاذا (3) .

| 901 - 
# وروينا في كتاب ابن السني، عن عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت: " دخل علي النبي

(صلى الله عليه وسلم) وأنا غضبى، فأخذ بطرف المفصل من أنفي، فعركه، ثم قال:

يا عويش قولي: اللهم اغفر لي ذنبي، وأذهب غيظ قلبي، وأجرني من الشيطان "

(4) .

| 902 - 
# وروينا في سنن أبي داود، عن عطية بن عروة السعدي الصحابي رضي الله عنه،

قال: قال رسول الله (صلى الله عليه  وسلم) : " إن الغضب من الشيطان، وإن

الشيطان خلق من النار، وإنما تطفأ النار بالماء، فإذا غضب أحدكم فليتوضأ "

(5) .

| (باب استحباب إعلام الرجل من يحبه أنه يحبه، وما يقوله له إذا أعلمه)

| 903 - 
# روينا في سنن أبي داود والترمذي عن المقدام بن معد يكرب رضي الله عنه عن

النبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم) قال: " إذا أحب الرجل أخاه فليخبره أنه يحبه "

قال الترمذي: حديث حسن صحيح.

| 904 - 
# وروينا في سنن أبي داود، عن أنس رضي الله عنه " أن رجلا كان عند النبي

(صلى الله عليه وسلم) ، فمر رجل فقال: يا رسول الله إني لأحب هذا، فقال له

النبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم) : أعلمته؟ قال: لا، قال: أعلمه، فلحقه فقال:

إني أحبك في الله، قال: أحبك الذي أحببتني له " (1) .

| 905 - 
# وروينا في سنن أبي داود والنسائي، عن معاذ بن جبل رضي الله عنه أن رسول

الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) أخذ بيده وقال: " يا معاذ، والله إني لأحبك،

أوصيك يا معاذ لا تدعن في دبر كل صلاة أن تقول: اللهم أعني على ذكرك وشكرك

وحسن عبادتك " (2) .

| 906 - 
# وروينا في كتاب الترمذي عن يزيد بن نعامة الضبي قال: قال رسول الله (صلى

الله عليه وسلم) : " إذا آخى الرجل الرجل فليسأله عن اسمه واسم أبيه وممن

هو، فإنه أوصل للمودة ".
# قال الترمذي: حديث غريب لا نعرفه إلا من هذا الوجه، قال: ولا نعلم ليزيد

بن نعامة سماعا من النبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم) قال: ويروى عن ابن عمر عن

النبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم) نحو هذا، ولا يصح إسناده.
# قلت: وقد اختلف في صحبة يزيد بن نعامة، فقال عبد الرحمن بن أبي حاتم: لا

صحبة له، قال: وحكى البخاري أن له صحبة، قال: وغلط.

| (باب ما يقول إذا رأى مبتلى بمرض أو غيره)

| 907 - 
# روينا في كتاب الترمذي عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن النبي (صلى الله

عليه وسلم) قال: " من رأى مبتلى فقال: الحمد لله الذي عافاني مما ابتلاك به

وفضلني على  كثير ممن خلق تفضيلا، لم يصبه ذلك البلاء " قال الترمذي: حديث

حسن.

| 908 - 
# وروينا في كتاب الترمذي عن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله (صلى

الله عليه وسلم) قال: " من رأى صاحب بلاء فقال: الحمد لله الذي عافاني مما

ابتلاك به وفضلني على كثير ممن خلق تفضيلا إلا عوفي من ذلك البلاء كائنا ما

كان ما عاش " ضعف الترمذي إسناده (1) .
# قلت: قال العلماء من أصحابنا وغيرهم: ينبغي أن يقو هذا الذكر سرا بحيث

يسمع نفسه ولا يسمعه المبتلى لئلا يتألم قلبه بذلك، إلا أن تكون بليته

معصية فلا بأس أن يسمعه ذلك إن لم يخف من ذلك مفسدة، والله أعلم.

| (باب استحباب حمد الله تعالى للمسؤول عن حاله أو حال محبوبه مع جوابه إذا كان في جوابه إخبار بطيب حاله)

| 909 - 
# روينا في " صحيح البخاري " عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما " أن عليا رضي

الله عنه خرج من عند رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) في وجعه الذي توفي
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ك-ظ-م (ka-ẓa-ma)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To restrain, suppress, or hold back; specifically the act of sealing a waterskin's mouth to prevent outflow — hence, the containment of an internal surge.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The deliberate suppression of anger (ghayẓ) through the faculty of reason; a virtue of prophetic character (ḥilm).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical containment; metaphorical (majāz) for the psychological mastery over one's emotional state.
- Root: غ-ض-ب (gha-ḍa-ba)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To become angry; the boiling agitation of the blood and temperament.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A passion (infiʿāl) of the soul that, if unchecked, leads to rash action; its opposite is forbearance (ḥilm).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the physiological state; metaphorical for divine wrath as a manifestation of justice.
- Root: ص-ر-ع (ṣa-ra-ʿa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To throw down, prostrate, or overcome in wrestling; the one who frequently overcomes others.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Physical overpowering; the Prophet's redefinition shifts the semantic field to self-mastery.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The pattern fuʿlah (ṣurʿah) denotes habitual action, like humazah and lumazah.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Predicate Emphasis (al-Qaṣr bi-al-innamā) — The restrictive particle innamā confines the predicate exclusively to the subject, negating all other possibilities, as in "innamā al-shadīd alladhī yamliku nafsahu."
chapters.translation:
I say: The Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وسلم) said: "The strong man is not the one who overcomes others in wrestling; rather, the strong man is the one who masters his own soul when angry."

| 897 -
We have related in "Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim" on the authority of Ibn Masʿūd (رضي الله عنه) who said: The Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وسلم) said: "Whom do you consider to be the strong man (al-ṣurʿah) among you?" We said: "The one whom other men cannot throw down." He said: "That is not it; rather, he is the one who masters his own soul when angry."

I say: Al-ṣurʿah — with ḍammah on the ṣād and fatḥah on the rāʾ — its origin is the one who frequently throws people down, like humazah and lumazah, which denote the one who frequently slanders and mocks them.

| 898 -
We have related in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd, al-Tirmidhī, and Ibn Mājah, on the authority of Muʿādh ibn Anas al-Juhanī, the Companion (رضي الله عنه), that the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) said: "Whoever suppresses his rage while being able to give vent to it, Allah (سبحانه وتعالى) will call him on the Day of Resurrection before the heads of all creation, until He gives him the choice of whichever of the ḥūr (maidens of Paradise) he wishes." Al-Tirmidhī said: A ḥasan (good) ḥadīth.

| 899 -
We have related in the two Ṣaḥīḥs of al-Bukhārī and Muslim, on the authority of Sulaymān ibn Ṣurad, the Companion (رضي الله عنه), who said: I was sitting with the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) when two men were exchanging insults, and one of them had his face reddened and his jugular veins swollen. The Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وسلم) said: "Indeed, I know a word which, if he were to say it, what he is experiencing would leave him. If he said: 'I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan' (aʿūdhu billāhi min al-shayṭāni al-rajīm), what he is experiencing would depart from him." So they said to him: "The Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) said: Seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan." He replied: "Is there madness in me?"

| 900 -
We have related it in the two books of Abū Dāwūd and al-Tirmidhī with its meaning, from the narration of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, on the authority of Muʿādh ibn Jabal (رضي الله عنه), from the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم). Al-Tirmidhī said: This is mursal (disconnected) — meaning that ʿAbd al-Raḥmān did not meet Muʿādh.

| 901 -
We have related in the book of Ibn al-Sunnī, on the authority of ʿĀʾishah (رضي الله عنها) who said: "The Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) entered upon me while I was angry. He took hold of the tip of my nose, rubbed it, then said: 'O ʿUwaysh (little ʿĀʾishah), say: O Allah, forgive me my sin, remove the rage from my heart, and grant me protection from Satan.'"

| 902 -
We have related in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd, on the authority of ʿAṭiyyah ibn ʿUrwah al-Saʿdī, the Companion (رضي الله عنه), who said: The Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وسلم) said: "Indeed, anger is from Satan, and indeed Satan was created from fire, and fire is extinguished only by water. So when one of you becomes angry, let him perform ablution (wuḍūʾ)."

| (Chapter: The Recommendation of Informing a Man Whom One Loves That He Loves Him, and What to Say to Him When Informing Him)

| 903 -
We have related in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd and al-Tirmidhī, on the authority of al-Miqdām ibn Maʿdīkarib (رضي الله عنه), from the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) who said: "When a man loves his brother, let him inform him that he loves him." Al-Tirmidhī said: A ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ (good and authentic) ḥadīth.

| 904 -
We have related in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd, on the authority of Anas (رضي الله عنه), that a man was with the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) when another man passed by. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, indeed I love this man." The Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) said to him: "Have you informed him?" He said: "No." He said: "Inform him." So he caught up with him and said: "I love you for the sake of Allah." He replied: "May He who you loved me for love you."

| 905 -
We have related in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd and al-Nasāʾī, on the authority of Muʿādh ibn Jabal (رضي الله عنه), that the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وسلم) took his hand and said: "O Muʿādh, by Allah, indeed I love you. I advise you, O Muʿādh: do not abandon saying after every prayer: O Allah, help me to remember You, to thank You, and to worship You well."

| 906 -
We have related in the book of al-Tirmidhī, on the authority of Yazīd ibn Nuʿāmah al-Ḍabbī, who said: The Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وسلم) said: "When a man takes another as a brother, let him ask him about his name, his father's name, and from whom he descends, for that is more conducive to affection."

Al-Tirmidhī said: A gharīb (unfamiliar) ḥadīth which we do not know except from this chain. He said: We do not know of Yazīd ibn Nuʿāmah having heard directly from the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم). He said: It is related from Ibn ʿUmar from the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) something similar, but its chain is not authentic.

I say: There is disagreement concerning Yazīd ibn Nuʿāmah's status as a Companion. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Ḥātim said: He has no Companionship. He said: Al-Bukhārī reported that he has Companionship. He said: And he erred.

| (Chapter: What to Say When Seeing Someone Afflicted with Illness or Otherwise)

| 907 -
We have related in the book of al-Tirmidhī, on the authority of Abū Hurayrah (رضي الله عنه), from the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) who said: "Whoever sees an afflicted person and says: 'Praise be to Allah who has spared me from what He has afflicted you with, and has favored me above many of His creation with a great favor' (al-ḥamdu lillāhi alladhī ʿāfānī mimmā ibtalāka bihi wa faḍḍalanī ʿalā kathīrin mimman khalaqa tafḍīlan), that affliction will not befall him." Al-Tirmidhī said: A ḥasan ḥadīth.

| 908 -
We have related in the book of al-Tirmidhī, on the authority of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb (رضي الله عنه), that the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وسلم) said: "Whoever sees a person afflicted with a trial and says: 'Praise be to Allah who has spared me from what He has afflicted you with, and has favored me above many of His creation with a great favor,' he will be spared from that affliction, whatever it may be, for as long as he lives." Al-Tirmidhī declared its chain weak.

I say: The scholars among our companions and others have said: It is recommended that this remembrance be said quietly, such that one hears himself but the afflicted person does not hear him, lest his heart be pained by it. However, if the affliction is due to disobedience (maʿṣiyah), then there is no harm in the afflicted person hearing it, provided one does not fear resulting harm. And Allah knows best.

| (Chapter: The Recommendation of Praising Allah for the One Asked About His Condition or the Condition of His Beloved, Along with His Response, When the Response Contains Information of a Good State)

| 909 -
We have related in "Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī," on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās (رضي الله عنهما), that ʿAlī (رضي الله عنه) came out from the presence of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وسلم) during his illness from which he died...

chapters.title_en: Section 123 — Supplications for Entering the Market, Marriage Congratulations, Mirror, Cupping, Ear-Ringing, Numbness, and Permissibility of Imprecation Against Oppressors
chapters.arabic_text:
فيه، فقال الناس: يا أبا حسن
# كيف أصبح رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) فقال: أصبح بحمد الله تعالى

بارئا ".

| (باب ما يقول إذا دخل السوق)

| 910 - 
# روينا في كتاب الترمذي وغيره عن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله

(صلى الله عليه وسلم) قال: " من دخل السوق فقال: لا إله إلا الله وحده لا

شريك له، له الملك، وله الحمد، يحيي ويميت، وهو حي لا يموت، بيده الخير وهو

على كل شئ قدير: كتب الله له ألف ألف حسنة، ومحا عنه ألف ألف سيئة، ورفع له

ألف ألف درجة " رواه الحاكم أبو عبد الله في " المستدرك على الصحيحين " من

طرق كثيرة (2) .
# وزاد فيه في بعض طرقه " وبنى له بيتا في الجنة " وفيه من الزيادة: قال

الراوي: فقدمت خراسان، فأتيت قتيبة بن مسلم فقلت: أتيتك بهدية فحدثته

بالحديث، فكان قتيبة بن مسلم يركب في موكبه حتى يأتي السوق فيقولها ثم

ينصرف.
# ورواه الحاكم أيضا من رواية  ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما عن النبي (صلى الله

عليه وسلم) ، قال الحاكم: وفي الباب عن جابر، وأبي هريرة وبريدة الأسلمي،

وأنس، قال: وأقربها من شرائط هذا الكتاب حديث بريدة بغير هذا اللفظ.

| 911 - 
# فرواه بإسناده عن بريدة قال: " كان رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) إذا

دخل السوق قال: 
# بسم الله، اللهم إني أسألك خير هذه السوق وخير ما فيها، وأعوذ بك من شرها

وشر ما فيها، اللهم إني أعوذ بك أن أصيب فيها يمينا فاجرة أو صفقة خاسرة "

(1) .

| (باب استحباب قول الإنسان لمن تزوج تزوجا مستحبا، أو اشترى أو فعل فعلا يستحسنه الشرع: أصبت أو أحسنت ونحوه)

| 212 - 
# روينا في " صحيح مسلم " عن جابر رضي الله عنه قال: قال لي رسول الله (صلى

الله عليه وسلم) : " تزوجت يا جابر؟ قلت: نعم، قال: بكرا أم ثيبا؟ قلت:

ثيبا يا رسول الله، قال: فهلا جارية تلاعبها وتلاعبك؟ " أو قال: " تضاحكها

وتضاحكك "، قلت: إن عبد الله - يعني أباه - توفي وترك تسع بنات أو سبعا،

وإني كرهت أن أجيئهن بمثلهن، فأحببت أن أجئ بامرأة تقوم عليهن وتصلحهن،

قال: " أصبت ... " وذكر الحديث.

| (باب ما يقول إذا نظر في المرآة)

| 913 - 
# روينا في كتاب ابن السني، عن علي رضي الله عنه، أن النبي (صلى الله عليه

وسلم) كان إذا نظر في المرآة قال: " الحمد لله، اللهم كما حسنت خلقي فحسن

خلقي " (2) .
# ورويناه فيه (3) من رواية ابن عباس بزيادة (4) .
# ورويناه فيه (5) من رواية أنس قال: كان رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم)

إذا نظر وجهه في المرآة قال: " الحمد لله الذي سوى خلقي فعدله، وكرم صورة

وجهي فحسنها، وجعلني من المسلمين " (6) .

| (باب ما يقول عند الحجامة)

| 914 - 
# روينا في كتاب ابن السني عن علي رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله (صلى

الله عليه وسلم) : " من قرأ آية الكرسي عند الحجامة كانت منفعة حجامته "

(1) .

| (باب ما يقول إذا طنت أذنه)

| 915 - 
# روينا في كتاب ابن السني عن أبي رافع رضي الله عنه مولى رسول الله  (صلى

الله عليه وسلم) قال: قال رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) : " إذا طنت أذن

أحدكم فليذكرني، وليصل علي، وليقل: ذكر الله بخير من ذكرني " (2) .

| (باب ما يقوله إذا خدرت رجله)

| 916 - 
# روينا في كتاب ابن السني عن الهيثم بن حنش قال: " كنا عند عبد الله بن

عمر رضي الله عنهما فخدرت رجله، فقال له رجل: اذكر أحب الناس إليك، فقال:

يا محمد (صلى الله عليه وسلم) ، فكأنما نشط من عقال " (3) .

| 917 - 
# وروينا فيه (4) عن مجاهد قال: " خدرت رجل رجل عند ابن عباس، فقال ابن

عباس رضي الله عنهما: اذكر أحب الناس إليك، فقال: محمد (صلى الله عليه

وسلم) فذهب خدره (5) .

| 918 - 
# وروينا فيه (6) عن إبراهيم بن المنذر الحزامي أحد شيوخ البخاري الذين روى

عنهم في " صحيحه " قال: أهل المدينة يعجبون من حسن بيت أبي العتاهية: وتخدر

في بعض الأحايين رجله * فإن لم يقل يا عتب لم يذهب الخدر

| (باب جواز دعاء الإنسان على من ظلم المسلمين أو ظلمه وحده)
# اعلم أن هذا الباب واسع جدا، وقد تظاهر على جوازه نصوص الكتاب والسنة

وأفعال سلف الأمة وخلفها، وقد أخبر الله سبحانه وتعالى في مواضع كثيرة

معلومة من القرآن عن الأنبياء صلوات الله وسلامه عليهم بدعائهم على الكفار.

| 919 - 
# رواه ينا في " صحيح البخاري ومسلم " عن علي رضي الله عنه: أن النبي (صلى

الله عليه وسلم) قال يوم الأحزاب: " ملأ الله قبورهم وبيوتهم نارا كما

شغلونا عن الصلاة الوسطى ".

| 920 - 
# وروينا في " الصحيحين " من طرق: أنه (صلى الله عليه وسلم) دعا على الذين

قتلوا القراء (1) رضي الله عنهم، وأدام الدعاء عليهم شهرا يقول: " اللهم

العن رعلا وذكوان وعصية ".

| 921 - 
# وروينا في " صحيحيهما " عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه في حديثه الطويل في

قصة أبي جهل وأصحابه من قريش حين وضعوا سلا الجزور (2) على ظهر النبي (صلى

الله عليه وسلم) فدعا عليهم وكان إذا دعا، دعا ثلاثا ثم قال: " اللهم عليك
chapters.anchors:
- Root: د-خ-ل (dakhala)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Entry, penetration into a place or state; ingress.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Physical entering (dukhūl ḥissī) as opposed to spiritual entry (dukhūl maʿnawī); here literal market-entry.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Ḥaqīqah — actual spatial entry; no metaphorical extension in this context.
- Root: س-و-ق (sūq)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Market; place of commerce; from sāqa (to drive, impel) — where goods are driven.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Worldly venue of transaction; contrast with the Hereafter's reckoning (mawqif al-ḥisāb).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal market; rhetorically, a locus of distraction from dhikr, hence the prescribed invocation.
- Root: خ-د-ر (khadara)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Numbness, torpor; also concealment (as in a curtain, khidr).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Physical paralysis of a limb; metaphorically, spiritual heedlessness.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal bodily numbness; the cure via dhikr is a ḥaqīqah of divine causation, not mere metaphor.
- Root: ل-ع-ن (laʿana)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To curse, banish from mercy; root denotes remoteness and expulsion.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Kalām, duʿāʾ ʿalā (imprecation) is permissible against wrongdoers as an act of justice, not vindictiveness.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal invocation of divine punishment; permissible when warranted by oppression, as in prophetic practice.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — In "بسم الله، اللهم إني أسألك..." the basmalah stands as an independent clause, followed by vocative (nidāʾ) with "اللهم" substituting for yā Allāhu, governing the following request in nasb via the verb "asʾaluka."
chapters.translation:
I say: And the people said: O Abā Ḥasan — how did the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) arise this morning? He replied: He arose, by the praise of Allah the Exalted, in a state of well-being.

(Chapter on What One Says Upon Entering the Market)

910 — We have related in the Book of al-Tirmidhī and others, on the authority of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever enters the market and says: 'There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner; His is the sovereignty, and His is the praise; He gives life and causes death, and He is Living and dies not; in His hand is all good, and He is over all things Omnipotent' — Allah writes for him a thousand thousand good deeds, erases from him a thousand thousand evil deeds, and raises him a thousand thousand degrees." Al-Ḥākim Abū ʿAbd Allāh related it in "Al-Mustadrak ʿalā al-Ṣaḥīḥayn" through numerous chains. And in some of its chains he added: "And He builds for him a house in Paradise." Among the additions therein is that the narrator said: I arrived in Khurāsān, and I came to Qutaybah ibn Muslim and said: I have brought you a gift. So I narrated the ḥadīth to him, and Qutaybah ibn Muslim would ride in his procession until he reached the market, utter this supplication, and then depart.

Al-Ḥākim also related it from the narration of Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both) from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him). Al-Ḥākim said: On this topic there are reports from Jābir, Abū Hurayrah, Buraydah al-Aslamī, and Anas. He said: The closest of these to the conditions of this book is the ḥadīth of Buraydah, though with different wording.

911 — He related it with his chain from Buraydah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him), when he entered the market, would say: "In the name of Allah. O Allah, I ask You for the good of this market and the good of what is in it, and I seek refuge in You from its evil and the evil of what is in it. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from striking therein a false oath or a losing bargain."

(Chapter on the Recommendation of One Saying to a Person Who Marries a Recommended Marriage, or Buys, or Performs an Act the Law Deems Good: "You Have Done Right" or "You Have Done Well" and the Like)

212 — We have related in "Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim" on the authority of Jābir (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said to me: "Have you married, O Jābir?" I said: Yes. He said: "A virgin or a previously married woman?" I said: A previously married woman, O Messenger of Allah. He said: "Why not a young maiden, that you might sport with her and she with you?" — or he said: "that you might jest with her and she with you." I said: Indeed, ʿAbd Allāh — meaning his father — had died, leaving nine daughters or seven, and I disliked bringing them someone like themselves, so I preferred to bring a woman who would stand over them and set them right. He said: "You have done right..." — and he mentioned the ḥadīth.

(Chapter on What One Says When Looking in the Mirror)

913 — We have related in the Book of Ibn al-Sunnī, on the authority of ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), when he looked in the mirror, would say: "Praise be to Allah. O Allah, just as You have made my form beautiful, so make my character beautiful." And we related it therein from the narration of Ibn ʿAbbās with an addition. And we related it therein from the narration of Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him), when he looked at his face in the mirror, would say: "Praise be to Allah who proportioned my creation and balanced it, honored the image of my face and beautified it, and made me among the Muslims."

(Chapter on What One Says at the Time of Cupping)

914 — We have related in the Book of Ibn al-Sunnī, on the authority of ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever recites the Āyat al-Kursī at the time of cupping, the benefit of his cupping will be increased."

(Chapter on What One Says When His Ear Rings)

915 — We have related in the Book of Ibn al-Sunnī, on the authority of Abū Rāfiʿ (may Allah be pleased with him), the freed slave of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "When the ear of any of you rings, let him remember me, send blessings upon me, and say: 'May Allah mention with good the one who has mentioned me.'"

(Chapter on What One Says When His Leg Goes Numb)

916 — We have related in the Book of Ibn al-Sunnī, on the authority of al-Haytham ibn Ḥanash, who said: We were with ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both), and his leg went numb. A man said to him: Mention the most beloved of people to you. He said: O Muḥammad (peace and blessings be upon him) — and it was as though he were untied from a fetter.
