- Root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Placing a thing in other than its proper place; exceeding the bound; darkness of wrongdoing.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Wrongdoing (ẓulm) as transgression against right order, whether against self, other, or divine command.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: to act unjustly; metaphorical: to obscure truth as night darkens.
- Root: ن-ص-ح (n-ṣ-ḥ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Sincerity, purity of intent; to sew a garment (khayāṭah) — the counselor mends the fabric of faith.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Sincere counsel (naṣīḥah) as desiring good for the advised, free of deceit.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: pure honey; metaphorical: unadulterated advice.
- Root: ج-ر-ح (j-r-ḥ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Wounding the body; disparagement of character.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technical term for declaring a narrator or witness unreliable (al-jarḥ wa-l-taʿdīl).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: physical wound; metaphorical: exposing a defect in probity.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Permissibility (al-ibāḥah bi-l-sharṭ) — The permissibility of each ground is governed by intent (niyyah) and necessity (ḥājah), parsed as a conditional clause where the apodosis (jawāz al-dhikr) is valid only when the protasis (qaṣd al-naṣīḥah) is fulfilled.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that backbiting (al-ghībah) is rendered permissible by six causes, which the scholars have enumerated. I shall mention them, along with their evidences, by the permission of Allah Most High.

**The First Cause: Seeking Redress for Wrongdoing (al-taẓallum).** It is permissible for the wronged person to complain to the ruler, the judge, or anyone else who holds authority or has the power to obtain justice for him against his oppressor. He may say: "So-and-so wronged me," "He did such-and-such to me," "He took such-and-such from me," and the like.

**The Second Cause: Seeking Assistance in Changing an Evil and Returning a Sinner to Righteousness.** One may say to a person whose ability to remove the evil is hoped for: "So-and-so is doing such-and-such; rebuke him for it," and the like. His intention must be to achieve the removal of the evil. If that is not his intention, then it is unlawful (ḥarām).

**The Third Cause: Seeking a Legal Ruling (al-istiftāʾ).** One may say to the muftī: "My father, my brother, or so-and-so wronged me in such-and-such a manner. Is he entitled to do that or not? What is my way to be delivered from him, to obtain my right, and to repel the wrong from me?" and the like. Likewise, one may say: "My wife does such-and-such to me," or "My husband does such-and-such," and the like. This is permissible due to necessity (al-ḥājah). However, the more cautious approach is to say: "What do you say about a man whose affair was such-and-such?" or "about a husband or wife who does such-and-such," and the like — for the purpose is achieved without specification. Nevertheless, specification is permissible, due to the ḥadīth of Hind which we shall mention, Allah willing, and her saying: {«يا رسول الله، إن أبا سفيان رجل شحيح»} — "O Messenger of Allah, verily Abū Sufyān is a miserly man..." — and the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) did not forbid her.

**The Fourth Cause: Warning Muslims Against Evil and Giving Them Sincere Counsel (al-taḥdhīr wa-l-naṣīḥah).** This takes several forms:

- Among them is the disparagement (al-jarḥ) of defective narrators of ḥadīth and witnesses. This is permissible by the consensus of the Muslims — nay, it is obligatory (wājib) due to necessity.

- Among them: If a person seeks your counsel regarding intermarriage with someone, entering into partnership with him, depositing something with him, having him deposit with you, or any other form of transaction with him, then it is incumbent upon you to mention to him what you know of that person, by way of sincere counsel. If the purpose is achieved by merely saying: "It is not proper for you to deal with him," or "to intermarry with him," or "Do not do this," and the like, then it is not permissible to add further mention of his faults. But if the purpose cannot be achieved except by explicit specification of the fault itself, then mention it explicitly.

- Among them: If you see someone purchasing a slave known for theft, fornication, drinking, or other vices, then you must make that clear to the buyer if he is unaware of it. This is not restricted to slaves alone; rather, whoever knows of a defect in any commodity being sold must disclose it to the buyer if the buyer does not know it.

- Among them: If you see a student of sacred knowledge (mutafaqqih) frequenting an innovator (mubtadiʿ) or a sinner (fāsiq) to take knowledge from him, and you fear the student will be harmed by that, then you must counsel him by clarifying that person's condition. It is a condition that one intend sincere counsel. This is a matter in which people often err — the speaker may be driven by envy, or Satan may disguise the matter for him and make him imagine that it is counsel and compassion. Let him be vigilant about this.

- Among them: If a person holds a position of authority (wilāyah) which he does not discharge properly — either because he is not fit for it, or because he is a sinner (fāsiq), or negligent (mughaffal), and the like — then it is obligatory to mention this to the one who has general authority over him, so that he may remove him and appoint one who is fit. Or one may inform the person himself of what is known of him, so that he may deal with him according to his actual state and not be deceived by him. One should also strive to urge him toward uprightness or to have him replaced.

**The Fifth Cause: Open Flagrancy in Sin (al-mujāharah).** If a person openly commits his sin or innovation — such as one who openly drinks wine, or seizes people's property, or collects illegal taxes (al-maks), or levies wealth unjustly, or undertakes false offices — then it is permissible to mention him regarding what he openly does. It is unlawful to mention him for other faults, unless there is another cause for permissibility from among those we have mentioned.

**The Sixth Cause: Identification (al-taʿrīf).** If a person is known by a nickname — such as al-Aʿmash (the blear-eyed), al-Aʿraj (the lame), al-Aṣamm (the deaf), al-Aʿmā (the blind), al-Aḥwal (the cross-eyed), al-Afṭas (the flat-nosed), and others — it is permissible to identify him by that, with the intention of identification. It is unlawful to utter it by way of belittlement. If identification could be achieved by another means, that would be preferable.

These, then, are the six causes which the scholars have mentioned as rendering backbiting permissible, as we have stated. Among those who explicitly enumerated them in this manner is the Imām Abū Ḥāmid al-Ghazālī in his "Iḥyāʾ ʿUlūm al-Dīn," along with other scholars. Their evidences are manifest in the well-known authentic ḥadīths, and most of these causes are agreed upon (mujmaʿ ʿalayhā) as permitting backbiting.

**1040 —** We have related in the two Ṣaḥīḥs of al-Bukhārī and Muslim, on the authority of ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her), that a man sought permission to enter upon the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), whereupon he said: {«ائذنوا له بئس أخو العشيرة»} — "Give him permission. Evil is the brother of the clan." Al-Bukhārī adduced this as evidence for the permissibility of backbiting against people of corruption and people of suspicion.

**1041 —** We have related in the two Ṣaḥīḥs of al-Bukhārī and Muslim, on the authority of Ibn Masʿūd (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) made a distribution, whereupon a man from the Anṣār said: "By Allah, Muhammad did not intend the Face of Allah by this." So I came to the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) and informed him of it. His face changed color, and he said: {«رحم الله موسى لقد أوذي بأكثر من هذا فصبر»} — "May Allah have mercy on Moses; he was harmed with more than this, yet he was patient." In some of its narrations: Ibn Masʿūd said: "So I said: I shall not convey any report to him after this."

I say: Al-Bukhārī adduced this as evidence for a man informing his brother of what is said about him.

**1042 —** We have related in the Ṣaḥīḥ of al-Bukhārī, on the authority of ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: {«ما أظن فلانا وفلانا يعرفان من ديننا شيئا»} — "I do not think that so-and-so and so-and-so know anything of our religion." Al-Layth ibn Saʿd, one of the narrators, said: "They were two men from the hypocrites (al-munāfiqīn)."

**1043 —** We have related in the two Ṣaḥīḥs of al-Bukhārī and Muslim, on the authority of Zayd ibn Arqam (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: We went out with the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) on a journey, and the people were struck by hardship therein. ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy said: "Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse from around him." And he said: "If we return to Medina, the mightier will surely expel the meaner." So I came to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) and informed him of that. He sent word to ʿAbdullāh...

chapters.title_en: Section 138 — On Commanding Whoever Hears Backbiting of His Shaykh, Companion, or Others to Reject It and Nullify It; and On Backbiting by the Heart
chapters.arabic_text:
بن أبي ... وذكر الحديث.
# وأنزل الله تعالى تصديقه: (إذا جاءك المنافقون) [المنافقون: 1] .
# 
# 1044 م - وفي الصحيح حديث هند (1) امرأة أبي سفيان وقولها للنبي (2) (صلى

الله عليه وسلم) : " إن أبا سفيان رجل شحيح ... " إلى آخره.

| 1044 - 
# وحديث فاطمة بنت قيس وقول النبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم) لها: " أما معاوية

فصعلوك (3) ، وأما أبو جهم فلا يضع العصا عن عاتقه " (5) .

| (باب أمر من سمع غيبة شيخه أو صاحبه أو غيرهما بردها وإبطالها)
# اعلم أنه ينبغي لمن سمع غيبة مسلم أن يردها ويزجر قائلها، فإن لم ينزجر

بالكلام زجره بيده، فإن لم يستطع باليد ولا باللسان، فارق ذلك المجلس، فإن

سمع غيبة شيخه أو غيره ممن له عليه حق، أو كان من أهل الفضل والصلاح، كان

الاعتناء بما ذكرناه أكثر.

| 1045 - 
# روينا في كتاب الترمذي عن أبي الدرداء رضي الله عنه عن النبي (صلى الله

عليه وسلم) قال: " من رد عن عرض أخيه رد الله عن وجهه النار يوم القيامة "

قال الترمذي: حديث
# حسن (6) .

| 1046 - 
# وروينا في " صحيحي البخاري ومسلم " في حديث عتبان - بكسر العين على

المشهور، وحكي بضمها - رضي الله عنه في حديثه الطويل المشهور قال: " قام

النبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم) يصلي، فقالوا: أين مالك بن الدخشم؟ فقال رجل:

ذلك منافق لا يحب الله ورسوله، فقال النبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم) : لا تقل

ذلك، ألا تراه قد قال لا إله إلا الله، يريد بذلك وجه الله؟ ".

| 1047 - 
# وروينا في " صحيح مسلم " عن الحسن البصري رحمه الله: أن عائذ بن

# عمرو وكان من أصحاب رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) دخل على عبيد الله بن

زياد فقال: أي بني إني سمعت رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) يقول: " إن شر

الرعاء الحطمة، فإياك أن تكون منهم، فقال له: اجلس، فإنما أنت من نخالة

أصحاب محمد (صلى الله عليه وسلم) ، فقال: وهل كانت لهم نخالة: إنما كانت

النخالة بعدهم وفي غيرهم ".

| 1048 - 
# وروينا في " صحيحيهما " عن كعب بن مالك رضي الله عنه في حديثه
# الطويل في قصة توبته قال: قال النبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم) وهو جالس في

القوم بتبوك " ما فعل كعب بن مالك؟ " فقال رجل من بني سلمة: يا رسول الله

حبسه برداه والنظر في عطفيه، فقال له معاذ بن جبل رضي الله عنه: بئس ما

قلت، والله يا رسول  الله ما علمنا عليه إلا خيرا، فسكت رسول الله (صلى الله

عليه وسلم) .
# قلت: سلمة بكسر اللام، وعطفاه: جانباه، وهو إشارة إلى إعجابه بنفسه.

| 1049 - 
# ورويناه في سنن أبي داود عن جابر بن عبد الله وأبي طلحة رضي الله عنهم

قالا: قال رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) : " ما من امرئ يخذل امرءا مسلما

في موضع تنتهك فيه حرمته وينتقص فيه من عرضه إلا خذله الله في موطن يحب فيه

نصرته، وما من امرئ ينصر مسلما في موضع ينتقص فيه من عرضه، وينتهك فيه من

حرمته إلا نصره الله في موطن يحب نصرته " (1) .

| 1050 - 
# وروينا فيه عن معاذ بن أنس عن النبي (صلى الله عليه وسلم) قال: " من حمى

مؤمنا من منافق - أراه قال - بعث الله تعالى ملكا يحمي لحمه يوم القيامة من

نار جهنم، ومن رمى مسلما بشئ يريد شينه حبسه الله على جسر جهنم حتى يخرج

مما قال ".

| (باب الغيبة بالقلب)
# اعلم أن سوء الظن حرام مثل القول، فكما يحرم أن تحدث غيرك بمساوئ إنسان،

يحرم أن تحدث نفسك بذلك وتسئ الظن به، قال الله تعالى: (اجتنبوا كثيرا من

الظن) [الحجرات: 12] .

| 1051 - 
# وروينا في " صحيحي البخاري ومسلم " عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه أن رسول

الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) قال: " إياكم والظن فإن الظن أكذب الحديث "

والأحاديث بمعنى ما ذكرته 
# كثيرة، والمراد بذلك (1) عقد القلب (2) وحكمه على غيرك بالسوء، فأما

الخواطر، وحديث النفس، إذا لم يستقر ويستمر عليه صاحبه فمعفو عنه باتفاق

العلماء، لأنه لا اختيار له في وقوعه، ولا طريق له إلى الانفكاك عنه.

| 1052 - 
# وهذا هو المراد بما ثبت في الصحيح عن رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) أنه

قال: " إن الله تجاوز لأمتي ما حدثت به أنفسها ما لم تتكلم به أو تعمل "

(3) .
# قال العلماء: المراد به الخواطر التي لا تستقر.
# قالوا: وسواء كان ذلك الخاطر غيبة أو كفرا أو غيره، فمن خطر له الكفر

مجرد خطر من غير تعمد لتحصيله، ثم صرفه في  الحال، فليس بكافر، ولا شئ عليه.
# وقد قدمنا في " باب الوسوسة " في الحديث الصحيح أنهم قالوا: " يا رسول

الله يجد أحدنا ما يتعاظم أن يتكلم به، قال: ذلك صريح الإيمان " (4) وغير

ذلك مما ذكرناه هناك وما هو في معناه.
# وسبب العفو ما ذكرناه من تعذر اجتنابه، وإنما الممكن اجتناب الاستمرار

عليه فلهذا كان الاستمرار وعقد القلب حراما ومهما عرض لك هذا الخاطر

بالغيبة وغيرها من المعاصي، وجب عليك دفعه بالإعراض عنه وذكر التأويلات

الصارفة له عن ظاهره.
# قال الإمام أبو حامد الغزالي في " الإحياء ": إذا وقع في قلبك ظن السوء،
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ر-د-د (r-d-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To return, repel, reject; the act of turning something back to its source or preventing its advance.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological context, "radd" signifies the repudiation of falsehood and the restoration of honor (ʿirḍ) to its rightful state, mirroring divine repulsion of harm.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in physical return; metaphorical (majāz) in verbal defense of another's reputation, as in "radda ʿan ʿirḍi akhīhi" (he repelled from his brother's honor).
- Root: غ-ي-ب (gh-y-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Absence, concealment; ghībah is mentioning a person in his absence with what he dislikes.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ghībah is a moral failing rooted in the heart's hidden malice; its prohibition is absolute, whether spoken or internalized.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal absence of the person; metaphorical for the hidden vice being exposed, contrasting with the speaker's own hidden faults.
- Root: ظ-ن-ن (ẓ-n-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Doubt, suspicion, conjecture; a belief not firmly established.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ẓann in the Quranic verse {«اجتنبوا كثيرا من الظن»} denotes sinful suspicion that settles in the heart, as opposed to transient thoughts (khawāṭir).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal suspicion; metaphorical for the heart's verdict (ʿaqd al-qalb) against another, which is the true object of prohibition.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — The phrase "fa-in lam yanzajir... fa-in lam yastaṭiʿ..." employs layered conditionals to establish a graded obligation (repel by tongue, then hand, then departure), each clause governing the next with precise syntactic dependency.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that it is incumbent upon whoever hears the backbiting of a Muslim to reject it and rebuke its speaker. If he is not deterred by speech, then he should rebuke him with his hand. If he is unable to do so, neither by hand nor by tongue, then he must leave that gathering. If he hears the backbiting of his shaykh, or of anyone who holds a right over him, or of a person of virtue and righteousness, then the care in what we have mentioned becomes even greater.

We have related in the Book of al-Tirmidhī, from Abū al-Dardāʾ (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), who said: "Whoever repels from the honor of his brother, Allah will repel the Fire from his face on the Day of Resurrection." Al-Tirmidhī said: This is a ḥasan (good) hadith.

And we have related in the two Ṣaḥīḥs of al-Bukhārī and Muslim, in the hadith of ʿItbān — with kasrah on the ʿayn according to the well-known reading, and it is also narrated with ḍammah — may Allah be pleased with him, in his long, famous hadith, he said: "The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) stood to pray, and they said: 'Where is Mālik ibn al-Dukhshum?' A man said: 'That is a hypocrite who does not love Allah and His Messenger.' The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: 'Do not say that. Do you not see that he has said: There is no god but Allah, seeking thereby the Face of Allah?'"

And we have related in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, from al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī (may Allah have mercy on him): that ʿĀʾidh ibn ʿAmr — who was among the companions of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) — entered upon ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Ziyād and said: "O my son, I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) say: 'Indeed, the worst of shepherds are those who crush (al-ḥuṭamah). Beware of being among them.' He said to him: 'Sit down, for you are but of the chaff of the companions of Muḥammad (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him).' He replied: 'Did they even have chaff? Rather, the chaff came after them and among others.'"

And we have related in both Ṣaḥīḥs, from Kaʿb ibn Mālik (may Allah be pleased with him), in his long hadith concerning the story of his repentance, he said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said, while sitting among the people at Tabūk: "What has Kaʿb ibn Mālik done?" A man from the Banū Salamah said: "O Messenger of Allah, his two garments and his looking at his sides have detained him." Muʿādh ibn Jabal (may Allah be pleased with him) said to him: "Evil is what you have said. By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, we know nothing of him but good." The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) remained silent.

I say: Salamah is with kasrah on the lām, and his "two sides" (ʿiṭfāhu) refers to his two flanks, which is an allusion to his self-admiration.

And we have related it in the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd, from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh and Abū Ṭalḥah (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "There is no man who abandons a Muslim man in a place where his sanctity is violated and his honor is diminished, except that Allah will abandon him in a place where he loves His support. And there is no man who supports a Muslim in a place where his honor is diminished and his sanctity is violated, except that Allah will support him in a place where he loves His support."

And we have related therein, from Muʿādh ibn Anas, from the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), who said: "Whoever protects a believer from a hypocrite — I think he said — Allah the Exalted will send an angel to protect his flesh on the Day of Resurrection from the Fire of Hell. And whoever accuses a Muslim of something, intending to disgrace him, Allah will detain him on the Bridge of Hell until he emerges from what he has said."

Section on Backbiting by the Heart:
Know that evil suspicion (sūʾ al-ẓann) is forbidden just as speech is forbidden. For just as it is unlawful to inform others of a person's faults, it is unlawful to inform yourself of that and to think evil of him. Allah the Exalted said: {«اجتنبوا كثيرا من الظن»} (Avoid much suspicion) [al-Ḥujurāt: 12].

And we have related in the two Ṣaḥīḥs of al-Bukhārī and Muslim, from Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "Beware of suspicion, for suspicion is the most false of speech." The hadiths to the meaning of what I have mentioned are numerous. What is intended by that is the heart's firm resolve (ʿaqd al-qalb) and its verdict against another with evil. As for passing thoughts (al-khawāṭir) and inner speech, if they do not settle and the person does not persist upon them, they are excused by the consensus of the scholars, because he has no choice in their occurrence, nor any path to free himself from them.

And this is what is intended by what is established in the Ṣaḥīḥ, from the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), that he said: "Indeed, Allah has excused for my nation what their souls whisper to them, as long as they do not speak it or act upon it." The scholars said: What is intended is the passing thoughts that do not settle. They said: It is the same whether that thought is backbiting, disbelief, or anything else. Whoever has disbelief occur to him as a mere passing thought, without intending to acquire it, then repels it immediately, he is not a disbeliever, and nothing is upon him. We have already presented in the "Section on Whispering (al-waswasah)" in the authentic hadith that they said: "O Messenger of Allah, one of us finds within himself something too great to speak of." He said: "That is clear faith." And other things we mentioned there and what is in its meaning.

The cause of the pardon is what we mentioned: the impossibility of avoiding it. Rather, what is possible is avoiding persistence upon it. For this reason, persistence and the heart's firm resolve are forbidden. Whenever this thought occurs to you — whether of backbiting or other sins — it is obligatory upon you to repel it by turning away from it and by mentioning interpretations (taʾwīlāt) that divert it from its apparent meaning.

Imam Abū Ḥāmid al-Ghazālī said in al-Iḥyāʾ: "When evil suspicion falls into your heart..."

chapters.title_en: Section 139 — On the Whisper of Satan, the Prohibition of Ill-Thought (Sū’ al-Ẓann), and the Expiation of Backbiting (Kaffārat al-Ghībah)
chapters.arabic_text:
فهو من وسوسة الشيطان يلقيه إليك، فينبغي أن تكذبه فإنه أفسق الفساق، وقد

قال الله تعالى: (إن جاءكم فاسق بنبإ فتبينوا أن تصيبوا قوما بجهالة

فتصبحوا على ما فعلتم نادمين) [الحجرات: 7] فلا يجوز تصديق إبليس، فإن كان

هناك قرينة تدل على فساد، واحتمل خلافه، لم تجز إساءة الظن، ومن علامة

إساءة الظن أن يتغير قلبك معه عما كان عليه، 
# فتنفر منه وتستثقله وتفتر عن مراعاته وإكرامه والاغتمام بسيئته، فإن

الشيطان قد يقرب إلى القلب بأدنى خيال مساوئ الناس، ويلقي إليه: أن هذا من

فطنتك وذكائك وسرعة تنبهك، وإن المؤمن ينظر بنور الله، وإنما هو على

التحقيق ناطق بغرور الشيطان وظلمته، وإن أخبرك عدل بذلك، فلا تصدقه ولا

تكذبه لئلا تسئ الظن بأحدهما، ومهما خطر لك سوء في مسلم، فزد في مراعاته

وإكرامه، فإن ذلك يغيظ الشيطان ويدفعه عنك فلا يلقي إليك مثله خيفة من

اشتغالك بالدعاء له، ومهما عرفت هفوة مسلم بحجة لا شك فيها، فالصحه في

السر، ولا يخدعنك الشيطان فيدعوك إلى اغتيابه، وإذا وعظته فلا تعظه وأنت

مسرور باطلاعك على نقصه فينظر إليك بعين التعظيم وتنظر إليه بالاستصغار،

ولكن اقصد تخليصه من الإثم وأنت حزين كما تحزن على نفسك إذا دخلك نقص،

وينبغي أن يكون تركه لذلك النقص بغير وعظك أحب إليك من تركه بوعظك، هذا

كلام الغزالي.
# قلت: قد ذكرنا أنه يجب عليه إذا عرض له خاطر  بسوء الظن أن يقطعه، وهذا

إذا لم تدع إلى الفكر في ذلك مصلحة شرعية، فإذا دعت جاز الفكر في نقيصته

والتنقيب عنها كما في جرح الشهود والرواة وغير ذلك مما ذكرناه في " باب ما

يباح من الغيبة ".

| (باب كفارة الغيبة والتوبة منها)
# اعلم أن كل من ارتكب معصية لزمه المبادرة إلى التوبة منها، والتوبة من

حقوق الله
# تعالى يشترط فيها ثلاثة أشياء: أن يقلع عن المعصية في الحال، وأن يندم

على فعلها، وأن يعزم ألا يعود إليها.
# والتوبة من حقوق الآدميين يشترط فيها هذه الثلاثة، ورابع: وهو رد الظلامة

إلى صاحبها أو طلب عفوه عنها والإبراء منها، فيجب على المغتاب التوبة بهذه

الأمور الأربعة، لأن الغيبة حق آدمي، ولا بد من استحلاله من اغتابه، وهل

يكفيه أن يقول: قد اغتبتك فاجعلني في حل، أم لا بد أن يبين ما اغتابه به؟

فيه وجهان لأصحاب الشافعي رحمهم الله: أحدهما يشترط بيانه، فإن أبرأه من

غير بيانه، لم يصح، كما لو أبرأه عن مال مجهول.
# والثاني لا يشترط، لأن هذا مما يتسامح فيه، فلا يشترط علمه، بخلاف المال،

والأول أظهر، لأن الإنسان قد يسمح بالعفو عن غيبة دون غيبة، فإن كان صاحب

الغيبة ميتا أو غائبا فقد تعذر تحصيل البراءة منها، لكن قال العلماء: ينبغي

أن يكثر من الاستغفار له والدعاء ويكثر من الحسنات.
# 
# واعلم أنه يستحب لصاحب الغيبة أن يبرئه منها ولا يجب عليه ذلك لأنه تبرع

وإسقاط حق، فكان إلى خيرته، ولكن يستحب له استحبابا متأكدا الإبراء ليخلص

أخاه المسلم من وبال هذه المعصية، ويفوز هو بعظيم ثواب الله تعالى في العفو

ومحبة الله سبحانه وتعالى، قال الله تعالى: (والكاظمين الغيظ والعافين عن

الناس والله يحب المحسنين) [آل عمران: 134] وطريقه في تطبيب نفسه بالعفو أن

يذكر نفسه أن هذا الأمر قد وقع، ولا سبيل إلى رفعه، فلا ينبغي أن أفوت

ثوابه وخلاص أخي المسلم، وقد قال الله تعالى: (ولمن صبر وغفر إن ذلك لمن

عزم الأمور) [الشورى: 43] وقال تعالى: (خذ  العفو ... ) الاية [الأعراف:

199] .
# والآيات بنحو ما ذكرنا كثيرة.

| 1053 - 
# وفي الحديث الصحيح أن رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وسلم) قال: " والله في

عون العبد ما كان العبد في عون أخيه " (1) وقد قال الشافعي رحمه الله: من

استرضي فلم يرض فهو شيطان.
# وقد أنشد المتقدمون:
# قيل لي قد أساء إليك فلان * ومقام الفتى على الذل عار
# قلت: قد جاءنا وأحدث عذرا * دية الذنب عندنا الاعتذار
# فهذا الذي ذكرناه من الحث على الإبراء عن الغيبة هو الصواب.
# وأما ما جاء عن سعيد بن المسيب أنه قال: لا أحلل من ظلمني.
# وعن ابن سيرين: لم أحرمها عليه فأحللها له، لأن الله تعالى حرم الغيبة

عليه، وما كنت لأحلل ما حرمه الله تعالى أبدا، فهو ضعيف أو غلط، فإن المبرئ

لا يحلل محرما، وإنما يسقط حقا ثبت له، وقد تظاهرت نصوص الكتاب والسنة على

استحباب العفو وإسقاط الحقوق المختصة بالمسقط، أو يحمل كلام ابن سيرين على

أني لا أبيح غيبتي أبدا، وهذا صحيح فإن الإنسان لو قال: أبحت عرضي لمن

اغتابني لم يصر مباحا، بل يحرم على كل أحد غيبة غيره.

| 1054 - 
# وأما الحديث: " أيعجز أحدكم أن يكون كأبي ضمضم كان إذا خرج من بيته قال

إني تصدقت بعرضي على الناس " (2) فمعناه: لا أطلب مظلمتي ممن ظلمني لا في

الدنيا ولا في الآخرة، وهذا ينفع في إسقاط مظلمة كانت موجودة قبل الإبراء.
# فأما يحدث بعده، فلا بد من إبراء جديد بعدها، وبالله التوفيق.

| (باب في النميمة)
# قد ذكرنا تحريمها ودلائلها وما جاء في الوعيد عليها، وذكرنا بيان
chapters.anchors:
- Root: و-س-و-س (waswasa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The faint, subtle sound; the insinuation that creeps into the heart without volition.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The satanic suggestion that blurs discernment between truth and falsehood, planted to corrupt certainty.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: a soft rustling sound; Metaphorical: the covert whisper of Satan into the soul.
- Root: ظ-ن-ن (ẓanna)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Doubt, suspicion, or belief not grounded in certainty.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, ill-thought (sū’ al-ẓann) toward a believer is a moral failing, opposed to ḥusn al-ẓann (good opinion).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: conjecture; Metaphorical: the heart’s inclination without decisive evidence.
- Root: غ-ي-ب (ghayba)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Absence; speaking of someone in their absence.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The mention of a person’s fault behind their back, legally defined as a violation of their honor (ʿirḍ).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: being hidden; Metaphorical: the verbal assault on one’s reputation while absent.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause (al-Sharṭ wa al-Jawāb) — The structure “if a sinner brings you news, then verify” (fa-tabayyanū) mandates a legal consequence (jawāb) contingent upon the condition (sharṭ), indicating the obligation of investigation before action.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that this [ill-thought] is from the whispering of Satan, which he casts into you. It is incumbent upon you to give it the lie, for he is the most wicked of the wicked. Allah the Exalted has said: {«If a wicked person brings you news, then verify, lest you harm a people in ignorance and become regretful over what you have done»} [al-Ḥujurāt: 7]. Thus, it is not permissible to believe Iblīs. If there is an indication suggesting corruption, yet the opposite remains possible, it is not permissible to harbor ill-thought. Among the signs of ill-thought is that your heart changes toward him from what it was, so you recoil from him, find him burdensome, and slacken in attending to him, honoring him, and grieving over his misdeed. For Satan may draw near to the heart with the slightest fancy of people’s faults, casting into it: “This is from your acumen, your intelligence, and your quick perceptiveness, and the believer sees with the light of Allah.” In truth, this is but speech adorned by Satan’s deception and darkness. If a just person informs you of such, do not affirm him nor deny him, lest you think ill of either. And whenever evil occurs to your mind regarding a Muslim, increase in attending to him and honoring him, for that enrages Satan and repels him from you, so he will not cast the like of it into you, fearing your occupation with supplication for him. And whenever you discern a slip of a Muslim with an undeniable proof, then conceal it in secret, and let not Satan deceive you into calling you to backbite him. If you admonish him, do not admonish him while you are delighted at your discovery of his deficiency, so that he looks at you with veneration while you look at him with belittlement. Rather, intend his deliverance from sin while you are sorrowful, just as you sorrow for yourself when a deficiency enters you. And it is fitting that his abandonment of that deficiency without your admonition be dearer to you than his abandonment through your admonition. This is the speech of al-Ghazālī.

I say: We have already mentioned that it is obligatory upon him, when a thought of ill-opinion occurs, to cut it off. This applies when no legitimate religious interest (maṣlaḥah sharʿiyyah) calls for reflection upon it. But if such an interest calls, then it is permissible to reflect upon his deficiency and to investigate it, as in the case of discrediting witnesses (jarḥ al-shuhūd) and narrators (al-ruwāh), and other matters we have mentioned in the chapter “On What Is Permissible of Backbiting.”

| (Chapter on the Expiation of Backbiting and Repentance from It)

Know that whoever commits a sin is obligated to hasten to repentance from it. Repentance from the rights of Allah the Exalted requires three conditions: that he desist from the sin immediately, that he regret having done it, and that he resolve never to return to it. Repentance from the rights of human beings requires these three, plus a fourth: the restoration of the wrong to its owner, or seeking his pardon and absolution from it. Thus, the backbiter must repent through these four matters, for backbiting is a right of a human being, and it is indispensable to seek absolution from the one he backbit. Is it sufficient for him to say, “I have backbit you, so absolve me,” or must he specify what he backbit him with? There are two opinions among the companions of al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah have mercy on them: One holds that specification is required, for if he absolves him without specification, it is invalid, just as if he absolved him of an unknown debt. The second holds that specification is not required, because this is a matter in which leniency is tolerated, so knowledge of it is not required, unlike wealth. The first is more apparent (aẓhar), for a person may be generous in pardoning one backbiting but not another. If the one backbit is dead or absent, then obtaining absolution is rendered impossible, but the scholars said: He should increase in seeking forgiveness for him, supplicating for him, and increasing in good deeds.

Know that it is recommended (mustaḥabb) for the one backbit to absolve him, though it is not obligatory upon him, for it is a voluntary act and a waiver of a right, so it is left to his choice. However, it is strongly recommended that he grant absolution, to deliver his Muslim brother from the burden of this sin, and to attain the immense reward of Allah the Exalted in pardoning and the love of Allah, Glorified and Exalted be He. Allah the Exalted has said: {«And those who restrain anger and pardon people — and Allah loves the doers of good»} [Āl ʿImrān: 134]. His way of healing his soul through pardon is to remind himself that this matter has occurred, and there is no means to remove it, so it is not fitting that I forfeit its reward and the deliverance of my Muslim brother. Allah the Exalted has said: {«And whoever is patient and forgives — indeed, that is of the matters of determination»} [al-Shūrā: 43], and He said: {«Take forgiveness...»} the verse [al-Aʿrāf: 199]. The verses along the lines of what we have mentioned are numerous.

| 1053 —
In the authentic ḥadīth, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “Allah is in the aid of the servant as long as the servant is in the aid of his brother.” Al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah have mercy on him, said: “Whoever is asked to pardon and does not pardon is a devil.” The early poets recited:
“It was said to me: So-and-so has wronged you — and the station of a man upon humiliation is disgrace.
I said: He came to us and offered an excuse — the ransom of the fault with us is the apology.”
Thus, what we have mentioned of urging absolution from backbiting is the correct view. As for what is reported from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib that he said, “I do not absolve whoever wronged me,” and from Ibn Sīrīn, “I have not made it unlawful for him, so I would absolve him, for Allah the Exalted has made backbiting unlawful upon him, and I would never make lawful what Allah has made unlawful,” — this is weak or erroneous. For the one who absolves does not make lawful what is unlawful; he merely waives a right established for him. The texts of the Book and the Sunnah have concurred on the recommendation of pardon and the waiver of rights specific to the one who waives them. Or Ibn Sīrīn’s statement may be interpreted as: “I do not permit my backbiting ever,” and this is sound, for if a man said, “I have made my honor permissible to whoever backbites me,” it would not become permissible; rather, it remains unlawful for everyone to backbite another.

| 1054 —
As for the ḥadīth: “Is any of you unable to be like Abū Ḍamḍam, who, when he left his house, said: ‘Indeed, I have given my honor in charity to the people’,” its meaning is: I do not seek my claim from whoever wrongs me, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter. This benefits in waiving a claim that existed before the absolution. As for what occurs after it, a new absolution is required after it. And with Allah is success.

| (Chapter on Tale-Bearing (Namīmah))
We have already mentioned its prohibition, its proofs, and what has come regarding the threat against it, and we have mentioned the clarification...
